# Phase 3: Provider Framework, Linux/SSH Targets and `alice-helper` — Implementation Plan

> **For agentic workers:** REQUIRED SUB-SKILL: Use superpowers:subagent-driven-development (recommended) or superpowers:executing-plans to implement this plan task-by-task. Steps use checkbox (`- [ ]`) syntax for tracking.

**Goal:** An administrator prepares a Linux server with the setup snippet Alice generates (root-owned static `alice-helper`, `alice-svc` service user, restricted sudoers profile), adds it in Alice, confirms its SSH host-key fingerprint, and sees every `authorized_keys` entry on it in an inventory with filters; Alice refuses to remove its own key, blocks every operation on a server whose host key changed until an Administrator re-confirms it with step-up, counts servers against the license, and runs all remote work through a durable, license-gated PostgreSQL job queue that survives crashes.

**Architecture:** `internal/providers` defines the compile-time provider interface, capability set and registry; `internal/providers/linuxssh` implements the `linuxssh` provider on `golang.org/x/crypto/ssh` with strict host-key pinning (TOFU only after an Administrator confirms the fingerprint), a bounded connection pool, per-command timeouts and output caps, and a remote command surface limited to `sudo -n /usr/local/libexec/alice-helper <subcommand> <validated args>`; its pure parsers (`authorized_keys`, `sshd -T`) are fuzzed. `cmd/alice-helper` is the static Go helper installed root-owned on targets; it validates every argument itself, computes the allowed `authorized_keys` paths from `/etc/passwd` and `sshd -T`, and writes files with compare-and-swap, backup and atomic rename. `internal/inventory` owns targets, credentials (the platform Ed25519 key, envelope-encrypted), pinned host keys and the SSH key inventory; every target insert passes `license.Service.CheckCanAddTarget` in its transaction. `internal/jobs` grows a durable queue (`FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED`, leases with heartbeats, a reaper, retries with backoff and jitter, per-target locks taken in the claim transaction, HMAC'd payloads, `blocked_license` with Administrator confirmation per R29) next to the Phase 2 periodic scheduler, which gains a cross-process leader lock; `internal/jobs/targetjobs` holds the handlers that connect providers to inventory. The API adds targets, host keys, SSH keys, jobs and providers routes, all in the route table with permissions and license classes; the SPA adds Servers and SSH keys screens, the add-server flow with fingerprint confirmation, the changed-key re-pin dialog and a wizard step with Alice's public key.

**Tech Stack:** Go 1.27.1 (stdlib `crypto/ed25519`, `crypto/hmac`, `crypto/sha256`, `debug/elf`, `os/exec`, `syscall`), `golang.org/x/crypto/ssh` (already a dependency through x/crypto), pgx v5, goose v3, testify, testcontainers-go v0.44 (PostgreSQL module and generic containers built from Dockerfiles); React 18 + TypeScript 6 + Vite 8, Mantine 8, React Router 7, TanStack Query 5, i18next, Vitest 5 + Testing Library + msw 2, Playwright 1.63 + axe-core.

**Spec:** `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-09-29-alice-v1-design.md` and `docs/superpowers/specs/alice-v1/` — especially `00-decisions.md` (Integrations "Linux SSH keys", Security, R9, R11, R13, R21, R24, R29, R30, R33, R34, R35, R36), `02-architecture.md` §5.3, §5.4, §6 (provider interface, registry, `linuxssh` connector, host-key pinning, remote command surface), §7.2 (credentials), §7.3 (targets, host_keys, ssh_keys, ssh_key_locations), §7.4 (target_locks, jobs, job_attempts), §8 (queue, job types, scheduler, retries, concurrency, lock gating, crash recovery), §9 (API conventions, errors, endpoint groups), `03-integrations.md` §12.2–§12.3 (service account, sudoers, helper interface, path validation), §13 (Linux SSH key management), `04-security.md` §14.4 (Job runner, SSH connector and target helper), SEC-016, SEC-040..SEC-044, SEC-050, SEC-060..SEC-065, SEC-080..SEC-082, §17.2 (Phase 3 gate), `05-operations.md` §18.5 step 7, §21 (`docs/nginx-host-preparation.md`), `06-quality.md` §22.3 (testcontainers OpenSSH images), §22.6 (SSH fixtures), §23.7 (L-70..L-79), §23.8 (L-81), §24.2 (F-30..F-39), §24.4 (F-66, F-69), §25.1, §25.2, §25.4 (A-12), §25.6 (`FuzzParseAuthorizedKeys`, `FuzzParseSSHDConfig`), §26.1, §26.5. `00-decisions.md` wins on conflict; this plan proposes **R37** (Task 23) for the conflicts listed under "Spec conflicts resolved by this plan". The Phase 2 plan (`docs/superpowers/plans/2026-09-30-phase-2-licensing.md`), `docs/superpowers/rulings/phase-{1,2}.md` and `docs/security/reviews/phase-{1,2}.md` are the style and carry references.

**Plan verification:** the tasks were written against the code on branch `phase-3` at `5f39dab`; every "Modify" step quotes the text it replaces, and every existing symbol a task uses was checked with `grep` in that tree. Owner verification (Task 23) runs at execution time.

## Global Constraints

- Go module path is `alice`; toolchain `go 1.27.1`. Every shell step assumes `export PATH="$HOME/.local/go/bin:$HOME/go/bin:$PATH"` and the repository root as working directory.
- All code, identifiers, comments, file names, commit messages and technical docs are in English. Turkish appears only as translation values in `tr.json` files.
- Commits: Conventional Commits, made with `git -c user.name="Eren Altan" -c user.email=erenaltan@gmail.com commit`, message ending with the line `Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>`.
- Code blocks in this plan are gofmt-clean except for column alignment of consecutive one-line declarations and struct fields: run `gofmt -w` (or `make lint`) on every changed Go file before committing.
- Tests: Go stdlib `testing` plus testify `require`/`assert` only; small hand fakes, no mock frameworks. Integration tests carry `//go:build integration`, call `pgtest.Main` from `TestMain` and get a fresh database per test from `pgtest.New(t)` (pools `Owner` and `App`; the application always uses `App`). A red step in a brand-new package may fail with "no non-test Go files"; that is the expected failure.
- Build tags: `integration` (PostgreSQL and container tests), `e2e` (test-only `/test/*` endpoints, demo clock), `testlicense` (trusts the test signing key), `releasecheck`. Release images are built with no tag; the e2e image with `e2e testlicense`. Integration tests that need a license use `licensetest.KeySet()` and `licensetest.Sign` (no tag needed).
- Lint is golangci-lint v2 (`make lint`): gosec, errorlint, forbidigo, bodyclose, misspell, noctx, gofmt, goimports (`local-prefixes: alice`). Forbidden: `fmt.Print*`, `strings.ToUpper`/`ToLower`/`Title`, `time.Now` outside `internal/platform/clock` and tests (`cmd/alice-helper` is a separate binary without an injected clock: it reads time only through its `sys.now` field, set to `time.Now` in `main.go` with `//nolint:forbidigo // the helper is a separate binary; its clock is injected through sys.now`). No `//nolint` without a reason. `ssh.InsecureIgnoreHostKey` and the string `StrictHostKeyChecking` are forbidden everywhere (a forbidigo pattern `^ssh\.InsecureIgnoreHostKey$` is added in Task 8 and a repository grep test in Task 8 fails on `StrictHostKeyChecking=no`).
- Module import rules are enforced by `internal/archtest` (unchanged in this phase): `providers` imports `platform` and `secrets`; `providers/*` import `platform`, `providers` and `providers/linuxssh/...` — never `platform/db`; `inventory` imports `platform`, `secrets`, `audit`, `license`, `rbac`, `providers`; `jobs/...` imports `platform`, `audit`, `license`, `inventory`, `providers`, `notify`; `api` never imports a provider implementation; `cmd/*` is the composition root (the only place importing `providers/linuxssh`). `cmd/alice-helper` imports only the standard library, `golang.org/x/crypto/ssh` and `alice/internal/providers/linuxssh/{helperproto,sshdconf}`.
- Runtime Go dependencies of `alice` are unchanged (pgx, goose, x/text, google/uuid, x/crypto, pquerna/otp). Test-only: testcontainers-go (already present). No new web dependencies.
- No SQL string building (SEC-060). SQL time comes from the injected clock as a bind parameter, never from `now()` in a statement that decides anything (the e2e demo clock must move job leases and schedules). `alice_app` gets explicit grants for every new table; the grant guard (`migrations/roles_integration_test.go`) lists every non-default grant set.
- **Remote command rule (security-critical, R13, SEC-063):** Alice sends only two kinds of command lines over SSH: the fixed `cat /etc/os-release`, and `sudo -n /usr/local/libexec/alice-helper <subcommand> [args]` built by the constructors in `internal/providers/linuxssh/command.go`, where every argument passes `helperproto.ValidArg` and is wrapped by the single quoting function `quoteArg`. `alice-helper version` runs without sudo. No other code path writes to an SSH session's command string; a test in Task 8 parses the package and fails on any `session.Run`, `session.Start`, `session.Output` or `session.CombinedOutput` call outside `dial.go`.
- **Host key rule (security-critical, SEC-080):** every SSH connection uses the pinned-key callback of `linuxssh.Dialer`; a connection to a target without a pinned key stops at the key exchange (no authentication attempt) and records the presented key as `observed`; only an Administrator's confirmation pins it; a different key or a missing algorithm marks the target `host_key_changed`, stops at the key exchange, and nothing runs on that target until an Administrator re-pins with step-up and a reason. Background jobs never pin.
- **Secret rule:** the platform SSH private key exists in plaintext only inside `inventory.Service.SSHSigner` for the duration of one dial; it is stored only as an envelope (`credentials.ciphertext`, AAD `credentials/<id>/ciphertext`), never logged, never in an error, audit detail, job payload/result or API response; the public key and fingerprint are not secret. Audit detail keys must pass the Phase 1 denylist (`key`, `secret`, `token`, … segments are refused): use `algorithm`, `fingerprint`, `old_fingerprint`, `new_fingerprint`, `os_user`, `file_path`, never `key_type` or `public_key`. Log attribute keys ending in `key` are redacted by the logger; never log key material under another name.
- API JSON conventions from Phase 1 (snake_case, UTC RFC 3339, error body with `code`, `reason`, `message_key`, `message`, `request_id`, `retryable`, `params`, `details`; lists `{items, next_cursor}`); every new code `ALC-<AREA>-<NNNN>` has `errors.<reason>.title|cause|action` in `locales/common/{en,tr}.json` and a section in `docs/troubleshooting.md` (tests in `internal/api/errors_test.go` enforce both).
- Every new route is in the route table with a permission and (for non-GET methods) an explicit license class, in `api/openapi.yaml` with the same `x-permission`, in `docs/authz-matrix.md` (`make authz-doc`), and in the authz matrix test. Long operations answer `202 {"job_id": …, "status_url": "/api/v1/jobs/<id>"}`.
- i18n: every user-visible string is a key in English and Turkish (`make i18n-check`); placeholders `{{name}}` without spaces; no sentence assembly and no suffixes attached to placeholders; plural forms use `_one`/`_other` in both languages. The English and Turkish UI copy in the "UI copy" table below is exact and is what the Playwright tests match.
- Accessibility: new screens and dialogs have no serious or critical axe violation at 640, 1280 and 1920 px (`expectAccessible`) and at 375 px for the Servers and SSH keys pages (header and tables wrap or scroll inside their own container, never the page), in English and Turkish, are keyboard usable, and do not scroll horizontally.
- Frontend: no `dangerouslySetInnerHTML`, no `toUpperCase`/`toLowerCase`; fingerprints, host names, paths, commands and key comments are rendered with the existing `<Code>`/monospace styling, never translated or case-transformed, and always as text (A-11).
- Container: unchanged hardening. The e2e overlay adds one test target service `sshtarget` on the internal `backend` network; no test ever runs commands in any container that is not part of the `alice` compose project or created by testcontainers in the same test.

## Review Focus

1. **`authorized_keys` files as they exist in the wild** — CRLF line endings, no trailing newline, options with quoted commas and spaces (`command="echo a,b",from="10.0.0.0/8"`), the same key twice, `cert-authority` and `@cert-authority`-style lines, an `sk-ssh-ed25519@openssh.com` key, NUL bytes and binary garbage, a 2 MiB file. Expected: every parseable key is listed with its user and line, unreadable lines are reported as "unreadable line N" and preserved byte-for-byte on any rewrite, a file over 1 MiB is not read (warning `file_too_large`), and removing one key never touches another line. Tests: Task 5 (`TestParsePreservesUnreadableLinesVerbatim`, `TestRemoveTouchesOnlyMatchingLines`, `TestParseRejectsOversizedFile`, fuzz corpus seeds) and Task 10 (`TestRemoveKeepsCRLFAndForeignLines`).
2. **A server address typed the way people type it** — `WEB-01.Example.com.`, ` web-01 ` with spaces, `web-01:2222`, `[2001:db8::5]`, `ssh://web-01`, `169.254.169.254`, an IDN host `sunucu.örnek.com.tr`. Expected: case and a trailing dot are normalized, the port field is the only place for a port, IPv6 literals work, metadata/link-local/multicast/unspecified addresses and non-ASCII host names are refused with a field error that says why, and `WEB-01` and `web-01` are the same server for the duplicate check. Test: Task 13 (`TestNormalizeHostTable`, `TestDuplicateTargetIsCaseInsensitive`).
3. **A slow or flapping server** — 10 s latency per command, a connection that drops in the middle of `authkeys-write`, a server that sends 50 MiB on stdout or terminal escape sequences. Expected: each step times out on its own budget, the job fails cleanly with `ssh.timeout`/`ssh.output_too_large`, the connection is closed and its pool slot released, the remote file is either the old or the new version (never partial), and nothing from the remote output reaches logs or the UI unescaped. Tests: Task 8 (`TestRunTimesOutAndClosesSession`, `TestRunCapsOutput`), Task 9 (`TestPoolReleasesSlotAfterFailure`), Task 7 (`TestWriteIsAtomicWhenInterrupted`).
4. **Alice restarts, or two Alice processes run during an update, while jobs are queued and running** — Expected: each job runs exactly once to completion (no duplicate removal, no duplicate audit row), a job that held a lease when its process died is re-queued once with `job.lease_expired` and audited `job.recovered`, two jobs for the same server never overlap, and only one process schedules periodic work. Tests: Task 11 (`TestTwentyWorkersRunThousandJobsExactlyOnce`, `TestSameTargetJobsNeverOverlap`), Task 12 (`TestKilledWorkerJobIsRecoveredOnce`, `TestOnlyOneSchedulerLeads`).
5. **The customer legitimately reinstalls a server (new host key) while nightly discovery is scheduled** — Expected: no command runs on it, the target is marked "Server identity changed", Administrators get exactly one email (not one per job or per retry), Operators cannot accept the new key (403), an Administrator accepts it with step-up and a reason, the old fingerprint stays in the history as superseded, and scheduled discovery resumes. Tests: Task 14 (`TestChangedKeyNotifiesOnceAndBlocks`, `TestRepinKeepsHistory`), Task 17 (`TestChangedHostKeyJourney`).

## Spec conflicts resolved by this plan (proposed R37, written in Task 23)

| # | Conflict | Resolution |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Platform SSH private key: a host file `/opt/alice/keys/ssh_ed25519` (§18.3, §20.2) vs "stored the same way" as generated keys in the encrypted store (§13.5, decisions "Secrets protection") | Encrypted store: one `credentials` row (`purpose = 'platform_ssh'`, `kind = 'ssh_private_key'`), payload = the 32-byte Ed25519 seed, envelope AAD `credentials/<id>/ciphertext`; generated on the first start after migration (or after the e2e reset); no host file. Backups carry it inside the database dump (Phase 8). The public key and fingerprint are in `public_info` |
| 2 | §12.2 `curl … /api/v1/setup/alice-helper` from the target, while §9.6 makes that route Admin-only (a target has no Admin session) | Phase 3 serves no binary over HTTP. `make helper` builds `bin/alice-helper-linux-{amd64,arm64}` and `bin/alice-helper.sha256`; the setup script installs the copy the administrator placed next to it; Phase 8 ships the same files in the release tarball's `helper/` directory. `GET /api/v1/ssh-keys/platform-key` (§9.6 name) returns the public key, fingerprint, the `authorized_keys` line and the per-profile setup script and sudoers text |
| 3 | §12.3 lists nginx subcommands that Phase 3 cannot use yet | Helper protocol 1 implements `version`, `sshd-dump`, `hostkeys`, `authkeys-list`, `authkeys-read`, `authkeys-write`, `cleanup`; every other subcommand answers exit 2 `UNKNOWN_SUBCOMMAND`. Both sudoers profiles (`linux`, `nginx`) are generated now; Phase 4 adds the nginx subcommands as protocol 2 |
| 4 | §12.3 `hostkeys` runs `ssh-keygen -lf`; §13.1 `authkeys-list` uses `getent passwd` | The static helper computes fingerprints in Go from the `.pub` files named by `sshd -T` and reads `/etc/passwd` directly (no NSS in a static binary). Users only known to LDAP/SSSD are not listed (warning `directory_users_not_listed` when `/etc/nsswitch.conf` names `ldap` or `sss` for `passwd`); the account that runs the helper through sudo (`SUDO_USER`, normally `alice-svc`, a system UID) is always listed so Alice's own key appears in the inventory |
| 5 | SC-5 "TestConnection verifies `sudo -l`" vs §6.6 "`cat /etc/os-release` is the only non-helper command" | §6.6 wins: no `sudo -l`. A missing or refused helper is detected by `sudo -n … sshd-dump` failing (`ssh.helper_missing`); the nginx-profile check arrives with `nginx-test` in Phase 4 |
| 6 | F-30 "nothing stored until confirmation" vs the confirmation needing the presented key | The presented key is stored as a `host_keys` row with the new status `observed` (never trusted, never used for a connection); only a confirmation turns it into `pinned`. Exactly one key is pinned per target (stricter than §7.3's one per type); `HostKeyAlgorithms` is restricted to the pinned key's algorithms. Target status gains `checking` (after a confirmation, until the next connection test). The informational host-key inventory of §13.3 lives in `targets.facts` (JSON), not in a table |
| 7 | §8.1 claim query uses `now()` and takes the target lock in the handler; §8.1 LISTEN/NOTIFY | Times are bind parameters from the injected clock; the claim transaction also inserts the `target_locks` row (so two jobs for one target can never both start); workers poll every second (single host, R20) instead of LISTEN/NOTIFY. `jobs` gains `class`, `payload_mac` (HMAC-SHA256 under `alice/job/v1`, J-1), `result`, `created_by_role`, `confirmed_by`, `confirmed_at`, `started_at`, `finished_at`, and the status `blocked_license` (L-81) |
| 8 | Lock classes of target actions: §8.6 makes discovery ClassReadOnly, while the Phase 2 lock rule demands ClassChange for every state-changing route under `/targets` | The lock rule accepts either gated class (`ClassChange`, `ClassReadOnly`) under the infrastructure groups; `test` and `discover` routes are `ClassReadOnly`, everything else under `/targets`, `/ssh-keys` and `/jobs` is `ClassChange`. `/api/v1/jobs` joins the infrastructure groups (confirming a paused job starts external work) |
| 9 | Phase 3 owner step 4 ("try to remove Alice's own key") and F-36..F-38 need key removal and addition, which §26.8 places in Phase 6 | Phase 3 delivers removal of discovered keys (Admin and Operator, §15.4) through `POST /ssh-keys/locations/{id}/actions/remove` and the `sshkey.remove` job, and `AddAuthorizedKey` at provider level (tested by F-37/F-38); key generation, deployment and rotation stay in Phase 6 |
| 10 | Editing a target's address | Only `name` and the discovery interval can be changed; another host, port or user is another server (its pinned key belongs to the old endpoint): delete and add again |
| 11 | `credentials` columns (§7.2) | Adds `purpose`; `target_id` is added with the first target-bound credential (Azure, Phase 5). `credentials` is append-only for `alice_app` (`INSERT, SELECT`); replacing the platform key is a documented manual procedure (§13.5) |
| 12 | Permissions for the new routes (§15.4 table) | `targets.manage` (Admin; operate tokens), `hostkeys.confirm` (Admin; browser session), `hostkeys.repin` (Admin; browser session with step-up, §25.1 "host key acceptance"), `inventory.operate` (Admin and Operator; operate tokens: test connection, discovery, key removal), `jobs.confirm` (Admin; browser session, R29); reads use `read` |
| 13 | F-34 "no more than 3 attempts per hour" | Authentication failure is a permanent job failure (§8.4) that marks the target `auth_failed`; scheduled discovery runs at most once per discovery interval (minimum 1 hour), so a failing key is offered at most once per hour per target |
| 14 | Alerts for a changed host key or failed authentication (F-31, F-34) before the Phase 7 alert engine | An email to every Administrator through `notify.AdminNotifier` on the transition into `host_key_changed` or `auth_failed` (templates `target.host_key_changed`, `target.auth_failed`), plus the red target status in the UI; the `alerts` table arrives in Phase 7 |
| 15 | Phase 1/2 re-deferred scheduled work | `audit.verify` (daily, ClassAlways, audited `audit.verified` as system) and `maintenance.cleanup` (hourly: expired sessions and setup sessions through `auth.Service.PruneExpired`, finished jobs older than 90 days) run on the periodic scheduler, which now holds a PostgreSQL advisory lock so only one process schedules (P2-06) |
| 16 | Audit action names (none fixed by the spec except `hostkey.pinned`, `job.recovered`) | `target.created`, `target.updated`, `target.deleted`, `target.add.denied_license`, `target.status_changed`, `target.discovered`, `hostkey.pinned`, `hostkey.changed`, `hostkey.repinned`, `sshkey.remove_requested`, `sshkey.remove.denied`, `sshkey.removed`, `sshkey.remove_failed`, `job.recovered`, `job.dead`, `job.tampered`, `job.blocked_license`, `job.confirmed`, `job.discarded`, `platform_key.created` |
| 17 | Connection limits (`ssh.max_parallel` setting, §12.5) before Settings exist | Constants in `linuxssh`: 10 connections in total, 2 per target, idle connections closed after 60 s; dial 10 s, handshake 15 s, command 30 s (`sshd-dump`, `authkeys-list` 60 s); output 8 MiB (`authkeys-read` 2 MiB) |


Task order is bottom-up: carries (1–2), schema (3), provider framework and pure parsers (4–5), helper (6–7), connector (8–10), jobs (11–12), inventory and handlers (13–15), HTTP (16–17), wiring and e2e infrastructure (18), real-OpenSSH matrix (19), web (20–21), end-to-end (22), docs and verification (23). Each task leaves the repository green.

### Task index

1. API lock-rule hardening, error fallbacks, status before the first evaluation (carries 1, 2)
2. Installation tamper episodes and the safe `00004` Down (carry 4)
3. Migration `00005`: inventory and job tables, protection trigger, grants
4. Provider framework: interface, capabilities, registry, errors, fake provider, conformance suite
5. Pure parsers: `authorized_keys`, `sshd -T`, helper protocol vocabulary (+ both fuzz targets)
6. `alice-helper` part 1: dispatch, path rules, `version`, `sshd-dump`, `hostkeys`, `authkeys-list`, `authkeys-read`, static build
7. `alice-helper` part 2: `authkeys-write` (lock, compare-and-swap, backup, atomic replace), `cleanup`
8. SSH connector: fake SSH server (`linuxsshtest`), command constructors and quoting (A-12), dialer with pinning, command runner (F-30, F-31, F-39)
9. Connection pool, the `linuxssh` provider (TestConnection, Discover) and setup snippets
10. `authorized_keys` changes over SSH: remove/add with compare-and-swap and own-key refusal (F-36, F-37, F-38)
11. Durable job queue: enqueue, claim with per-target locks, runner, retries, license gate, `blocked_license` (F-69, L-81)
12. Crash recovery kill test, graceful shutdown, scheduler leader lock, `audit.verify` and `maintenance.cleanup` (F-66)
13. Inventory: platform key, targets with the license check (L-04, L-70..L-79), address validation
14. Inventory: host-key store, confirmation, re-pin, status transitions and admin emails (F-30..F-33)
15. Inventory: SSH key reconciliation, queries, removal requests; job handlers (L-29)
16. API: routes, DTOs, permissions, error codes, OpenAPI, authz matrix
17. API integration: journeys with the fake SSH server, secret-leak suite with SSH keys, lock (L-26, L-29, L-81)
18. Wiring: providers, services, runner lifecycle, e2e test API, e2e SSH target, Makefile and CI
19. Real OpenSSH matrix: Ubuntu 22.04, Debian 12, Rocky 9 with the generated setup snippet
20. Web: Servers page, add-server flow with fingerprint confirmation, server detail, re-pin, platform key panel
21. Web: SSH keys inventory and detail, key removal, wizard platform step, navigation
22. End-to-end: Phase 3 owner journeys in EN and TR, license banners carry, axe
23. Docs, R37, security review, coverage floors, owner verification

---

## Cross-task contract

Every task's **Interfaces** block repeats the parts of this contract it consumes or produces. When a task and this
section disagree, this section wins and the task is a plan defect to fix at execution time.

### Database (migration `00005_inventory_jobs.sql`, Task 3)

```sql
-- +goose Up
-- Phase 3: providers, targets, SSH key inventory and the durable job queue (spec §7.2–§7.4, §8; R37).

CREATE TABLE credentials (
    id          uuid PRIMARY KEY,
    purpose     text NOT NULL CHECK (purpose IN ('platform_ssh')),
    kind        text NOT NULL CHECK (kind IN ('ssh_private_key', 'ssh_password_unused', 'azure_sp_secret', 'azure_sp_cert', 'azure_managed_identity')),
    public_info jsonb NOT NULL DEFAULT '{}',
    ciphertext  bytea NOT NULL,
    nonce       bytea NOT NULL CHECK (octet_length(nonce) = 12),
    wrapped_dek bytea NOT NULL,
    key_version integer NOT NULL CHECK (key_version >= 1),
    created_at  timestamptz NOT NULL,
    rotated_at  timestamptz
);
CREATE UNIQUE INDEX credentials_one_platform_key ON credentials (purpose) WHERE purpose = 'platform_ssh';

CREATE TABLE targets (
    id                         uuid PRIMARY KEY,
    name                       citext NOT NULL CHECK (char_length(name::text) BETWEEN 1 AND 100),
    type                       text NOT NULL CHECK (type IN ('nginx', 'linux', 'azure_key_vault')),
    config                     jsonb NOT NULL,
    credential_id              uuid NOT NULL REFERENCES credentials (id),
    status                     text NOT NULL CHECK (status IN ('pending_host_key', 'checking', 'ok', 'unreachable', 'host_key_changed', 'auth_failed', 'disabled')),
    last_error_code            text NOT NULL DEFAULT '',
    last_success_at            timestamptz,
    last_discovery_at          timestamptz,
    discovery_interval_seconds integer NOT NULL DEFAULT 86400 CHECK (discovery_interval_seconds BETWEEN 3600 AND 2592000),
    keys_managed_elsewhere     boolean NOT NULL DEFAULT false,
    facts                      jsonb NOT NULL DEFAULT '{}',
    capabilities               text[] NOT NULL DEFAULT '{}',
    counts_toward_license      boolean NOT NULL DEFAULT true,
    version                    integer NOT NULL DEFAULT 1 CHECK (version >= 1),
    created_by                 uuid REFERENCES users (id),
    created_at                 timestamptz NOT NULL,
    updated_at                 timestamptz NOT NULL,
    deleted_at                 timestamptz
);
CREATE UNIQUE INDEX targets_name_live ON targets (name) WHERE deleted_at IS NULL;
CREATE UNIQUE INDEX targets_endpoint_live ON targets (type, (config->>'host'), (config->>'port')) WHERE deleted_at IS NULL;
CREATE INDEX targets_live_created ON targets (created_at, id) WHERE deleted_at IS NULL;

CREATE TABLE host_keys (
    id                 uuid PRIMARY KEY,
    target_id          uuid NOT NULL REFERENCES targets (id),
    key_type           text NOT NULL,
    public_key         bytea NOT NULL,
    fingerprint_sha256 text NOT NULL,
    status             text NOT NULL CHECK (status IN ('observed', 'pinned', 'superseded', 'rejected')),
    observed_at        timestamptz NOT NULL,
    confirmed_by       uuid REFERENCES users (id),
    confirmed_at       timestamptz,
    superseded_at      timestamptz,
    UNIQUE (target_id, fingerprint_sha256)
);
CREATE UNIQUE INDEX host_keys_one_pinned ON host_keys (target_id) WHERE status = 'pinned';

CREATE TABLE ssh_keys (
    id                 uuid PRIMARY KEY,
    fingerprint_sha256 text NOT NULL UNIQUE,
    key_type           text NOT NULL,
    bits               integer NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
    public_key         text NOT NULL,
    managed            boolean NOT NULL DEFAULT false,
    is_platform_key    boolean NOT NULL DEFAULT false,
    weak               boolean NOT NULL DEFAULT false,
    label              text NOT NULL DEFAULT '',
    first_seen_at      timestamptz NOT NULL,
    created_at         timestamptz NOT NULL,
    retired_at         timestamptz
);

CREATE TABLE ssh_key_locations (
    id                      uuid PRIMARY KEY,
    ssh_key_id              uuid NOT NULL REFERENCES ssh_keys (id),
    target_id               uuid NOT NULL REFERENCES targets (id),
    os_user                 text NOT NULL,
    file_path               text NOT NULL,
    line_no                 integer NOT NULL CHECK (line_no >= 1),
    options                 text NOT NULL DEFAULT '',
    comment                 text NOT NULL DEFAULT '',
    flags                   text[] NOT NULL DEFAULT '{}',
    first_seen_at           timestamptz NOT NULL,
    last_seen_at            timestamptz NOT NULL,
    missing_since           timestamptz,
    removed_by_alice_at     timestamptz,
    is_alice_connection_key boolean NOT NULL DEFAULT false,
    UNIQUE (ssh_key_id, target_id, os_user, file_path)
);
CREATE INDEX ssh_key_locations_target ON ssh_key_locations (target_id);

-- The platform's own key can never be marked removed or deleted (spec §7.3, SEC-081). The
-- service layer and the provider refuse first; this trigger holds even if both had a bug.
-- +goose StatementBegin
CREATE FUNCTION ssh_key_locations_protect_alice_key() RETURNS trigger LANGUAGE plpgsql AS $$
BEGIN
    IF TG_OP = 'DELETE' THEN
        IF OLD.is_alice_connection_key THEN
            RAISE EXCEPTION 'the location of Alice''s own connection key cannot be deleted' USING ERRCODE = 'P0001';
        END IF;
        RETURN OLD;
    END IF;
    IF OLD.is_alice_connection_key AND NEW.removed_by_alice_at IS NOT NULL THEN
        RAISE EXCEPTION 'Alice''s own connection key cannot be removed' USING ERRCODE = 'P0001';
    END IF;
    RETURN NEW;
END $$;
-- +goose StatementEnd
CREATE TRIGGER ssh_key_locations_protect BEFORE UPDATE OR DELETE ON ssh_key_locations
    FOR EACH ROW EXECUTE FUNCTION ssh_key_locations_protect_alice_key();

CREATE TABLE jobs (
    id              uuid PRIMARY KEY,
    type            text NOT NULL,
    class           text NOT NULL CHECK (class IN ('always', 'read_only', 'change')),
    kind            text NOT NULL CHECK (kind IN ('scheduled', 'user', 'system')),
    payload         jsonb NOT NULL DEFAULT '{}',
    payload_mac     bytea NOT NULL CHECK (octet_length(payload_mac) = 32),
    target_id       uuid REFERENCES targets (id),
    dedupe_key      text,
    status          text NOT NULL CHECK (status IN ('queued', 'running', 'succeeded', 'failed', 'cancelled', 'dead', 'blocked_license')),
    priority        smallint NOT NULL DEFAULT 5,
    run_at          timestamptz NOT NULL,
    attempts        integer NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
    max_attempts    integer NOT NULL CHECK (max_attempts >= 1),
    locked_by       text,
    locked_until    timestamptz,
    heartbeat_at    timestamptz,
    last_error_code text NOT NULL DEFAULT '',
    result          jsonb NOT NULL DEFAULT '{}',
    created_by      uuid REFERENCES users (id),
    created_by_role text NOT NULL DEFAULT '',
    confirmed_by    uuid REFERENCES users (id),
    confirmed_at    timestamptz,
    created_at      timestamptz NOT NULL,
    started_at      timestamptz,
    finished_at     timestamptz
);
CREATE INDEX jobs_due ON jobs (priority, run_at) WHERE status = 'queued';
CREATE INDEX jobs_running_lease ON jobs (locked_until) WHERE status = 'running';
CREATE INDEX jobs_target ON jobs (target_id, created_at DESC);
CREATE INDEX jobs_finished ON jobs (finished_at) WHERE finished_at IS NOT NULL;
CREATE UNIQUE INDEX jobs_dedupe_live ON jobs (dedupe_key) WHERE status IN ('queued', 'running', 'blocked_license');

CREATE TABLE job_attempts (
    id          uuid PRIMARY KEY,
    job_id      uuid NOT NULL REFERENCES jobs (id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
    attempt     integer NOT NULL,
    worker_id   text NOT NULL,
    started_at  timestamptz NOT NULL,
    finished_at timestamptz,
    error_code  text NOT NULL DEFAULT '',
    UNIQUE (job_id, attempt)
);

CREATE TABLE target_locks (
    target_id    uuid PRIMARY KEY REFERENCES targets (id),
    job_id       uuid NOT NULL REFERENCES jobs (id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
    operation    text NOT NULL,
    locked_by    text NOT NULL,
    heartbeat_at timestamptz NOT NULL,
    lease_until  timestamptz NOT NULL
);

-- Credentials are append-only for the application; inventory rows are never deleted (soft delete
-- and missing_since keep the history); jobs, attempts and target locks are working tables.
GRANT SELECT, INSERT ON credentials TO alice_app;
GRANT SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE ON targets, host_keys, ssh_keys, ssh_key_locations TO alice_app;
GRANT SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE ON jobs, job_attempts, target_locks TO alice_app;

-- +goose Down
DROP TABLE target_locks;
DROP TABLE job_attempts;
DROP TABLE jobs;
DROP TRIGGER ssh_key_locations_protect ON ssh_key_locations;
DROP FUNCTION ssh_key_locations_protect_alice_key();
DROP TABLE ssh_key_locations;
DROP TABLE ssh_keys;
DROP TABLE host_keys;
DROP TABLE targets;
DROP TABLE credentials;
```

`targets.config` is `{"host": "<normalized host>", "port": <int>, "username": "<os user>"}`. `targets.facts` is the JSON
of `inventory.Facts`. Grant guard additions (`explicitGrants`): `public.credentials: {INSERT, SELECT}`,
`public.targets`, `public.host_keys`, `public.ssh_keys`, `public.ssh_key_locations`: `{INSERT, SELECT, UPDATE}`.
The e2e `resetSQL` (`cmd/alice/testapi_e2e.go`) truncates `target_locks, job_attempts, jobs, ssh_key_locations, ssh_keys,
host_keys, targets, credentials` together with the Phase 2 list; Task 3 extends it in the same commit as the migration,
because `TRUNCATE users` fails once `targets.created_by` references `users`.

### Package `alice/internal/providers` (Task 4)

```go
package providers

type Kind string

const (
	KindLinuxSSH Kind = "linuxssh"
	KindNginx    Kind = "nginx"
	KindAzureKV  Kind = "azurekv"
)

// KindForTargetType maps targets.type to the provider kind (spec §6.4).
func KindForTargetType(t string) (Kind, bool) // "linux"->linuxssh, "nginx"->nginx, "azure_key_vault"->azurekv

type Capability string

const (
	CapTestConnection    Capability = "test_connection"
	CapDiscoverCerts     Capability = "discover_certificates"
	CapDiscoverSSHKeys   Capability = "discover_ssh_keys"
	CapDiscoverKVKeys    Capability = "discover_kv_keys"
	CapDiscoverKVSecrets Capability = "discover_kv_secret_metadata"
	CapDeployCertificate Capability = "deploy_certificate"
	CapImportCertificate Capability = "import_certificate"
	CapAuthorizedKeys    Capability = "authorized_keys"
	CapVerifyDeployment  Capability = "verify_deployment"
)

type CapabilitySet map[Capability]struct{}

func NewCapabilitySet(caps ...Capability) CapabilitySet
func (c CapabilitySet) Has(x Capability) bool
func (c CapabilitySet) Sorted() []Capability

type FieldType string // "string" | "int" | "bool" | "enum" | "path" | "host"

type Field struct {
	Name     string
	Type     FieldType
	Required bool
	Default  any
	LabelKey string // i18n key, e.g. "provider.linuxssh.fields.host.label"
	HelpKey  string
	Pattern  string // Go regexp, anchored
	Min, Max int    // ints: value range; strings: length range (0 = unbounded)
	Values   []string
}

type ConfigSchema struct{ Fields []Field }
type CredentialSchema struct{ Fields []Field }

// TargetConfig is the non-secret target configuration (targets.config).
type TargetConfig map[string]any

type TargetRef struct {
	ID     uuid.UUID
	Name   string
	Kind   Kind
	Config TargetConfig
}

// HostKey is an SSH server key in wire form plus its SHA-256 fingerprint ("SHA256:…").
type HostKey struct {
	Type        string // ssh.PublicKey.Type(), e.g. "ssh-ed25519"
	PublicKey   []byte // ssh.PublicKey.Marshal()
	Fingerprint string // ssh.FingerprintSHA256
}

var ErrNoPinnedKey = errors.New("providers: no pinned host key")

// HostKeyStore is implemented by inventory. Pinned returns ErrNoPinnedKey when nothing is pinned.
// Observed records a presented key that is not pinned; changed is true when another key is pinned.
type HostKeyStore interface {
	Pinned(ctx context.Context, target uuid.UUID) (HostKey, error)
	Observed(ctx context.Context, target uuid.UUID, key HostKey, changed bool) error
}

// CredentialSource hands a provider the secret of one session. release zeroes what was decrypted.
type CredentialSource interface {
	SSHSigner(ctx context.Context) (signer ssh.Signer, release func(), err error)
}

type Env struct {
	Clock    clock.Clock
	HostKeys HostKeyStore
	Log      *slog.Logger // already redacting
}

type Provider interface {
	Kind() Kind
	DisplayNameKey() string
	Capabilities() CapabilitySet
	ConfigSchema() ConfigSchema
	CredentialSchema() CredentialSchema
	ValidateConfig(cfg TargetConfig) []validate.FieldError
	Open(ctx context.Context, t TargetRef, cred CredentialSource, env Env) (Session, error)
}

// Session is one connection scope. Methods of capabilities a provider does not advertise return
// ErrUnsupported (embed UnsupportedSession). Later phases add deploy/import methods.
type Session interface {
	Close() error
	TestConnection(ctx context.Context) (ConnectionReport, error)
	Discover(ctx context.Context, req DiscoverRequest) (DiscoveryResult, error)
	ListAuthorizedKeys(ctx context.Context) ([]DiscoveredSSHKey, error)
	AddAuthorizedKey(ctx context.Context, req AuthKeyChange, log StepLogger) (AuthKeyResult, error)
	RemoveAuthorizedKey(ctx context.Context, req AuthKeyChange, log StepLogger) (AuthKeyResult, error)
}

var ErrUnsupported = errors.New("providers: operation not supported by this provider")

type UnsupportedSession struct{} // every method returns ErrUnsupported; Close returns nil

// SetupGuide is implemented by providers that need host preparation (linuxssh).
type SetupGuide interface {
	SetupSnippets(authorizedKeysLine string) map[string]SetupSnippet // key: profile "linux" | "nginx"
	HelperInfo() (path string, protocol int)                         // "/usr/local/libexec/alice-helper", helperproto.Protocol
}

type SetupSnippet struct {
	Profile string // "linux" | "nginx"
	Sudoers string // content of /etc/sudoers.d/alice
	Script  string // shell script to run as root on the target
}

type OSRelease struct{ ID, VersionID, PrettyName string }

type ConnectionReport struct {
	HostKey        HostKey
	HelperVersion  string
	HelperProtocol int
	OS             OSRelease
	Warnings       []Warning
}

type DiscoverRequest struct{ SSHKeys bool }

type DiscoveryResult struct {
	SSHKeys         []DiscoveredSSHKey
	HostKeys        []DiscoveredHostKey
	SSHD            SSHDSummary
	UnreadableLines []UnreadableLine
	Warnings        []Warning
	Partial         bool // some source failed: inventory never marks anything missing from a partial scan
	ReadFiles       []string // files read completely (missing marking is limited to these)
}

type DiscoveredSSHKey struct {
	OSUser      string
	FilePath    string
	LineNo      int
	PublicKey   string // "ssh-ed25519 AAAA…" (type and base64 blob, no options, no comment)
	Fingerprint string // "SHA256:…"
	KeyType     string
	Bits        int
	Comment     string
	Options     string   // verbatim option text, "" when none
	Flags       []string // FlagWeak, FlagCommand, FlagRootWithoutFrom, FlagDuplicate, FlagCertAuthority, FlagSecurityKey
}

const (
	FlagWeak            = "weak"              // RSA < 2048, DSA
	FlagCommand         = "command"           // command= present (shown, never touched)
	FlagRootWithoutFrom = "root_without_from" // root key without from=
	FlagDuplicate       = "duplicate"         // same key more than once in the file
	FlagCertAuthority   = "cert_authority"    // cert-authority line: inventory only, never managed
	FlagSecurityKey     = "security_key"      // sk-* (FIDO) key
)

type DiscoveredHostKey struct {
	KeyType     string
	Bits        int
	Fingerprint string
	Weak        bool // DSA, RSA < 2048
}

type SSHDSummary struct {
	Read                   bool // false: sshd -T failed, defaults were assumed
	PubkeyAuthentication   string
	PasswordAuthentication string
	PermitRootLogin        string
	AuthorizedKeysFile     []string
	AuthorizedKeysCommand  string // "none" or the program
	KeysManagedElsewhere   bool   // AuthorizedKeysCommand is set (F-35)
	CertificatesInUse      bool   // TrustedUserCAKeys or AuthorizedPrincipalsFile set
}

type UnreadableLine struct {
	OSUser, FilePath string
	LineNo           int
}

// Warning is a stable code (i18n key "warnings.<code>") and its parameters.
type Warning struct {
	Code   string
	Params map[string]string
}

type AuthKeyChange struct {
	OperationID           uuid.UUID
	OSUser                string
	FilePath              string
	Fingerprint           string   // remove: the key to remove
	Line                  string   // add: the authorized_keys line to add
	ProtectedFingerprints []string // keys that must never be removed (the platform key)
	AllowLastRootKey      bool
}

type AuthKeyResult struct {
	Changed   bool
	Removed   int
	OldSHA256 string
	NewSHA256 string
	Verified  bool
}

type StepStatus string // "started" | "ok" | "failed" | "skipped"

type StepLogger interface {
	Step(name string, status StepStatus, params map[string]string)
}

// Error is the only error type providers return (spec §6.3 item 5). Code is a stable reason
// ("ssh.auth_failed"); the API maps it to an ALC code. Cause is for logs (type only) and is
// never shown.
type Error struct {
	Code      string
	Params    map[string]string
	Retryable bool
	Cause     error
}

func (e *Error) Error() string // "providers: <code>" (never Cause's text)
func (e *Error) Unwrap() error
func NewError(code string, retryable bool, cause error, params map[string]string) *Error

type Descriptor struct {
	Kind             Kind
	DisplayNameKey   string
	Capabilities     []Capability
	ConfigSchema     ConfigSchema
	CredentialSchema CredentialSchema
}

type Registry struct{ /* map[Kind]Provider, frozen flag, mutex */ }

func NewRegistry() *Registry
func (r *Registry) Register(p Provider) // panics: duplicate kind, after Freeze, empty capabilities, invalid schema
func (r *Registry) Freeze()
func (r *Registry) Get(k Kind) (Provider, bool)
func (r *Registry) List() []Descriptor // sorted by kind
```

Provider error codes (reasons) used in this phase: `ssh.unreachable` (retryable), `ssh.auth_failed`, `ssh.timeout`
(retryable), `ssh.helper_missing`, `ssh.helper_outdated`, `ssh.helper_refused` (param `helper_code`),
`ssh.file_changed` (retryable), `ssh.keys_managed_elsewhere`, `ssh.output_too_large`, `ssh.protocol_error`,
`target.host_key_unconfirmed` (param `fingerprint`), `target.host_key_changed` (params `old_fingerprint`,
`new_fingerprint`), `sshkey.own_key_protected`, `sshkey.last_root_key`, `sshkey.not_removable`.

### Package `alice/internal/providers/linuxssh` and sub-packages (Tasks 5, 8, 9, 10)

```go
// helperproto (pure, shared with cmd/alice-helper)
package helperproto

const (
	Protocol   = 1
	Version    = "1.0.0"
	HelperPath = "/usr/local/libexec/alice-helper"
	BackupRoot = "/var/lib/alice-helper/backups"

	SubVersion      = "version"
	SubSSHDDump     = "sshd-dump"
	SubHostKeys     = "hostkeys"
	SubAuthKeysList = "authkeys-list"
	SubAuthKeysRead = "authkeys-read"
	SubAuthKeysWrite = "authkeys-write"
	SubCleanup      = "cleanup"

	ExitOK           = 0
	ExitRefused      = 2 // validation refused
	ExitPrecondition = 3 // hash mismatch, missing file
	ExitFailed       = 4 // command failed

	CodeUsage              = "USAGE"
	CodeUnknownSubcommand  = "UNKNOWN_SUBCOMMAND"
	CodeNotRoot            = "NOT_ROOT"
	CodeInvalidArgument    = "INVALID_ARGUMENT"
	CodePathNotAllowed     = "PATH_NOT_ALLOWED"
	CodeNotRegularFile     = "NOT_REGULAR_FILE"
	CodeInsecurePermissions = "INSECURE_PERMISSIONS"
	CodeTooLarge           = "TOO_LARGE"
	CodeHashMismatch       = "HASH_MISMATCH"
	CodeNotFound           = "NOT_FOUND"
	CodeSSHDFailed         = "SSHD_FAILED"
	CodeIOError            = "IO_ERROR"

	MaxAuthorizedKeysSize = 1 << 20 // authkeys-read output and authkeys-write stdin
	AbsentSHA256          = "absent" // --expect-sha256 for a file that does not exist yet
)

type ErrorResponse struct {
	OK      bool   `json:"ok"`
	Code    string `json:"code"`
	Message string `json:"message"`
}
type VersionResponse struct {
	OK       bool   `json:"ok"`
	Helper   string `json:"helper"`
	Protocol int    `json:"protocol"`
}
type SSHDDumpResponse struct {
	OK       bool   `json:"ok"`
	Config   string `json:"config"`   // sshd -T output
	Fallback bool   `json:"fallback"` // sshd -T failed: Config is empty, defaults apply
}
type HostKeyInfo struct {
	Type        string `json:"type"`
	Bits        int    `json:"bits"`
	Fingerprint string `json:"fingerprint"`
	Path        string `json:"path"`
}
type HostKeysResponse struct {
	OK   bool          `json:"ok"`
	Keys []HostKeyInfo `json:"keys"`
}
type FileInfo struct {
	Path          string `json:"path"`
	Exists        bool   `json:"exists"`
	Size          int64  `json:"size"`
	SHA256        string `json:"sha256"` // "" when absent
	Mode          string `json:"mode"`   // "0600"
	Owner         string `json:"owner"`
	StrictModesOK bool   `json:"strict_modes_ok"`
	TooLarge      bool   `json:"too_large"`
}
type UserFiles struct {
	User  string     `json:"user"`
	UID   int        `json:"uid"`
	Home  string     `json:"home"`
	Files []FileInfo `json:"files"`
}
type AuthKeysListResponse struct {
	OK                    bool        `json:"ok"`
	Users                 []UserFiles `json:"users"`
	AuthorizedKeysCommand string      `json:"authorized_keys_command"`
	Warnings              []string    `json:"warnings"`
}
type AuthKeysReadResponse struct {
	OK         bool   `json:"ok"`
	Path       string `json:"path"`
	SHA256     string `json:"sha256"`
	ContentB64 string `json:"content_b64"`
}
type AuthKeysWriteResponse struct {
	OK     bool   `json:"ok"`
	SHA256 string `json:"sha256"`
	Backup string `json:"backup"`
}
type CleanupResponse struct {
	OK      bool `json:"ok"`
	Removed int  `json:"removed"`
}

func ValidArg(s string) bool      // ^[A-Za-z0-9._/@:+-]{1,4096}$, no ".." path component, not starting with '-'
```

Algorithm lists (SEC-080): key exchange `mlkem768x25519-sha256`, `curve25519-sha256`, `curve25519-sha256@libssh.org`,
`ecdh-sha2-nistp256`, `ecdh-sha2-nistp384`, `ecdh-sha2-nistp521`; ciphers `chacha20-poly1305@openssh.com`,
`aes256-gcm@openssh.com`, `aes128-gcm@openssh.com`; MACs `hmac-sha2-256-etm@openssh.com`, `hmac-sha2-512-etm@openssh.com`;
host key algorithms when nothing is pinned: `ssh-ed25519`, `ecdsa-sha2-nistp256`, `ecdsa-sha2-nistp384`,
`ecdsa-sha2-nistp521`, `rsa-sha2-512`, `rsa-sha2-256`; when pinned: only the pinned type (`ssh-rsa` pins map to
`rsa-sha2-512`, `rsa-sha2-256`).

Reason strings for `RecordConnectionFailure`: `ssh.auth_failed` → status `auth_failed` (+ email on transition);
`ssh.unreachable`, `ssh.timeout` → `unreachable`; `target.host_key_unconfirmed` → `pending_host_key`;
`target.host_key_changed` → no status write (the host-key store already set it); anything else → status unchanged,
`last_error_code` set.

### e2e environment (Tasks 18, 22)

- Compose overlay service `sshtarget` (image `alice-e2e-sshtarget`, built from `test/images/e2e-target/Dockerfile`
  with the repository as context): Ubuntu 22.04, OpenSSH server, sudo, `alice-helper` built from this repository at
  `/opt/alice-bundle/alice-helper`, user `deploy` (uid 1001) with two keys generated at image build time
  (`deploy@laptop` Ed25519, `ci@build` RSA 3072), `root` with one key `root@bastion` carrying `from="10.0.0.0/8"`, and
  the scripts `/usr/local/sbin/alice-e2e-prepare` (runs the setup script from stdin as root in `/opt/alice-bundle`) and
  `/usr/local/sbin/alice-e2e-rotate-hostkey` (new host keys, `SIGHUP` to the listening sshd). Network `backend`,
  `init: true`, no published port; its address for Alice is `sshtarget`, port 22.
- Playwright helper `targetExec(args: string[], input?: string): string` runs
  `docker compose -f ../deploy/docker-compose.yml -f ../deploy/docker-compose.e2e.yml --env-file ../deploy/.env exec -T sshtarget …`.
- Test API additions (e2e build only): `/test/reset` also truncates the Phase 3 tables and calls
  `inventory.EnsurePlatformKey`; `POST /test/license/tamper` damages the newest stored license file (owner role) and runs
  the license evaluation; `POST /test/jobs/drain` runs due jobs until none is due (at most 50) so tests need not wait
  for the poll interval.

### Task 1: API lock-rule hardening, error fallbacks, status before the first evaluation (carries 1, 2)

Phase 3 adds the first real `ClassChange` and `ClassReadOnly` routes. Before they exist, the route-table rules
must be strict enough that a misfiled route cannot slip through: one shared `gated` helper decides which classes
lock mode refuses, every state-changing route must sit in exactly one of the two lock lists, and a route that has
no signed-in user (public, setup, pending sign-in) may never be gated (the gate's denial is audited per user, and a
public change route would be refused for everyone in lock). The two bare license errors get their codes, and the
license status endpoint stops answering "not expired" before the license service has evaluated anything.

**Files:**
- Modify: `internal/api/guard.go` (guard condition, new `gated`)
- Modify: `internal/api/authz_test.go` (`lockRefused`, `lockRuleViolations`, `TestLockRuleViolationsCatchesMistakes`, `TestRouteTableInLock`)
- Modify: `internal/api/guard_test.go` (two new tests)
- Modify: `internal/api/errors.go` (`errorMap`)
- Modify: `internal/api/httpx_test.go` (`TestFailMapsDomainErrors`, one new test)
- Modify: `internal/api/license_handlers.go` (`licenseStatus`)
- Modify: `internal/api/license_handlers_test.go` (one new test)

**Interfaces:**
- Consumes: `license.Class` constants (`ClassUnset`, `ClassAlways`, `ClassReadOnly`, `ClassChange`), `rbac.PolicyFor(p) (Policy, bool)` with `Policy.Anonymous`, `Policy.Setup`, `Policy.Pending`; `license.Snapshot.Ready`; `ErrUnavailable`, `ErrLicenseTargetLimit`, `ErrLicenseWrongInstallation` (all existing).
- Produces (`internal/api/guard.go`): `func gated(c license.Class) bool` — true for `ClassChange` and `ClassReadOnly`. Task 16 relies on it and on these test rules: `lockRefused` = `/api/v1/targets`, `/api/v1/certificates`, `/api/v1/locations`, `/api/v1/deployments`, `/api/v1/ssh-keys`, `/api/v1/rotation`, `/api/v1/keyvault`, `/api/v1/jobs`; a state-changing route under `lockRefused` must be gated, under `lockAvailable` must be `ClassAlways`, under neither is a violation.

- [ ] **Step 1: Write the failing guard tests**

Append to `internal/api/guard_test.go`:

```go
// gated is the single definition of "refused while the license is locked" (R9, §8.6):
// changes to managed systems and recurring read-only work on them.
```

```go
// gated reports whether lock mode refuses work of class c: changes to managed systems and
// recurring read-only work on them (R9, §8.6). The guard and the route-table tests share this
// one definition, so a new class cannot be gated in one place and not in the other.
func gated(c license.Class) bool { return c == license.ClassChange || c == license.ClassReadOnly }
```

- [ ] **Step 4: Rewrite the lock rules on top of `gated`**

In `internal/api/authz_test.go` replace the whole function `lockRuleViolations` (from its comment line
`// lockRuleViolations: reads are never refused in lock; …` to its closing brace) with:

```go
// lockRuleViolations: reads are never refused in lock; every state-changing route declares a
// license class and belongs to exactly one of the two lock lists; infrastructure routes are
// gated (ClassChange or ClassReadOnly); platform administration is ClassAlways; a route that
// has no signed-in user (public, setup session, pending sign-in) is never gated, because the
// gate's refusal is audited per user and would lock everyone out of it.
func lockRuleViolations(routes []route) []string {
	var out []string
	for _, rt := range routes {
		key := rt.method + " " + rt.pattern
		if safeMethod(rt.method) {
			if rt.lic != license.ClassUnset && rt.lic != license.ClassAlways {
				out = append(out, key+": reads stay available in lock")
			}
			continue
		}
		if pol, ok := rbac.PolicyFor(rt.perm); ok && (pol.Anonymous || pol.Setup || pol.Pending) && gated(rt.lic) {
			out = append(out, key+": a route without a signed-in user is never refused by the license gate")
		}
		refused, available := underAny(rt.pattern, lockRefused), underAny(rt.pattern, lockAvailable)
		switch {
		case !rt.lic.Valid():
			out = append(out, key+": declares no license class")
		case refused && available:
			out = append(out, key+": route group is in both lock lists")
		case refused && !gated(rt.lic):
			out = append(out, key+": infrastructure work must be refused in lock (ClassChange or ClassReadOnly)")
		case available && rt.lic != license.ClassAlways:
			out = append(out, key+": platform administration must stay available (ClassAlways)")
		case !refused && !available:
			out = append(out, key+": route group is in neither lock list")
		}
	}
	return out
}
```

### Task 2: Installation tamper episodes and the safe `00004` Down (carry 4)

Phase 2 audits a changed installation record once per installation ID, so a second tampering of the same
installation after the original record was restored goes unrecorded. Each tamper **episode** is now audited:
a changed record with no open episode opens one (`license.installation_tampered`), the record matching its seal again
closes it (`license.installation_restored`), and the next change opens a new one. The notice keys carry the episode
number (`installation_tampered:<id>:<n>`, `installation_restored:<id>:<n>`); the Phase 2 key
`installation_tampered:<id>` counts as episode 1, so an installation tampered under Phase 2 is not reported twice.
The license row lock taken by every evaluation serializes the decision, and the unique index on
`(license_id, notice)` makes it exactly-once. The `00004` Down section stops granting table-wide `UPDATE ON license`.

**Files:**
- Modify: `internal/license/installation.go` (`recordInstallationTampered` → `recordInstallationEpisode`, new `episodes`)
- Modify: `internal/license/tick.go` (step list)
- Modify: `internal/license/installation_integration_test.go` (detail assertion; new tests)
- Modify: `migrations/00004_license_installation_seal.sql` (Down section)
- Create: `migrations/down_integration_test.go`
- Modify: `web/src/locales/en.json`, `web/src/locales/tr.json` (two labels each)
- Modify: `web/src/pages/AuditPage.test.tsx`, `web/src/pages/LicensePage.test.tsx`

**Interfaces:**

```go
// notices returns the installation notices of the history in the order they were written.
func (e *env) installationNotices() []string {
	e.t.Helper()
	rows, err := e.db.Owner.Query(e.ctx, `SELECT notice FROM license_history
WHERE event = 'notice' AND (notice LIKE 'installation\_tampered:%' OR notice LIKE 'installation\_restored:%') ORDER BY id`)
	require.NoError(e.t, err)
	defer rows.Close()
	var out []string
	for rows.Next() {
		var n string
		require.NoError(e.t, rows.Scan(&n))
		out = append(out, n)
	}
	require.NoError(e.t, rows.Err())
	return out
}

func (e *env) auditEpisodes(action string) []string {
	e.t.Helper()
	rows, err := e.db.Owner.Query(e.ctx, "SELECT details->>'episode' FROM audit_log WHERE action = $1 ORDER BY seq", action)
	require.NoError(e.t, err)
	defer rows.Close()
	var out []string
	for rows.Next() {
		var n string
		require.NoError(e.t, rows.Scan(&n))
		out = append(out, n)
	}
	require.NoError(e.t, rows.Err())
	return out
}

// Carry 4a: every tamper episode is audited once; restoring the original record closes the
// episode, and a later change opens a new one.
func TestInstallationTamperEpisodes(t *testing.T) {
	e := newEnv(t)
	id := e.installation()
	original := e.svc.Snapshot().InstalledAt

	e.ownerExec("UPDATE license SET installed_at = $1", original.Add(20*day))
	e.tickAt(installedAt.Add(time.Hour))
	e.requireTamperedLock()
	e.tickAt(installedAt.Add(2 * time.Hour))
	assert.Equal(t, []string{"1"}, e.auditEpisodes("license.installation_tampered"), "one episode, audited once")

	e.ownerExec("UPDATE license SET installed_at = $1", original)
	e.tickAt(installedAt.Add(3 * time.Hour))
	assert.False(t, e.svc.Snapshot().InstallationTampered, "the original record is trusted again")
	assert.Equal(t, license.PhaseEvaluation, e.svc.Snapshot().Eval.Phase)
	assert.Equal(t, []string{"1"}, e.auditEpisodes("license.installation_restored"))
	assert.Equal(t, map[string]string{"installation_id": id, "episode": "1"}, e.auditDetails("license.installation_restored"))
	e.tickAt(installedAt.Add(4 * time.Hour))
	assert.Equal(t, 1, e.auditCount("license.installation_restored"), "a clean record closes an episode once")

	e.ownerExec("UPDATE license SET installation_seal = decode(repeat('ab', 32), 'hex')")
	e.restart()
	e.requireTamperedLock()
	assert.Equal(t, []string{"1", "2"}, e.auditEpisodes("license.installation_tampered"), "the second tampering is recorded")
	assert.Equal(t, []string{
		"installation_tampered:" + id + ":1",
		"installation_restored:" + id + ":1",
		"installation_tampered:" + id + ":2",
	}, e.installationNotices())
}

// An installation tampered under Phase 2 has the notice without an episode number: it counts as
// the open episode 1, so it is not reported again, and restoring the record closes it.
func TestPhase2TamperNoticeCountsAsEpisodeOne(t *testing.T) {
	e := newEnv(t)
	id := e.installation()
	original := e.svc.Snapshot().InstalledAt
	e.ownerExec(`INSERT INTO license_history (id, at, event, license_id, notice, details)
VALUES (gen_random_uuid(), now(), 'notice', '', $1, '{}')`, "installation_tampered:"+id)
	e.ownerExec("UPDATE license SET installed_at = $1", original.Add(20*day))
	e.restart()
	e.requireTamperedLock()
	assert.Zero(t, e.auditCount("license.installation_tampered"), "episode 1 was already recorded by Phase 2")

	e.ownerExec("UPDATE license SET installed_at = $1", original)
	e.tickAt(installedAt.Add(time.Hour))
	assert.Equal(t, []string{"1"}, e.auditEpisodes("license.installation_restored"))
	assert.Contains(t, e.installationNotices(), "installation_restored:"+id+":1")
}

// The episode prefix is matched exactly: a notice of another installation whose ID starts with
// this one's characters never counts.
func TestInstallationEpisodesIgnoreOtherInstallations(t *testing.T) {
	e := newEnv(t)
	id := e.installation()
	e.ownerExec(`INSERT INTO license_history (id, at, event, license_id, notice, details)
VALUES (gen_random_uuid(), now(), 'notice', '', $1, '{}')`, "installation_tampered:"+id+"X:1")
	e.ownerExec("UPDATE license SET installed_at = installed_at + interval '1 day'")
	e.restart()
	assert.Equal(t, []string{"1"}, e.auditEpisodes("license.installation_tampered"))
}
```

In `internal/license/installation.go` replace the whole function `recordInstallationTampered` (from the comment
`// recordInstallationTampered audits an untrusted installation row once per installation ID.` to its closing brace) with:

```go
// Notice kinds of the installation record episodes: "<kind>:<installation id>:<n>". Phase 2 wrote
// "installation_tampered:<installation id>" without a number; it counts as episode 1.
const (
	noticeInstallationTampered = "installation_tampered"
	noticeInstallationRestored = "installation_restored"
)

// episodes counts the notices of kind for installation id: the Phase 2 key "<kind>:<id>" and every
// "<kind>:<id>:<n>". The prefix is compared exactly (no LIKE), so another ID never matches.
func episodes(ctx context.Context, tx pgx.Tx, kind, id string) (int, error) {
	prefix := kind + ":" + id
	var n int
	err := tx.QueryRow(ctx, `SELECT count(*) FROM license_history
WHERE event = 'notice' AND license_id = '' AND (notice = $1::text OR left(notice, length($1::text) + 1) = $1::text || ':')`,
		prefix).Scan(&n)
	if err != nil {
		return 0, fmt.Errorf("read the installation notices: %w", err)
	}
	return n, nil
}

// recordInstallationEpisode audits each tamper episode of the installation row once: an untrusted
// row with no open episode opens the next one (license.installation_tampered); a trusted row with
// an open episode closes it (license.installation_restored). The caller holds the license row
// lock, so two evaluations cannot both open the same episode; the unique notice index makes it
// exactly-once even across processes.
func (s *Service) recordInstallationEpisode(ctx context.Context, tx pgx.Tx, c computed, now time.Time) ([]audit.Event, error) {
	id := c.row.ID
	tampered, err := episodes(ctx, tx, noticeInstallationTampered, id)
	if err != nil {
		return nil, err
	}
	restored, err := episodes(ctx, tx, noticeInstallationRestored, id)
	if err != nil {
		return nil, err
	}
	open := tampered > restored
	switch {
	case c.row.Tampered != "" && !open:
		n := strconv.Itoa(tampered + 1)
		d := map[string]string{"problem": c.row.Tampered, "installation_id": id, "episode": n}
		inserted, err := insertHistory(ctx, tx, now, "notice", "", "", "", noticeInstallationTampered+":"+id+":"+n, d)
		if err != nil || !inserted {
			return nil, err
		}
		s.log.Error("the installation record was changed outside Alice; the evaluation counts as ended and no license "+
			"file is used until the original record is restored", "problem", c.row.Tampered, "episode", n)
		return []audit.Event{{Actor: systemActor, Action: "license.installation_tampered", ObjectType: "license",
			ObjectID: id, Result: audit.Failure, Details: d}}, nil
	case c.row.Tampered == "" && open:
		n := strconv.Itoa(tampered)
		d := map[string]string{"installation_id": id, "episode": n}
		inserted, err := insertHistory(ctx, tx, now, "notice", "", "", "", noticeInstallationRestored+":"+id+":"+n, d)
		if err != nil || !inserted {
			return nil, err
		}
		s.log.Info("the installation record matches its seal again; licenses count again", "episode", n)
		return []audit.Event{{Actor: systemActor, Action: "license.installation_restored", ObjectType: "license",
			ObjectID: id, Result: audit.Success, Details: d}}, nil
	}
	return nil, nil
}
```

```go
	require.NoError(t, d.Owner.QueryRow(context.Background(),
		"SELECT has_column_privilege('alice_app', 'license', $1, $2)", column, priv).Scan(&ok))
	return ok
}

// Carry 4b: migrating below 00004 (an emergency downgrade) must not give the application back
// table-wide UPDATE on the installation row: the ID and the timestamp stay read-only.
func TestDownBelowTheSealKeepsTheInstallationReadOnly(t *testing.T) {
	d := pgtest.New(t)
	ctx := context.Background()
	p, err := goose.NewProvider(goose.DialectPostgres, stdlib.OpenDBFromPool(d.Owner), migrations.FS)
	require.NoError(t, err)
	_, err = p.DownTo(ctx, 3)
	require.NoError(t, err)
	version, err := p.GetDBVersion(ctx)
	require.NoError(t, err)
	require.Equal(t, int64(3), version)

	var tableUpdate bool
	require.NoError(t, d.Owner.QueryRow(ctx, "SELECT has_table_privilege('alice_app', 'license', 'UPDATE')").Scan(&tableUpdate))
	assert.False(t, tableUpdate, "no table-wide UPDATE after the Down")
	assert.False(t, appColumnPrivilege(t, d, "installed_at", "UPDATE"))
	assert.False(t, appColumnPrivilege(t, d, "installation_id", "UPDATE"))
	for _, col := range []string{"state", "clock_jump", "updated_at"} {
		assert.True(t, appColumnPrivilege(t, d, col, "UPDATE"), col)
	}
	_, err = d.App.Exec(ctx, `INSERT INTO license (id, installation_id, installed_at, state, updated_at)
VALUES (1, 'ALICE-TEST', now(), 'evaluation', now())`)
	require.NoError(t, err)
	_, err = d.App.Exec(ctx, "UPDATE license SET installed_at = now() - interval '1 day'")
	require.Error(t, err, "the application cannot move the installation time after a downgrade")

	_, err = p.Up(ctx)
	require.NoError(t, err, "the schema migrates up again")
}
```

### Task 3: Migration `00005`: inventory and job tables, protection trigger, grants

The schema of the cross-task contract, verbatim, with the grant sets the grant guard enforces, the trigger that
keeps Alice's own key location from being marked removed or deleted, and the e2e reset list (which must name every
table that references `users`, or `TRUNCATE users` fails).

**Files:**
- Create: `migrations/00005_inventory_jobs.sql`
- Create: `migrations/inventory_integration_test.go`
- Modify: `migrations/roles_integration_test.go` (`explicitGrants`)
- Modify: `cmd/alice/testapi_e2e.go` (`resetSQL`)

**Interfaces:**
- Consumes: `pgtest.New(t)` (`Owner`, `App`), `explicitGrants`, `grantProblems` (existing).
- Produces: tables `credentials`, `targets`, `host_keys`, `ssh_keys`, `ssh_key_locations`, `jobs`, `job_attempts`, `target_locks`; function and trigger `ssh_key_locations_protect_alice_key` / `ssh_key_locations_protect`; indexes `credentials_one_platform_key`, `targets_name_live`, `targets_endpoint_live`, `host_keys_one_pinned`, `jobs_due`, `jobs_running_lease`, `jobs_target`, `jobs_finished`, `jobs_dedupe_live`; grants: `credentials` {INSERT, SELECT}; `targets`, `host_keys`, `ssh_keys`, `ssh_key_locations` {INSERT, SELECT, UPDATE}; `jobs`, `job_attempts`, `target_locks` default {SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE}. The e2e reset truncates all eight tables.

```go
//go:build integration

package migrations_test

import (
	"context"
	"errors"
	"testing"

	"github.com/jackc/pgx/v5/pgconn"
	"github.com/jackc/pgx/v5/pgxpool"
	"github.com/stretchr/testify/assert"
	"github.com/stretchr/testify/require"

	"alice/internal/testutil/pgtest"
)

func sqlState(err error) string {
	var pgErr *pgconn.PgError
	if errors.As(err, &pgErr) {
		return pgErr.Code
	}
	return ""
}

func exec(t *testing.T, pool *pgxpool.Pool, sql string, args ...any) error {
	t.Helper()
	_, err := pool.Exec(context.Background(), sql, args...)
	return err
}

// seedTarget inserts the platform credential and one target through the application role and
// returns the target ID.
func seedTarget(t *testing.T, d *pgtest.DB, name, host string) string {
	t.Helper()
	ctx := context.Background()
	var cred string
	err := d.App.QueryRow(ctx, "SELECT id::text FROM credentials WHERE purpose = 'platform_ssh'").Scan(&cred)
	if err != nil {
		require.NoError(t, d.App.QueryRow(ctx, `INSERT INTO credentials (id, purpose, kind, ciphertext, nonce, wrapped_dek, key_version, created_at)
VALUES (gen_random_uuid(), 'platform_ssh', 'ssh_private_key', '\x01', decode(repeat('00', 12), 'hex'), '\x02', 1, now())
RETURNING id::text`).Scan(&cred))
	}
	var id string
	require.NoError(t, d.App.QueryRow(ctx, `INSERT INTO targets (id, name, type, config, credential_id, status, created_at, updated_at)
VALUES (gen_random_uuid(), $1, 'linux', jsonb_build_object('host', $2::text, 'port', 22, 'username', 'alice-svc'), $3, 'pending_host_key', now(), now())
RETURNING id::text`, name, host, cred).Scan(&id))
	return id
}

func seedJob(t *testing.T, d *pgtest.DB, dedupe *string, status string) (string, error) {
	t.Helper()
	var id string
	err := d.App.QueryRow(context.Background(), `INSERT INTO jobs (id, type, class, kind, payload_mac, dedupe_key, status, run_at, max_attempts, created_at)
VALUES (gen_random_uuid(), 'target.discover', 'read_only', 'scheduled', decode(repeat('00', 32), 'hex'), $1, $2, now(), 5, now())
RETURNING id::text`, dedupe, status).Scan(&id)
	return id, err
}

func TestInventoryTablesGrantOnlyWhatTheAppNeeds(t *testing.T) {
	d := pgtest.New(t)
	target := seedTarget(t, d, "web-01", "web-01.example.com")

	for _, stmt := range []string{
		"DELETE FROM targets",
		"DELETE FROM credentials",
		"UPDATE credentials SET rotated_at = now()",
		"DELETE FROM host_keys",
		"DELETE FROM ssh_keys",
		"DELETE FROM ssh_key_locations",
	} {
		assert.Equal(t, "42501", sqlState(exec(t, d.App, stmt)), "%s must be refused for alice_app", stmt)
	}
	require.NoError(t, exec(t, d.App, "UPDATE targets SET deleted_at = now() WHERE id = $1", target), "soft delete")
	jobID, err := seedJob(t, d, nil, "succeeded")
	require.NoError(t, err)
	require.NoError(t, exec(t, d.App, "DELETE FROM jobs WHERE id = $1", jobID), "finished jobs are pruned")
}

func TestTargetNamesAndEndpointsAreUniqueAmongLiveTargets(t *testing.T) {
	d := pgtest.New(t)
	first := seedTarget(t, d, "web-01", "web-01.example.com")

	_, err := d.App.Exec(context.Background(), `INSERT INTO targets (id, name, type, config, credential_id, status, created_at, updated_at)
SELECT gen_random_uuid(), 'WEB-01', 'linux', jsonb_build_object('host', 'other.example.com', 'port', 22, 'username', 'alice-svc'), credential_id, 'pending_host_key', now(), now() FROM targets WHERE id = $1`, first)
	assert.Equal(t, "23505", sqlState(err), "names are case-insensitive (citext)")
	_, err = d.App.Exec(context.Background(), `INSERT INTO targets (id, name, type, config, credential_id, status, created_at, updated_at)
SELECT gen_random_uuid(), 'web-02', 'linux', config, credential_id, 'pending_host_key', now(), now() FROM targets WHERE id = $1`, first)
	assert.Equal(t, "23505", sqlState(err), "one live target per type, host and port")

	require.NoError(t, exec(t, d.App, "UPDATE targets SET deleted_at = now() WHERE id = $1", first))
	seedTarget(t, d, "web-01", "web-01.example.com") // a deleted target frees its name and address
}

// SEC-081: the location of Alice's own connection key can neither be marked removed nor deleted,
// whatever role asks; other locations can be marked removed.
func TestAliceKeyLocationIsProtectedByTrigger(t *testing.T) {
	d := pgtest.New(t)
	ctx := context.Background()
	target := seedTarget(t, d, "web-01", "web-01.example.com")
	var key string
	require.NoError(t, d.App.QueryRow(ctx, `INSERT INTO ssh_keys (id, fingerprint_sha256, key_type, public_key, is_platform_key, first_seen_at, created_at)
VALUES (gen_random_uuid(), 'SHA256:alice', 'ssh-ed25519', 'ssh-ed25519 AAAA', true, now(), now()) RETURNING id::text`).Scan(&key))
	var own, other string
	require.NoError(t, d.App.QueryRow(ctx, `INSERT INTO ssh_key_locations (id, ssh_key_id, target_id, os_user, file_path, line_no, first_seen_at, last_seen_at, is_alice_connection_key)
VALUES (gen_random_uuid(), $1, $2, 'alice-svc', '/var/lib/alice-svc/.ssh/authorized_keys', 1, now(), now(), true) RETURNING id::text`, key, target).Scan(&own))
	require.NoError(t, d.App.QueryRow(ctx, `INSERT INTO ssh_key_locations (id, ssh_key_id, target_id, os_user, file_path, line_no, first_seen_at, last_seen_at)
VALUES (gen_random_uuid(), $1, $2, 'deploy', '/home/deploy/.ssh/authorized_keys', 1, now(), now()) RETURNING id::text`, key, target).Scan(&other))

	assert.Equal(t, "P0001", sqlState(exec(t, d.App, "UPDATE ssh_key_locations SET removed_by_alice_at = now() WHERE id = $1", own)))
	assert.Equal(t, "P0001", sqlState(exec(t, d.Owner, "UPDATE ssh_key_locations SET removed_by_alice_at = now() WHERE id = $1", own)), "the owner role too")
	assert.Equal(t, "P0001", sqlState(exec(t, d.Owner, "DELETE FROM ssh_key_locations WHERE id = $1", own)))
	require.NoError(t, exec(t, d.App, "UPDATE ssh_key_locations SET last_seen_at = now() WHERE id = $1", own), "discovery still updates it")
	require.NoError(t, exec(t, d.App, "UPDATE ssh_key_locations SET removed_by_alice_at = now() WHERE id = $1", other))
	require.NoError(t, exec(t, d.Owner, "DELETE FROM ssh_key_locations WHERE id = $1", other))
}

func TestOneHostKeyIsPinnedPerTarget(t *testing.T) {
	d := pgtest.New(t)
	target := seedTarget(t, d, "web-01", "web-01.example.com")
	insert := func(fp, status string) error {
		return exec(t, d.App, `INSERT INTO host_keys (id, target_id, key_type, public_key, fingerprint_sha256, status, observed_at)
VALUES (gen_random_uuid(), $1, 'ssh-ed25519', '\x00', $2, $3, now())`, target, fp, status)
	}
	require.NoError(t, insert("SHA256:a", "pinned"))
	require.NoError(t, insert("SHA256:b", "observed"))
	assert.Equal(t, "23505", sqlState(insert("SHA256:c", "pinned")), "a second pinned key")
	assert.Equal(t, "23505", sqlState(insert("SHA256:a", "superseded")), "one row per fingerprint and target")
	assert.Equal(t, "23514", sqlState(insert("SHA256:d", "trusted")), "status is a closed set")
}

func TestJobDedupeKeysAreUniqueAmongLiveJobsOnly(t *testing.T) {
	d := pgtest.New(t)
	key := "target.discover:x:1"
	first, err := seedJob(t, d, &key, "queued")
	require.NoError(t, err)
	_, err = seedJob(t, d, &key, "queued")
	assert.Equal(t, "23505", sqlState(err))
	require.NoError(t, exec(t, d.App, "UPDATE jobs SET status = 'blocked_license' WHERE id = $1", first))
	_, err = seedJob(t, d, &key, "queued")
	assert.Equal(t, "23505", sqlState(err), "a job waiting for the license is still live")
	require.NoError(t, exec(t, d.App, "UPDATE jobs SET status = 'succeeded' WHERE id = $1", first))
	_, err = seedJob(t, d, &key, "queued")
	require.NoError(t, err, "a finished job frees its dedupe key")
	_, err = seedJob(t, d, nil, "waiting")
	assert.Equal(t, "23514", sqlState(err))
}

func TestJobChildrenFollowTheirJob(t *testing.T) {
	d := pgtest.New(t)
	ctx := context.Background()
	target := seedTarget(t, d, "web-01", "web-01.example.com")
	job, err := seedJob(t, d, nil, "running")
	require.NoError(t, err)
	require.NoError(t, exec(t, d.App, `INSERT INTO job_attempts (id, job_id, attempt, worker_id, started_at) VALUES (gen_random_uuid(), $1, 1, 'w', now())`, job))
	require.NoError(t, exec(t, d.App, `INSERT INTO target_locks (target_id, job_id, operation, locked_by, heartbeat_at, lease_until)
VALUES ($1, $2, 'target.discover', 'w', now(), now() + interval '45 seconds')`, target, job))
	require.NoError(t, exec(t, d.App, "DELETE FROM jobs WHERE id = $1", job))
	var attempts, locks int
	require.NoError(t, d.Owner.QueryRow(ctx, "SELECT (SELECT count(*) FROM job_attempts), (SELECT count(*) FROM target_locks)").Scan(&attempts, &locks))
	assert.Zero(t, attempts)
	assert.Zero(t, locks)
}
```
