```sql
-- +goose Up
-- Phase 3: providers, targets, SSH key inventory and the durable job queue (spec §7.2–§7.4, §8; R37).

CREATE TABLE credentials (
    id          uuid PRIMARY KEY,
    purpose     text NOT NULL CHECK (purpose IN ('platform_ssh')),
    kind        text NOT NULL CHECK (kind IN ('ssh_private_key', 'ssh_password_unused', 'azure_sp_secret', 'azure_sp_cert', 'azure_managed_identity')),
    public_info jsonb NOT NULL DEFAULT '{}',
    ciphertext  bytea NOT NULL,
    nonce       bytea NOT NULL CHECK (octet_length(nonce) = 12),
    wrapped_dek bytea NOT NULL,
    key_version integer NOT NULL CHECK (key_version >= 1),
    created_at  timestamptz NOT NULL,
    rotated_at  timestamptz
);
CREATE UNIQUE INDEX credentials_one_platform_key ON credentials (purpose) WHERE purpose = 'platform_ssh';

CREATE TABLE targets (
    id                         uuid PRIMARY KEY,
    name                       citext NOT NULL CHECK (char_length(name::text) BETWEEN 1 AND 100),
    type                       text NOT NULL CHECK (type IN ('nginx', 'linux', 'azure_key_vault')),
    config                     jsonb NOT NULL,
    credential_id              uuid NOT NULL REFERENCES credentials (id),
    status                     text NOT NULL CHECK (status IN ('pending_host_key', 'checking', 'ok', 'unreachable', 'host_key_changed', 'auth_failed', 'disabled')),
    last_error_code            text NOT NULL DEFAULT '',
    last_success_at            timestamptz,
    last_discovery_at          timestamptz,
    discovery_interval_seconds integer NOT NULL DEFAULT 86400 CHECK (discovery_interval_seconds BETWEEN 3600 AND 2592000),
    keys_managed_elsewhere     boolean NOT NULL DEFAULT false,
    facts                      jsonb NOT NULL DEFAULT '{}',
    capabilities               text[] NOT NULL DEFAULT '{}',
    counts_toward_license      boolean NOT NULL DEFAULT true,
    version                    integer NOT NULL DEFAULT 1 CHECK (version >= 1),
    created_by                 uuid REFERENCES users (id),
    created_at                 timestamptz NOT NULL,
    updated_at                 timestamptz NOT NULL,
    deleted_at                 timestamptz
);
CREATE UNIQUE INDEX targets_name_live ON targets (name) WHERE deleted_at IS NULL;
CREATE UNIQUE INDEX targets_endpoint_live ON targets (type, (config->>'host'), (config->>'port')) WHERE deleted_at IS NULL;
CREATE INDEX targets_live_created ON targets (created_at, id) WHERE deleted_at IS NULL;

CREATE TABLE host_keys (
    id                 uuid PRIMARY KEY,
    target_id          uuid NOT NULL REFERENCES targets (id),
    key_type           text NOT NULL,
    public_key         bytea NOT NULL,
    fingerprint_sha256 text NOT NULL,
    status             text NOT NULL CHECK (status IN ('observed', 'pinned', 'superseded', 'rejected')),
    observed_at        timestamptz NOT NULL,
    confirmed_by       uuid REFERENCES users (id),
    confirmed_at       timestamptz,
    superseded_at      timestamptz,
    UNIQUE (target_id, fingerprint_sha256)
);
CREATE UNIQUE INDEX host_keys_one_pinned ON host_keys (target_id) WHERE status = 'pinned';

CREATE TABLE ssh_keys (
    id                 uuid PRIMARY KEY,
    fingerprint_sha256 text NOT NULL UNIQUE,
    key_type           text NOT NULL,
    bits               integer NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
    public_key         text NOT NULL,
    managed            boolean NOT NULL DEFAULT false,
    is_platform_key    boolean NOT NULL DEFAULT false,
    weak               boolean NOT NULL DEFAULT false,
    label              text NOT NULL DEFAULT '',
    first_seen_at      timestamptz NOT NULL,
    created_at         timestamptz NOT NULL,
    retired_at         timestamptz
);

CREATE TABLE ssh_key_locations (
    id                      uuid PRIMARY KEY,
    ssh_key_id              uuid NOT NULL REFERENCES ssh_keys (id),
    target_id               uuid NOT NULL REFERENCES targets (id),
    os_user                 text NOT NULL,
    file_path               text NOT NULL,
    line_no                 integer NOT NULL CHECK (line_no >= 1),
    options                 text NOT NULL DEFAULT '',
    comment                 text NOT NULL DEFAULT '',
    flags                   text[] NOT NULL DEFAULT '{}',
    first_seen_at           timestamptz NOT NULL,
    last_seen_at            timestamptz NOT NULL,
    missing_since           timestamptz,
    removed_by_alice_at     timestamptz,
    is_alice_connection_key boolean NOT NULL DEFAULT false,
    UNIQUE (ssh_key_id, target_id, os_user, file_path)
);
CREATE INDEX ssh_key_locations_target ON ssh_key_locations (target_id);

-- The platform's own key can never be marked removed or deleted (spec §7.3, SEC-081). The
-- service layer and the provider refuse first; this trigger holds even if both had a bug.
-- +goose StatementBegin
CREATE FUNCTION ssh_key_locations_protect_alice_key() RETURNS trigger LANGUAGE plpgsql AS $$
BEGIN
    IF TG_OP = 'DELETE' THEN
        IF OLD.is_alice_connection_key THEN
            RAISE EXCEPTION 'the location of Alice''s own connection key cannot be deleted' USING ERRCODE = 'P0001';
        END IF;
        RETURN OLD;
    END IF;
    IF OLD.is_alice_connection_key AND NEW.removed_by_alice_at IS NOT NULL THEN
        RAISE EXCEPTION 'Alice''s own connection key cannot be removed' USING ERRCODE = 'P0001';
    END IF;
    RETURN NEW;
END $$;
-- +goose StatementEnd
CREATE TRIGGER ssh_key_locations_protect BEFORE UPDATE OR DELETE ON ssh_key_locations
    FOR EACH ROW EXECUTE FUNCTION ssh_key_locations_protect_alice_key();

CREATE TABLE jobs (
    id              uuid PRIMARY KEY,
    type            text NOT NULL,
    class           text NOT NULL CHECK (class IN ('always', 'read_only', 'change')),
    kind            text NOT NULL CHECK (kind IN ('scheduled', 'user', 'system')),
    payload         jsonb NOT NULL DEFAULT '{}',
    payload_mac     bytea NOT NULL CHECK (octet_length(payload_mac) = 32),
    target_id       uuid REFERENCES targets (id),
    dedupe_key      text,
    status          text NOT NULL CHECK (status IN ('queued', 'running', 'succeeded', 'failed', 'cancelled', 'dead', 'blocked_license')),
    priority        smallint NOT NULL DEFAULT 5,
    run_at          timestamptz NOT NULL,
    attempts        integer NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
    max_attempts    integer NOT NULL CHECK (max_attempts >= 1),
    locked_by       text,
    locked_until    timestamptz,
    heartbeat_at    timestamptz,
    last_error_code text NOT NULL DEFAULT '',
    result          jsonb NOT NULL DEFAULT '{}',
    created_by      uuid REFERENCES users (id),
    created_by_role text NOT NULL DEFAULT '',
    confirmed_by    uuid REFERENCES users (id),
    confirmed_at    timestamptz,
    created_at      timestamptz NOT NULL,
    started_at      timestamptz,
    finished_at     timestamptz
);
CREATE INDEX jobs_due ON jobs (priority, run_at) WHERE status = 'queued';
CREATE INDEX jobs_running_lease ON jobs (locked_until) WHERE status = 'running';
CREATE INDEX jobs_target ON jobs (target_id, created_at DESC);
CREATE INDEX jobs_finished ON jobs (finished_at) WHERE finished_at IS NOT NULL;
CREATE UNIQUE INDEX jobs_dedupe_live ON jobs (dedupe_key) WHERE status IN ('queued', 'running', 'blocked_license');

CREATE TABLE job_attempts (
    id          uuid PRIMARY KEY,
    job_id      uuid NOT NULL REFERENCES jobs (id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
    attempt     integer NOT NULL,
    worker_id   text NOT NULL,
    started_at  timestamptz NOT NULL,
    finished_at timestamptz,
    error_code  text NOT NULL DEFAULT '',
    UNIQUE (job_id, attempt)
);

CREATE TABLE target_locks (
    target_id    uuid PRIMARY KEY REFERENCES targets (id),
    job_id       uuid NOT NULL REFERENCES jobs (id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
    operation    text NOT NULL,
    locked_by    text NOT NULL,
    heartbeat_at timestamptz NOT NULL,
    lease_until  timestamptz NOT NULL
);

-- Credentials are append-only for the application; inventory rows are never deleted (soft delete
-- and missing_since keep the history); jobs, attempts and target locks are working tables.
GRANT SELECT, INSERT ON credentials TO alice_app;
GRANT SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE ON targets, host_keys, ssh_keys, ssh_key_locations TO alice_app;
GRANT SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE ON jobs, job_attempts, target_locks TO alice_app;

-- +goose Down
DROP TABLE target_locks;
DROP TABLE job_attempts;
DROP TABLE jobs;
DROP TRIGGER ssh_key_locations_protect ON ssh_key_locations;
DROP FUNCTION ssh_key_locations_protect_alice_key();
DROP TABLE ssh_key_locations;
DROP TABLE ssh_keys;
DROP TABLE host_keys;
DROP TABLE targets;
DROP TABLE credentials;
```

### Task 4: Provider framework: interface, capabilities, registry, errors, fake provider, conformance suite

The compile-time provider framework of spec §6: the `Provider` and `Session` interfaces, the capability set, the
declarative config schemas, the frozen registry (registration validates the schemas and panics on mistakes, so a
broken provider never starts), the one error type providers return (whose text never contains the cause), and the
types every later task exchanges. A scriptable in-memory provider (`fake`) serves the inventory and job tests, and
`providertest` holds the conformance checks every provider runs.

**Files:**
- Create: `internal/providers/provider.go`, `internal/providers/capability.go`, `internal/providers/schema.go`,
  `internal/providers/registry.go`, `internal/providers/errors.go`, `internal/providers/types.go`,
  `internal/providers/unsupported.go`
- Create: `internal/providers/providers_test.go`
- Create: `internal/providers/fake/fake.go`, `internal/providers/fake/fake_test.go`
- Create: `internal/providers/providertest/providertest.go`

**Interfaces:**
- Consumes: `clock.Clock` (`alice/internal/platform/clock`), `validate.FieldError`, `validate.Required` (`alice/internal/platform/validate`), `uuid.UUID`, `ssh.Signer` (`golang.org/x/crypto/ssh`).
- Produces (`alice/internal/providers`): everything in the contract section "Package `alice/internal/providers`" verbatim: `Kind`, `KindLinuxSSH`, `KindNginx`, `KindAzureKV`, `KindForTargetType`, `Capability` and the nine `Cap*` constants, `CapabilitySet`, `NewCapabilitySet`, `Has`, `Sorted`, `FieldType` with constants `FieldString`, `FieldInt`, `FieldBool`, `FieldEnum`, `FieldPath`, `FieldHost`, `Field`, `ConfigSchema`, `CredentialSchema`, `TargetConfig`, `TargetRef`, `HostKey`, `ErrNoPinnedKey`, `HostKeyStore`, `CredentialSource`, `Env`, `Provider`, `Session`, `ErrUnsupported`, `UnsupportedSession`, `SetupGuide` (with `HelperInfo`), `SetupSnippet`, `OSRelease`, `ConnectionReport`, `DiscoverRequest`, `DiscoveryResult`, `DiscoveredSSHKey`, the six `Flag*` constants, `DiscoveredHostKey`, `SSHDSummary`, `UnreadableLine`, `Warning`, `AuthKeyChange`, `AuthKeyResult`, `StepStatus` with `StepStarted`, `StepOK`, `StepFailed`, `StepSkipped`, `StepLogger`, `Error`, `NewError`, `Descriptor`, `Registry`, `NewRegistry`, `Register`, `Freeze`, `Get`, `List`.

```go
type Config struct {
```

  `Open` mirrors the real dialer: with `env.HostKeys` set and `SkipHostKeyCheck` false it calls `Pinned`; on
  `ErrNoPinnedKey` it calls `Observed(ctx, target, PresentedKey, false)` (when `PresentedKey.Fingerprint != ""`) and
  returns `*providers.Error{Code: "target.host_key_unconfirmed", Params: {"fingerprint": …}}`; when the pinned
  fingerprint differs from `PresentedKey.Fingerprint` it calls `Observed(…, true)` and returns
  `*providers.Error{Code: "target.host_key_changed", Params: {"old_fingerprint", "new_fingerprint"}}`. With a non-nil
  `CredentialSource` it calls `SSHSigner` and its release function once. Session methods of capabilities the provider
  lacks return `providers.ErrUnsupported`.
- Produces (`alice/internal/providers/providertest`): `func CheckProvider(t testing.TB, p providers.Provider)`, `func CheckUnsupported(t testing.TB, s providers.Session, caps providers.CapabilitySet)`.

```go
func TestRegistryRegistersFreezesAndLists(t *testing.T) {
	r := providers.NewRegistry()
	r.Register(validStub(providers.KindNginx))
	r.Register(validStub(providers.KindLinuxSSH))
	r.Freeze()

	p, ok := r.Get(providers.KindLinuxSSH)
	require.True(t, ok)
	assert.Equal(t, providers.KindLinuxSSH, p.Kind())
	_, ok = r.Get(providers.KindAzureKV)
	assert.False(t, ok)

	list := r.List()
	require.Len(t, list, 2)
	assert.Equal(t, providers.KindLinuxSSH, list[0].Kind, "sorted by kind")
	assert.Equal(t, providers.KindNginx, list[1].Kind)
	assert.Equal(t, []providers.Capability{providers.CapTestConnection}, list[0].Capabilities)
	assert.Equal(t, "provider.stub.name", list[0].DisplayNameKey)
	assert.Len(t, list[0].ConfigSchema.Fields, 3)

	})

func TestRegistryRefusesBrokenProviders(t *testing.T) {
	cases := map[string]func(s *stub){

		"no display name":    func(s *stub) { s.name = "" },
		"no capabilities":    func(s *stub) { s.caps = providers.NewCapabilitySet() },
		"bad field name":     func(s *stub) { s.config.Fields[0].Name = "Host" },
		"field name digit":   func(s *stub) { s.config.Fields[0].Name = "1host" },
		"duplicate field":    func(s *stub) { s.config.Fields[1].Name = "host" },
		"bad field type":     func(s *stub) { s.config.Fields[0].Type = "url" },
		"empty label key":    func(s *stub) { s.config.Fields[0].LabelKey = "" },
		"bad pattern":        func(s *stub) { s.config.Fields[2].Pattern = `^[a` },
		"enum without value": func(s *stub) { s.config.Fields[2].Values = nil },
		"min above max":      func(s *stub) { s.config.Fields[1].Min = 70000 },
		"bad credential field": func(s *stub) {

	for name, breakIt := range cases {

		})

// Spec §6.3 item 5: no secret in errors. The message is the stable code only, whatever the cause says.
func TestErrorNeverShowsItsCause(t *testing.T) {
	cause := errors.New("ssh: handshake failed: password=CANARY-hunter2")
	err := providers.NewError("ssh.auth_failed", false, cause, map[string]string{"host": "web-01"})
	assert.Equal(t, "providers: ssh.auth_failed", err.Error())
	for _, s := range []string{fmt.Sprint(err), fmt.Sprintf("%v %+v %s %q", err, err, err, err), fmt.Errorf("job: %w", err).Error()} {
		assert.NotContains(t, s, "CANARY", s)
	}
	assert.ErrorIs(t, err, cause, "the cause stays reachable for errors.Is")
	var pe *providers.Error
	require.True(t, errors.As(fmt.Errorf("wrapped: %w", err), &pe))
	assert.Equal(t, "ssh.auth_failed", pe.Code)
	assert.False(t, pe.Retryable)
	assert.Equal(t, map[string]string{"host": "web-01"}, pe.Params)

	retry := providers.NewError("ssh.unreachable", true, nil, nil)
	assert.True(t, retry.Retryable)
	assert.NotNil(t, retry.Params, "params are never nil")
	assert.NoError(t, retry.Unwrap())
}

func TestUnsupportedSession(t *testing.T) {
	ctx := context.Background()
	s := providers.UnsupportedSession{}
	assert.NoError(t, s.Close())
	_, err := s.TestConnection(ctx)
	assert.ErrorIs(t, err, providers.ErrUnsupported)
	_, err = s.Discover(ctx, providers.DiscoverRequest{SSHKeys: true})
	assert.ErrorIs(t, err, providers.ErrUnsupported)
	_, err = s.ListAuthorizedKeys(ctx)
	assert.ErrorIs(t, err, providers.ErrUnsupported)
	_, err = s.AddAuthorizedKey(ctx, providers.AuthKeyChange{}, nil)
	assert.ErrorIs(t, err, providers.ErrUnsupported)
	_, err = s.RemoveAuthorizedKey(ctx, providers.AuthKeyChange{}, nil)
	assert.ErrorIs(t, err, providers.ErrUnsupported)
}
```

Create `internal/providers/provider.go`:

```go
// Package providers defines the compile-time provider framework (spec §6): the Provider and
// Session interfaces, capabilities, declarative config schemas, the frozen registry and the one
// error type providers return. Providers are pure adapters: no database access (archtest), no
// runtime code loading.
package providers

import (
	"context"
	"errors"
	"log/slog"

	"github.com/google/uuid"
	"golang.org/x/crypto/ssh"

	"alice/internal/platform/clock"
	"alice/internal/platform/validate"
)

// Kind names a provider.
type Kind string

// Provider kinds of v1.
const (
	KindLinuxSSH Kind = "linuxssh"
	KindNginx    Kind = "nginx"
	KindAzureKV  Kind = "azurekv"
)

// KindForTargetType maps targets.type to the provider kind (spec §6.4).
func KindForTargetType(t string) (Kind, bool) {
	switch t {
	case "linux":
		return KindLinuxSSH, true
	case "nginx":
		return KindNginx, true
	case "azure_key_vault":
		return KindAzureKV, true
	default:
		return "", false
	}
}

// TargetConfig is the non-secret target configuration (targets.config).
type TargetConfig map[string]any

// TargetRef identifies the target a session works on.
type TargetRef struct {
	ID     uuid.UUID
	Name   string
	Kind   Kind
	Config TargetConfig
}

// HostKey is an SSH server key in wire form plus its SHA-256 fingerprint ("SHA256:…").
type HostKey struct {
	Type        string // ssh.PublicKey.Type(), e.g. "ssh-ed25519"
	PublicKey   []byte // ssh.PublicKey.Marshal()
	Fingerprint string // ssh.FingerprintSHA256
}

// ErrNoPinnedKey is returned by HostKeyStore.Pinned when no key is pinned for the target.
var ErrNoPinnedKey = errors.New("providers: no pinned host key")

// HostKeyStore is implemented by inventory. Pinned returns ErrNoPinnedKey when nothing is pinned.
// Observed records a presented key that is not pinned; changed is true when another key is pinned.
type HostKeyStore interface {
	Pinned(ctx context.Context, target uuid.UUID) (HostKey, error)
	Observed(ctx context.Context, target uuid.UUID, key HostKey, changed bool) error
}

// CredentialSource hands a provider the secret of one session. release zeroes what was decrypted.
type CredentialSource interface {
	SSHSigner(ctx context.Context) (signer ssh.Signer, release func(), err error)
}

// Env carries injected dependencies so providers stay pure.
type Env struct {
	Clock    clock.Clock
	HostKeys HostKeyStore
	Log      *slog.Logger // already redacting
}

// Provider is one kind of managed system.
type Provider interface {
	Kind() Kind
	DisplayNameKey() string
	Capabilities() CapabilitySet
	ConfigSchema() ConfigSchema
	CredentialSchema() CredentialSchema
	ValidateConfig(cfg TargetConfig) []validate.FieldError
	Open(ctx context.Context, t TargetRef, cred CredentialSource, env Env) (Session, error)
}

// Session is one connection scope. Methods of capabilities a provider does not advertise return
// ErrUnsupported (embed UnsupportedSession). Later phases add deploy and import methods.
type Session interface {
	Close() error
	TestConnection(ctx context.Context) (ConnectionReport, error)
	Discover(ctx context.Context, req DiscoverRequest) (DiscoveryResult, error)
	ListAuthorizedKeys(ctx context.Context) ([]DiscoveredSSHKey, error)
	AddAuthorizedKey(ctx context.Context, req AuthKeyChange, log StepLogger) (AuthKeyResult, error)
	RemoveAuthorizedKey(ctx context.Context, req AuthKeyChange, log StepLogger) (AuthKeyResult, error)
}

// SetupGuide is implemented by providers that need host preparation (linuxssh).
type SetupGuide interface {
	SetupSnippets(authorizedKeysLine string) map[string]SetupSnippet // key: profile "linux" | "nginx"
	HelperInfo() (path string, protocol int)                         // "/usr/local/libexec/alice-helper", helperproto.Protocol
}

// SetupSnippet is the host preparation for one sudoers profile.
type SetupSnippet struct {
	Profile string // "linux" | "nginx"
	Sudoers string // content of /etc/sudoers.d/alice
	Script  string // shell script to run as root on the target
}
```

Create `internal/providers/capability.go`:

```go
package providers

import "sort"

// Capability is one thing a provider can do (spec §6.1).
type Capability string

// Capabilities of v1 providers.
const (
	CapTestConnection    Capability = "test_connection"
	CapDiscoverCerts     Capability = "discover_certificates"
	CapDiscoverSSHKeys   Capability = "discover_ssh_keys"
	CapDiscoverKVKeys    Capability = "discover_kv_keys"
	CapDiscoverKVSecrets Capability = "discover_kv_secret_metadata"
	CapDeployCertificate Capability = "deploy_certificate"
	CapImportCertificate Capability = "import_certificate"
	CapAuthorizedKeys    Capability = "authorized_keys"
	CapVerifyDeployment  Capability = "verify_deployment"
)

// CapabilitySet is the static set a provider advertises.
type CapabilitySet map[Capability]struct{}

// NewCapabilitySet builds a set; duplicates are ignored.
func NewCapabilitySet(caps ...Capability) CapabilitySet {
	c := make(CapabilitySet, len(caps))
	for _, x := range caps {
		c[x] = struct{}{}
	}
	return c
}

// Has reports whether x is in the set (false for a nil set).
func (c CapabilitySet) Has(x Capability) bool {
	_, ok := c[x]
	return ok
}

// Sorted returns the capabilities in lexical order (stable API output).
func (c CapabilitySet) Sorted() []Capability {
	out := make([]Capability, 0, len(c))
	for x := range c {
		out = append(out, x)
	}
	sort.Slice(out, func(i, j int) bool { return out[i] < out[j] })
	return out
}
```

Create `internal/providers/schema.go`:

```go
package providers

import (
	"fmt"
	"regexp"
)

// FieldType is the type of a config field; the server validator and the SPA form generator use it.
type FieldType string

// Field types.
const (
	FieldString FieldType = "string"
	FieldInt    FieldType = "int"
	FieldBool   FieldType = "bool"
	FieldEnum   FieldType = "enum"
	FieldPath   FieldType = "path"
	FieldHost   FieldType = "host"
)

// Field describes one config or credential field. Labels are i18n keys, never text.
type Field struct {
	Name     string
	Type     FieldType
	Required bool
	Default  any
	LabelKey string // i18n key, e.g. "provider.linuxssh.fields.host.label"
	HelpKey  string
	Pattern  string // Go regexp, anchored
	Min, Max int    // ints: value range; strings: length range (0 = unbounded)
	Values   []string
}

// ConfigSchema describes the non-secret target config.
type ConfigSchema struct{ Fields []Field }

// CredentialSchema describes secret fields (never echoed back).
type CredentialSchema struct{ Fields []Field }

var fieldNameRE = regexp.MustCompile(`^[a-z][a-z0-9_]*$`)

var fieldTypes = map[FieldType]bool{FieldString: true, FieldInt: true, FieldBool: true, FieldEnum: true, FieldPath: true, FieldHost: true}

// checkFields validates a schema at registration: snake_case unique names, known types,
// translatable labels, compiling patterns, enums with values, sane ranges.
func checkFields(fields []Field) error {
	seen := map[string]bool{}
	for _, f := range fields {
		switch {
		case !fieldNameRE.MatchString(f.Name):
			return fmt.Errorf("field name %q is not snake_case", f.Name)
		case seen[f.Name]:
			return fmt.Errorf("field %q is declared twice", f.Name)
		case !fieldTypes[f.Type]:
			return fmt.Errorf("field %q has unknown type %q", f.Name, f.Type)
		case f.LabelKey == "":
			return fmt.Errorf("field %q has no label key", f.Name)
		case f.Type == FieldEnum && len(f.Values) == 0:
			return fmt.Errorf("enum field %q has no values", f.Name)
		case f.Max > 0 && f.Min > f.Max:
			return fmt.Errorf("field %q has min %d above max %d", f.Name, f.Min, f.Max)
		}
		if f.Pattern != "" {
			if _, err := regexp.Compile(f.Pattern); err != nil {
				return fmt.Errorf("field %q has a pattern that does not compile", f.Name)
			}
		}
		seen[f.Name] = true
	}
	return nil
}
```

```go
package providers

import "github.com/google/uuid"

// OSRelease is the part of /etc/os-release Alice shows.
type OSRelease struct{ ID, VersionID, PrettyName string }

// ConnectionReport is the result of TestConnection.
type ConnectionReport struct {

	HelperVersion  string
	HelperProtocol int

	Warnings       []Warning
}

// DiscoverRequest selects what Discover reads.
type DiscoverRequest struct{ SSHKeys bool }

// DiscoveryResult is read-only data; inventory reconciles it.
type DiscoveryResult struct {
	SSHKeys         []DiscoveredSSHKey
	HostKeys        []DiscoveredHostKey
	SSHD            SSHDSummary
	UnreadableLines []UnreadableLine
	Warnings        []Warning
	Partial         bool     // some source failed: inventory never marks anything missing from a partial scan
	ReadFiles       []string // files read completely (missing marking is limited to these)
}

// DiscoveredSSHKey is one authorized_keys entry.
type DiscoveredSSHKey struct {
	OSUser      string
	FilePath    string
	LineNo      int
	PublicKey   string // "ssh-ed25519 AAAA…" (type and base64 blob, no options, no comment)
	Fingerprint string // "SHA256:…"
	KeyType     string
	Bits        int
	Comment     string
	Options     string   // verbatim option text, "" when none
	Flags       []string // Flag* values
}

// Flags of discovered keys (spec §13.3 item 5).
const (
	FlagWeak            = "weak"              // RSA < 2048, DSA
	FlagCommand         = "command"           // command= present (shown, never touched)
	FlagRootWithoutFrom = "root_without_from" // root key without from=
	FlagDuplicate       = "duplicate"         // same key more than once in the file
	FlagCertAuthority   = "cert_authority"    // cert-authority line: inventory only, never managed
	FlagSecurityKey     = "security_key"      // sk-* (FIDO) key
)

// DiscoveredHostKey is one server host key from the host key inventory (informational).
type DiscoveredHostKey struct {
	KeyType     string
	Bits        int
	Fingerprint string
	Weak        bool // DSA, RSA < 2048
}

// SSHDSummary is what Alice shows from sshd's effective configuration (spec §13.2).
type SSHDSummary struct {
	Read                   bool // false: sshd -T failed, defaults were assumed
	PubkeyAuthentication   string
	PasswordAuthentication string
	PermitRootLogin        string
	AuthorizedKeysFile     []string
	AuthorizedKeysCommand  string // "none" or the program
	KeysManagedElsewhere   bool   // AuthorizedKeysCommand is set (F-35)
	CertificatesInUse      bool   // TrustedUserCAKeys or AuthorizedPrincipalsFile set
}

// UnreadableLine is an authorized_keys line that does not parse (kept verbatim, never changed).
type UnreadableLine struct {
	OSUser, FilePath string
	LineNo           int
}

// Warning is a stable code (i18n key "warnings.<code>") and its parameters.
type Warning struct {
	Code   string
	Params map[string]string
}

// AuthKeyChange asks for one authorized_keys change.
type AuthKeyChange struct {
	OperationID           uuid.UUID
	OSUser                string
	FilePath              string
	Fingerprint           string   // remove: the key to remove
	Line                  string   // add: the authorized_keys line to add
	ProtectedFingerprints []string // keys that must never be removed (the platform key)
	AllowLastRootKey      bool
}

// AuthKeyResult is the outcome of a change.
type AuthKeyResult struct {
	Changed   bool
	Removed   int
	OldSHA256 string
	NewSHA256 string
	Verified  bool
}

// StepStatus is the state of one externally visible step.
type StepStatus string

// Step states.
const (
	StepStarted StepStatus = "started"
	StepOK      StepStatus = "ok"
	StepFailed  StepStatus = "failed"
	StepSkipped StepStatus = "skipped"
)

// StepLogger records the steps of a mutating operation (params are redacted, never secrets).
type StepLogger interface {
	Step(name string, status StepStatus, params map[string]string)
}

// Descriptor is what GET /providers shows.
type Descriptor struct {
	Kind             Kind
	DisplayNameKey   string
	Capabilities     []Capability
	ConfigSchema     ConfigSchema
	CredentialSchema CredentialSchema
}
```

```go
package providers

import "errors"

// ErrUnsupported is returned by sessions for capabilities the provider does not have.
var ErrUnsupported = errors.New("providers: operation not supported by this provider")

// Error is the only error type providers return (spec §6.3 item 5). Code is a stable reason
// ("ssh.auth_failed"); the API maps it to an ALC code. Cause is kept for errors.Is and for logs
// (its type only) and is never part of the message, because SDK and SSH errors can echo
// remote output or secrets.
type Error struct {
	Code      string
	Params    map[string]string
	Retryable bool
	Cause     error
}

// Error returns "providers: <code>", never the cause's text.
func (e *Error) Error() string { return "providers: " + e.Code }

// Unwrap returns the cause.
func (e *Error) Unwrap() error { return e.Cause }

// NewError builds an Error; params are never nil.
func NewError(code string, retryable bool, cause error, params map[string]string) *Error {
	if params == nil {
		params = map[string]string{}
	}
	return &Error{Code: code, Params: params, Retryable: retryable, Cause: cause}
}
```

```go
package providers

import "context"

// UnsupportedSession answers ErrUnsupported for every operation; providers embed it and
// implement only what they advertise.
type UnsupportedSession struct{}

// Close does nothing.
func (UnsupportedSession) Close() error { return nil }

// TestConnection is not supported.
func (UnsupportedSession) TestConnection(context.Context) (ConnectionReport, error) {
	return ConnectionReport{}, ErrUnsupported
}

// Discover is not supported.
func (UnsupportedSession) Discover(context.Context, DiscoverRequest) (DiscoveryResult, error) {
	return DiscoveryResult{}, ErrUnsupported
}

// ListAuthorizedKeys is not supported.
func (UnsupportedSession) ListAuthorizedKeys(context.Context) ([]DiscoveredSSHKey, error) {
	return nil, ErrUnsupported
}

// AddAuthorizedKey is not supported.
func (UnsupportedSession) AddAuthorizedKey(context.Context, AuthKeyChange, StepLogger) (AuthKeyResult, error) {
	return AuthKeyResult{}, ErrUnsupported
}

// RemoveAuthorizedKey is not supported.
func (UnsupportedSession) RemoveAuthorizedKey(context.Context, AuthKeyChange, StepLogger) (AuthKeyResult, error) {
	return AuthKeyResult{}, ErrUnsupported
}

var _ Session = UnsupportedSession{}
```

```go
package providers

import (
	"fmt"
	"sort"
	"sync"
)

// Registry holds the providers of this build. It is filled in cmd/alice (no init magic) and
// frozen before the first request (spec §6.4).
type Registry struct {
	mu        sync.RWMutex
	providers map[Kind]Provider
	frozen    bool
}

// NewRegistry returns an empty registry.
func NewRegistry() *Registry { return &Registry{providers: map[Kind]Provider{}} }

// Register adds p. It panics on a nil provider, an empty kind or display name, no capabilities,
// an invalid schema, a duplicate kind or a frozen registry: a broken provider never starts.
func (r *Registry) Register(p Provider) {
	if p == nil {
		panic("providers: nil provider")
	}
	k := p.Kind()
	switch {
	case k == "":
		panic("providers: provider without a kind")
	case p.DisplayNameKey() == "":
		panic(fmt.Sprintf("providers: %s has no display name key", k))
	case len(p.Capabilities()) == 0:
		panic(fmt.Sprintf("providers: %s advertises no capabilities", k))
	}
	if err := checkFields(p.ConfigSchema().Fields); err != nil {
		panic(fmt.Sprintf("providers: %s config schema: %v", k, err))
	}
	if err := checkFields(p.CredentialSchema().Fields); err != nil {
		panic(fmt.Sprintf("providers: %s credential schema: %v", k, err))
	}
	r.mu.Lock()
	defer r.mu.Unlock()
	if r.frozen {
		panic(fmt.Sprintf("providers: registry is frozen; cannot register %s", k))
	}
	if _, dup := r.providers[k]; dup {
		panic(fmt.Sprintf("providers: kind %s is registered twice", k))
	}
	r.providers[k] = p
}

// Freeze makes the registry immutable.
func (r *Registry) Freeze() {
	r.mu.Lock()
	defer r.mu.Unlock()
	r.frozen = true
}

// Get returns the provider of kind k.
func (r *Registry) Get(k Kind) (Provider, bool) {
	r.mu.RLock()
	defer r.mu.RUnlock()
	p, ok := r.providers[k]
	return p, ok
}

// List describes every provider, sorted by kind.
func (r *Registry) List() []Descriptor {
	r.mu.RLock()
	defer r.mu.RUnlock()
	out := make([]Descriptor, 0, len(r.providers))
	for _, p := range r.providers {
		out = append(out, Descriptor{
			Kind: p.Kind(), DisplayNameKey: p.DisplayNameKey(), Capabilities: p.Capabilities().Sorted(),
			ConfigSchema: p.ConfigSchema(), CredentialSchema: p.CredentialSchema(),
		})
	}
	sort.Slice(out, func(i, j int) bool { return out[i].Kind < out[j].Kind })
	return out
}
```

```go
package fake_test

import (
	"context"
	"errors"
	"sync"
	"testing"

	"github.com/google/uuid"
	"github.com/stretchr/testify/assert"
	"github.com/stretchr/testify/require"
	"golang.org/x/crypto/ssh"

	"alice/internal/providers"
	"alice/internal/providers/fake"
	"alice/internal/providers/providertest"
)

type memStore struct {
	mu       sync.Mutex
	pinned   map[uuid.UUID]providers.HostKey
	observed []observation
}

type observation struct {
	key     providers.HostKey
	changed bool
}

func (m *memStore) Pinned(_ context.Context, id uuid.UUID) (providers.HostKey, error) {
	m.mu.Lock()
	defer m.mu.Unlock()
	k, ok := m.pinned[id]
	if !ok {
		return providers.HostKey{}, providers.ErrNoPinnedKey
	}
	return k, nil
}

func (m *memStore) Observed(_ context.Context, _ uuid.UUID, k providers.HostKey, changed bool) error {
	m.mu.Lock()
	defer m.mu.Unlock()
	m.observed = append(m.observed, observation{k, changed})
	return nil
}

type countingCreds struct{ signers, releases int }

func (c *countingCreds) SSHSigner(context.Context) (ssh.Signer, func(), error) {
	c.signers++
	return nil, func() { c.releases++ }, nil
}

var (
	keyA = providers.HostKey{Type: "ssh-ed25519", PublicKey: []byte{1}, Fingerprint: "SHA256:A"}
	keyB = providers.HostKey{Type: "ssh-ed25519", PublicKey: []byte{2}, Fingerprint: "SHA256:B"}
)

func TestFakeIsAConformingProvider(t *testing.T) {
	p := fake.New(providers.KindLinuxSSH)
	providertest.CheckProvider(t, p)
	s, err := p.Open(context.Background(), providers.TargetRef{ID: uuid.New()}, nil, providers.Env{})
	require.NoError(t, err)
	providertest.CheckUnsupported(t, s, p.Capabilities())

	limited := fake.New(providers.KindNginx, providers.CapTestConnection)
	s, err = limited.Open(context.Background(), providers.TargetRef{ID: uuid.New()}, nil, providers.Env{})
	require.NoError(t, err)
	providertest.CheckUnsupported(t, s, limited.Capabilities())
	_, err = s.Discover(context.Background(), providers.DiscoverRequest{SSHKeys: true})
	assert.ErrorIs(t, err, providers.ErrUnsupported, "no discover_ssh_keys capability")
}

// The fake mirrors the pinning rules of the real dialer (F-30, F-31), so inventory and job tests
// see the same errors and Observed calls.
func TestFakeOpenFollowsThePinningRules(t *testing.T) {
	ctx := context.Background()
	target := uuid.New()
	store := &memStore{pinned: map[uuid.UUID]providers.HostKey{}}
	p := fake.New(providers.KindLinuxSSH)
	p.Configure(func(c *fake.Config) { c.PresentedKey = keyA })
	env := providers.Env{HostKeys: store}

	_, err := p.Open(ctx, providers.TargetRef{ID: target}, nil, env)
	var pe *providers.Error
	require.True(t, errors.As(err, &pe))
	assert.Equal(t, "target.host_key_unconfirmed", pe.Code)
	assert.Equal(t, "SHA256:A", pe.Params["fingerprint"])
	require.Len(t, store.observed, 1)
	assert.Equal(t, observation{keyA, false}, store.observed[0])

	store.pinned[target] = keyA
	creds := &countingCreds{}
	s, err := p.Open(ctx, providers.TargetRef{ID: target}, creds, env)
	require.NoError(t, err)
	assert.Equal(t, 1, creds.signers)
	assert.Equal(t, 1, creds.releases, "the credential is released after the dial")
	rep, err := s.TestConnection(ctx)
	require.NoError(t, err)
	assert.Equal(t, "SHA256:A", rep.HostKey.Fingerprint, "the report carries the presented key by default")

	p.Configure(func(c *fake.Config) { c.PresentedKey = keyB })
	_, err = p.Open(ctx, providers.TargetRef{ID: target}, creds, env)
	require.True(t, errors.As(err, &pe))
	assert.Equal(t, "target.host_key_changed", pe.Code)
	assert.Equal(t, map[string]string{"old_fingerprint": "SHA256:A", "new_fingerprint": "SHA256:B"}, pe.Params)
	assert.Equal(t, observation{keyB, true}, store.observed[len(store.observed)-1])
	assert.Equal(t, 1, creds.signers, "no credential is decrypted for a changed key")

	p.Configure(func(c *fake.Config) { c.SkipHostKeyCheck = true })
	_, err = p.Open(ctx, providers.TargetRef{ID: target}, nil, env)
	assert.NoError(t, err)
}

func TestFakeRecordsCallsAndReturnsScriptedResults(t *testing.T) {
	ctx := context.Background()
	target := uuid.New()
	boom := providers.NewError("ssh.timeout", true, nil, nil)
	p := fake.New(providers.KindLinuxSSH)
	p.Configure(func(c *fake.Config) {
		c.Discovery = providers.DiscoveryResult{SSHKeys: []providers.DiscoveredSSHKey{{OSUser: "deploy", Fingerprint: "SHA256:K"}}}
		c.RemoveResult = providers.AuthKeyResult{Changed: true, Removed: 1}
		c.AddErr = boom
	})
	s, err := p.Open(ctx, providers.TargetRef{ID: target}, nil, providers.Env{})
	require.NoError(t, err)
	res, err := s.Discover(ctx, providers.DiscoverRequest{SSHKeys: true})
	require.NoError(t, err)
	assert.Equal(t, "SHA256:K", res.SSHKeys[0].Fingerprint)
	change := providers.AuthKeyChange{OSUser: "deploy", Fingerprint: "SHA256:K"}
	out, err := s.RemoveAuthorizedKey(ctx, change, nil)
	require.NoError(t, err)
	assert.Equal(t, 1, out.Removed)
	_, err = s.AddAuthorizedKey(ctx, change, nil)
	assert.Same(t, boom, err)
	require.NoError(t, s.Close())

	assert.Equal(t, 1, p.Count("Open"))
	assert.Equal(t, 1, p.Count("RemoveAuthorizedKey"))
	calls := p.Calls()
	require.Len(t, calls, 5)
	assert.Equal(t, []string{"Open", "Discover", "RemoveAuthorizedKey", "AddAuthorizedKey", "Close"},
		[]string{calls[0].Method, calls[1].Method, calls[2].Method, calls[3].Method, calls[4].Method})
	assert.Equal(t, target, calls[2].Target)
	assert.Equal(t, change, calls[2].Change)

	p.Configure(func(c *fake.Config) { c.OpenErr = boom })
	_, err = p.Open(ctx, providers.TargetRef{ID: target}, nil, providers.Env{})
	assert.Same(t, boom, err)
}
```

```go
// Package providertest holds the conformance checks every provider runs (spec §6.5 item 5).
// It uses only testing.TB, so it never pulls test libraries into a build that imports it.
package providertest

import (
	"context"
	"errors"
	"testing"

	"alice/internal/platform/validate"
	"alice/internal/providers"
)

// CheckProvider verifies the static contract: kind, display name, capabilities, schemas that a
// registry accepts, and that ValidateConfig reports every required field of an empty config.
func CheckProvider(t testing.TB, p providers.Provider) {
	t.Helper()
	if p.Kind() == "" {
		t.Errorf("provider has no kind")
	}
	if p.DisplayNameKey() == "" {
		t.Errorf("%s: no display name key", p.Kind())
	}
	if len(p.Capabilities()) == 0 {
		t.Errorf("%s: no capabilities", p.Kind())
	}
	func() {
		defer func() {
			if r := recover(); r != nil {
				t.Errorf("%s: a registry refuses it: %v", p.Kind(), r)
			}
		}()
		providers.NewRegistry().Register(p)
	}()
	reported := map[string]bool{}
	for _, fe := range p.ValidateConfig(providers.TargetConfig{}) {
		if fe.Code == validate.Required {
			reported[fe.Field] = true
		}
	}
	for _, f := range p.ConfigSchema().Fields {
		if f.Required && f.Default == nil && !reported[f.Name] {
			t.Errorf("%s: an empty config does not report the required field %q", p.Kind(), f.Name)
		}
	}
}

// CheckUnsupported verifies that every operation of a capability the provider does not
// advertise answers ErrUnsupported (spec §6.1), so the job layer can rely on Capabilities().
func CheckUnsupported(t testing.TB, s providers.Session, caps providers.CapabilitySet) {
	t.Helper()
	ctx := context.Background()
	expect := func(name string, err error) {
		t.Helper()
		if !errors.Is(err, providers.ErrUnsupported) {
			t.Errorf("%s without its capability: got %v, want ErrUnsupported", name, err)
		}
	}
	if !caps.Has(providers.CapTestConnection) {
		_, err := s.TestConnection(ctx)
		expect("TestConnection", err)
	}
	if !caps.Has(providers.CapDiscoverSSHKeys) {
		_, err := s.Discover(ctx, providers.DiscoverRequest{SSHKeys: true})
		expect("Discover", err)
	}
	if !caps.Has(providers.CapAuthorizedKeys) {
		_, err := s.ListAuthorizedKeys(ctx)
		expect("ListAuthorizedKeys", err)
		_, err = s.AddAuthorizedKey(ctx, providers.AuthKeyChange{}, nil)
		expect("AddAuthorizedKey", err)
		_, err = s.RemoveAuthorizedKey(ctx, providers.AuthKeyChange{}, nil)
		expect("RemoveAuthorizedKey", err)
	}
}
```

Create `internal/providers/fake/fake.go`:

```go
// Package fake is an in-memory provider for inventory and job tests. Behaviour is scripted with
// Configure; every call is recorded. Open follows the pinning rules of the real linuxssh dialer.
package fake

import (
	"context"
	"errors"
	"sync"

	"github.com/google/uuid"

	"alice/internal/platform/validate"
	"alice/internal/providers"
)

// Call is one recorded method call.
type Call struct {
	Method string // "Open", "TestConnection", "Discover", "ListAuthorizedKeys", "AddAuthorizedKey", "RemoveAuthorizedKey", "Close"
	Target uuid.UUID
	Change providers.AuthKeyChange // Add/Remove only
}

// Config is the scripted behaviour.
type Config struct {
	OpenErr          error
	SkipHostKeyCheck bool              // Open does not consult env.HostKeys
	PresentedKey     providers.HostKey // the key "the server" presents; "" fingerprint = do not check
	Report           providers.ConnectionReport
	TestErr          error
	Discovery        providers.DiscoveryResult
	DiscoverErr      error
	Keys             []providers.DiscoveredSSHKey
	ListErr          error
	AddResult        providers.AuthKeyResult
	AddErr           error
	RemoveResult     providers.AuthKeyResult
	RemoveErr        error
}

// Provider is the scriptable provider.
type Provider struct {
	kind  providers.Kind
	caps  providers.CapabilitySet
	mu    sync.Mutex
	cfg   Config
	calls []Call
}

// New returns a fake of kind with caps (test_connection, discover_ssh_keys and authorized_keys
// when none are given).
func New(kind providers.Kind, caps ...providers.Capability) *Provider {
	if len(caps) == 0 {
		caps = []providers.Capability{providers.CapTestConnection, providers.CapDiscoverSSHKeys, providers.CapAuthorizedKeys}
	}
	return &Provider{kind: kind, caps: providers.NewCapabilitySet(caps...)}
}

// Configure changes the scripted behaviour under the lock.
func (p *Provider) Configure(fn func(c *Config)) {
	p.mu.Lock()
	defer p.mu.Unlock()
	fn(&p.cfg)
}

// Calls returns a copy of the recorded calls.
func (p *Provider) Calls() []Call {
	p.mu.Lock()
	defer p.mu.Unlock()
	return append([]Call(nil), p.calls...)
}

// Count returns how many calls of method were recorded.
func (p *Provider) Count(method string) int {
	n := 0
	for _, c := range p.Calls() {
		if c.Method == method {
			n++
		}
	}
	return n
}

func (p *Provider) record(c Call) Config {
	p.mu.Lock()
	defer p.mu.Unlock()
	p.calls = append(p.calls, c)
	return p.cfg
}

// Kind implements providers.Provider.
func (p *Provider) Kind() providers.Kind { return p.kind }

// DisplayNameKey implements providers.Provider.
func (p *Provider) DisplayNameKey() string { return "provider.fake.name" }

// Capabilities implements providers.Provider.
func (p *Provider) Capabilities() providers.CapabilitySet { return p.caps }

// ConfigSchema implements providers.Provider.
func (p *Provider) ConfigSchema() providers.ConfigSchema {
	return providers.ConfigSchema{Fields: []providers.Field{
		{Name: "host", Type: providers.FieldHost, Required: true, LabelKey: "provider.fake.fields.host.label"},
		{Name: "port", Type: providers.FieldInt, Min: 1, Max: 65535, Default: 22, LabelKey: "provider.fake.fields.port.label"},
		{Name: "username", Type: providers.FieldString, Default: "alice-svc", LabelKey: "provider.fake.fields.username.label"},
	}}
}

// CredentialSchema implements providers.Provider.
func (p *Provider) CredentialSchema() providers.CredentialSchema { return providers.CredentialSchema{} }

// ValidateConfig implements providers.Provider: only host is required.
func (p *Provider) ValidateConfig(cfg providers.TargetConfig) []validate.FieldError {
	if h, _ := cfg["host"].(string); h == "" {
		return []validate.FieldError{{Field: "host", Code: validate.Required}}
	}
	return nil
}

// Open implements providers.Provider with the pinning rules of the real dialer.
func (p *Provider) Open(ctx context.Context, t providers.TargetRef, cred providers.CredentialSource, env providers.Env) (providers.Session, error) {
	cfg := p.record(Call{Method: "Open", Target: t.ID})
	if cfg.OpenErr != nil {
		return nil, cfg.OpenErr
	}
	presented := cfg.PresentedKey
	if !cfg.SkipHostKeyCheck && env.HostKeys != nil && presented.Fingerprint != "" {
		pinned, err := env.HostKeys.Pinned(ctx, t.ID)
		switch {
		case errors.Is(err, providers.ErrNoPinnedKey):
			if err := env.HostKeys.Observed(ctx, t.ID, presented, false); err != nil {
				return nil, err
			}
			return nil, providers.NewError("target.host_key_unconfirmed", false, nil, map[string]string{"fingerprint": presented.Fingerprint})
		case err != nil:
			return nil, err
		case pinned.Fingerprint != presented.Fingerprint:
			if err := env.HostKeys.Observed(ctx, t.ID, presented, true); err != nil {
				return nil, err
			}
			return nil, providers.NewError("target.host_key_changed", false, nil,
				map[string]string{"old_fingerprint": pinned.Fingerprint, "new_fingerprint": presented.Fingerprint})
		}
	}
	if cred != nil {
		_, release, err := cred.SSHSigner(ctx)
		if err != nil {
			return nil, err
		}
		release()
	}
	return &session{p: p, target: t.ID}, nil
}

type session struct {
	p      *Provider
	target uuid.UUID
}

func (s *session) Close() error {
	s.p.record(Call{Method: "Close", Target: s.target})
	return nil
}

func (s *session) TestConnection(context.Context) (providers.ConnectionReport, error) {
	cfg := s.p.record(Call{Method: "TestConnection", Target: s.target})
	if !s.p.caps.Has(providers.CapTestConnection) {
		return providers.ConnectionReport{}, providers.ErrUnsupported
	}
	rep := cfg.Report
	if rep.HostKey.Fingerprint == "" {
		rep.HostKey = cfg.PresentedKey
	}
	return rep, cfg.TestErr
}

func (s *session) Discover(context.Context, providers.DiscoverRequest) (providers.DiscoveryResult, error) {
	cfg := s.p.record(Call{Method: "Discover", Target: s.target})
	if !s.p.caps.Has(providers.CapDiscoverSSHKeys) {
		return providers.DiscoveryResult{}, providers.ErrUnsupported
	}
	return cfg.Discovery, cfg.DiscoverErr
}

func (s *session) ListAuthorizedKeys(context.Context) ([]providers.DiscoveredSSHKey, error) {
	cfg := s.p.record(Call{Method: "ListAuthorizedKeys", Target: s.target})
	if !s.p.caps.Has(providers.CapAuthorizedKeys) {
		return nil, providers.ErrUnsupported
	}
	return cfg.Keys, cfg.ListErr
}

func (s *session) AddAuthorizedKey(_ context.Context, req providers.AuthKeyChange, _ providers.StepLogger) (providers.AuthKeyResult, error) {
	cfg := s.p.record(Call{Method: "AddAuthorizedKey", Target: s.target, Change: req})
	if !s.p.caps.Has(providers.CapAuthorizedKeys) {
		return providers.AuthKeyResult{}, providers.ErrUnsupported
	}
	return cfg.AddResult, cfg.AddErr
}

func (s *session) RemoveAuthorizedKey(_ context.Context, req providers.AuthKeyChange, _ providers.StepLogger) (providers.AuthKeyResult, error) {
	cfg := s.p.record(Call{Method: "RemoveAuthorizedKey", Target: s.target, Change: req})
	if !s.p.caps.Has(providers.CapAuthorizedKeys) {
		return providers.AuthKeyResult{}, providers.ErrUnsupported
	}
	return cfg.RemoveResult, cfg.RemoveErr
}

var (
	_ providers.Provider = (*Provider)(nil)
	_ providers.Session  = (*session)(nil)
)
```

capabilities present) by design; the limited fake is the real check, and the explicit `Discover` assertion below it
fails if `CheckUnsupported` ever skips that capability.

### Task 5: Pure parsers — helper protocol vocabulary, `sshd -T`, `authorized_keys` (+ both fuzz targets)

Three pure packages that both sides of the SSH boundary share. `helperproto` is the wire contract between Alice and
`alice-helper` (subcommand names, exit codes, error codes, JSON shapes) plus the argument vocabulary that Alice's
command builder (Task 8) and the helper (Tasks 6–7) both enforce (SEC-063). `sshdconf` parses `sshd -T` output (and
plain `sshd_config` text) and expands `AuthorizedKeysFile` tokens; the helper uses it to compute the only paths it will
ever read or write (§13.3 step 2). `linuxssh/authkeys.go` parses `authorized_keys` files byte-exactly, so a rewrite
by Alice changes only the lines it means to change (§13.3 step 3, §13.4). All three use only the standard library and
`golang.org/x/crypto/ssh` so the static helper binary can import them. Review Focus item 1 is pinned here.

**Files:**
- Create: `internal/providers/linuxssh/helperproto/helperproto.go`, `internal/providers/linuxssh/helperproto/helperproto_test.go`
- Create: `internal/providers/linuxssh/sshdconf/sshdconf.go`, `internal/providers/linuxssh/sshdconf/sshdconf_test.go`
- Create: `internal/providers/linuxssh/doc.go`, `internal/providers/linuxssh/authkeys.go`, `internal/providers/linuxssh/authkeys_test.go`
- Modify: `Makefile` (new target `fuzz-ssh`)

**Interfaces:**
- Consumes (Task 4, `alice/internal/providers`): `providers.DiscoveredSSHKey`, `providers.UnreadableLine`, the flag constants
  `providers.FlagWeak`, `FlagCommand`, `FlagRootWithoutFrom`, `FlagDuplicate`, `FlagCertAuthority`, `FlagSecurityKey`.
- Produces (`helperproto`, exactly as in the contract): constants `Protocol`, `Version`, `HelperPath`, `BackupRoot`,
  `Sub*`, `Exit*`, `Code*`, `MaxAuthorizedKeysSize`, `AbsentSHA256`; types `ErrorResponse`, `VersionResponse`,
  `SSHDDumpResponse`, `HostKeyInfo`, `HostKeysResponse`, `FileInfo`, `UserFiles`, `AuthKeysListResponse`,
  `AuthKeysReadResponse`, `AuthKeysWriteResponse`, `CleanupResponse`; `func ValidArg(s string) bool`,
  `func ValidPath(s string) bool`, `func ValidUser(s string) bool`, `func ValidOpID(s string) bool`,
  `func ValidSHA256(s string) bool`. Helper warning codes (strings in `AuthKeysListResponse.Warnings`):
  `WarnSSHDUnreadable = "sshd_unreadable"`, `WarnDirectoryUsers = "directory_users_not_listed"`,
  `WarnUnsupportedPath = "unsupported_path"` (additions; they equal the web `warnings.<code>` keys).
- Produces (`sshdconf`): `var DefaultAuthorizedKeysFile`, `type Config` (contract fields), `const MaxConfigSize`,
  `var ErrTooLarge`, `var ErrInvalidPattern` (addition), `func Parse(data []byte) (Config, error)`,
  `func Expand(pattern, user, home string, uid int) (string, error)`. `Parse` applies the OpenSSH defaults:
  `AuthorizedKeysFile` = `DefaultAuthorizedKeysFile` when absent (an explicit `none` gives an empty, non-nil slice),
  `AuthorizedKeysCommand` = `"none"` when absent; for every other keyword the first value wins (OpenSSH semantics);
  `hostkey` accumulates.
- Produces (`linuxssh`): `type LineKind` with `LineBlank`, `LineComment`, `LineKey`, `LineInvalid`; `type Line`,
  `type AuthorizedKeys` (contract fields); `func ParseAuthorizedKeys(data []byte) (AuthorizedKeys, error)`;
  methods `Bytes() []byte`, `Keys(osUser, filePath string) ([]providers.DiscoveredSSHKey, []providers.UnreadableLine)`,
  `AddLine(line string) (AuthorizedKeys, bool, error)`, `RemoveFingerprint(fp string) (AuthorizedKeys, int)`,
  `CountKeys() int`; `var ErrAuthorizedKeysTooLarge`, `var ErrInvalidKeyLine` (addition: `AddLine`'s error).

- [ ] **Step 2: Write the helper protocol**

Create `internal/providers/linuxssh/helperproto/helperproto.go`:

```go
// Package helperproto is the protocol between Alice and alice-helper (spec §12.3, §13.1, R21):
// subcommand names, exit codes, error codes, the JSON answers and the argument vocabulary that
// both sides enforce (SEC-063). It uses only the standard library because the static helper
// binary imports it too.
package helperproto

import (
	"path/filepath"
	"regexp"
	"strings"
)

// Protocol and file locations.
const (
	Protocol   = 1
	Version    = "1.0.0"
	HelperPath = "/usr/local/libexec/alice-helper"
	BackupRoot = "/var/lib/alice-helper/backups"
)

// Subcommands of protocol 1 (R37 item 3).
const (
	SubVersion       = "version"
	SubSSHDDump      = "sshd-dump"
	SubHostKeys      = "hostkeys"
	SubAuthKeysList  = "authkeys-list"
	SubAuthKeysRead  = "authkeys-read"
	SubAuthKeysWrite = "authkeys-write"
	SubCleanup       = "cleanup"
)

// Exit codes (spec §12.3).
const (
	ExitOK           = 0
	ExitRefused      = 2 // validation refused
	ExitPrecondition = 3 // hash mismatch, missing file
	ExitFailed       = 4 // command failed
)

// Error codes printed in ErrorResponse.Code. They are internal: Alice maps them to ALC codes.
const (
	CodeUsage               = "USAGE"
	CodeUnknownSubcommand   = "UNKNOWN_SUBCOMMAND"
	CodeNotRoot             = "NOT_ROOT"
	CodeInvalidArgument     = "INVALID_ARGUMENT"
	CodePathNotAllowed      = "PATH_NOT_ALLOWED"
	CodeNotRegularFile      = "NOT_REGULAR_FILE"
	CodeInsecurePermissions = "INSECURE_PERMISSIONS"
	CodeTooLarge            = "TOO_LARGE"
	CodeHashMismatch        = "HASH_MISMATCH"
	CodeNotFound            = "NOT_FOUND"
	CodeSSHDFailed          = "SSHD_FAILED"
	CodeIOError             = "IO_ERROR"
)

// Warning codes in AuthKeysListResponse.Warnings; they equal the web catalog keys warnings.<code>.
const (
	WarnSSHDUnreadable  = "sshd_unreadable"
	WarnDirectoryUsers  = "directory_users_not_listed"
	WarnUnsupportedPath = "unsupported_path"
)

// Size limits and markers.
const (
	MaxAuthorizedKeysSize = 1 << 20  // authkeys-read output and authkeys-write stdin
	AbsentSHA256          = "absent" // --expect-sha256 for a file that does not exist yet
	maxArgLen             = 4096
)

// ErrorResponse is the one JSON line printed on every failure.
type ErrorResponse struct {
	OK      bool   `json:"ok"`
	Code    string `json:"code"`
	Message string `json:"message"`
}

// VersionResponse answers "version" (runs without sudo).
type VersionResponse struct {
	OK       bool   `json:"ok"`
	Helper   string `json:"helper"`
	Protocol int    `json:"protocol"`
}

// SSHDDumpResponse answers "sshd-dump".
type SSHDDumpResponse struct {
	OK       bool   `json:"ok"`
	Config   string `json:"config"`   // sshd -T output
	Fallback bool   `json:"fallback"` // sshd -T failed: Config is empty, defaults apply
}

// HostKeyInfo is one host key of the server.
type HostKeyInfo struct {
	Type        string `json:"type"`
	Bits        int    `json:"bits"`
	Fingerprint string `json:"fingerprint"`
	Path        string `json:"path"`
}

// HostKeysResponse answers "hostkeys".
type HostKeysResponse struct {
	OK   bool          `json:"ok"`
	Keys []HostKeyInfo `json:"keys"`
}

// FileInfo describes one candidate authorized_keys file.
type FileInfo struct {
	Path          string `json:"path"`
	Exists        bool   `json:"exists"`
	Size          int64  `json:"size"`
	SHA256        string `json:"sha256"` // "" when absent or too large
	Mode          string `json:"mode"`   // "0600"
	Owner         string `json:"owner"`
	StrictModesOK bool   `json:"strict_modes_ok"`
	TooLarge      bool   `json:"too_large"`
}

// UserFiles is one account and its candidate files.
type UserFiles struct {
	User  string     `json:"user"`
	UID   int        `json:"uid"`
	Home  string     `json:"home"`
	Files []FileInfo `json:"files"`
}

// AuthKeysListResponse answers "authkeys-list".
type AuthKeysListResponse struct {
	OK                    bool        `json:"ok"`
	Users                 []UserFiles `json:"users"`
	AuthorizedKeysCommand string      `json:"authorized_keys_command"`
	Warnings              []string    `json:"warnings"`
}

// AuthKeysReadResponse answers "authkeys-read".
type AuthKeysReadResponse struct {
	OK         bool   `json:"ok"`
	Path       string `json:"path"`
	SHA256     string `json:"sha256"`
	ContentB64 string `json:"content_b64"`
}

// AuthKeysWriteResponse answers "authkeys-write".
type AuthKeysWriteResponse struct {
	OK     bool   `json:"ok"`
	SHA256 string `json:"sha256"`
	Backup string `json:"backup"`
}

// CleanupResponse answers "cleanup".
type CleanupResponse struct {
	OK      bool `json:"ok"`
	Removed int  `json:"removed"`
}

var (
	argRE  = regexp.MustCompile(`^[A-Za-z0-9._/@:+-]+$`)
	userRE = regexp.MustCompile(`^[a-z_][a-z0-9_-]{0,31}$`)
)

// ValidArg reports whether s may appear as a helper argument: 1 to 4096 characters from
// [A-Za-z0-9._/@:+-], no ".." path element and no leading "-" (it would read as an option).
// Everything else (spaces, quotes, shell metacharacters, control characters, non-ASCII) is refused.
func ValidArg(s string) bool {
	if len(s) == 0 || len(s) > maxArgLen || !argRE.MatchString(s) || strings.HasPrefix(s, "-") {
		return false
	}
	for _, part := range strings.Split(s, "/") {
		if part == ".." {
			return false
		}
	}
	return true
}

// ValidPath reports whether s is a valid argument that is also an absolute, already clean path.
func ValidPath(s string) bool {
	return ValidArg(s) && strings.HasPrefix(s, "/") && filepath.Clean(s) == s
}

// ValidUser reports whether s is an acceptable Linux user name (SEC-062).
func ValidUser(s string) bool { return userRE.MatchString(s) }

// ValidOpID reports whether s is a lowercase UUID in 8-4-4-4-12 form (the backup directory name).
func ValidOpID(s string) bool {
	if len(s) != 36 {
		return false
	}
	for i := 0; i < len(s); i++ {
		c := s[i]
		switch i {
		case 8, 13, 18, 23:
			if c != '-' {
				return false
			}
		default:
			if !isLowerHex(c) {
				return false
			}
		}
	}
	return true
}

// ValidSHA256 reports whether s is 64 lowercase hex digits or AbsentSHA256.
func ValidSHA256(s string) bool {
	if s == AbsentSHA256 {
		return true
	}
	if len(s) != 64 {
		return false
	}
	for i := 0; i < len(s); i++ {
		if !isLowerHex(s[i]) {
			return false
		}
	}
	return true
}

func isLowerHex(c byte) bool { return c >= '0' && c <= '9' || c >= 'a' && c <= 'f' }
```

Note: Go's RE2 caps a repetition count at 1000, so the 4096-character limit is a length check, not `{1,4096}`.
`ValidOpID` checks the UUID form without `google/uuid`, so the helper binary links only the standard library and
`golang.org/x/crypto` (Task 6, `TestHelperIsStatic`).

```go
package sshdconf

import (
	"strings"
	"testing"

	"github.com/stretchr/testify/assert"
	"github.com/stretchr/testify/require"
)

const sshdT = `port 22
addressfamily any
pubkeyauthentication yes
passwordauthentication no
permitrootlogin prohibit-password
strictmodes yes
authorizedkeysfile .ssh/authorized_keys .ssh/authorized_keys2
authorizedkeyscommand none
authorizedkeyscommanduser none
authorizedprincipalsfile none
trustedusercakeys none
hostkey /etc/ssh/ssh_host_rsa_key
hostkey /etc/ssh/ssh_host_ecdsa_key
hostkey /etc/ssh/ssh_host_ed25519_key
`

func TestParseSSHDT(t *testing.T) {
	c, err := Parse([]byte(sshdT))
	require.NoError(t, err)
	assert.Equal(t, []string{".ssh/authorized_keys", ".ssh/authorized_keys2"}, c.AuthorizedKeysFile)
	assert.Equal(t, "none", c.AuthorizedKeysCommand)
	assert.Equal(t, "none", c.AuthorizedKeysCommandUser)
	assert.Equal(t, "none", c.AuthorizedPrincipalsFile)
	assert.Equal(t, "none", c.TrustedUserCAKeys)
	assert.Equal(t, "yes", c.PubkeyAuthentication)
	assert.Equal(t, "no", c.PasswordAuthentication)
	assert.Equal(t, "prohibit-password", c.PermitRootLogin)
	assert.Equal(t, "yes", c.StrictModes)
	assert.Equal(t, []string{"/etc/ssh/ssh_host_rsa_key", "/etc/ssh/ssh_host_ecdsa_key", "/etc/ssh/ssh_host_ed25519_key"}, c.HostKeys)
}

func TestParseAppliesOpenSSHDefaults(t *testing.T) {
	c, err := Parse(nil)
	require.NoError(t, err)
	assert.Equal(t, DefaultAuthorizedKeysFile, c.AuthorizedKeysFile)
	assert.Equal(t, "none", c.AuthorizedKeysCommand)
	assert.Empty(t, c.HostKeys)
	c.AuthorizedKeysFile[0] = "changed"
	assert.Equal(t, ".ssh/authorized_keys", DefaultAuthorizedKeysFile[0], "Parse returns a copy of the defaults")
}

func TestParseConfigFileSyntax(t *testing.T) {
	text := "# Managed by the security team\r\n" +
		"  AuthorizedKeysFile = \"/etc/ssh/keys/%u\" .ssh/authorized_keys\r\n" +
		"PubkeyAuthentication\tno\r\n" +
		"AuthorizedKeysCommand /usr/bin/sss_ssh_authorizedkeys %u\n" +
		"HostKey=/etc/ssh/a\n" +
		"Match User bob\n" +
		"  AuthorizedKeysFile /bob/keys\n" +
		"  PubkeyAuthentication yes\n" +
		"HostKey /etc/ssh/after_match\n"
	c, err := Parse([]byte(text))
	require.NoError(t, err)
	assert.Equal(t, []string{"/etc/ssh/keys/%u", ".ssh/authorized_keys"}, c.AuthorizedKeysFile)
	assert.Equal(t, "no", c.PubkeyAuthentication, "values inside a Match block are ignored")
	assert.Equal(t, "/usr/bin/sss_ssh_authorizedkeys %u", c.AuthorizedKeysCommand)
	assert.Equal(t, []string{"/etc/ssh/a"}, c.HostKeys, "parsing stops at the first Match")
}

func TestParseFirstValueWinsAndNone(t *testing.T) {
	c, err := Parse([]byte("authorizedkeysfile /first\nauthorizedkeysfile /second\npermitrootlogin no\npermitrootlogin yes\n"))
	require.NoError(t, err)
	assert.Equal(t, []string{"/first"}, c.AuthorizedKeysFile)
	assert.Equal(t, "no", c.PermitRootLogin)

	c, err = Parse([]byte("authorizedkeysfile none\n"))
	require.NoError(t, err)
	require.NotNil(t, c.AuthorizedKeysFile)
	assert.Empty(t, c.AuthorizedKeysFile, "AuthorizedKeysFile none means no files")
}

func TestParseRejectsHugeInput(t *testing.T) {
	_, err := Parse([]byte(strings.Repeat("#", MaxConfigSize+1)))
	require.ErrorIs(t, err, ErrTooLarge)
	_, err = Parse([]byte(strings.Repeat("#", MaxConfigSize)))
	require.NoError(t, err)
}

func TestExpand(t *testing.T) {
	for _, tc := range []struct {
		pattern, user, home string
		uid                 int
		want                string
	}{
		{".ssh/authorized_keys", "deploy", "/home/deploy", 1001, "/home/deploy/.ssh/authorized_keys"},
		{"%h/.ssh/authorized_keys2", "deploy", "/home/deploy", 1001, "/home/deploy/.ssh/authorized_keys2"},
		{"/etc/ssh/keys/%u", "deploy", "/home/deploy", 1001, "/etc/ssh/keys/deploy"},
		{"/var/keys/%U", "deploy", "/home/deploy", 1001, "/var/keys/1001"},
		{"/k/100%%", "deploy", "/home/deploy", 1001, "/k/100%"},
		{"%h", "root", "/", 0, "/"},
		{".ssh//authorized_keys", "deploy", "/home/deploy/", 1001, "/home/deploy/.ssh/authorized_keys"},
	} {
		got, err := Expand(tc.pattern, tc.user, tc.home, tc.uid)
		require.NoError(t, err, tc.pattern)
		assert.Equal(t, tc.want, got, tc.pattern)
	}
}

func TestExpandRefusesEscapesAndUnknownTokens(t *testing.T) {
	for _, tc := range []struct{ pattern, user, home string }{
		{"%x/keys", "deploy", "/home/deploy"},
		{"keys%", "deploy", "/home/deploy"},
		{"../../etc/shadow", "deploy", "/home/deploy"},
		{"/etc/%u/../shadow", "deploy", "/home/deploy"},
		{"%h/../root/.ssh/authorized_keys", "deploy", "/home/deploy"},
		{"", "deploy", "/home/deploy"},
		{".ssh/a\nb", "deploy", "/home/deploy"},
		{".ssh/authorized_keys", "dep\x00loy", "/home/deploy"},
		{".ssh/authorized_keys", "deploy", "home/deploy"},
		{"/keys/%u", "..", "/home/deploy"},
	} {

}

// FuzzParseSSHDConfig (spec §25.6): Parse never panics, and every AuthorizedKeysFile it returns
// expands to a clean absolute path that never climbs out with "..".
func FuzzParseSSHDConfig(f *testing.F) {
	for _, seed := range []string{
		sshdT,
		"",
		"authorizedkeysfile none\n",
		"AuthorizedKeysFile %h/.ssh/authorized_keys /etc/ssh/keys/%u /var/%U/%%\n",
		"AuthorizedKeysFile \"/etc/ssh/keys/%u\" \"unterminated\n",
		"Match User bob\n AuthorizedKeysFile /bob\n",
		"authorizedkeysfile ../../etc/shadow %h/../x\r\nmatch all\r\n",
		"hostkey=/a\nhostkey = /b\nHostKey\t/c\n",
		"#only a comment",
		"authorizedkeysfile %",
	} {
		f.Add([]byte(seed))
	}
	f.Fuzz(func(t *testing.T, data []byte) {
		c, err := Parse(data)
		if err != nil {
			return
		}
		for _, p := range c.AuthorizedKeysFile {
			got, err := Expand(p, "u", "/home/u", 1000)
			if err != nil {
				continue
			}
			if !strings.HasPrefix(got, "/") || strings.Contains(got, "/../") || strings.HasSuffix(got, "/..") ||
				strings.ContainsAny(got, "\x00\n\r") {
				t.Fatalf("Expand(%q) = %q escapes or is not absolute", p, got)
			}
		}
	})
}
```

```go
// Package sshdconf reads OpenSSH server settings from "sshd -T" output (or sshd_config text) and
// expands AuthorizedKeysFile tokens (spec §13.2). It is pure and uses only the standard library:
// the static alice-helper binary imports it to compute the only authorized_keys paths it touches.
package sshdconf

import (
	"errors"
	"fmt"
	"path/filepath"
	"strconv"
	"strings"
)

// DefaultAuthorizedKeysFile is OpenSSH's default AuthorizedKeysFile.
var DefaultAuthorizedKeysFile = []string{".ssh/authorized_keys", ".ssh/authorized_keys2"}

// MaxConfigSize bounds the parsed text.
const MaxConfigSize = 1 << 20

var (
	// ErrTooLarge means the configuration text is larger than MaxConfigSize.
	ErrTooLarge = errors.New("sshdconf: configuration too large")
	// ErrInvalidPattern means an AuthorizedKeysFile pattern cannot be expanded safely.
	ErrInvalidPattern = errors.New("sshdconf: invalid AuthorizedKeysFile pattern")
)

// Config holds the settings Alice needs. Empty strings mean "not set"; Parse fills the
// OpenSSH defaults for AuthorizedKeysFile and AuthorizedKeysCommand.
type Config struct {
	AuthorizedKeysFile        []string
	AuthorizedKeysCommand     string // "none" when unset
	AuthorizedKeysCommandUser string
	AuthorizedPrincipalsFile  string
	TrustedUserCAKeys         string
	PubkeyAuthentication      string
	PasswordAuthentication    string
	PermitRootLogin           string
	StrictModes               string
	HostKeys                  []string
}

// Parse reads "keyword value…" lines. Keywords are case-insensitive, "=" may separate keyword
// and value, '#' starts a comment line, double quotes group a value. Like sshd, the first value of
// a keyword wins (hostkey accumulates). Parsing stops at the first Match block: its values apply
// only to some connections, and "sshd -T" without "-C" prints none.
func Parse(data []byte) (Config, error) {
	if len(data) > MaxConfigSize {
		return Config{}, ErrTooLarge
	}
	var c Config
	seen := map[string]bool{}
	for _, raw := range strings.Split(string(data), "\n") {
		line := strings.TrimSpace(raw)
		if line == "" || line[0] == '#' {
			continue
		}
		kw, rest := splitKeyword(line)
		kw = foldASCII(kw)
		if kw == "match" {
			break
		}
		vals := fields(rest)
		if len(vals) == 0 {
			continue
		}
		if kw == "hostkey" {
			c.HostKeys = append(c.HostKeys, vals...)
			continue
		}
		if seen[kw] {
			continue
		}
		seen[kw] = true
		one := strings.Join(vals, " ")
		switch kw {
		case "authorizedkeysfile":
			if len(vals) == 1 && foldASCII(vals[0]) == "none" {
				c.AuthorizedKeysFile = []string{}
			} else {
				c.AuthorizedKeysFile = vals
			}
		case "authorizedkeyscommand":
			c.AuthorizedKeysCommand = one
		case "authorizedkeyscommanduser":
			c.AuthorizedKeysCommandUser = one
		case "authorizedprincipalsfile":
			c.AuthorizedPrincipalsFile = one
		case "trustedusercakeys":
			c.TrustedUserCAKeys = one
		case "pubkeyauthentication":
			c.PubkeyAuthentication = one
		case "passwordauthentication":
			c.PasswordAuthentication = one
		case "permitrootlogin":
			c.PermitRootLogin = one
		case "strictmodes":
			c.StrictModes = one
		}
	}
	if c.AuthorizedKeysFile == nil {
		c.AuthorizedKeysFile = append([]string(nil), DefaultAuthorizedKeysFile...)
	}
	if c.AuthorizedKeysCommand == "" {
		c.AuthorizedKeysCommand = "none"
	}
	return c, nil
}

// splitKeyword splits "Keyword value", "Keyword=value" and "Keyword = value".
func splitKeyword(line string) (string, string) {
	i := strings.IndexAny(line, " \t=")
	if i < 0 {
		return line, ""
	}
	rest := strings.TrimLeft(line[i:], " \t")
	rest = strings.TrimPrefix(rest, "=")
	return line[:i], strings.TrimSpace(rest)
}

// fields splits on spaces and tabs; double quotes group (an unterminated quote runs to the end).
func fields(s string) []string {
	var out []string
	var cur strings.Builder
	inQuote, have := false, false
	for i := 0; i < len(s); i++ {
		c := s[i]
		switch {
		case c == '"':
			inQuote = !inQuote
			have = true
		case (c == ' ' || c == '\t') && !inQuote:
			if have {
				out = append(out, cur.String())
				cur.Reset()
				have = false
			}
		default:
			cur.WriteByte(c)
			have = true
		}
	}
	if have {
		out = append(out, cur.String())
	}
	return out
}

// foldASCII lowercases ASCII letters only (strings.ToLower is banned: Turkish casing, and
// sshd keywords are ASCII).
func foldASCII(s string) string {
	b := []byte(s)
	for i, c := range b {
		if 'A' <= c && c <= 'Z' {
			b[i] = c + ('a' - 'A')
		}
	}
	return string(b)
}

// Expand turns an AuthorizedKeysFile pattern into a path for one user: %h is the home directory,
// %u the user name, %U the numeric user ID, %% a percent sign; a relative result is relative to
// the home directory. A pattern or an expansion that contains NUL or a line break, an unknown
// token, a ".." path element or a result that is not absolute is refused with ErrInvalidPattern.
func Expand(pattern, user, home string, uid int) (string, error) {
	if pattern == "" || strings.ContainsAny(pattern+user+home, "\x00\n\r") {
		return "", ErrInvalidPattern
	}
	var b strings.Builder
	for i := 0; i < len(pattern); i++ {
		c := pattern[i]
		if c != '%' {
			b.WriteByte(c)
			continue
		}
		if i+1 >= len(pattern) {
			return "", fmt.Errorf("%w: trailing %%", ErrInvalidPattern)
		}
		i++
		switch pattern[i] {
		case '%':
			b.WriteByte('%')
		case 'h':
			b.WriteString(home)
		case 'u':
			b.WriteString(user)
		case 'U':
			b.WriteString(strconv.Itoa(uid))
		default:
			return "", fmt.Errorf("%w: unknown token %%%c", ErrInvalidPattern, pattern[i])
		}
	}
	p := b.String()
	if !strings.HasPrefix(p, "/") {
		p = home + "/" + p
	}
	for _, part := range strings.Split(p, "/") {
		if part == ".." {
			return "", fmt.Errorf("%w: the path climbs with ..", ErrInvalidPattern)
		}
	}
	p = filepath.Clean(p)
	if !filepath.IsAbs(p) {
		return "", fmt.Errorf("%w: the path is not absolute", ErrInvalidPattern)
	}
	return p, nil
}
```

```go
// FuzzParseAuthorizedKeys (spec §25.6): never panics; parsing then serializing returns the input
// byte for byte; a valid line keeps its blob and options after re-parsing; removing a key keeps
// every invalid line verbatim.
func FuzzParseAuthorizedKeys(f *testing.F) {
	k, _ := edKey(f)
	sk, _ := skKey(f)
	for _, seed := range []string{
		k + " user@host\n",
		`command="echo \"quoted\" a,b",from="10.0.0.0/8",no-pty ` + k + " c\n",
		`environment="A=B" ` + k,
		k + "\r\n# comment\r\n\r\n",
		"cert-authority " + k + " ca\n",
		sk + " security key\n",
		strings.Repeat("A", 70000) + "\n",
		"ssh-ed25519 \x00\x00\x00 nul\n",
		"\xff\xfe binary\n" + k,
		"",
	} {
		f.Add([]byte(seed))
	}
	f.Fuzz(func(t *testing.T, data []byte) {
		a, err := ParseAuthorizedKeys(data)
		if err != nil {
			if len(data) <= helperproto.MaxAuthorizedKeysSize {
				t.Fatalf("parse refused an input within the size limit: %v", err)
			}
			return
		}
		if !bytes.Equal(a.Bytes(), data) {
			t.Fatalf("round trip changed the file")
		}
		var invalid []string
		for _, l := range a.Lines {
			switch l.Kind {
			case LineKey:
				again, err := ParseAuthorizedKeys([]byte(l.Raw))
				if err != nil || len(again.Lines) != 1 || again.Lines[0].Fingerprint != l.Fingerprint ||
					again.Lines[0].OptionsText != l.OptionsText || again.Lines[0].PublicKey != l.PublicKey {
					t.Fatalf("a valid line did not survive re-parsing: %q", l.Raw)
				}
			case LineInvalid:
				invalid = append(invalid, l.Raw)
			}
		}
		if len(a.Lines) > 0 && a.Lines[0].Kind == LineKey {
			out, _ := a.RemoveFingerprint(a.Lines[0].Fingerprint)
			var kept []string
			for _, l := range out.Lines {
				if l.Kind == LineInvalid {
					kept = append(kept, l.Raw)
				}
			}
			if strings.Join(kept, "\n") != strings.Join(invalid, "\n") {
				t.Fatalf("removing a key changed invalid lines")
			}
		}
	})
}
```

Create `internal/providers/linuxssh/authkeys.go`:

```go
package linuxssh

import (
	"crypto/ecdsa"
	"crypto/ed25519"
	"crypto/rsa"
	"encoding/base64"
	"errors"
	"strings"

	"golang.org/x/crypto/ssh"

	"alice/internal/providers"
	"alice/internal/providers/linuxssh/helperproto"
)

var (
	// ErrAuthorizedKeysTooLarge means the file is larger than helperproto.MaxAuthorizedKeysSize.
	ErrAuthorizedKeysTooLarge = errors.New("linuxssh: authorized_keys file too large")
	// ErrInvalidKeyLine means a line to add is not exactly one valid key line.
	ErrInvalidKeyLine = errors.New("linuxssh: not a single valid authorized_keys line")
)

// LineKind classifies one line of an authorized_keys file.
type LineKind int

// Line kinds.
const (
	LineBlank LineKind = iota
	LineComment
	LineKey
	LineInvalid
)

// Line is one line of an authorized_keys file. Raw is kept verbatim so a rewrite changes only
// the lines Alice means to change (spec §13.3 step 3).
type Line struct {
	Raw         string // verbatim, without the line terminator
	CR          bool   // the line ended with "\r\n" (or is a last line ending in "\r")
	Kind        LineKind
	Options     []string
	OptionsText string // verbatim options prefix ("" when none)
	KeyType     string
	PublicKey   string // "type base64"
	Fingerprint string
	Bits        int
	Comment     string
}

// AuthorizedKeys is a parsed file.
type AuthorizedKeys struct {
	Lines           []Line
	TrailingNewline bool
}

// ParseAuthorizedKeys parses data line by line. It never fails on content: lines that are not a
// valid key are kept as LineInvalid. Only a file over the size limit is refused.
func ParseAuthorizedKeys(data []byte) (AuthorizedKeys, error) {
	if len(data) > helperproto.MaxAuthorizedKeysSize {
		return AuthorizedKeys{}, ErrAuthorizedKeysTooLarge
	}
	var a AuthorizedKeys
	if len(data) == 0 {
		return a, nil
	}
	text := string(data)
	if strings.HasSuffix(text, "\n") {
		a.TrailingNewline = true
		text = text[:len(text)-1]
	}
	for _, raw := range strings.Split(text, "\n") {
		a.Lines = append(a.Lines, parseLine(raw))
	}
	return a, nil
}

func parseLine(raw string) Line {
	l := Line{Raw: raw}
	if strings.HasSuffix(raw, "\r") {
		l.CR = true
		l.Raw = raw[:len(raw)-1]
	}
	t := strings.TrimSpace(l.Raw)
	switch {
	case t == "":
		l.Kind = LineBlank
	case t[0] == '#':
		l.Kind = LineComment
	default:
		parseKeyLine(&l)
	}
	return l
}

// parseKeyLine fills l from a line that should hold one key. x/crypto/ssh ignores everything after
// a '\r' inside a line, so such a line is refused instead of half-trusted.
func parseKeyLine(l *Line) {
	l.Kind = LineInvalid
	if strings.ContainsRune(l.Raw, '\r') {
		return
	}
	key, comment, options, rest, err := ssh.ParseAuthorizedKey([]byte(l.Raw))
	if err != nil || len(rest) != 0 {
		return
	}
	l.Kind = LineKey
	l.Options = options
	l.KeyType = key.Type()
	l.PublicKey = strings.TrimSpace(string(ssh.MarshalAuthorizedKey(key)))
	l.Fingerprint = ssh.FingerprintSHA256(key)
	l.Bits = keyBits(key)
	l.Comment = comment
	l.OptionsText = optionsText(l.Raw, key)
}

// optionsText returns the verbatim text before the key type field: the part of the line between
// its start and the type token that precedes the base64 blob.
func optionsText(raw string, key ssh.PublicKey) string {
	blob := base64.StdEncoding.EncodeToString(key.Marshal())
	idx := strings.Index(raw, blob)
	if idx <= 0 {
		return ""
	}
	prefix := strings.TrimRight(raw[:idx], " \t")
	i := strings.LastIndexAny(prefix, " \t")
	if i < 0 {
		return ""
	}
	return strings.TrimSpace(prefix[:i])
}

// keyBits is the RSA modulus size, the ECDSA curve size or 256 for Ed25519 (also for FIDO keys).
func keyBits(k ssh.PublicKey) int {
	ck, ok := k.(ssh.CryptoPublicKey)
	if !ok {
		return 0
	}
	switch p := ck.CryptoPublicKey().(type) {
	case *rsa.PublicKey:
		return p.N.BitLen()
	case *ecdsa.PublicKey:
		return p.Curve.Params().BitSize
	case ed25519.PublicKey:
		return 256
	default:
		return 0
	}
}

// Bytes serializes the file; for an unchanged parse it is byte-for-byte the input.
func (a AuthorizedKeys) Bytes() []byte {
	var b strings.Builder
	for i, l := range a.Lines {
		b.WriteString(l.Raw)
		if l.CR {
			b.WriteByte('\r')
		}
		if i < len(a.Lines)-1 || a.TrailingNewline {
			b.WriteByte('\n')
		}
	}
	return []byte(b.String())
}

// CountKeys returns the number of key lines.
func (a AuthorizedKeys) CountKeys() int {
	n := 0
	for _, l := range a.Lines {
		if l.Kind == LineKey {
			n++
		}
	}
	return n
}

// Keys lists the key lines as discovered keys (line numbers start at 1) and the lines that are
// neither keys, comments nor blank.
func (a AuthorizedKeys) Keys(osUser, filePath string) ([]providers.DiscoveredSSHKey, []providers.UnreadableLine) {
	count := map[string]int{}
	for _, l := range a.Lines {
		if l.Kind == LineKey {
			count[l.Fingerprint]++
		}
	}
	var keys []providers.DiscoveredSSHKey
	var bad []providers.UnreadableLine
	for i, l := range a.Lines {
		switch l.Kind {
		case LineKey:
			keys = append(keys, providers.DiscoveredSSHKey{
				OSUser: osUser, FilePath: filePath, LineNo: i + 1, PublicKey: l.PublicKey, Fingerprint: l.Fingerprint,
				KeyType: l.KeyType, Bits: l.Bits, Comment: l.Comment, Options: l.OptionsText,
				Flags: flagsFor(l, osUser, count[l.Fingerprint] > 1),
			})
		case LineInvalid:
			bad = append(bad, providers.UnreadableLine{OSUser: osUser, FilePath: filePath, LineNo: i + 1})
		}
	}
	return keys, bad
}

// flagsFor returns the dangerous-finding flags of §13.3 step 5 in a fixed order.
func flagsFor(l Line, osUser string, duplicate bool) []string {
	var f []string
	if (l.KeyType == ssh.KeyAlgoRSA && l.Bits < 2048) || l.KeyType == ssh.InsecureKeyAlgoDSA {
		f = append(f, providers.FlagWeak)
	}
	if hasOption(l.Options, "command") {
		f = append(f, providers.FlagCommand)
	}
	if osUser == "root" && !hasOption(l.Options, "from") {
		f = append(f, providers.FlagRootWithoutFrom)
	}
	if duplicate {
		f = append(f, providers.FlagDuplicate)
	}
	if hasOption(l.Options, "cert-authority") {
		f = append(f, providers.FlagCertAuthority)
	}
	if strings.HasPrefix(l.KeyType, "sk-") {
		f = append(f, providers.FlagSecurityKey)
	}
	return f
}

// hasOption reports whether an option name is present (OpenSSH option names are case-insensitive).
func hasOption(opts []string, name string) bool {
	for _, o := range opts {
		k := o
		if i := strings.IndexByte(o, '='); i >= 0 {
			k = o[:i]
		}
		if strings.EqualFold(strings.TrimSpace(k), name) {
			return true
		}
	}
	return false
}

// AddLine returns a copy with line appended on a line of its own (F-37) and true, or the file
// unchanged and false when a line with the same fingerprint exists. line must be exactly one
// valid key line without control characters. A file whose lines all end in CRLF keeps CRLF.
func (a AuthorizedKeys) AddLine(line string) (AuthorizedKeys, bool, error) {
	for _, r := range line {
		if r < 0x20 || r == 0x7f {
			return a, false, ErrInvalidKeyLine
		}
	}
	nl := parseLine(line)
	if nl.Kind != LineKey {
		return a, false, ErrInvalidKeyLine
	}
	for _, l := range a.Lines {
		if l.Kind == LineKey && l.Fingerprint == nl.Fingerprint {
			return a, false, nil
		}
	}
	if len(a.Lines) > 0 {
		allCR := true
		for _, l := range a.Lines {
			allCR = allCR && l.CR
		}
		nl.CR = allCR
	}
	lines := make([]Line, 0, len(a.Lines)+1)
	lines = append(append(lines, a.Lines...), nl)
	return AuthorizedKeys{Lines: lines, TrailingNewline: true}, true, nil
}

// RemoveFingerprint returns a copy without every key line of that fingerprint and how many were
// removed. Comment, blank and invalid lines are never touched, and the line before a removed
// last line keeps its terminator.
func (a AuthorizedKeys) RemoveFingerprint(fp string) (AuthorizedKeys, int) {
	out := AuthorizedKeys{TrailingNewline: a.TrailingNewline}
	removed := 0
	lastRemoved := false
	for i, l := range a.Lines {
		if l.Kind == LineKey && l.Fingerprint == fp {
			removed++
			lastRemoved = i == len(a.Lines)-1
			continue
		}
		out.Lines = append(out.Lines, l)
	}
	if lastRemoved && !a.TrailingNewline && len(out.Lines) > 0 {
		out.TrailingNewline = true
	}
	if len(out.Lines) == 0 {
		out.TrailingNewline = false
	}
	return out, removed
}
```
