### Task 6: `alice-helper` part 1 — dispatch, path rules, `version`, `sshd-dump`, `hostkeys`, `authkeys-list`, `authkeys-read`, static build

The helper is the second, independent enforcement layer of Alice's remote command surface (spec §6.6, §12.3, R13,
R21, SC-3, SC-5): sudoers can only say "the helper may run", so the helper itself treats every argument as hostile.
It never trusts a path from Alice: the `authorized_keys` files it reads (and, in Task 7, writes) are the candidates it
computes itself from `/etc/passwd` and `sshd -T -C user=…`, and a candidate whose resolved path leaves the user's home
(or the directory of an absolute `AuthorizedKeysFile` pattern) is never a candidate (A-13). Every answer is exactly one
JSON line on stdout; nothing else is ever printed, and file contents never appear in an error. All filesystem and
process access goes through a `sys` value, so the tests run every subcommand against a temporary directory as an
unprivileged user. The binary is static (`CGO_ENABLED=0`, no program interpreter, no shared libraries) and links only
the standard library, `golang.org/x/crypto` (with its `golang.org/x/sys` dependency) and two pure `alice` packages.

**Files:**
- Create: `cmd/alice-helper/main.go`, `cmd/alice-helper/sys.go`, `cmd/alice-helper/run.go`, `cmd/alice-helper/paths.go`,
  `cmd/alice-helper/accounts.go`, `cmd/alice-helper/sshd.go`, `cmd/alice-helper/authkeys.go`
- Test: `cmd/alice-helper/helper_test.go`, `cmd/alice-helper/static_test.go`
- Modify: `Makefile` (new target `helper`)

**Interfaces:**
- Consumes (Task 5): `helperproto` constants, response types and `ValidArg`, `ValidPath`, `ValidUser`, `ValidOpID`,
  `ValidSHA256`, the warning codes `WarnSSHDUnreadable`, `WarnDirectoryUsers`, `WarnUnsupportedPath`;
  `sshdconf.Parse`, `sshdconf.Expand`, `sshdconf.DefaultAuthorizedKeysFile`, `sshdconf.Config`.
- Produces (package `main`, used by Task 7): `type sys struct{ root string; euid func() int; sudoUser func() string;
  now func() time.Time; runSSHD func(ctx context.Context, args ...string) ([]byte, error); stdin io.Reader;
  stdout io.Writer; syslog func(subcommand, path string) }` with `(*sys).host(guest string) string`,
  `(*sys).guest(host string) (string, bool)`, `(*sys).sudoUserName() string`,
  `(*sys).readRegular(guest string, limit int) ([]byte, error)`, `(*sys).resolveNearest(guest string) (string, bool)`,
  `(*sys).scan(ctx context.Context) (scanResult, error)`, `func within(p, dir string) bool`, `func hexSHA(b []byte) string`,
  `func refused(code, msg string) error`, `func precondition(code, msg string) error`, `func failed(code, msg string) error`,
  `var errTooLarge`, `type candidate struct{ acct account; path, real, dir string }`,
  `type account struct{ name string; uid, gid int; home, shell string }`, `(scanResult).find(path string) (candidate, bool)`,
  the dispatch table `commands` (`map[string]command`, `type command struct{ privileged bool; handle func(ctx context.Context, s *sys, args []string) (any, error) }`)
  and `run(args []string, s *sys) int`; test helpers `newFixture(t) *fixture`, `(*fixture).run(args ...string) (int, map[string]any)`,
  `(*fixture).write(guest, content string, mode os.FileMode)`, `(*fixture).mkdir(guest string, mode os.FileMode)`,
  `testNow`, `globalSSHD`.
- Produces (behaviour Task 9's emulator mimics): `authkeys-list` takes no arguments; users are `root` (uid 0), every
  account with uid ≥ 1000 (not 65534) that has an existing home directory and a login shell, plus `SUDO_USER`; sorted by
  uid then name, at most 200; a user's `files` are the expanded `AuthorizedKeysFile` entries in configuration order;
  `owner` is the account name of the file's uid (the decimal uid when unknown); `mode` is four octal digits;
  `sha256` is lowercase hex; `warnings` is never `null`. `authkeys-read` of a candidate that does not exist answers exit 3
  `NOT_FOUND`; of anything that is not a candidate exit 2 `PATH_NOT_ALLOWED`; of an argument outside the vocabulary exit 2
  `INVALID_ARGUMENT`.

```go
//go:build linux

// globalSSHD is canned "sshd -T" output.

passwordauthentication no
authorizedkeysfile .ssh/authorized_keys .ssh/authorized_keys2
authorizedkeyscommand none
hostkey /etc/ssh/ssh_host_ed25519_key
hostkey /etc/ssh/ssh_host_rsa_key
`

const deployCtx = "user=deploy,host=localhost,addr=127.0.0.1"

// testUID is the uid the fixture gives "deploy": the test's own uid when it is a normal user,
// else 1000 (files created by a root test run are then root-owned, which StrictModes accepts too).
func testUID() int {
	if u := os.Getuid(); u >= 1000 {
		return u
	}
	return 1000
}

// skipOddUID skips ownership assertions when the tests run as a system user (1..999): the files
// they create are then owned by neither "deploy" nor root.
func skipOddUID(t *testing.T) {
	if u := os.Getuid(); u != 0 && u < 1000 {
		t.Skip("ownership checks need a test uid of 0 or >= 1000")
	}
}

type fixture struct {

func newFixture(t *testing.T) *fixture {

		{"/var/lib/alice-svc", 0o755}, {"/var/lib/alice-svc/.ssh", 0o700},
	} {

daemon:x:1:1:daemon:/usr/sbin:/usr/sbin/nologin
alice-svc:x:998:998:Alice:/var/lib/alice-svc:/bin/bash
deploy:x:%d:%d:Deploy:/home/deploy:/bin/bash
nologin:x:1002:1002::/home/nologin:/usr/sbin/nologin
nobody:x:65534:65534:nobody:/nonexistent:/bin/false
ghost:x:1003:1003::/home/ghost:/bin/bash
Bad Name:x:1004:1004::/home/deploy:/bin/bash
broken line
`, f.uid, f.uid), 0o644)

func (f *fixture) runSSHD(_ context.Context, args ...string) ([]byte, error) {

	if len(args) == 3 && args[0] == "-T" && args[1] == "-C" {

func (f *fixture) loggedLines() []string {

// run runs the helper and checks the output contract: exactly one line of valid JSON.
func (f *fixture) run(args ...string) (int, map[string]any) {
	f.t.Helper()
	f.out.Reset()
	code := run(args, f.s)

	require.Equal(f.t, 1, strings.Count(line, "\n"), "exactly one line: %q", line)
	var m map[string]any
	require.NoError(f.t, json.Unmarshal([]byte(line), &m), line)
	return code, m
}

func hexOf(s string) string {
	h := sha256.Sum256([]byte(s))
	return hex.EncodeToString(h[:])
}

// listUser returns the "users" entry of an authkeys-list answer for name.
func listUser(t *testing.T, m map[string]any, name string) map[string]any {
	t.Helper()
	for _, u := range m["users"].([]any) {
		if u.(map[string]any)["user"] == name {
			return u.(map[string]any)
		}
	}
	t.Fatalf("user %s not listed", name)
	return nil
}

func filesOf(u map[string]any) []map[string]any {
	var out []map[string]any
	for _, f := range u["files"].([]any) {
		out = append(out, f.(map[string]any))
	}
	return out
}

// A-13: a symlink that leaves the home directory is never a candidate, never listed, never read.
func TestEscapingSymlinkIsNotACandidate(t *testing.T) {
	f := newFixture(t)
	f.write("/etc/shadow", "root:SECRET-HASH:19000::::::\n", 0o600)
	require.NoError(t, os.Symlink("../../../etc/shadow", f.host("/home/deploy/.ssh/authorized_keys2")))

	_, m := f.run("authkeys-list")
	assert.Equal(t, []any{helperproto.WarnUnsupportedPath}, m["warnings"])
	for _, fi := range filesOf(listUser(t, m, "deploy")) {
		assert.NotEqual(t, "/home/deploy/.ssh/authorized_keys2", fi["path"])
	}

	for _, p := range []string{"/home/deploy/.ssh/authorized_keys2", "/etc/shadow", "/root/.ssh/../../etc/shadow"} {
		code, m := f.run("authkeys-read", p)
		assert.Equal(t, helperproto.ExitRefused, code, p)
		assert.Contains(t, []any{helperproto.CodePathNotAllowed, helperproto.CodeInvalidArgument}, m["code"], p)
		assert.NotContains(t, f.out.String(), "SECRET-HASH")
	}
}

	assert.Equal(t, helperproto.ExitRefused, code)

// A-12: an argument outside the vocabulary is refused before anything is read, run or logged.
func TestArgumentsOutsideTheVocabularyAreRefused(t *testing.T) {
	f := newFixture(t)
	for _, bad := range []string{
		"/home/deploy/.ssh/authorized_keys; cat /etc/shadow",
		"/home/deploy/.ssh/authorized_keys`id`",
		"/home/deploy/.ssh/$(id)",
		"/home/deploy/.ssh/authorized_keys\n/etc/shadow",
		"/home/kullanıcı/.ssh/authorized_keys",
		"/home/deploy/.ssh/../../../etc/shadow",
		"/home/deploy/.ssh//authorized_keys",
		"home/deploy/.ssh/authorized_keys",
		"-rf",
		"",
		strconv.Quote("/home/deploy/.ssh/authorized_keys"),
	} {
		code, m := f.run("authkeys-read", bad)
		assert.Equal(t, helperproto.ExitRefused, code, "%q", bad)
		assert.Equal(t, helperproto.CodeInvalidArgument, m["code"], "%q", bad)
	}
	assert.Zero(t, f.sshdCalls.Load(), "nothing ran")
	assert.Empty(t, f.loggedLines(), "nothing was logged with a hostile path")
}
```

```go
//go:build linux

package main

import (
	"debug/elf"
	"os"
	"os/exec"
	"path/filepath"
	"strings"
	"testing"

	"github.com/stretchr/testify/assert"
	"github.com/stretchr/testify/require"
)

// TestHelperIsStatic builds the helper the way `make helper` does and proves it is a static binary
// (no program interpreter, no shared libraries) that links only the allowed modules (R21).
func TestHelperIsStatic(t *testing.T) {
	if testing.Short() {
		t.Skip("builds the helper binary")
	}
	goBin, err := exec.LookPath("go")
	if err != nil {
		t.Skip("the go command is not on PATH")
	}
	out := filepath.Join(t.TempDir(), "alice-helper")
	build := exec.Command(goBin, "build", "-trimpath", "-ldflags", "-s -w", "-o", out, ".")
	build.Env = append(os.Environ(), "CGO_ENABLED=0", "GOOS=linux")
	msg, err := build.CombinedOutput()
	require.NoError(t, err, string(msg))

	f, err := elf.Open(out)
	require.NoError(t, err)
	defer func() { _ = f.Close() }()
	for _, p := range f.Progs {
		assert.NotEqual(t, elf.PT_INTERP, p.Type, "a static binary has no program interpreter")
	}
	libs, err := f.ImportedLibraries()
	require.NoError(t, err)
	assert.Empty(t, libs, "a static binary needs no shared library")

	mods, err := exec.Command(goBin, "version", "-m", out).CombinedOutput()
	require.NoError(t, err, string(mods))
	assert.Contains(t, string(mods), "\tmod\talice")
	deps := 0
	for _, line := range strings.Split(string(mods), "\n") {
		fields := strings.Fields(line)
		if len(fields) >= 2 && fields[0] == "dep" {
			deps++
			assert.Contains(t, []string{"golang.org/x/crypto", "golang.org/x/sys"}, fields[1], "unexpected module in alice-helper")
		}
	}
	assert.Positive(t, deps, "the build info lists golang.org/x/crypto")
}
```

```go
//go:build linux

// Command alice-helper is the root-owned static helper Alice runs on managed Linux servers through
// sudo (spec §6.6, §12.2, §12.3, §13.1, R13, R21). It is the enforcement point of Alice's remote
// command surface: every argument is hostile, authorized_keys paths are computed by the helper
// itself from /etc/passwd and sshd -T, and every answer is exactly one JSON line on stdout.
package main

import (
	"context"
	"io"
	"log/syslog"
	"os"
	"os/exec"
	"syscall"
	"time"

	"alice/internal/providers/linuxssh/helperproto"
)

func main() {
	syscall.Umask(0o077)
	os.Exit(run(os.Args[1:], productionSys()))
}

// productionSys is the real environment: the whole filesystem, the real user IDs and sshd.
func productionSys() *sys {
	return &sys{
		euid:     os.Geteuid,
		sudoUser: func() string { return os.Getenv("SUDO_USER") },
		now:      time.Now, //nolint:forbidigo // the helper is a separate binary; its clock is injected through sys.now
		runSSHD:  runSSHD,
		stdin:    os.Stdin,
		stdout:   os.Stdout,
		syslog:   writeSyslog,
	}
}

// sshdPath is the OpenSSH server binary on every supported distribution (spec §12.1).
const sshdPath = "/usr/sbin/sshd"

// runSSHD runs sshd with a clean environment; stdout is capped at sshdOutputLimit, stderr dropped.
func runSSHD(ctx context.Context, args ...string) ([]byte, error) {
	cmd := exec.CommandContext(ctx, sshdPath, args...) //nolint:gosec // G204: fixed binary; arguments are fixed flags and validated user names
	cmd.Env = []string{"PATH=/usr/sbin:/usr/bin:/sbin:/bin", "LANG=C"}
	out := &capWriter{max: sshdOutputLimit}
	cmd.Stdout = out
	cmd.Stderr = io.Discard
	if err := cmd.Run(); err != nil {
		return nil, err
	}
	if out.over {
		return nil, errTooLarge
	}
	return out.buf, nil
}

// capWriter keeps at most max bytes and notes that more arrived.
type capWriter struct {
	max  int
	buf  []byte
	over bool
}

func (w *capWriter) Write(p []byte) (int, error) {
	if len(w.buf)+len(p) > w.max {
		w.over = true
		return len(p), nil
	}
	w.buf = append(w.buf, p...)
	return len(p), nil
}

// writeSyslog records the call in the authpriv log (spec §12.3): the calling user, the subcommand
// and the normalized path, never contents. Failures are ignored (the answer to Alice still counts).
func writeSyslog(subcommand, path string) {
	w, err := syslog.New(syslog.LOG_AUTHPRIV|syslog.LOG_INFO, "alice-helper")
	if err != nil {
		return
	}
	defer func() { _ = w.Close() }()
	user := os.Getenv("SUDO_USER")
	if !helperproto.ValidUser(user) {
		user = "unknown"
	}
	_ = w.Info("user=" + user + " subcommand=" + subcommand + " path=" + path)
}
```

Create `cmd/alice-helper/sys.go`:

```go
//go:build linux

package main

import (
	"context"
	"io"
	"path/filepath"
	"strings"
	"time"

	"alice/internal/providers/linuxssh/helperproto"
)

// sys is everything the helper touches outside its own memory. Paths inside the helper are
// "guest" paths (as on the server); host turns them into real paths under root, so tests can run
// every subcommand against a temporary directory as an unprivileged user.
type sys struct {
	root     string // filesystem prefix: "" in production, a temporary directory in tests
	euid     func() int
	sudoUser func() string
	now      func() time.Time
	runSSHD  func(ctx context.Context, args ...string) ([]byte, error)
	stdin    io.Reader
	stdout   io.Writer
	syslog   func(subcommand, path string)
}

// host returns the real path of an absolute guest path.
func (s *sys) host(guest string) string { return filepath.Join(s.root, guest) }

// guest returns the guest path of a real path, or false when it lies outside root.
func (s *sys) guest(host string) (string, bool) {
	if s.root == "" {
		return host, true
	}
	if host == s.root {
		return "/", true
	}
	rel, ok := strings.CutPrefix(host, s.root)
	if !ok || !strings.HasPrefix(rel, "/") {
		return "", false
	}
	return rel, true
}

// sudoUserName is the account that called the helper through sudo, when it is a valid user name.
func (s *sys) sudoUserName() string {
	if u := s.sudoUser(); helperproto.ValidUser(u) {
		return u
	}
	return ""
}
```

Create `cmd/alice-helper/run.go`:

```go
//go:build linux

package main

import (
	"context"
	"encoding/json"
	"errors"
	"io"
	"time"

	"alice/internal/providers/linuxssh/helperproto"
)

// helperError is a refusal or failure with its exit code (spec §12.3) and an internal code.
// Messages are fixed texts: never a path from the caller, never file contents, never OS errors.
type helperError struct {
	exit    int
	code    string
	message string
}

func (e *helperError) Error() string { return e.code + ": " + e.message }

func refused(code, msg string) error {
	return &helperError{exit: helperproto.ExitRefused, code: code, message: msg}
}

func precondition(code, msg string) error {
	return &helperError{exit: helperproto.ExitPrecondition, code: code, message: msg}
}

func failed(code, msg string) error {
	return &helperError{exit: helperproto.ExitFailed, code: code, message: msg}
}

// command is one subcommand. Privileged ones need euid 0 (sudo).
type command struct {
	privileged bool
	handle     func(ctx context.Context, s *sys, args []string) (any, error)
}

var commands = map[string]command{
	helperproto.SubVersion:      {handle: cmdVersion},
	helperproto.SubSSHDDump:     {privileged: true, handle: cmdSSHDDump},
	helperproto.SubHostKeys:     {privileged: true, handle: cmdHostKeys},
	helperproto.SubAuthKeysList: {privileged: true, handle: cmdAuthKeysList},
	helperproto.SubAuthKeysRead: {privileged: true, handle: cmdAuthKeysRead},
}

// commandBudget bounds one call; Alice gives up after 30–60 s (R37 item 17).
const commandBudget = 55 * time.Second

// run executes one call and returns the exit code. It prints exactly one JSON line.
func run(args []string, s *sys) int {
	if len(args) == 0 {
		return reply(s, nil, refused(helperproto.CodeUsage, "usage: alice-helper <subcommand> [arguments]"))
	}
	c, ok := commands[args[0]]
	if !ok {
		return reply(s, nil, refused(helperproto.CodeUnknownSubcommand, "unknown subcommand"))
	}
	if c.privileged && s.euid() != 0 {
		return reply(s, nil, refused(helperproto.CodeNotRoot, "this subcommand must run as root through sudo"))
	}
	ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(context.Background(), commandBudget)
	defer cancel()
	out, err := c.handle(ctx, s, args[1:])
	return reply(s, out, err)
}

// reply prints the answer or the error and returns the exit code.
func reply(s *sys, out any, err error) int {
	if err != nil {
		var he *helperError
		if !errors.As(err, &he) {
			he = &helperError{exit: helperproto.ExitFailed, code: helperproto.CodeIOError, message: "the operation failed"}
		}
		writeJSON(s.stdout, helperproto.ErrorResponse{OK: false, Code: he.code, Message: he.message})
		return he.exit
	}
	writeJSON(s.stdout, out)
	return helperproto.ExitOK
}

func writeJSON(w io.Writer, v any) {
	b, err := json.Marshal(v)
	if err != nil {
		b = []byte(`{"ok":false,"code":"IO_ERROR","message":"the answer could not be encoded"}`)
	}
	_, _ = w.Write(append(b, '\n'))
}

func cmdVersion(_ context.Context, _ *sys, args []string) (any, error) {
	if len(args) != 0 {
		return nil, refused(helperproto.CodeUsage, "version takes no arguments")
	}
	return helperproto.VersionResponse{OK: true, Helper: helperproto.Version, Protocol: helperproto.Protocol}, nil
}
```

```go
//go:build linux

package main

import (
	"crypto/sha256"
	"encoding/hex"
	"errors"
	"io"
	"io/fs"
	"os"
	"path/filepath"
	"syscall"
)

var (
	errTooLarge   = errors.New("file too large")
	errNotRegular = errors.New("not a regular file")
)

// readRegular reads a regular file of at most limit bytes. It never follows a symlink in the last
// path element and never blocks on a FIFO or device.
func (s *sys) readRegular(guest string, limit int) ([]byte, error) {
	f, err := os.OpenFile(s.host(guest), os.O_RDONLY|syscall.O_NOFOLLOW|syscall.O_NONBLOCK|syscall.O_CLOEXEC, 0) //nolint:gosec // G304: the path is computed and validated by the helper
	if err != nil {
		return nil, err
	}
	defer func() { _ = f.Close() }()
	st, err := f.Stat()
	if err != nil {
		return nil, err
	}
	if !st.Mode().IsRegular() {
		return nil, errNotRegular
	}
	data, err := io.ReadAll(io.LimitReader(f, int64(limit)+1))
	if err != nil {
		return nil, err
	}
	if len(data) > limit {
		return nil, errTooLarge
	}
	return data, nil
}

// resolveNearest resolves every symlink of an absolute guest path. Missing trailing elements are
// kept as they are (a file or a .ssh directory that does not exist yet). It reports false when the
// path resolves outside the filesystem root or cannot be resolved.
func (s *sys) resolveNearest(guest string) (string, bool) {
	cur := filepath.Clean(guest)
	var rest []string
	for {
		real, err := filepath.EvalSymlinks(s.host(cur))
		if err == nil {
			g, ok := s.guest(real)
			if !ok {
				return "", false
			}
			parts := []string{g}
			for i := len(rest) - 1; i >= 0; i-- {
				parts = append(parts, rest[i])
			}
			return filepath.Join(parts...), true
		}
		if !errors.Is(err, fs.ErrNotExist) || cur == "/" {
			return "", false
		}
		rest = append(rest, filepath.Base(cur))
		cur = filepath.Dir(cur)
	}
}

// within reports whether p is dir or lies below it.
func within(p, dir string) bool {
	return dir == "/" || p == dir || len(p) > len(dir) && p[:len(dir)] == dir && p[len(dir)] == '/'
}

// owner returns the uid and gid of a stat result.
func owner(st fs.FileInfo) (int, int) {
	if stat, ok := st.Sys().(*syscall.Stat_t); ok {
		return int(stat.Uid), int(stat.Gid)
	}
	return -1, -1
}

func hexSHA(b []byte) string {
	h := sha256.Sum256(b)
	return hex.EncodeToString(h[:])
}
```

Create `cmd/alice-helper/accounts.go`:

```go
//go:build linux

package main

import (
	"os"
	"sort"
	"strconv"
	"strings"

	"alice/internal/providers/linuxssh/helperproto"
)

// account is one /etc/passwd entry.
type account struct {
	name       string
	uid, gid   int
	home, shell string
}

const (
	passwdLimit   = 4 << 20
	nsswitchLimit = 64 << 10
	maxUsers      = 200 // spec §13.2
	nobodyUID     = 65534
)

// accounts reads /etc/passwd directly: the static helper has no NSS (R37 item 4). Malformed lines
// are skipped.
func (s *sys) accounts() ([]account, error) {
	data, err := s.readRegular("/etc/passwd", passwdLimit)
	if err != nil {
		return nil, err
	}
	var out []account
	for _, line := range strings.Split(string(data), "\n") {
		f := strings.Split(line, ":")
		if len(f) != 7 {
			continue
		}
		uid, err1 := strconv.Atoi(f[2])
		gid, err2 := strconv.Atoi(f[3])
		if err1 != nil || err2 != nil || uid < 0 || gid < 0 {
			continue
		}
		out = append(out, account{name: f[0], uid: uid, gid: gid, home: f[5], shell: f[6]})
	}
	return out, nil
}

// toScan selects the accounts whose keys are inventoried (spec §13.1): root, every normal account
// (uid >= 1000, not nobody) with an existing home and a login shell, and the account that runs the
// helper through sudo (alice-svc, a system account) so Alice's own key appears in the inventory.
func (s *sys) toScan(accts []account) []account {
	sudo := s.sudoUserName()
	seen := map[string]bool{}
	var out []account
	for _, a := range accts {
		if seen[a.name] || !helperproto.ValidUser(a.name) || !helperproto.ValidPath(a.home) {
			continue
		}
		ok := (a.name == "root" && a.uid == 0) || (sudo != "" && a.name == sudo) ||
			(a.uid >= 1000 && a.uid != nobodyUID && loginShell(a.shell) && s.isDir(a.home))
		if !ok {
			continue
		}
		seen[a.name] = true
		out = append(out, a)
	}
	sort.SliceStable(out, func(i, j int) bool {
		if out[i].uid != out[j].uid {
			return out[i].uid < out[j].uid
		}
		return out[i].name < out[j].name
	})
	if len(out) > maxUsers {
		out = out[:maxUsers]
	}
	return out
}

func loginShell(shell string) bool {
	return shell != "" && !strings.HasSuffix(shell, "/nologin") && !strings.HasSuffix(shell, "/false")
}

func (s *sys) isDir(guest string) bool {
	st, err := os.Stat(s.host(guest))
	return err == nil && st.IsDir()
}

// directoryUsers reports whether accounts may come from a directory service the helper cannot list.
func (s *sys) directoryUsers() bool {
	data, err := s.readRegular("/etc/nsswitch.conf", nsswitchLimit)
	if err != nil {
		return false
	}
	for _, line := range strings.Split(string(data), "\n") {
		rest, ok := strings.CutPrefix(strings.TrimSpace(line), "passwd:")
		if !ok {
			continue
		}
		for _, src := range strings.Fields(rest) {
			if src == "ldap" || src == "sss" {
				return true
			}
		}
	}
	return false
}

// owners maps uids to account names (the first entry wins).
func owners(accts []account) map[int]string {
	m := map[int]string{}
	for _, a := range accts {
		if _, ok := m[a.uid]; !ok {
			m[a.uid] = a.name
		}
	}
	return m
}
```

Create `cmd/alice-helper/sshd.go`:

```go
//go:build linux

package main

import (
	"context"
	"crypto/ecdsa"
	"crypto/ed25519"
	"crypto/rsa"

	"golang.org/x/crypto/ssh"

	"alice/internal/providers/linuxssh/helperproto"
	"alice/internal/providers/linuxssh/sshdconf"
)

// sshdOutputLimit caps sshd -T output (it is a few KiB in practice).
const sshdOutputLimit = sshdconf.MaxConfigSize

// sshdConfig runs "sshd -T" (plus extra arguments) and parses the output.
func (s *sys) sshdConfig(ctx context.Context, extra ...string) (sshdconf.Config, []byte, error) {
	out, err := s.runSSHD(ctx, append([]string{"-T"}, extra...)...)
	if err != nil {
		return sshdconf.Config{}, nil, err
	}
	if len(out) > sshdOutputLimit {
		return sshdconf.Config{}, nil, errTooLarge
	}
	cfg, err := sshdconf.Parse(out)
	if err != nil {
		return sshdconf.Config{}, nil, err
	}
	return cfg, out, nil
}

func cmdSSHDDump(ctx context.Context, s *sys, args []string) (any, error) {
	if len(args) != 0 {
		return nil, refused(helperproto.CodeUsage, "sshd-dump takes no arguments")
	}
	s.syslog(helperproto.SubSSHDDump, "")
	_, out, err := s.sshdConfig(ctx)
	if err != nil {
		return helperproto.SSHDDumpResponse{OK: true, Fallback: true}, nil
	}
	return helperproto.SSHDDumpResponse{OK: true, Config: string(out)}, nil
}

// defaultHostKeys are OpenSSH's default HostKey files.
var defaultHostKeys = []string{"/etc/ssh/ssh_host_ed25519_key", "/etc/ssh/ssh_host_ecdsa_key", "/etc/ssh/ssh_host_rsa_key"}

const maxPublicKeySize = 64 << 10

// cmdHostKeys lists the server's host public keys with their fingerprints. The helper computes
// the fingerprints itself (R37 item 4); a .pub file that is a symlink, too large or unparseable
// is skipped.
func cmdHostKeys(ctx context.Context, s *sys, args []string) (any, error) {
	if len(args) != 0 {
		return nil, refused(helperproto.CodeUsage, "hostkeys takes no arguments")
	}
	s.syslog(helperproto.SubHostKeys, "")
	paths := defaultHostKeys
	if cfg, _, err := s.sshdConfig(ctx); err == nil && len(cfg.HostKeys) > 0 {
		paths = cfg.HostKeys
	}
	keys := []helperproto.HostKeyInfo{}
	for _, p := range paths {
		pub := p + ".pub"
		if !helperproto.ValidPath(pub) {
			continue
		}
		data, err := s.readRegular(pub, maxPublicKeySize)
		if err != nil {
			continue
		}
		k, _, _, _, err := ssh.ParseAuthorizedKey(data)
		if err != nil {
			continue
		}
		keys = append(keys, helperproto.HostKeyInfo{Type: k.Type(), Bits: keyBits(k), Fingerprint: ssh.FingerprintSHA256(k), Path: pub})
	}
	return helperproto.HostKeysResponse{OK: true, Keys: keys}, nil
}

// keyBits is the RSA modulus size, the ECDSA curve size, or 256 for Ed25519.
func keyBits(k ssh.PublicKey) int {
	ck, ok := k.(ssh.CryptoPublicKey)
	if !ok {
		return 0
	}
	switch p := ck.CryptoPublicKey().(type) {
	case *rsa.PublicKey:
		return p.N.BitLen()
	case *ecdsa.PublicKey:
		return p.Curve.Params().BitSize
	case ed25519.PublicKey:
		return 256
	default:
		return 0
	}
}
```

Create `cmd/alice-helper/authkeys.go`:

```go
//go:build linux

package main

import (
	"context"
	"encoding/base64"
	"errors"
	"fmt"
	"io/fs"
	"os"
	"path/filepath"
	"slices"
	"strconv"
	"strings"
	"syscall"

	"alice/internal/providers/linuxssh/helperproto"
	"alice/internal/providers/linuxssh/sshdconf"
)

// candidate is one authorized_keys file the helper may read or write (spec §13.3 step 2).
type candidate struct {
	acct account
	path string // the expanded path, as listed to Alice and as Alice names it
	real string // the path after resolving symlinks (missing trailing elements kept)
	dir  string // the resolved directory real must stay in: the home, or the directory of an absolute pattern
}

type userScan struct {
	acct  account
	cands []candidate
}

type scanResult struct {
	users    []userScan
	warnings []string
	command  string
	owners   map[int]string
}

func (r *scanResult) warn(code string) {
	if !slices.Contains(r.warnings, code) {
		r.warnings = append(r.warnings, code)
	}
}

// find returns the candidate whose listed path is exactly path.
func (r scanResult) find(path string) (candidate, bool) {
	for _, u := range r.users {
		for _, c := range u.cands {
			if c.path == path {
				return c, true
			}
		}
	}
	return candidate{}, false
}

// scan computes every candidate file from /etc/passwd and sshd -T. It is the only source of
// paths for authkeys-read and authkeys-write: a path from the caller is only ever compared to it.
func (s *sys) scan(ctx context.Context) (scanResult, error) {
	accts, err := s.accounts()
	if err != nil {
		return scanResult{}, failed(helperproto.CodeIOError, "cannot read /etc/passwd")
	}
	r := scanResult{warnings: []string{}, owners: owners(accts)}
	global, _, gerr := s.sshdConfig(ctx)
	if gerr != nil {
		global = sshdconf.Config{AuthorizedKeysFile: sshdconf.DefaultAuthorizedKeysFile, AuthorizedKeysCommand: "none"}
		r.warn(helperproto.WarnSSHDUnreadable)
	}
	r.command = global.AuthorizedKeysCommand
	if s.directoryUsers() {
		r.warn(helperproto.WarnDirectoryUsers)
	}
	for _, a := range s.toScan(accts) {
		files := global.AuthorizedKeysFile
		if gerr == nil {
			if cfg, _, err := s.sshdConfig(ctx, "-C", "user="+a.name+",host=localhost,addr=127.0.0.1"); err == nil {
				files = cfg.AuthorizedKeysFile
			}
		}
		us := userScan{acct: a}
		for _, pattern := range files {
			c, ok := s.candidateFor(a, pattern)
			if !ok {
				r.warn(helperproto.WarnUnsupportedPath)
				continue
			}
			if !slices.ContainsFunc(us.cands, func(x candidate) bool { return x.path == c.path }) {
				us.cands = append(us.cands, c)
			}
		}
		r.users = append(r.users, us)
	}
	return r, nil
}

// candidateFor expands one AuthorizedKeysFile pattern for a. The result must be a valid helper
// path, and after resolving symlinks it must stay inside the user's home, or inside the directory
// of an absolute pattern (/etc/ssh/keys/%u stays in /etc/ssh/keys).
func (s *sys) candidateFor(a account, pattern string) (candidate, bool) {
	p, err := sshdconf.Expand(pattern, a.name, a.home, a.uid)
	if err != nil || !helperproto.ValidPath(p) {
		return candidate{}, false
	}
	allowed := a.home
	if strings.HasPrefix(pattern, "/") {
		allowed = filepath.Dir(p)
	}
	dir, ok := s.resolveNearest(allowed)
	if !ok {
		return candidate{}, false
	}
	real, ok := s.resolveNearest(p)
	if !ok || !within(real, dir) {
		return candidate{}, false
	}
	return candidate{acct: a, path: p, real: real, dir: dir}, true
}

func cmdAuthKeysList(ctx context.Context, s *sys, args []string) (any, error) {
	if len(args) != 0 {
		return nil, refused(helperproto.CodeUsage, "authkeys-list takes no arguments")
	}
	s.syslog(helperproto.SubAuthKeysList, "")
	r, err := s.scan(ctx)
	if err != nil {
		return nil, err
	}
	resp := helperproto.AuthKeysListResponse{OK: true, Users: []helperproto.UserFiles{}, AuthorizedKeysCommand: r.command, Warnings: r.warnings}
	for _, u := range r.users {
		uf := helperproto.UserFiles{User: u.acct.name, UID: u.acct.uid, Home: u.acct.home, Files: []helperproto.FileInfo{}}
		for _, c := range u.cands {
			uf.Files = append(uf.Files, s.fileInfo(c, r.owners))
		}
		resp.Users = append(resp.Users, uf)
	}
	return resp, nil
}

// fileInfo describes a candidate without returning its content.
func (s *sys) fileInfo(c candidate, names map[int]string) helperproto.FileInfo {
	fi := helperproto.FileInfo{Path: c.path}
	st, err := os.Lstat(s.host(c.real))
	if err != nil {
		fi.StrictModesOK = s.strictModes(c, nil)
		return fi
	}
	fi.Exists, fi.Size, fi.Mode = true, st.Size(), fmt.Sprintf("%04o", st.Mode().Perm())
	uid, _ := owner(st)
	fi.Owner = names[uid]
	if fi.Owner == "" {
		fi.Owner = strconv.Itoa(uid)
	}
	if !st.Mode().IsRegular() {
		return fi
	}
	if st.Size() > helperproto.MaxAuthorizedKeysSize {
		fi.TooLarge = true
	} else if data, err := s.readRegular(c.real, helperproto.MaxAuthorizedKeysSize); err == nil {
		fi.SHA256 = hexSHA(data)
	}
	fi.StrictModesOK = s.strictModes(c, st)
	return fi
}

// strictModes mirrors sshd's StrictModes: the file and every existing directory from it up to
// the allowed directory are owned by the user or root and not writable by group or others.
func (s *sys) strictModes(c candidate, file fs.FileInfo) bool {
	ok := func(st fs.FileInfo) bool {
		uid, _ := owner(st)
		return st.Mode().Perm()&0o022 == 0 && (uid == c.acct.uid || uid == 0)
	}
	if file != nil && !ok(file) {
		return false
	}
	for d := filepath.Dir(c.real); within(d, c.dir); d = filepath.Dir(d) {
		if st, err := os.Stat(s.host(d)); err == nil && !ok(st) {
			return false
		}
		if d == c.dir || d == "/" {
			break
		}
	}
	return true
}

func cmdAuthKeysRead(ctx context.Context, s *sys, args []string) (any, error) {
	if len(args) != 1 {
		return nil, refused(helperproto.CodeUsage, "usage: authkeys-read <path>")
	}
	path := args[0]
	if !helperproto.ValidPath(path) {
		return nil, refused(helperproto.CodeInvalidArgument, "the path is not allowed")
	}
	s.syslog(helperproto.SubAuthKeysRead, path)
	r, err := s.scan(ctx)
	if err != nil {
		return nil, err
	}
	c, ok := r.find(path)
	if !ok {
		return nil, refused(helperproto.CodePathNotAllowed, "the path is not an authorized_keys file of a listed user")
	}
	data, err := s.readRegular(c.real, helperproto.MaxAuthorizedKeysSize)
	switch {
	case errors.Is(err, fs.ErrNotExist):
		return nil, precondition(helperproto.CodeNotFound, "the file does not exist")
	case errors.Is(err, errTooLarge):
		return nil, refused(helperproto.CodeTooLarge, "the file is too large")
	case errors.Is(err, errNotRegular), errors.Is(err, syscall.ELOOP):
		return nil, refused(helperproto.CodeNotRegularFile, "the path is not a regular file")
	case err != nil:
		return nil, failed(helperproto.CodeIOError, "the file cannot be read")
	}
	return helperproto.AuthKeysReadResponse{OK: true, Path: path, SHA256: hexSHA(data), ContentB64: base64.StdEncoding.EncodeToString(data)}, nil
}
```

A directory at a candidate path opens with
`O_NONBLOCK` and fails the regular-file check (`errNotRegular`); a symlink in the last element fails with `ELOOP`
because `readRegular` uses `O_NOFOLLOW` (both answer `NOT_REGULAR_FILE`); a symlink that `scan` accepted is read
through its resolved path `c.real`, so it never reaches `O_NOFOLLOW`.

### Task 7: `alice-helper` part 2 — `authkeys-write` (lock, compare-and-swap, backup, atomic replace) and `cleanup`

`authkeys-write` is the only subcommand that changes a managed server in Phase 3 (spec §13.1, §13.4 step 4). Alice
sends the full new file content on stdin together with the SHA-256 of the content it read; the helper takes an
exclusive `flock` on the file's directory, re-reads the file, refuses with exit 3 `HASH_MISMATCH` when someone changed
it meanwhile (F-38, Alice re-reads and retries), backs up the old content into a root-only directory named after the
operation, stages the new content in a temporary file in the same directory (`O_EXCL`, mode 0600), copies the
original owner, mode and SELinux label, `fsync`s, renames it over the real file and `fsync`s the directory. Any
failure before the rename removes the staging file and leaves the original untouched, so the file is always either the
old or the new version (Review Focus item 3). `cleanup --op` removes one operation's backups; every privileged call also
removes backup directories older than 30 days (§12.3). The target path must be one of the candidates computed by
`scan` (Task 6) — never a caller-supplied arbitrary path — and the file must be a regular file with one hard link.

**Files:**
- Create: `cmd/alice-helper/write.go`, `cmd/alice-helper/cleanup.go`
- Modify: `cmd/alice-helper/sys.go` (fields `chown`, `beforeRename`), `cmd/alice-helper/main.go` (production `chown`),
  `cmd/alice-helper/run.go` (dispatch entries, backup sweep)
- Test: `cmd/alice-helper/write_test.go`

**Interfaces:**
- Consumes (Task 6): `sys` (`host`, `readRegular`, `scan`, `resolveNearest`), `scanResult.find`, `candidate`
  (`acct`, `path`, `real`, `dir`), `account` (`uid`, `gid`), `refused`, `precondition`, `failed`, `errTooLarge`,
  `hexSHA`, `owner`, `commands`, `run`; test helpers `newFixture`, `(*fixture).run`, `write`, `mkdir`, `read`,
  `host`, `loggedLines`, `testNow`, `hexOf`. Task 5: `helperproto.SubAuthKeysWrite`, `SubCleanup`, `BackupRoot`,
  `AbsentSHA256`, `MaxAuthorizedKeysSize`, `ValidPath`, `ValidSHA256`, `ValidOpID`, `AuthKeysWriteResponse`,
  `CleanupResponse`, the `Code*` constants.
- Produces (wire behaviour Tasks 9, 10 and 19 rely on): `authkeys-write <path> --expect-sha256 <sha256|absent> --op <uuid>`
  with the new content on stdin (≤ 1 MiB) answers `{"ok":true,"sha256":"<new>","backup":"/var/lib/alice-helper/backups/<op>/<n>.bak"}`;
  a stale hash answers exit 3 `HASH_MISMATCH` and changes nothing; a missing `<home>/.ssh` directory is created
  (0700, owned by the user) only for a candidate under the user's home; a new file gets mode 0600 and the user's
  uid/gid, an existing file keeps its mode, uid and gid. Backups: `<n>.bak` (old content, empty when absent) and
  `<n>.json` (`{"path","absent","mode","uid","gid","sha256"}`), both 0600 in a 0700 directory. `cleanup --op <uuid>`
  answers `{"ok":true,"removed":1|0}`.

```go
	op1      = "0190f5a0-0000-7000-8000-0000000000a1"
	op2      = "0190f5a0-0000-7000-8000-0000000000a2"

type chownCall struct {

	uid, gid int
}

// newWriteFixture is newFixture with a chown that records instead of changing owners (the tests
// do not run as root).
func newWriteFixture(t *testing.T) (*fixture, func() []chownCall) {
	t.Helper()
	f := newFixture(t)
	var mu sync.Mutex
	var calls []chownCall
	f.s.chown = func(file *os.File, uid, gid int) error {
		mu.Lock()
		defer mu.Unlock()
		calls = append(calls, chownCall{name: filepath.Base(file.Name()), uid: uid, gid: gid})

	}
	return f, func() []chownCall {

func (f *fixture) runWith(stdin string, args ...string) (int, map[string]any) {

	f.s.stdin = strings.NewReader(stdin)
	return f.run(args...)
}

func writeArgs(path, expect, op string) []string {
	return []string{"authkeys-write", path, "--expect-sha256", expect, "--op", op}
}

// sshDirEntries lists the names in the deploy .ssh directory (no staging file may remain).
func (f *fixture) sshDirEntries() []string {
	f.t.Helper()
	entries, err := os.ReadDir(f.host("/home/deploy/.ssh"))
	require.NoError(f.t, err)
	var names []string
	for _, e := range entries {
		names = append(names, e.Name())
	}
	return names
}

func TestWriteReplacesWithCompareAndSwap(t *testing.T) {
	f, chowns := newWriteFixture(t)
	f.write(keysPath, "old\n", 0o640)
	st, err := os.Stat(f.host(keysPath))
	require.NoError(t, err)
	uid, gid := owner(st)

	code, m := f.runWith("new\n", writeArgs(keysPath, hexOf("old\n"), op1)...)
	require.Equal(t, 0, code, "%v", m)
	assert.Equal(t, map[string]any{"ok": true, "sha256": hexOf("new\n"),
		"backup": "/var/lib/alice-helper/backups/" + op1 + "/1.bak"}, m)
	assert.Equal(t, "new\n", f.read(keysPath))
	st, err = os.Stat(f.host(keysPath))
	require.NoError(t, err)
	assert.Equal(t, os.FileMode(0o640), st.Mode().Perm(), "the original mode is kept")
	require.Len(t, chowns(), 1)
	assert.Equal(t, uid, chowns()[0].uid, "the original owner is kept")
	assert.Equal(t, gid, chowns()[0].gid)
	assert.True(t, strings.HasPrefix(chowns()[0].name, ".authorized_keys.alice-"), "the staging file is chowned before the rename")
	assert.Equal(t, []string{"authorized_keys"}, f.sshDirEntries(), "no staging file remains")

	backupDir := "/var/lib/alice-helper/backups/" + op1
	assert.Equal(t, "old\n", f.read(backupDir+"/1.bak"))
	var meta map[string]any
	require.NoError(t, json.Unmarshal([]byte(f.read(backupDir+"/1.json")), &meta))
	assert.Equal(t, map[string]any{"path": keysPath, "absent": false, "mode": "0640", "uid": float64(uid), "gid": float64(gid),
		"sha256": hexOf("old\n")}, meta)
	for _, p := range []string{"/var/lib/alice-helper/backups", backupDir} {
		dst, err := os.Stat(f.host(p))
		require.NoError(t, err)
		assert.Equal(t, os.FileMode(0o700), dst.Mode().Perm(), p)
	}
	bst, err := os.Stat(f.host(backupDir + "/1.bak"))
	require.NoError(t, err)
	assert.Equal(t, os.FileMode(0o600), bst.Mode().Perm())
	assert.Contains(t, f.loggedLines(), "authkeys-write "+keysPath)

	// A second write in the same operation gets the next backup number.
	code, m = f.runWith("newer\n", writeArgs(keysPath, hexOf("new\n"), op1)...)
	require.Equal(t, 0, code)
	assert.Equal(t, "/var/lib/alice-helper/backups/"+op1+"/2.bak", m["backup"])
	assert.Equal(t, "new\n", f.read(backupDir+"/2.bak"))
}

// F-38: a file changed since Alice read it is refused and left as it is.
func TestWriteRefusesAStaleHash(t *testing.T) {
	f, _ := newWriteFixture(t)
	f.write(keysPath, "changed by someone\n", 0o600)
	code, m := f.runWith("new\n", writeArgs(keysPath, hexOf("what alice read\n"), op1)...)
	assert.Equal(t, helperproto.ExitPrecondition, code)
	assert.Equal(t, helperproto.CodeHashMismatch, m["code"])
	assert.Equal(t, "changed by someone\n", f.read(keysPath))
	_, err := os.Stat(f.host(helperproto.BackupRoot + "/" + op1))
	assert.True(t, errors.Is(err, os.ErrNotExist), "nothing is backed up for a refused write")

	code, m = f.runWith("new\n", writeArgs(keysPath, helperproto.AbsentSHA256, op1)...)
	assert.Equal(t, helperproto.ExitPrecondition, code, "absent expected but the file exists")
	assert.Equal(t, helperproto.CodeHashMismatch, m["code"])
}

func TestWriteCreatesAMissingFileAndSSHDirectory(t *testing.T) {
	f, chowns := newWriteFixture(t)
	require.NoError(t, os.RemoveAll(f.host("/home/deploy/.ssh")))
	code, m := f.runWith("ssh-ed25519 AAAA new\n", writeArgs(keysPath, helperproto.AbsentSHA256, op1)...)
	require.Equal(t, 0, code, "%v", m)

	dst, err := os.Stat(f.host("/home/deploy/.ssh"))
	require.NoError(t, err)
	assert.Equal(t, os.FileMode(0o700), dst.Mode().Perm())
	fst, err := os.Stat(f.host(keysPath))
	require.NoError(t, err)
	assert.Equal(t, os.FileMode(0o600), fst.Mode().Perm())
	calls := chowns()
	require.Len(t, calls, 2)
	assert.Equal(t, chownCall{name: ".ssh", uid: f.uid, gid: f.uid}, calls[0], "the new .ssh belongs to the user")
	assert.Equal(t, f.uid, calls[1].uid, "the new file belongs to the user")
	assert.Equal(t, f.uid, calls[1].gid)

	var meta map[string]any
	require.NoError(t, json.Unmarshal([]byte(f.read(helperproto.BackupRoot+"/"+op1+"/1.json")), &meta))
	assert.Equal(t, true, meta["absent"])
	assert.Equal(t, helperproto.AbsentSHA256, meta["sha256"])
	assert.Equal(t, "", f.read(helperproto.BackupRoot+"/"+op1+"/1.bak"))
}

func TestWriteIsAtomicWhenInterrupted(t *testing.T) {

// Two writers that read the same content: the directory lock serializes them, exactly one wins
// and the other sees the changed hash.
func TestConcurrentWritersSerialize(t *testing.T) {
	f, _ := newWriteFixture(t)
	f.write(keysPath, "base\n", 0o600)
	codes := make([]int, 2)
	var wg sync.WaitGroup
	for i, content := range []string{"first\n", "second\n"} {
		wg.Add(1)
		go func() {
			defer wg.Done()
			s := *f.s
			var out strings.Builder
			s.stdout = &out
			s.stdin = strings.NewReader(content)
			codes[i] = run(writeArgs(keysPath, hexOf("base\n"), []string{op1, op2}[i]), &s)
		}()
	}
	wg.Wait()
	assert.ElementsMatch(t, []int{0, helperproto.ExitPrecondition}, codes)
	assert.Contains(t, []string{"first\n", "second\n"}, f.read(keysPath))
}

func TestWriteRefusesBadRequests(t *testing.T) {
	f, chowns := newWriteFixture(t)
	f.write(keysPath, "old\n", 0o600)
	f.write("/etc/shadow", "root:HASH:1::::::\n", 0o600)
	good := hexOf("old\n")
	for _, tc := range []struct {
		name  string
		args  []string
		stdin string
		exit  int
		code  string
	}{
		{"not a candidate", writeArgs("/etc/shadow", hexOf("root:HASH:1::::::\n"), op1), "x", helperproto.ExitRefused, helperproto.CodePathNotAllowed},
		{"another user's home", writeArgs("/home/nologin/.ssh/authorized_keys", helperproto.AbsentSHA256, op1), "x", helperproto.ExitRefused, helperproto.CodePathNotAllowed},
		{"injection in the path", writeArgs(keysPath+";id", good, op1), "x", helperproto.ExitRefused, helperproto.CodeInvalidArgument},
		{"newline in the path", writeArgs(keysPath+"\n/etc/shadow", good, op1), "x", helperproto.ExitRefused, helperproto.CodeInvalidArgument},
		{"upper-case hash", writeArgs(keysPath, strings.Repeat("A", 64), op1), "x", helperproto.ExitRefused, helperproto.CodeInvalidArgument},
		{"traversal in the op id", writeArgs(keysPath, good, "../../../../etc/cron.d/x"), "x", helperproto.ExitRefused, helperproto.CodeInvalidArgument},
		{"flags swapped", []string{"authkeys-write", keysPath, "--op", op1, "--expect-sha256", good}, "x", helperproto.ExitRefused, helperproto.CodeUsage},
		{"missing flags", []string{"authkeys-write", keysPath}, "x", helperproto.ExitRefused, helperproto.CodeUsage},
		{"content too large", writeArgs(keysPath, good, op1), strings.Repeat("#", helperproto.MaxAuthorizedKeysSize+1), helperproto.ExitRefused, helperproto.CodeTooLarge},
	} {
		code, m := f.runWith(tc.stdin, tc.args...)
		assert.Equal(t, tc.exit, code, tc.name)
		assert.Equal(t, tc.code, m["code"], tc.name)
	}
	assert.Equal(t, "old\n", f.read(keysPath))
	assert.Equal(t, "root:HASH:1::::::\n", f.read("/etc/shadow"))
	assert.Empty(t, chowns())
	_, err := os.Stat(f.host(helperproto.BackupRoot))
	assert.True(t, errors.Is(err, os.ErrNotExist), "no refused request creates backups")
}

func TestCleanupAndBackupRetention(t *testing.T) {
	f, _ := newWriteFixture(t)
	old := "0190f5a0-0000-7000-8000-0000000000b1"
	f.mkdir(helperproto.BackupRoot+"/"+old, 0o700)
	f.mkdir(helperproto.BackupRoot+"/"+op1, 0o700)
	f.mkdir(helperproto.BackupRoot+"/"+op2, 0o700)
	f.mkdir(helperproto.BackupRoot+"/notes", 0o700)
	for p, age := range map[string]time.Duration{old: 31 * 24 * time.Hour, op1: 29 * 24 * time.Hour, op2: time.Hour, "notes": 400 * 24 * time.Hour} {
		at := testNow.Add(-age)
		require.NoError(t, os.Chtimes(f.host(helperproto.BackupRoot+"/"+p), at, at))
	}
	exists := func(name string) bool {
		_, err := os.Stat(f.host(helperproto.BackupRoot + "/" + name))
		return err == nil
	}

	code, m := f.run("version")
	require.Equal(t, 0, code, "%v", m)
	assert.True(t, exists(old), "an unprivileged call does not sweep")

	code, m = f.run("cleanup", "--op", op2)
	require.Equal(t, 0, code)
	assert.Equal(t, map[string]any{"ok": true, "removed": float64(1)}, m)
	assert.False(t, exists(op2), "cleanup removes the operation's backups")
	assert.False(t, exists(old), "every privileged call removes backups older than 30 days")
	assert.True(t, exists(op1), "29 days old: kept")
	assert.True(t, exists("notes"), "only operation directories are swept")

	code, m = f.run("cleanup", "--op", op2)
	require.Equal(t, 0, code)
	assert.Equal(t, float64(0), m["removed"])

	for _, args := range [][]string{{"cleanup"}, {"cleanup", "--op"}, {"cleanup", "--op", "../.."}, {"cleanup", "--op", "0190F5A0-0000-7000-8000-0000000000A1"}} {
		code, m = f.run(args...)
		assert.Equal(t, helperproto.ExitRefused, code, "%v", args)
		assert.Contains(t, []any{helperproto.CodeUsage, helperproto.CodeInvalidArgument}, m["code"], "%v", args)
	}
	assert.True(t, exists(op1))
}
```

- [ ] **Step 3: Write `authkeys-write` and `cleanup`**

Create `cmd/alice-helper/write.go`:

```go
//go:build linux

package main

import (
	"context"
	"crypto/rand"
	"encoding/hex"
	"encoding/json"
	"errors"
	"fmt"
	"io"
	"io/fs"
	"os"
	"path/filepath"
	"strconv"
	"strings"
	"syscall"

	"alice/internal/providers/linuxssh/helperproto"
)

// selinuxXattr is the extended attribute that holds a file's SELinux label.
const selinuxXattr = "security.selinux"

// cmdAuthKeysWrite replaces one candidate authorized_keys file with stdin, but only when its
// current content still has the hash Alice read (spec §13.4 step 4).
func cmdAuthKeysWrite(ctx context.Context, s *sys, args []string) (any, error) {
	if len(args) != 5 || args[1] != "--expect-sha256" || args[3] != "--op" {
		return nil, refused(helperproto.CodeUsage, "usage: authkeys-write <path> --expect-sha256 <sha256|absent> --op <operation id>")
	}
	path, expect, op := args[0], args[2], args[4]
	if !helperproto.ValidPath(path) || !helperproto.ValidSHA256(expect) || !helperproto.ValidOpID(op) {
		return nil, refused(helperproto.CodeInvalidArgument, "an argument is not allowed")
	}
	content, err := io.ReadAll(io.LimitReader(s.stdin, helperproto.MaxAuthorizedKeysSize+1))
	if err != nil {
		return nil, failed(helperproto.CodeIOError, "the new content cannot be read")
	}
	if len(content) > helperproto.MaxAuthorizedKeysSize {
		return nil, refused(helperproto.CodeTooLarge, "the new content is too large")
	}
	s.syslog(helperproto.SubAuthKeysWrite, path)
	r, err := s.scan(ctx)
	if err != nil {
		return nil, err
	}
	c, ok := r.find(path)
	if !ok {
		return nil, refused(helperproto.CodePathNotAllowed, "the path is not an authorized_keys file of a listed user")
	}
	return s.writeCandidate(c, expect, op, content)
}

// current is the file as found under the lock.
type current struct {
	absent   bool
	data     []byte
	mode     os.FileMode
	uid, gid int
}

func (c current) sha256() string {
	if c.absent {
		return helperproto.AbsentSHA256
	}
	return hexSHA(c.data)
}

// writeCandidate is the locked compare, backup and atomic replace.
func (s *sys) writeCandidate(c candidate, expect, op string, content []byte) (any, error) {
	dir := filepath.Dir(c.real)
	if err := s.ensureSSHDir(c, dir); err != nil {
		return nil, err
	}
	d, err := os.OpenFile(s.host(dir), os.O_RDONLY|syscall.O_DIRECTORY|syscall.O_NOFOLLOW|syscall.O_CLOEXEC, 0) //nolint:gosec // G304: the directory of a helper-computed candidate
	if err != nil {
		return nil, failed(helperproto.CodeIOError, "the directory cannot be opened")
	}
	defer func() { _ = d.Close() }()
	fd := int(d.Fd()) //nolint:gosec // G115: a file descriptor always fits an int
	if err := syscall.Flock(fd, syscall.LOCK_EX); err != nil {
		return nil, failed(helperproto.CodeIOError, "the directory cannot be locked")
	}
	defer func() { _ = syscall.Flock(fd, syscall.LOCK_UN) }()

	cur, err := s.readCurrent(c.real)
	if err != nil {
		return nil, err
	}
	if cur.sha256() != expect {
		return nil, precondition(helperproto.CodeHashMismatch, "the file changed since it was read")
	}
	backup, err := s.backup(op, c.path, cur)
	if err != nil {
		return nil, failed(helperproto.CodeIOError, "the backup cannot be written")
	}
	if err := s.replace(c, d, cur, content); err != nil {
		return nil, err
	}
	return helperproto.AuthKeysWriteResponse{OK: true, SHA256: hexSHA(content), Backup: backup}, nil
}

// ensureSSHDir creates <home>/.ssh (0700, owned by the user) when it is missing (spec §13.4 step 4).
// No other missing directory is ever created.
func (s *sys) ensureSSHDir(c candidate, dir string) error {
	st, err := os.Lstat(s.host(dir))
	if err == nil {
		if st.IsDir() {
			return nil
		}
		return refused(helperproto.CodeNotRegularFile, "the key directory is not a directory")
	}
	if !errors.Is(err, fs.ErrNotExist) {
		return failed(helperproto.CodeIOError, "the key directory cannot be checked")
	}
	if filepath.Base(dir) != ".ssh" || filepath.Dir(dir) != c.dir {
		return precondition(helperproto.CodeNotFound, "the key directory does not exist")
	}
	if err := os.Mkdir(s.host(dir), 0o700); err != nil {
		return failed(helperproto.CodeIOError, "the key directory cannot be created")
	}
	f, err := os.OpenFile(s.host(dir), os.O_RDONLY|syscall.O_DIRECTORY|syscall.O_NOFOLLOW|syscall.O_CLOEXEC, 0) //nolint:gosec // G304: created above
	if err != nil {
		return failed(helperproto.CodeIOError, "the key directory cannot be opened")
	}
	defer func() { _ = f.Close() }()
	if err := s.chown(f, c.acct.uid, c.acct.gid); err != nil {
		return failed(helperproto.CodeIOError, "the key directory owner cannot be set")
	}
	if err := f.Chmod(0o700); err != nil {
		return failed(helperproto.CodeIOError, "the key directory mode cannot be set")
	}
	return nil
}

// readCurrent reads the file under the lock. A file that is not regular, or has more than one hard
// link (writing it would change another name too), is refused (spec §12.3 path rule 4).
func (s *sys) readCurrent(real string) (current, error) {
	st, err := os.Lstat(s.host(real))
	if errors.Is(err, fs.ErrNotExist) {
		return current{absent: true}, nil
	}
	if err != nil {
		return current{}, failed(helperproto.CodeIOError, "the file cannot be checked")
	}
	stat, ok := st.Sys().(*syscall.Stat_t)
	if !st.Mode().IsRegular() || !ok || stat.Nlink > 1 {
		return current{}, refused(helperproto.CodeNotRegularFile, "the path is not a regular file with one link")
	}
	data, err := s.readRegular(real, helperproto.MaxAuthorizedKeysSize)
	if errors.Is(err, errTooLarge) {
		return current{}, refused(helperproto.CodeTooLarge, "the file is too large")
	}
	if err != nil {
		return current{}, failed(helperproto.CodeIOError, "the file cannot be read")
	}
	uid, gid := owner(st)
	return current{data: data, mode: st.Mode().Perm(), uid: uid, gid: gid}, nil
}

// backupMeta is written next to each backup.
type backupMeta struct {
	Path   string `json:"path"`
	Absent bool   `json:"absent"`
	Mode   string `json:"mode"`
	UID    int    `json:"uid"`
	GID    int    `json:"gid"`
	SHA256 string `json:"sha256"`
}

// backup stores the old content as <BackupRoot>/<op>/<n>.bak with metadata in <n>.json.
// It returns the guest path of the .bak file.
func (s *sys) backup(op, path string, cur current) (string, error) {
	dir := filepath.Join(helperproto.BackupRoot, op)
	if err := os.MkdirAll(s.host(dir), 0o700); err != nil {
		return "", err
	}
	for _, d := range []string{helperproto.BackupRoot, dir} {
		if err := os.Chmod(s.host(d), 0o700); err != nil {
			return "", err
		}
	}
	entries, err := os.ReadDir(s.host(dir))
	if err != nil {
		return "", err
	}
	n := 1
	for _, e := range entries {
		if strings.HasSuffix(e.Name(), ".bak") {
			n++
		}
	}
	name := filepath.Join(dir, strconv.Itoa(n)+".bak")
	meta := backupMeta{Path: path, Absent: cur.absent, SHA256: cur.sha256()}
	if !cur.absent {
		meta.Mode, meta.UID, meta.GID = fmt.Sprintf("%04o", cur.mode), cur.uid, cur.gid
	}
	raw, err := json.Marshal(meta)
	if err != nil {
		return "", err
	}
	if err := writeNew(s.host(name), cur.data); err != nil {
		return "", err
	}
	if err := writeNew(s.host(strings.TrimSuffix(name, ".bak")+".json"), raw); err != nil {
		return "", err
	}
	return name, nil
}

// writeNew creates a new 0600 file (never over an existing one) and syncs it.
func writeNew(path string, data []byte) error {
	f, err := os.OpenFile(path, os.O_WRONLY|os.O_CREATE|os.O_EXCL|syscall.O_NOFOLLOW|syscall.O_CLOEXEC, 0o600) //nolint:gosec // G304: helper-computed backup path
	if err != nil {
		return err
	}
	if _, err := f.Write(data); err != nil {
		_ = f.Close()
		return err
	}
	if err := f.Sync(); err != nil {
		_ = f.Close()
		return err
	}
	return f.Close()
}

// replace stages content next to the real file, copies owner, mode and SELinux label, syncs, and
// renames it over the real file; then it syncs the directory. Before the rename any failure
// removes the staging file, so the real file is always the old or the new version.
func (s *sys) replace(c candidate, dir *os.File, cur current, content []byte) error {
	var rnd [8]byte
	_, _ = rand.Read(rnd[:])
	tmp := filepath.Join(filepath.Dir(c.real), ".authorized_keys.alice-"+hex.EncodeToString(rnd[:]))
	f, err := os.OpenFile(s.host(tmp), os.O_WRONLY|os.O_CREATE|os.O_EXCL|syscall.O_NOFOLLOW|syscall.O_CLOEXEC, 0o600) //nolint:gosec // G304: staging file in a helper-computed directory
	if err != nil {
		return failed(helperproto.CodeIOError, "the staging file cannot be created")
	}
	renamed := false
	defer func() {
		_ = f.Close()
		if !renamed {
			_ = os.Remove(s.host(tmp))
		}
	}()
	uid, gid, mode := c.acct.uid, c.acct.gid, os.FileMode(0o600)
	if !cur.absent {
		uid, gid, mode = cur.uid, cur.gid, cur.mode
	}
	if _, err := f.Write(content); err != nil {
		return failed(helperproto.CodeIOError, "the staging file cannot be written")
	}
	if err := s.chown(f, uid, gid); err != nil {
		return failed(helperproto.CodeIOError, "the owner cannot be set")
	}
	if err := f.Chmod(mode); err != nil {
		return failed(helperproto.CodeIOError, "the mode cannot be set")
	}
	if !cur.absent {
		copySELinux(s.host(c.real), s.host(tmp))
	}
	if err := f.Sync(); err != nil {
		return failed(helperproto.CodeIOError, "the staging file cannot be synced")
	}
	if s.beforeRename != nil {
		if err := s.beforeRename(); err != nil {
			return failed(helperproto.CodeIOError, "the file cannot be replaced")
		}
	}
	if err := os.Rename(s.host(tmp), s.host(c.real)); err != nil {
		return failed(helperproto.CodeIOError, "the file cannot be replaced")
	}
	renamed = true
	if err := dir.Sync(); err != nil {
		return failed(helperproto.CodeIOError, "the directory cannot be synced")
	}
	return nil
}

// copySELinux copies the SELinux label of src to dst (spec §13.4 step 4), best effort: a system
// without SELinux has no label (ENODATA, ENOTSUP), and a new file inherits its directory's label.
func copySELinux(src, dst string) {
	size, err := syscall.Getxattr(src, selinuxXattr, nil)
	if err != nil || size <= 0 || size > 4096 {
		return
	}
	buf := make([]byte, size)
	n, err := syscall.Getxattr(src, selinuxXattr, buf)
	if err != nil {
		return
	}
	_ = syscall.Setxattr(dst, selinuxXattr, buf[:n], 0)
}
```

Create `cmd/alice-helper/cleanup.go`:

```go
//go:build linux

package main

import (
	"context"
	"errors"
	"io/fs"
	"os"
	"path/filepath"
	"time"

	"alice/internal/providers/linuxssh/helperproto"
)

// backupRetention is the helper's hard cap for backups (spec §12.6 step 8).
const backupRetention = 30 * 24 * time.Hour

// cmdCleanup removes the backups of one operation.
func cmdCleanup(_ context.Context, s *sys, args []string) (any, error) {
	if len(args) != 2 || args[0] != "--op" {
		return nil, refused(helperproto.CodeUsage, "usage: cleanup --op <operation id>")
	}
	if !helperproto.ValidOpID(args[1]) {
		return nil, refused(helperproto.CodeInvalidArgument, "the operation id is not allowed")
	}
	guest := filepath.Join(helperproto.BackupRoot, args[1])
	s.syslog(helperproto.SubCleanup, guest)
	_, err := os.Lstat(s.host(guest))
	if errors.Is(err, fs.ErrNotExist) {
		return helperproto.CleanupResponse{OK: true}, nil
	}
	if err != nil {
		return nil, failed(helperproto.CodeIOError, "the backups cannot be checked")
	}
	if err := os.RemoveAll(s.host(guest)); err != nil {
		return nil, failed(helperproto.CodeIOError, "the backups cannot be removed")
	}
	return helperproto.CleanupResponse{OK: true, Removed: 1}, nil
}

// sweepBackups removes operation backup directories older than backupRetention. It runs before
// every privileged subcommand; failures are ignored (they never block the call).
func (s *sys) sweepBackups() {
	root := s.host(helperproto.BackupRoot)
	entries, err := os.ReadDir(root)
	if err != nil {
		return
	}
	for _, e := range entries {
		if !e.IsDir() || !helperproto.ValidOpID(e.Name()) {
			continue
		}
		info, err := e.Info()
		if err != nil {
			continue
		}
		if s.now().Sub(info.ModTime()) > backupRetention {
			_ = os.RemoveAll(filepath.Join(root, e.Name()))
		}
	}
}
```

### Task 8: SSH connector — fake SSH server, helper command surface (A-12), pinned-key dialer and command runner (F-30, F-31, F-39)

This task builds the only path by which Alice talks to a server. `linuxsshtest.Server` is an in-process SSH server
(x/crypto/ssh) that counts authentication attempts and records every command line, so tests can prove that a host-key
refusal happens before authentication and that only exact helper command lines arrive. `command.go` holds the
`HelperCommand` constructors and the single quoting function `quoteArg` (SEC-063). `dial.go` holds the `Dialer`
(pinned-key callback, restricted algorithms, dial/handshake timeouts), `Conn.Run` (per-command timeout, output cap,
exit-status mapping), `Conn.OSRelease` and `DecodeHelper`. Two guard tests keep the surface closed: no file except
`dial.go` opens SSH sessions, and nothing in the repository accepts any host key.

**Files:**
- Create: `internal/providers/linuxssh/linuxsshtest/server.go`
- Create: `internal/providers/linuxssh/command.go`, `internal/providers/linuxssh/command_test.go`
- Create: `internal/providers/linuxssh/dial.go`, `internal/providers/linuxssh/dial_test.go`
- Create: `internal/providers/linuxssh/helpers_test.go`, `internal/providers/linuxssh/guard_test.go`
- Modify: `.golangci.yml` (forbidigo pattern for `ssh.InsecureIgnoreHostKey`)

**Interfaces:**

  (`Pinned`, `Observed`), `ErrNoPinnedKey`, `CredentialSource.SSHSigner(ctx) (ssh.Signer, func(), error)`,

- [ ] **Step 1: Create the fake SSH server**

Create `internal/providers/linuxssh/linuxsshtest/server.go`:

```go
// Package linuxsshtest provides an in-process SSH server and an alice-helper emulator for the
// tests of the linuxssh provider and of the packages that use it. It is never linked into the
// alice binary (only test files import it).
package linuxsshtest

import (
	"bytes"
	"crypto/ecdsa"
	"crypto/ed25519"
	"crypto/elliptic"
	"crypto/rand"
	"errors"
	"io"
	"net"
	"sync"
	"testing"
	"time"

	"golang.org/x/crypto/ssh"
)

// Response is what the server answers to one exec request.
type Response struct {
	Stdout []byte
	Stderr []byte
	// Exit is the exit status; a negative value closes the channel without an exit status.
	Exit int
	// Delay is waited before answering (a slow host, F-39). The wait ends early when the client
	// closes the connection.
	Delay time.Duration
}

// Handler answers one command line; stdin is everything the client sent before closing its input.
type Handler func(cmd string, stdin []byte) Response

// Server is an SSH server on 127.0.0.1 that accepts one authorized client key, records every
// authentication attempt and every exec command line, and answers commands with a Handler.
type Server struct {
	ln   net.Listener
	done chan struct{}
	wg   sync.WaitGroup

	mu         sync.Mutex
	signers    []ssh.Signer
	authorized []byte
	handler    Handler
	attempts   int
	commands   []string
	conns      map[net.Conn]struct{}
}

// NewServer starts a server with a random Ed25519 host key. It stops when the test ends.
func NewServer(t testing.TB, h Handler) *Server {
	t.Helper()
	ln, err := net.Listen("tcp", "127.0.0.1:0")
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("linuxsshtest: listen: %v", err)
	}
	s := &Server{
		ln:      ln,
		done:    make(chan struct{}),
		signers: []ssh.Signer{NewHostKey(t)},
		handler: h,
		conns:   map[net.Conn]struct{}{},
	}
	s.wg.Add(1)
	go s.serve()
	t.Cleanup(s.stop)
	return s
}

func (s *Server) stop() {
	close(s.done)
	_ = s.ln.Close()
	s.mu.Lock()
	for c := range s.conns {
		_ = c.Close()
	}
	s.mu.Unlock()
	s.wg.Wait()
}

// Addr returns the address clients dial.
func (s *Server) Addr() (host string, port int) {
	a := s.ln.Addr().(*net.TCPAddr)
	return a.IP.String(), a.Port
}

// HostKey returns the first host key the server offers.
func (s *Server) HostKey() ssh.PublicKey {
	s.mu.Lock()
	defer s.mu.Unlock()
	return s.signers[0].PublicKey()
}

// SetHostKey makes the next connections see another host key (a reinstalled server or a MITM, F-31).
func (s *Server) SetHostKey(k ssh.Signer) { s.SetHostKeyAlgorithms(k) }

// SetHostKeyAlgorithms makes the server offer exactly these host keys from the next connection on.
func (s *Server) SetHostKeyAlgorithms(signers ...ssh.Signer) {
	s.mu.Lock()
	defer s.mu.Unlock()
	s.signers = append([]ssh.Signer(nil), signers...)
}

// Authorize sets the one client key the server accepts.
func (s *Server) Authorize(k ssh.PublicKey) {
	s.mu.Lock()
	defer s.mu.Unlock()
	s.authorized = k.Marshal()
}

// AuthAttempts counts public-key authentication callbacks over all connections.
func (s *Server) AuthAttempts() int {
	s.mu.Lock()
	defer s.mu.Unlock()
	return s.attempts
}

// Commands returns every exec command line received, in order.
func (s *Server) Commands() []string {
	s.mu.Lock()
	defer s.mu.Unlock()
	return append([]string(nil), s.commands...)
}

// SetHandler replaces the command handler.
func (s *Server) SetHandler(h Handler) {
	s.mu.Lock()
	defer s.mu.Unlock()
	s.handler = h
}

// NewHostKey returns a random Ed25519 signer.
func NewHostKey(t testing.TB) ssh.Signer {
	t.Helper()
	_, priv, err := ed25519.GenerateKey(rand.Reader)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("linuxsshtest: ed25519 key: %v", err)
	}
	s, err := ssh.NewSignerFromKey(priv)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("linuxsshtest: signer: %v", err)
	}
	return s
}

// NewECDSAHostKey returns a random ECDSA P-256 signer.
func NewECDSAHostKey(t testing.TB) ssh.Signer {
	t.Helper()
	priv, err := ecdsa.GenerateKey(elliptic.P256(), rand.Reader)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("linuxsshtest: ecdsa key: %v", err)
	}
	s, err := ssh.NewSignerFromKey(priv)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("linuxsshtest: signer: %v", err)
	}
	return s
}

func (s *Server) serve() {
	defer s.wg.Done()
	for {
		c, err := s.ln.Accept()
		if err != nil {
			return
		}
		s.mu.Lock()
		s.conns[c] = struct{}{}
		s.mu.Unlock()
		s.wg.Add(1)
		go func() {
			defer s.wg.Done()
			s.handleConn(c)
		}()
	}
}

func (s *Server) checkKey(_ ssh.ConnMetadata, key ssh.PublicKey) (*ssh.Permissions, error) {
	s.mu.Lock()
	defer s.mu.Unlock()
	s.attempts++
	if s.authorized != nil && bytes.Equal(key.Marshal(), s.authorized) {
		return &ssh.Permissions{}, nil
	}
	return nil, errors.New("linuxsshtest: key not authorized")
}

func (s *Server) handleConn(c net.Conn) {
	defer func() {
		s.mu.Lock()
		delete(s.conns, c)
		s.mu.Unlock()
		_ = c.Close()
	}()
	cfg := &ssh.ServerConfig{PublicKeyCallback: s.checkKey}
	s.mu.Lock()
	for _, k := range s.signers {
		cfg.AddHostKey(k)
	}
	s.mu.Unlock()
	sc, chans, reqs, err := ssh.NewServerConn(c, cfg)
	if err != nil {
		return
	}
	go ssh.DiscardRequests(reqs)
	closed := make(chan struct{})
	go func() {
		_ = sc.Wait()
		close(closed)
	}()
	var sessions sync.WaitGroup
	for nc := range chans {
		if nc.ChannelType() != "session" {
			_ = nc.Reject(ssh.UnknownChannelType, "only session channels")
			continue
		}
		ch, creqs, err := nc.Accept()
		if err != nil {
			continue
		}
		sessions.Add(1)
		go func() {
			defer sessions.Done()
			s.serveSession(ch, creqs, closed)
		}()
	}
	sessions.Wait()
}

func (s *Server) serveSession(ch ssh.Channel, reqs <-chan *ssh.Request, closed <-chan struct{}) {
	defer func() { _ = ch.Close() }()
	for req := range reqs {
		if req.Type != "exec" {
			if req.WantReply {
				_ = req.Reply(false, nil)
			}
			continue
		}
		var p struct{ Command string }
		if err := ssh.Unmarshal(req.Payload, &p); err != nil {
			_ = req.Reply(false, nil)
			continue
		}
		_ = req.Reply(true, nil)
		s.mu.Lock()
		s.commands = append(s.commands, p.Command)
		h := s.handler
		s.mu.Unlock()
		stdin, err := io.ReadAll(ch)
		if err != nil {
			return
		}
		resp := Response{Stderr: []byte("sh: command not found\n"), Exit: 127}
		if h != nil {
			resp = h(p.Command, stdin)
		}
		if resp.Delay > 0 {
			select {
			case <-time.After(resp.Delay):
			case <-closed:
				return
			case <-s.done:
				return
			}
		}
		_, _ = ch.Write(resp.Stdout)
		_, _ = ch.Stderr().Write(resp.Stderr)
		if resp.Exit >= 0 {
			status := struct{ Status uint32 }{uint32(resp.Exit)} //nolint:gosec // G115: test exit codes are small non-negative numbers
			_, _ = ch.SendRequest("exit-status", false, ssh.Marshal(status))
		}
		return
	}
}
```

```go
package linuxssh

import (
	"strings"
	"testing"

	"github.com/google/uuid"
	"github.com/stretchr/testify/assert"
	"github.com/stretchr/testify/require"

	"alice/internal/providers/linuxssh/helperproto"
)

var testOp = uuid.MustParse("0190f5a0-0000-7000-8000-0000000000aa")

func TestQuoteArgIsTheOnlyQuoting(t *testing.T) {
	q, err := quoteArg("/home/deploy/.ssh/authorized_keys")
	require.NoError(t, err)
	assert.Equal(t, "'/home/deploy/.ssh/authorized_keys'", q)
	for _, bad := range []string{"a'b", "a b", "", "-x", "a\nb", "$(id)"} {
		_, err := quoteArg(bad)
		assert.ErrorIs(t, err, ErrInvalidArgument, "%q", bad)
	}
}

func TestCommandLinesAreExact(t *testing.T) {
	read, err := CmdAuthKeysRead("/home/deploy/.ssh/authorized_keys")
	require.NoError(t, err)
	write, err := CmdAuthKeysWrite("/root/.ssh/authorized_keys", helperproto.AbsentSHA256, testOp, []byte("x\n"))
	require.NoError(t, err)
	sha := strings.Repeat("ab", 32)
	writeSHA, err := CmdAuthKeysWrite("/root/.ssh/authorized_keys", sha, testOp, nil)
	require.NoError(t, err)
	cleanup, err := CmdCleanup(testOp)
	require.NoError(t, err)

	for _, tc := range []struct {
		cmd  HelperCommand
		line string
		sub  string
	}{
		{CmdVersion(), "/usr/local/libexec/alice-helper version", "version"},
		{CmdSSHDDump(), "sudo -n /usr/local/libexec/alice-helper sshd-dump", "sshd-dump"},
		{CmdHostKeys(), "sudo -n /usr/local/libexec/alice-helper hostkeys", "hostkeys"},
		{CmdAuthKeysList(), "sudo -n /usr/local/libexec/alice-helper authkeys-list", "authkeys-list"},
		{read, "sudo -n /usr/local/libexec/alice-helper authkeys-read '/home/deploy/.ssh/authorized_keys'", "authkeys-read"},
		{write, "sudo -n /usr/local/libexec/alice-helper authkeys-write '/root/.ssh/authorized_keys' --expect-sha256 'absent' --op '0190f5a0-0000-7000-8000-0000000000aa'", "authkeys-write"},
		{writeSHA, "sudo -n /usr/local/libexec/alice-helper authkeys-write '/root/.ssh/authorized_keys' --expect-sha256 '" + sha + "' --op '0190f5a0-0000-7000-8000-0000000000aa'", "authkeys-write"},
		{cleanup, "sudo -n /usr/local/libexec/alice-helper cleanup --op '0190f5a0-0000-7000-8000-0000000000aa'", "cleanup"},
	} {
		assert.Equal(t, tc.line, tc.cmd.Line())
		assert.Equal(t, tc.sub, tc.cmd.Subcommand())
	}
}

func TestCommandBudgets(t *testing.T) {
	read, err := CmdAuthKeysRead("/root/.ssh/authorized_keys")
	require.NoError(t, err)
	assert.Equal(t, DefaultCommandTimeout, CmdVersion().timeout)
	assert.Equal(t, LongCommandTimeout, CmdSSHDDump().timeout)
	assert.Equal(t, LongCommandTimeout, CmdAuthKeysList().timeout)
	assert.Equal(t, DefaultCommandTimeout, read.timeout)
	assert.Equal(t, int64(DefaultMaxOutput), CmdAuthKeysList().maxOutput)
	// authkeys-read answers base64 of up to 1 MiB plus JSON: 2 MiB is enough and bounded.
	assert.Equal(t, int64(2<<20), read.maxOutput)
	assert.False(t, CmdVersion().sudo, "version runs without sudo (sudoers does not list it)")
	assert.True(t, read.sudo)
}

func TestWriteCopiesItsContent(t *testing.T) {
	content := []byte("ssh-ed25519 AAAA x\n")
	c, err := CmdAuthKeysWrite("/root/.ssh/authorized_keys", helperproto.AbsentSHA256, testOp, content)
	require.NoError(t, err)
	content[0] = 'X'
	assert.Equal(t, "ssh-ed25519 AAAA x\n", string(c.stdin))
}

// A-12: every string that would cross into a command line is validated; hostile values never
// produce a command.
func TestHostileArgumentsNeverBecomeCommands(t *testing.T) {
	hostile := []string{
		"",
		"relative/.ssh/authorized_keys",
		"/root/.ssh/authorized_keys; rm -rf /",
		"/root/`id`",
		"/root/$(id)",
		"/root/.ssh/authorized_keys\nid",
		"/root/.ssh/authorized_keys\r",
		"/root/a\x00b",
		"/home/çağla/.ssh/authorized_keys",
		"/home/a b/.ssh/authorized_keys",
		"/home/x/../../etc/shadow",
		"/root/./.ssh/authorized_keys",
		"/root/.ssh/'x'",
		"/root/.ssh/authorized_keys|cat",
		"/root/*",
		"/root/~x",
		"-rf",
		"/" + strings.Repeat("a/", 2048) + "x",
	}
	for _, p := range hostile {
		c, err := CmdAuthKeysRead(p)
		assert.ErrorIs(t, err, ErrInvalidArgument, "read %q", p)
		assert.Empty(t, c.Line(), "no command for %q", p)
		_, err = CmdAuthKeysWrite(p, helperproto.AbsentSHA256, testOp, nil)
		assert.ErrorIs(t, err, ErrInvalidArgument, "write %q", p)
	}
	for _, h := range []string{"absent; id", "ABAB", strings.Repeat("g", 64), "$(id)", strings.Repeat("A", 64)} {
		_, err := CmdAuthKeysWrite("/root/.ssh/authorized_keys", h, testOp, nil)
		assert.ErrorIs(t, err, ErrInvalidArgument, "sha %q", h)
	}
	_, err := CmdAuthKeysWrite("/root/.ssh/authorized_keys", helperproto.AbsentSHA256, uuid.Nil, nil)
	assert.ErrorIs(t, err, ErrInvalidArgument)
	_, err = CmdCleanup(uuid.Nil)
	assert.ErrorIs(t, err, ErrInvalidArgument)
	_, err = CmdAuthKeysWrite("/root/.ssh/authorized_keys", helperproto.AbsentSHA256, testOp,
		make([]byte, helperproto.MaxAuthorizedKeysSize+1))
	assert.ErrorIs(t, err, ErrInvalidArgument)
}
```

```go
package linuxssh

import (
	"errors"
	"fmt"
	"strings"
	"time"

	"github.com/google/uuid"

	"alice/internal/providers/linuxssh/helperproto"
)

// HelperCommand is one remote command line. Its fields are unexported, so a command can only be
// built by the constructors below: every argument passed helperproto's vocabulary check and
// quoteArg (spec §6.6, SEC-063). There is no way to send a free-form shell string.
type HelperCommand struct {
	sub       string
	tokens    []string // rendered arguments: constant flag names or quoteArg output
	stdin     []byte
	sudo      bool
	fixed     string // the one fixed non-helper command (cat /etc/os-release); set only in dial.go
	timeout   time.Duration
	maxOutput int64
}

const (
	smallOutput    = 64 << 10
	hostKeysOutput = 1 << 20
	readOutput     = 2 << 20 // base64 of a 1 MiB file plus the JSON around it
)

// OSReleaseCommand is the only command Alice runs that is not alice-helper (spec §6.6).
const OSReleaseCommand = "cat /etc/os-release"

// ErrInvalidArgument means a value is outside the helper's argument vocabulary; no command is built.
var ErrInvalidArgument = errors.New("linuxssh: argument outside the allowed vocabulary")

// quoteArg is the single audited quoting function for remote command lines (SEC-063). The value
// must be in helperproto's vocabulary ([A-Za-z0-9._/@:+-], no ".." component, no leading '-'),
// which contains no quote, no space and no shell metacharacter, so single quotes make it one
// literal word for the remote shell.
func quoteArg(s string) (string, error) {
	if !helperproto.ValidArg(s) || strings.ContainsRune(s, '\'') {
		return "", ErrInvalidArgument
	}
	return "'" + s + "'", nil
}

func privileged(sub string, timeout time.Duration, maxOutput int64, tokens ...string) HelperCommand {
	return HelperCommand{sub: sub, tokens: tokens, sudo: true, timeout: timeout, maxOutput: maxOutput}
}

// CmdVersion asks the helper for its version; it runs without sudo (sudoers does not list it).
func CmdVersion() HelperCommand {
	return HelperCommand{sub: helperproto.SubVersion, timeout: DefaultCommandTimeout, maxOutput: smallOutput}
}

// CmdSSHDDump returns the effective sshd configuration (sshd -T).
func CmdSSHDDump() HelperCommand {
	return privileged(helperproto.SubSSHDDump, LongCommandTimeout, DefaultMaxOutput)
}

// CmdHostKeys lists the server's host keys with their fingerprints.
func CmdHostKeys() HelperCommand {
	return privileged(helperproto.SubHostKeys, DefaultCommandTimeout, hostKeysOutput)
}

// CmdAuthKeysList lists the users and the authorized_keys files sshd would read for them.
func CmdAuthKeysList() HelperCommand {
	return privileged(helperproto.SubAuthKeysList, LongCommandTimeout, DefaultMaxOutput)
}

// CmdAuthKeysRead reads one authorized_keys file (the helper accepts only paths it computed itself).
func CmdAuthKeysRead(path string) (HelperCommand, error) {
	if !helperproto.ValidPath(path) {
		return HelperCommand{}, ErrInvalidArgument
	}
	q, err := quoteArg(path)
	if err != nil {
		return HelperCommand{}, err
	}
	return privileged(helperproto.SubAuthKeysRead, DefaultCommandTimeout, readOutput, q), nil
}

// CmdAuthKeysWrite replaces one authorized_keys file with content when its current SHA-256 is
// expectSHA256 (helperproto.AbsentSHA256 for a file that does not exist yet). op names the backup.
func CmdAuthKeysWrite(path, expectSHA256 string, op uuid.UUID, content []byte) (HelperCommand, error) {
	if !helperproto.ValidPath(path) || !helperproto.ValidSHA256(expectSHA256) || op == uuid.Nil || !helperproto.ValidOpID(op.String()) {
		return HelperCommand{}, ErrInvalidArgument
	}
	if len(content) > helperproto.MaxAuthorizedKeysSize {
		return HelperCommand{}, fmt.Errorf("%w: content is larger than %d bytes", ErrInvalidArgument, helperproto.MaxAuthorizedKeysSize)
	}
	qp, err := quoteArg(path)
	if err != nil {
		return HelperCommand{}, err
	}
	qh, err := quoteArg(expectSHA256)
	if err != nil {
		return HelperCommand{}, err
	}
	qo, err := quoteArg(op.String())
	if err != nil {
		return HelperCommand{}, err
	}
	c := privileged(helperproto.SubAuthKeysWrite, DefaultCommandTimeout, smallOutput, qp, "--expect-sha256", qh, "--op", qo)
	c.stdin = append([]byte(nil), content...)
	return c, nil
}

// CmdCleanup removes the helper's backup directory of one operation.
func CmdCleanup(op uuid.UUID) (HelperCommand, error) {
	if op == uuid.Nil || !helperproto.ValidOpID(op.String()) {
		return HelperCommand{}, ErrInvalidArgument
	}
	qo, err := quoteArg(op.String())
	if err != nil {
		return HelperCommand{}, err
	}
	return privileged(helperproto.SubCleanup, DefaultCommandTimeout, smallOutput, "--op", qo), nil
}

// Line is the exact command line sent over the SSH exec channel ("" for the zero value).
func (c HelperCommand) Line() string {
	if c.fixed != "" {
		return c.fixed
	}
	if c.sub == "" {
		return ""
	}
	var b strings.Builder
	if c.sudo {
		b.WriteString("sudo -n ")
	}
	b.WriteString(helperproto.HelperPath)
	b.WriteByte(' ')
	b.WriteString(c.sub)
	for _, t := range c.tokens {
		b.WriteByte(' ')
		b.WriteString(t)
	}
	return b.String()
}

// Subcommand names the helper subcommand ("os-release" for the fixed command).
func (c HelperCommand) Subcommand() string {
	if c.fixed != "" {
		return "os-release"
	}
	return c.sub
}
```

```go
package linuxssh

import (
	"context"
	"crypto/ed25519"
	"crypto/rand"
	"errors"
	"strconv"
	"sync"
	"testing"

	"github.com/google/uuid"
	"github.com/stretchr/testify/require"

	"alice/internal/providers"

)

var testTarget = uuid.MustParse("0190f5a0-0000-7000-8000-0000000000a1")

// fakeCred hands out one client key and counts releases.
type fakeCred struct {
	signer   ssh.Signer
	mu       sync.Mutex
	released int
}

func newFakeCred(t testing.TB) *fakeCred {
	t.Helper()
	_, priv, err := ed25519.GenerateKey(rand.Reader)
	require.NoError(t, err)
	s, err := ssh.NewSignerFromKey(priv)
	require.NoError(t, err)
	return &fakeCred{signer: s}
}

func (f *fakeCred) SSHSigner(context.Context) (ssh.Signer, func(), error) {
	return f.signer, func() {
		f.mu.Lock()
		f.released++
		f.mu.Unlock()
	}, nil
}

func (f *fakeCred) releases() int {
	f.mu.Lock()
	defer f.mu.Unlock()
	return f.released
}

type observation struct {
	key     providers.HostKey
	changed bool
}

// memHostKeys is an in-memory providers.HostKeyStore.
type memHostKeys struct {
	mu       sync.Mutex
	pinned   *providers.HostKey
	observed []observation
	fail     error
}

func (m *memHostKeys) Pinned(context.Context, uuid.UUID) (providers.HostKey, error) {
	m.mu.Lock()
	defer m.mu.Unlock()
	if m.fail != nil {
		return providers.HostKey{}, m.fail
	}
	if m.pinned == nil {
		return providers.HostKey{}, providers.ErrNoPinnedKey
	}
	return *m.pinned, nil
}

func (m *memHostKeys) Observed(_ context.Context, _ uuid.UUID, k providers.HostKey, changed bool) error {
	m.mu.Lock()
	defer m.mu.Unlock()
	m.observed = append(m.observed, observation{key: k, changed: changed})
	return nil
}

func (m *memHostKeys) pin(k ssh.PublicKey) {
	m.mu.Lock()
	defer m.mu.Unlock()
	hk := HostKeyOf(k)
	m.pinned = &hk
}

func (m *memHostKeys) observations() []observation {
	m.mu.Lock()
	defer m.mu.Unlock()
	return append([]observation(nil), m.observed...)
}

// testServer starts a fake SSH server answering with h and authorizing a fresh client key.
func testServer(t testing.TB, h linuxsshtest.Handler) (*linuxsshtest.Server, Config, *fakeCred) {
	t.Helper()
	srv := linuxsshtest.NewServer(t, h)
	cred := newFakeCred(t)
	srv.Authorize(cred.signer.PublicKey())
	host, port := srv.Addr()
	return srv, Config{Host: host, Port: port, Username: "alice-svc"}, cred
}

func newDialer(hk *memHostKeys) *Dialer {
	return &Dialer{Clock: clock.Real{}, HostKeys: hk}
}

// providerCode returns the reason code of a *providers.Error ("" otherwise).
func providerCode(t testing.TB, err error) *providers.Error {
	t.Helper()
	var pe *providers.Error
	require.True(t, errors.As(err, &pe), "want *providers.Error, got %T (%v)", err, err)
	return pe
}

// versionJSON is the helper's answer to "version".
func versionJSON(protocol int) linuxsshtest.Response {
	return linuxsshtest.Response{Stdout: []byte(`{"ok":true,"helper":"1.0.0","protocol":` + strconv.Itoa(protocol) + `}`)}
}
```
