```go
package linuxssh

import (
	"bytes"
	"context"
	"errors"
	"net"
	"sync"
	"testing"
	"time"

	"github.com/stretchr/testify/assert"
	"github.com/stretchr/testify/require"
	"golang.org/x/crypto/ssh"

	"alice/internal/platform/validate"
	"alice/internal/providers"
	"alice/internal/providers/linuxssh/helperproto"
	"alice/internal/providers/linuxssh/linuxsshtest"
)

func okHandler(cmd string, _ []byte) linuxsshtest.Response {
	if cmd == CmdVersion().Line() {
		return versionJSON(1)
	}
	return linuxsshtest.Response{Exit: 127}
}

// F-30: an unknown server's key is shown, never trusted: the connection stops at the key
// exchange, no authentication is attempted and no command runs.
func TestFirstContactStopsBeforeAuthentication(t *testing.T) {
	srv, cfg, cred := testServer(t, okHandler)
	hk := &memHostKeys{}
	_, err := newDialer(hk).Dial(context.Background(), testTarget, cfg, cred)
	pe := providerCode(t, err)
	assert.Equal(t, "target.host_key_unconfirmed", pe.Code)
	assert.False(t, pe.Retryable)
	assert.Equal(t, ssh.FingerprintSHA256(srv.HostKey()), pe.Params["fingerprint"])
	assert.Zero(t, srv.AuthAttempts(), "no authentication attempt before the key is confirmed")
	assert.Empty(t, srv.Commands())
	obs := hk.observations()
	require.Len(t, obs, 1)
	assert.False(t, obs[0].changed)
	assert.Equal(t, srv.HostKey().Marshal(), obs[0].key.PublicKey)
	assert.Equal(t, "ssh-ed25519", obs[0].key.Type)
	assert.Equal(t, 1, cred.releases(), "the decrypted key is released after the handshake")

	// After an administrator pins the key, the same server is reachable.
	hk.pin(srv.HostKey())
	c, err := newDialer(hk).Dial(context.Background(), testTarget, cfg, cred)
	require.NoError(t, err)
	defer func() { _ = c.Close() }()
	assert.Equal(t, ssh.FingerprintSHA256(srv.HostKey()), c.HostKey().Fingerprint)
	res, err := c.Run(context.Background(), CmdVersion())
	require.NoError(t, err)
	assert.Equal(t, 0, res.ExitCode)
	assert.Equal(t, []string{"/usr/local/libexec/alice-helper version"}, srv.Commands())
}

// F-31: a different key stops the connection before authentication and is reported as changed.
func TestChangedHostKeyStopsBeforeAuthentication(t *testing.T) {
	srv, cfg, cred := testServer(t, okHandler)
	hk := &memHostKeys{}
	old := srv.HostKey()
	hk.pin(old)
	newKey := linuxsshtest.NewHostKey(t)
	srv.SetHostKey(newKey)

	_, err := newDialer(hk).Dial(context.Background(), testTarget, cfg, cred)
	pe := providerCode(t, err)
	assert.Equal(t, "target.host_key_changed", pe.Code)
	assert.Equal(t, ssh.FingerprintSHA256(old), pe.Params["old_fingerprint"])
	assert.Equal(t, ssh.FingerprintSHA256(newKey.PublicKey()), pe.Params["new_fingerprint"])
	assert.Zero(t, srv.AuthAttempts())
	assert.Empty(t, srv.Commands())
	obs := hk.observations()
	require.Len(t, obs, 1)
	assert.True(t, obs[0].changed)
	assert.Equal(t, newKey.PublicKey().Marshal(), obs[0].key.PublicKey)
}

// A server that no longer offers the pinned key type (ed25519 pinned, only ECDSA offered) has
// changed its identity too; the pinned algorithm list makes the handshake fail, a key-only probe
// reports the new key.
func TestMissingPinnedAlgorithmCountsAsChanged(t *testing.T) {
	srv, cfg, cred := testServer(t, okHandler)
	hk := &memHostKeys{}
	hk.pin(srv.HostKey())
	ecdsaKey := linuxsshtest.NewECDSAHostKey(t)
	srv.SetHostKeyAlgorithms(ecdsaKey)

	_, err := newDialer(hk).Dial(context.Background(), testTarget, cfg, cred)
	pe := providerCode(t, err)
	assert.Equal(t, "target.host_key_changed", pe.Code)
	assert.Equal(t, ssh.FingerprintSHA256(ecdsaKey.PublicKey()), pe.Params["new_fingerprint"])
	assert.Zero(t, srv.AuthAttempts())
	obs := hk.observations()
	require.Len(t, obs, 1)
	assert.True(t, obs[0].changed)
	assert.Equal(t, "ecdsa-sha2-nistp256", obs[0].key.Type)
}

// The pinned key restricts the host-key algorithms: a server that offers both the pinned ECDSA
// key and an Ed25519 key is accepted with the pinned one.
func TestPinnedAlgorithmIsTheOnlyOneOffered(t *testing.T) {
	srv, cfg, cred := testServer(t, okHandler)
	ecdsaKey := linuxsshtest.NewECDSAHostKey(t)
	srv.SetHostKeyAlgorithms(linuxsshtest.NewHostKey(t), ecdsaKey)
	hk := &memHostKeys{}
	hk.pin(ecdsaKey.PublicKey())
	c, err := newDialer(hk).Dial(context.Background(), testTarget, cfg, cred)
	require.NoError(t, err)
	defer func() { _ = c.Close() }()
	assert.Equal(t, "ecdsa-sha2-nistp256", c.HostKey().Type)
	assert.Empty(t, hk.observations())
}

func TestAuthenticationFailure(t *testing.T) {
	srv, cfg, cred := testServer(t, okHandler)
	srv.Authorize(newFakeCred(t).signer.PublicKey()) // the server trusts another key
	hk := &memHostKeys{}
	hk.pin(srv.HostKey())
	_, err := newDialer(hk).Dial(context.Background(), testTarget, cfg, cred)
	pe := providerCode(t, err)
	assert.Equal(t, "ssh.auth_failed", pe.Code)
	assert.False(t, pe.Retryable)
	assert.Positive(t, srv.AuthAttempts())
	assert.Empty(t, srv.Commands())
}

func TestUnreachableServer(t *testing.T) {
	ln, err := net.Listen("tcp", "127.0.0.1:0")
	require.NoError(t, err)
	port := ln.Addr().(*net.TCPAddr).Port
	require.NoError(t, ln.Close())
	_, err = newDialer(&memHostKeys{}).Dial(context.Background(), testTarget,
		Config{Host: "127.0.0.1", Port: port, Username: "alice-svc"}, newFakeCred(t))
	pe := providerCode(t, err)
	assert.Equal(t, "ssh.unreachable", pe.Code)
	assert.True(t, pe.Retryable)
}

func TestHostKeyStoreFailureIsNotAConnection(t *testing.T) {
	srv, cfg, cred := testServer(t, okHandler)
	_, err := newDialer(&memHostKeys{fail: errors.New("database down")}).Dial(context.Background(), testTarget, cfg, cred)
	assert.Equal(t, "internal.unexpected", providerCode(t, err).Code)
	assert.Zero(t, srv.AuthAttempts())
}

func pinnedConn(t *testing.T, h linuxsshtest.Handler) (*linuxsshtest.Server, *Conn) {
	t.Helper()
	srv, cfg, cred := testServer(t, h)
	hk := &memHostKeys{}
	hk.pin(srv.HostKey())
	c, err := newDialer(hk).Dial(context.Background(), testTarget, cfg, cred)
	require.NoError(t, err)
	t.Cleanup(func() { _ = c.Close() })
	return srv, c
}

func TestRunPassesStdinAndReturnsExitCode(t *testing.T) {
	var mu sync.Mutex
	var gotStdin []byte
	_, c := pinnedConn(t, func(_ string, stdin []byte) linuxsshtest.Response {
		mu.Lock()
		gotStdin = stdin
		mu.Unlock()
		return linuxsshtest.Response{Stdout: []byte(`{"ok":false}`), Exit: 3}
	})
	cmd, err := CmdAuthKeysWrite("/root/.ssh/authorized_keys", helperproto.AbsentSHA256, testOp, []byte("line\n"))
	require.NoError(t, err)
	res, err := c.Run(context.Background(), cmd)
	require.NoError(t, err)
	assert.Equal(t, 3, res.ExitCode)
	assert.Equal(t, `{"ok":false}`, string(res.Stdout))
	mu.Lock()
	assert.Equal(t, "line\n", string(gotStdin))
	mu.Unlock()
	assert.True(t, c.Healthy())
}

func TestRunWithoutExitStatusIsAProtocolError(t *testing.T) {
	_, c := pinnedConn(t, func(string, []byte) linuxsshtest.Response { return linuxsshtest.Response{Exit: -1} })
	_, err := c.Run(context.Background(), CmdVersion())
	assert.Equal(t, "ssh.protocol_error", providerCode(t, err).Code)
}

// Review Focus 3: a host that sends more than a command may return is cut off.
func TestRunCapsOutput(t *testing.T) {
	_, c := pinnedConn(t, func(string, []byte) linuxsshtest.Response {
		return linuxsshtest.Response{Stdout: bytes.Repeat([]byte("A"), 512<<10)}
	})
	_, err := c.Run(context.Background(), CmdVersion()) // version may answer at most 64 KiB
	pe := providerCode(t, err)
	assert.Equal(t, "ssh.output_too_large", pe.Code)
	assert.Equal(t, "version", pe.Params["subcommand"])
	assert.False(t, c.Healthy(), "the connection is not reused after a flood")
}

// F-39, Review Focus 3: a slow host (10 s per command) fails the step on its own budget and the
// connection is closed; it is never reused.
func TestRunTimesOutAndClosesSession(t *testing.T) {
	_, c := pinnedConn(t, func(string, []byte) linuxsshtest.Response {
		return linuxsshtest.Response{Delay: 10 * time.Second, Stdout: []byte(`{"ok":true}`)}
	})
	cmd := CmdSSHDDump()
	cmd.timeout = 300 * time.Millisecond
	start := time.Now()
	_, err := c.Run(context.Background(), cmd)
	elapsed := time.Since(start)
	pe := providerCode(t, err)
	assert.Equal(t, "ssh.timeout", pe.Code)
	assert.True(t, pe.Retryable)
	assert.Equal(t, "sshd-dump", pe.Params["subcommand"])
	assert.Less(t, elapsed, 3*time.Second, "the 10 s answer was not awaited")
	assert.False(t, c.Healthy())
	_, err = c.Run(context.Background(), CmdVersion())
	assert.Equal(t, "ssh.unreachable", providerCode(t, err).Code, "a closed connection runs nothing")
}

func TestRunHonoursContextCancellation(t *testing.T) {
	_, c := pinnedConn(t, func(string, []byte) linuxsshtest.Response {
		return linuxsshtest.Response{Delay: 10 * time.Second}
	})
	ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(context.Background(), 200*time.Millisecond)
	defer cancel()
	_, err := c.Run(ctx, CmdVersion())
	assert.Equal(t, "ssh.timeout", providerCode(t, err).Code)
	assert.False(t, c.Healthy())
}

func TestOSReleaseIsParsedAndCleaned(t *testing.T) {
	srv, c := pinnedConn(t, func(cmd string, _ []byte) linuxsshtest.Response {
		if cmd != OSReleaseCommand {
			return linuxsshtest.Response{Exit: 127}
		}
		return linuxsshtest.Response{Stdout: []byte("NAME=\"Ubuntu\"\nVERSION_ID=\"22.04\"\nID=ubuntu\nPRETTY_NAME=\"Ubuntu \x1b[31m22.04 LTS\"\nHOME_URL=\"https://www.ubuntu.com/\"\n")}
	})
	r, err := c.OSRelease(context.Background())
	require.NoError(t, err)
	assert.Equal(t, "ubuntu", r.ID)
	assert.Equal(t, "22.04", r.VersionID)
	assert.Equal(t, "Ubuntu [31m22.04 LTS", r.PrettyName, "control characters (terminal escapes) are dropped")
	assert.Equal(t, []string{"cat /etc/os-release"}, srv.Commands())
}

func TestDecodeHelper(t *testing.T) {
	type out = helperproto.VersionResponse
	ok, err := DecodeHelper[out](Result{Stdout: []byte(`{"ok":true,"helper":"1.0.0","protocol":1}`)}, "version")
	require.NoError(t, err)
	assert.Equal(t, 1, ok.Protocol)

	for _, tc := range []struct {
		name   string
		r      Result
		code   string
		helper string
		retry  bool
	}{
		{"ok false", Result{Stdout: []byte(`{"ok":false}`)}, "ssh.protocol_error", "", false},
		{"no ok field", Result{Stdout: []byte(`{"helper":"1"}`)}, "ssh.protocol_error", "", false},
		{"not json", Result{Stdout: []byte("hello")}, "ssh.protocol_error", "", false},
		{"two values", Result{Stdout: []byte(`{"ok":true}{"ok":true}`)}, "ssh.protocol_error", "", false},
		{"refused", Result{ExitCode: 2, Stdout: []byte(`{"ok":false,"code":"PATH_NOT_ALLOWED","message":"no"}`)}, "ssh.helper_refused", "PATH_NOT_ALLOWED", false},
		{"failed", Result{ExitCode: 4, Stdout: []byte(`{"ok":false,"code":"IO_ERROR","message":"no"}`)}, "ssh.helper_refused", "IO_ERROR", false},
		{"hash mismatch", Result{ExitCode: 3, Stdout: []byte(`{"ok":false,"code":"HASH_MISMATCH","message":"x"}`)}, "ssh.file_changed", "HASH_MISMATCH", true},
		{"not found", Result{ExitCode: 3, Stdout: []byte(`{"ok":false,"code":"NOT_FOUND","message":"x"}`)}, "ssh.helper_refused", "NOT_FOUND", false},
		{"hostile code", Result{ExitCode: 2, Stdout: []byte(`{"ok":false,"code":"X; rm -rf /","message":"x"}`)}, "ssh.protocol_error", "", false},
		{"error with ok true", Result{ExitCode: 2, Stdout: []byte(`{"ok":true,"code":"USAGE"}`)}, "ssh.protocol_error", "", false},
		{"sudo refused", Result{ExitCode: 1, Stdout: nil}, "ssh.helper_missing", "", false},
		{"not installed", Result{ExitCode: 127}, "ssh.helper_missing", "", false},
	} {
		_, err := DecodeHelper[out](tc.r, "authkeys-read")
		pe := providerCode(t, err)
		assert.Equal(t, tc.code, pe.Code, tc.name)
		assert.Equal(t, tc.retry, pe.Retryable, tc.name)
		assert.Equal(t, tc.helper, pe.Params["helper_code"], tc.name)
		assert.Equal(t, "authkeys-read", pe.Params["subcommand"], tc.name)
	}
}

func TestParseConfig(t *testing.T) {
	c, errs := ParseConfig(providers.TargetConfig{"host": "web-01.example.com", "port": float64(2222), "username": "deploy"})
	require.Empty(t, errs)
	assert.Equal(t, Config{Host: "web-01.example.com", Port: 2222, Username: "deploy"}, c)

	c, errs = ParseConfig(providers.TargetConfig{"host": "2001:db8::5"})
	require.Empty(t, errs)
	assert.Equal(t, Config{Host: "2001:db8::5", Port: 22, Username: "alice-svc"}, c)

	_, errs = ParseConfig(providers.TargetConfig{"port": 0, "username": "Root!"})
	fields := map[string]string{}
	for _, e := range errs {
		fields[e.Field] = e.Code
	}
	assert.Equal(t, map[string]string{"host": validate.Required, "port": validate.OutOfRange, "username": validate.Pattern}, fields)

	_, errs = ParseConfig(providers.TargetConfig{"host": "web 01; id", "port": "22"})
	fields = map[string]string{}
	for _, e := range errs {
		fields[e.Field] = e.Code
	}
	assert.Equal(t, map[string]string{"host": validate.Pattern, "port": validate.OutOfRange}, fields)
}
```

```go
// Only dial.go opens SSH sessions, so Conn.Run (with its timeout, output cap and the
// constructor-built command line) is the only way a command reaches a server (SEC-063).
func TestOnlyDialCreatesSessions(t *testing.T) {
	files, err := filepath.Glob("*.go")
	require.NoError(t, err)
	fset := token.NewFileSet()
	found := 0
	for _, name := range files {
		if strings.HasSuffix(name, "_test.go") {
			continue
		}
		f, err := parser.ParseFile(fset, name, nil, 0)
		require.NoError(t, err)
		ast.Inspect(f, func(n ast.Node) bool {
			call, ok := n.(*ast.CallExpr)
			if !ok {
				return true
			}
			sel, ok := call.Fun.(*ast.SelectorExpr)
			if !ok {
				return true
			}
			switch sel.Sel.Name {
			case "NewSession", "Shell", "RequestPty":
				if name != "dial.go" || sel.Sel.Name != "NewSession" {
					t.Errorf("%s: %s outside dial.go's Conn.Run", fset.Position(call.Pos()), sel.Sel.Name)
				}
				found++
			}
			return true
		})
	}
	assert.Equal(t, 1, found, "exactly one NewSession call, in Conn.Run")
}

// Nothing in the repository may accept every host key (SEC-080). The needles are built at run
// time so this file does not match itself.
func TestNoCodeAcceptsAnyHostKey(t *testing.T) {
	root, err := filepath.Abs("../../..")
	require.NoError(t, err)
	_, err = os.Stat(filepath.Join(root, "go.mod"))
	require.NoError(t, err, "repository root not found")
	insecure := "ssh." + "InsecureIgnoreHostKey"
	strict := "StrictHostKeyChecking" + "=no"
	skip := map[string]bool{".git": true, "node_modules": true, "docs": true, "bin": true, "dist": true,
		"playwright-report": true, "test-results": true}
	scanned := 0
	err = filepath.WalkDir(root, func(path string, d fs.DirEntry, err error) error {
		if err != nil {
			return err
		}
		if d.IsDir() {
			if skip[d.Name()] {
				return filepath.SkipDir
			}
			return nil
		}
		ext := filepath.Ext(path)
		switch {
		case ext == ".go", ext == ".sh", ext == ".yml", ext == ".yaml", ext == ".ts", ext == ".tsx", ext == ".js",
			strings.HasPrefix(d.Name(), "Dockerfile"), ext == ".conf":
		default:
			return nil
		}
		b, err := os.ReadFile(path) //nolint:gosec // G304: walking the repository in a test
		if err != nil {
			return err
		}
		scanned++
		if strings.Contains(string(b), insecure) {
			t.Errorf("%s uses %s", path, insecure)
		}
		if strings.Contains(string(b), strict) {
			t.Errorf("%s disables host key checking", path)
		}
		return nil
	})
	require.NoError(t, err)
	assert.Greater(t, scanned, 100, "the walk found too few files; is it scanning the repository?")
}
```

```go
// Package linuxssh is the linuxssh provider: an SSH connector with strict host-key pinning whose
// only remote command surface is the root-owned alice-helper (spec §6.6, §12.3, §13; R13, R21).
package linuxssh

import (
	"bytes"
	"context"
	"crypto/subtle"
	"encoding/json"
	"errors"
	"io"
	"net"
	"regexp"
	"strconv"
	"strings"
	"sync"
	"sync/atomic"
	"time"
	"unicode/utf8"

	"github.com/google/uuid"
	"golang.org/x/crypto/ssh"

	"alice/internal/platform/clock"
	"alice/internal/platform/validate"
	"alice/internal/providers"
	"alice/internal/providers/linuxssh/helperproto"
)

// Budgets of one connection and one command (R37 item 17).
const (
	DefaultDialTimeout      = 10 * time.Second
	DefaultHandshakeTimeout = 15 * time.Second
	DefaultCommandTimeout   = 30 * time.Second
	LongCommandTimeout      = 60 * time.Second
	DefaultMaxOutput        = 8 << 20

	maxStderr      = 64 << 10
	osReleaseLimit = 64 << 10
	maxFactLength  = 200
)

// Algorithms (SEC-080). x/crypto adds the curve25519-sha256@libssh.org alias itself when
// curve25519-sha256 is requested.
var (
	kexAlgorithms = []string{ssh.KeyExchangeMLKEM768X25519, ssh.KeyExchangeCurve25519,
		ssh.KeyExchangeECDHP256, ssh.KeyExchangeECDHP384, ssh.KeyExchangeECDHP521}
	cipherAlgorithms     = []string{ssh.CipherChaCha20Poly1305, ssh.CipherAES256GCM, ssh.CipherAES128GCM}
	macAlgorithms        = []string{ssh.HMACSHA256ETM, ssh.HMACSHA512ETM}
	allHostKeyAlgorithms = []string{ssh.KeyAlgoED25519, ssh.KeyAlgoECDSA256, ssh.KeyAlgoECDSA384,
		ssh.KeyAlgoECDSA521, ssh.KeyAlgoRSASHA512, ssh.KeyAlgoRSASHA256}
)

// hostKeyAlgorithmsFor restricts the handshake to the pinned key's algorithms: an RSA key is
// accepted only with SHA-2 signatures.
func hostKeyAlgorithmsFor(pinnedType string) []string {
	if pinnedType == ssh.KeyAlgoRSA {
		return []string{ssh.KeyAlgoRSASHA512, ssh.KeyAlgoRSASHA256}
	}
	return []string{pinnedType}
}

func sshConfig() ssh.Config {
	return ssh.Config{KeyExchanges: kexAlgorithms, Ciphers: cipherAlgorithms, MACs: macAlgorithms}
}

// HostKeyOf converts an SSH public key into the stored form.
func HostKeyOf(k ssh.PublicKey) providers.HostKey {
	return providers.HostKey{Type: k.Type(), PublicKey: k.Marshal(), Fingerprint: ssh.FingerprintSHA256(k)}
}

// Config is the SSH endpoint of a target (targets.config).
type Config struct {
	Host     string
	Port     int
	Username string
}

func (c Config) addr() string { return net.JoinHostPort(c.Host, strconv.Itoa(c.Port)) }

// ServiceUser is the account the setup script creates on every target.
const ServiceUser = "alice-svc"

// ParseConfig reads a target configuration. The inventory normalizes and validates the address
// when a target is added; this is the provider's own check (no network).
func ParseConfig(cfg providers.TargetConfig) (Config, []validate.FieldError) {
	var errs validate.Errors
	c := Config{Port: 22, Username: ServiceUser}
	host, _ := cfg["host"].(string)
	switch {
	case host == "":
		errs.Add("host", validate.Required, nil)
	case len(host) > 253 || strings.ContainsAny(host, " \t\r\n/\\@'\"`$;|&<>()*?~") || !utf8.ValidString(host):
		errs.Add("host", validate.Pattern, nil)
	default:
		c.Host = host
	}
	if v, ok := cfg["port"]; ok && v != nil {
		p, ok := toInt(v)
		if !ok || p < 1 || p > 65535 {
			errs.Add("port", validate.OutOfRange, map[string]string{"min": "1", "max": "65535"})
		} else {
			c.Port = p
		}
	}
	if v, ok := cfg["username"]; ok && v != nil {
		u, _ := v.(string)
		if !helperproto.ValidUser(u) {
			errs.Add("username", validate.Pattern, nil)
		} else {
			c.Username = u
		}
	}
	if len(errs) == 0 {
		return c, nil
	}
	return c, []validate.FieldError(errs)
}

func toInt(v any) (int, bool) {
	switch n := v.(type) {
	case int:
		return n, true
	case int64:
		if n < -1<<31 || n > 1<<31-1 {
			return 0, false
		}
		return int(n), true
	case float64:
		if n != float64(int(n)) {
			return 0, false
		}
		return int(n), true
	case json.Number:
		i, err := n.Int64()
		if err != nil || i < -1<<31 || i > 1<<31-1 {
			return 0, false
		}
		return int(i), true
	default:
		return 0, false
	}
}

// Dialer opens SSH connections that trust only the pinned host key of a target (SEC-080).
type Dialer struct {
	Clock            clock.Clock
	HostKeys         providers.HostKeyStore
	DialTimeout      time.Duration
	HandshakeTimeout time.Duration
	NetDial          func(ctx context.Context, network, addr string) (net.Conn, error) // nil = net.Dialer
}

func (d *Dialer) clk() clock.Clock {
	if d.Clock == nil {
		return clock.Real{}
	}
	return d.Clock
}

func (d *Dialer) dialTimeout() time.Duration {
	if d.DialTimeout <= 0 {
		return DefaultDialTimeout
	}
	return d.DialTimeout
}

func (d *Dialer) handshakeTimeout() time.Duration {
	if d.HandshakeTimeout <= 0 {
		return DefaultHandshakeTimeout
	}
	return d.HandshakeTimeout
}

var (
	errHostKeyRefused = errors.New("linuxssh: host key refused")
	errConnClosed     = errors.New("linuxssh: connection closed")
	errOutputTooLarge = errors.New("linuxssh: command output too large")
)

// hostKeyDecision is what the host-key callback saw; it is read after the handshake returns, so
// the outcome never depends on how x/crypto wraps the callback's error.
type hostKeyDecision struct {
	called    bool
	refused   bool
	changed   bool
	presented providers.HostKey
}

// Dial connects to target. Without a pinned key the presented key is recorded as observed and the
// connection stops before authentication (target.host_key_unconfirmed); a key other than the
// pinned one, or a server that no longer offers the pinned algorithm, is recorded as changed and
// the connection stops before authentication (target.host_key_changed). Background work can never
// pin a key: only the inventory's confirmation does.
func (d *Dialer) Dial(ctx context.Context, target uuid.UUID, cfg Config, cred providers.CredentialSource) (*Conn, error) {
	if d.HostKeys == nil {
		return nil, providers.NewError("internal.unexpected", false, errors.New("linuxssh: dialer has no host key store"), nil)
	}
	pinned, err := d.HostKeys.Pinned(ctx, target)
	havePin := err == nil
	if err != nil && !errors.Is(err, providers.ErrNoPinnedKey) {
		return nil, providers.NewError("internal.unexpected", true, err, nil)
	}
	signer, release, err := cred.SSHSigner(ctx)
	if err != nil {
		return nil, providers.NewError("internal.unexpected", false, err, nil)
	}
	defer release()

	var dec hostKeyDecision
	var observeErr error
	algorithms := allHostKeyAlgorithms
	if havePin {
		algorithms = hostKeyAlgorithmsFor(pinned.Type)
	}
	conf := &ssh.ClientConfig{
		Config:            sshConfig(),
		User:              cfg.Username,
		Auth:              []ssh.AuthMethod{ssh.PublicKeys(signer)},
		HostKeyAlgorithms: algorithms,
		HostKeyCallback: func(_ string, _ net.Addr, key ssh.PublicKey) error {
			dec.called = true
			dec.presented = HostKeyOf(key)
			if havePin && subtle.ConstantTimeCompare(key.Marshal(), pinned.PublicKey) == 1 {
				return nil
			}
			dec.refused, dec.changed = true, havePin
			observeErr = d.HostKeys.Observed(ctx, target, dec.presented, havePin)
			return errHostKeyRefused
		},
	}
	r := d.handshake(ctx, cfg.addr(), conf)
	if r.dialErr != nil {
		return nil, providers.NewError("ssh.unreachable", true, r.dialErr, nil)
	}
	if r.err != nil {
		switch {
		case observeErr != nil:
			return nil, providers.NewError("internal.unexpected", true, observeErr, nil)
		case dec.refused && dec.changed:
			return nil, changedError(pinned, dec.presented)
		case dec.refused:
			return nil, providers.NewError("target.host_key_unconfirmed", false, nil,
				map[string]string{"fingerprint": dec.presented.Fingerprint})
		case r.timedOut:
			return nil, providers.NewError("ssh.timeout", true, r.err, nil)
		case havePin && !dec.called:
			return nil, d.probeChanged(ctx, target, cfg, pinned, r.err)
		case dec.called && strings.Contains(r.err.Error(), "unable to authenticate"):
			return nil, providers.NewError("ssh.auth_failed", false, r.err, nil)
		default:
			return nil, providers.NewError("ssh.unreachable", true, r.err, nil)
		}
	}
	return &Conn{client: r.client, target: target, cfg: cfg, hostKey: dec.presented, clock: d.clk()}, nil
}

func changedError(old, presented providers.HostKey) error {
	return providers.NewError("target.host_key_changed", false, nil,
		map[string]string{"old_fingerprint": old.Fingerprint, "new_fingerprint": presented.Fingerprint})
}

// probeChanged runs after a handshake with the pinned algorithms failed before any host key was
// presented: it asks once for any host key (and always aborts before authentication). A key other
// than the pinned one means the server's identity changed.
func (d *Dialer) probeChanged(ctx context.Context, target uuid.UUID, cfg Config, pinned providers.HostKey, cause error) error {
	var seen *providers.HostKey
	conf := &ssh.ClientConfig{
		Config:            sshConfig(),
		User:              cfg.Username,
		HostKeyAlgorithms: allHostKeyAlgorithms,
		HostKeyCallback: func(_ string, _ net.Addr, key ssh.PublicKey) error {
			hk := HostKeyOf(key)
			seen = &hk
			return errHostKeyRefused
		},
	}
	r := d.handshake(ctx, cfg.addr(), conf)
	if r.client != nil {
		_ = r.client.Close() // cannot happen: the callback always refuses
	}
	switch {
	case seen == nil && r.dialErr != nil:
		return providers.NewError("ssh.unreachable", true, r.dialErr, nil)
	case seen == nil && r.timedOut:
		return providers.NewError("ssh.timeout", true, cause, nil)
	case seen == nil, subtle.ConstantTimeCompare(seen.PublicKey, pinned.PublicKey) == 1:
		return providers.NewError("ssh.protocol_error", false, cause, nil)
	}
	if err := d.HostKeys.Observed(ctx, target, *seen, true); err != nil {
		return providers.NewError("internal.unexpected", true, err, nil)
	}
	return changedError(pinned, *seen)
}

type handshakeResult struct {
	client   *ssh.Client
	dialErr  error
	err      error
	timedOut bool
}

// handshake dials addr and runs the SSH handshake within the handshake budget of the injected
// clock; cancelling ctx aborts it.
func (d *Dialer) handshake(ctx context.Context, addr string, conf *ssh.ClientConfig) handshakeResult {
	dial := d.NetDial
	if dial == nil {
		dial = (&net.Dialer{Timeout: d.dialTimeout()}).DialContext
	}
	nc, err := dial(ctx, "tcp", addr)
	if err != nil {
		return handshakeResult{dialErr: err}
	}
	done := make(chan struct{})
	var timedOut atomic.Bool
	go func() {
		select {
		case <-done:
		case <-ctx.Done():
			timedOut.Store(true)
			_ = nc.Close()
		case <-d.clk().After(d.handshakeTimeout()):
			timedOut.Store(true)
			_ = nc.Close()
		}
	}()
	c, chans, reqs, err := ssh.NewClientConn(nc, addr, conf)
	close(done)
	if err != nil {
		_ = nc.Close()
		return handshakeResult{err: err, timedOut: timedOut.Load()}
	}
	client := ssh.NewClient(c, chans, reqs)
	if timedOut.Load() {
		_ = client.Close()
		return handshakeResult{err: errConnClosed, timedOut: true}
	}
	return handshakeResult{client: client}
}

// Conn is one authenticated SSH connection to a target whose host key matched its pin.
type Conn struct {
	client  *ssh.Client
	target  uuid.UUID
	cfg     Config
	hostKey providers.HostKey
	clock   clock.Clock

	mu     sync.Mutex
	broken bool
	closed bool
}

// Result is what a command returned. Helper exit codes stay here; DecodeHelper interprets them.
type Result struct {
	Stdout   []byte
	ExitCode int
}

// HostKey is the (pinned) key the server presented.
func (c *Conn) HostKey() providers.HostKey { return c.hostKey }

// Healthy reports whether the connection may run further commands.
func (c *Conn) Healthy() bool {
	c.mu.Lock()
	defer c.mu.Unlock()
	return !c.broken && !c.closed
}

func (c *Conn) markBroken() {
	c.mu.Lock()
	c.broken = true
	c.mu.Unlock()
	_ = c.client.Close()
}

// Close closes the connection.
func (c *Conn) Close() error {
	c.mu.Lock()
	already := c.closed
	c.closed = true
	c.mu.Unlock()
	if already {
		return nil
	}
	return c.client.Close()
}

// Run executes one constructor-built command in a new session. A command that exceeds its time
// budget, a cancelled context or an output flood closes the whole connection (it is never reused).
// Remote stderr is capped and discarded: it is never logged or shown (SC-4).
func (c *Conn) Run(ctx context.Context, cmd HelperCommand) (Result, error) {
	line := cmd.Line()
	params := map[string]string{"subcommand": cmd.Subcommand()}
	if line == "" {
		return Result{}, providers.NewError("ssh.protocol_error", false, ErrInvalidArgument, params)
	}
	if !c.Healthy() {
		return Result{}, providers.NewError("ssh.unreachable", true, errConnClosed, params)
	}
	sess, err := c.client.NewSession()
	if err != nil {
		c.markBroken()
		return Result{}, providers.NewError("ssh.unreachable", true, err, params)
	}
	defer func() { _ = sess.Close() }()
	stdout := &cappedWriter{max: cmd.maxOutput, onOverflow: func() { _ = sess.Close() }}
	sess.Stdout = stdout
	sess.Stderr = &cappedWriter{max: maxStderr, discard: true}
	sess.Stdin = bytes.NewReader(cmd.stdin)
	timeout := cmd.timeout
	if timeout <= 0 {
		timeout = DefaultCommandTimeout
	}
	done := make(chan error, 1)
	go func() { done <- sess.Run(line) }()
	var runErr error
	select {
	case runErr = <-done:
	case <-c.clock.After(timeout):
		c.markBroken()
		<-done
		return Result{}, providers.NewError("ssh.timeout", true, nil, params)
	case <-ctx.Done():
		c.markBroken()
		<-done
		return Result{}, providers.NewError("ssh.timeout", true, ctx.Err(), params)
	}
	if stdout.overflowed() {
		c.markBroken()
		return Result{}, providers.NewError("ssh.output_too_large", false, errOutputTooLarge, params)
	}
	var exitErr *ssh.ExitError
	var missing *ssh.ExitMissingError
	switch {
	case runErr == nil:
		return Result{Stdout: stdout.bytes()}, nil
	case errors.As(runErr, &exitErr):
		return Result{Stdout: stdout.bytes(), ExitCode: exitErr.ExitStatus()}, nil
	case errors.As(runErr, &missing):
		return Result{}, providers.NewError("ssh.protocol_error", false, runErr, params)
	default:
		c.markBroken()
		return Result{}, providers.NewError("ssh.unreachable", true, runErr, params)
	}
}

// OSRelease runs the one fixed non-helper command and keeps ID, VERSION_ID and PRETTY_NAME.
func (c *Conn) OSRelease(ctx context.Context) (providers.OSRelease, error) {
	res, err := c.Run(ctx, HelperCommand{fixed: OSReleaseCommand, timeout: DefaultCommandTimeout, maxOutput: osReleaseLimit})
	if err != nil {
		return providers.OSRelease{}, err
	}
	if res.ExitCode != 0 {
		return providers.OSRelease{}, providers.NewError("ssh.protocol_error", false, nil, map[string]string{"subcommand": "os-release"})
	}
	var r providers.OSRelease
	for _, l := range strings.Split(string(res.Stdout), "\n") {
		k, v, ok := strings.Cut(strings.TrimSpace(l), "=")
		if !ok {
			continue
		}
		switch k {
		case "ID":
			r.ID = cleanValue(v, maxFactLength)
		case "VERSION_ID":
			r.VersionID = cleanValue(v, maxFactLength)
		case "PRETTY_NAME":
			r.PrettyName = cleanValue(v, maxFactLength)
		}
	}
	return r, nil
}

// cleanValue makes remote text safe to store and show: quotes around it removed, invalid UTF-8
// and control characters (terminal escapes) dropped, length limited (SC-4).
func cleanValue(v string, limit int) string {
	v = strings.TrimSpace(v)
	if len(v) >= 2 && (v[0] == '"' || v[0] == '\'') && v[len(v)-1] == v[0] {
		v = v[1 : len(v)-1]
	}
	v = strings.ToValidUTF8(v, "")
	v = strings.Map(func(r rune) rune {
		if r < 0x20 || r == 0x7f {
			return -1
		}
		return r
	}, v)
	if utf8.RuneCountInString(v) > limit {
		v = string([]rune(v)[:limit])
	}
	return v
}

// cappedWriter keeps at most max bytes. Over the cap it either discards (stderr) or fails and
// closes the session through onOverflow (stdout).
type cappedWriter struct {
	mu         sync.Mutex
	buf        bytes.Buffer
	max        int64
	discard    bool
	over       bool
	onOverflow func()
}

func (w *cappedWriter) Write(p []byte) (int, error) {
	w.mu.Lock()
	defer w.mu.Unlock()
	if w.over {
		if w.discard {
			return len(p), nil
		}
		return 0, errOutputTooLarge
	}
	if int64(w.buf.Len())+int64(len(p)) > w.max {
		w.over = true
		if w.discard {
			w.buf.Write(p[:int(w.max)-w.buf.Len()])
			return len(p), nil
		}
		if w.onOverflow != nil {
			go w.onOverflow() // not inside Write: the session's copy goroutine is calling us
		}
		return 0, errOutputTooLarge
	}
	w.buf.Write(p)
	return len(p), nil
}

func (w *cappedWriter) overflowed() bool {
	w.mu.Lock()
	defer w.mu.Unlock()
	return w.over && !w.discard
}

func (w *cappedWriter) bytes() []byte {
	w.mu.Lock()
	defer w.mu.Unlock()
	return append([]byte(nil), w.buf.Bytes()...)
}

var helperCodeRE = regexp.MustCompile(`^[A-Z][A-Z_]{0,39}$`)

// decodeOne decodes exactly one JSON value.
func decodeOne(b []byte, dst any) error {
	dec := json.NewDecoder(bytes.NewReader(b))
	if err := dec.Decode(dst); err != nil {
		return err
	}
	if _, err := dec.Token(); !errors.Is(err, io.EOF) {
		return errors.New("linuxssh: trailing data after the helper's answer")
	}
	return nil
}

// DecodeHelper turns a helper Result into its typed answer or a *providers.Error. Exit 0 must carry
// {"ok": true, …}; exits 2, 3 and 4 carry the helper's error code (only a fixed-format code is
// kept: remote text never reaches messages); any other exit means sudo or the helper itself is
// missing (spec §12.9).
func DecodeHelper[T any](r Result, sub string) (T, error) {
	var zero T
	params := map[string]string{"subcommand": sub}
	protocol := func(cause error) (T, error) {
		return zero, providers.NewError("ssh.protocol_error", false, cause, map[string]string{"subcommand": sub})
	}
	switch r.ExitCode {
	case helperproto.ExitOK:
		var head struct {
			OK *bool `json:"ok"`
		}
		if err := decodeOne(r.Stdout, &head); err != nil {
			return protocol(err)
		}
		if head.OK == nil || !*head.OK {
			return protocol(errors.New("linuxssh: helper answer without ok=true"))
		}
		var out T
		if err := decodeOne(r.Stdout, &out); err != nil {
			return protocol(err)
		}
		return out, nil
	case helperproto.ExitRefused, helperproto.ExitPrecondition, helperproto.ExitFailed:
		var e helperproto.ErrorResponse
		if err := decodeOne(r.Stdout, &e); err != nil {
			return protocol(err)
		}
		if e.OK || !helperCodeRE.MatchString(e.Code) {
			return protocol(errors.New("linuxssh: malformed helper error"))
		}
		params["helper_code"] = e.Code
		if r.ExitCode == helperproto.ExitPrecondition && e.Code == helperproto.CodeHashMismatch {
			return zero, providers.NewError("ssh.file_changed", true, nil, params)
		}
		return zero, providers.NewError("ssh.helper_refused", false, nil, params)
	default:
		params["exit_code"] = strconv.Itoa(r.ExitCode)
		return zero, providers.NewError("ssh.helper_missing", false, nil, params)
	}
}
```

### Task 9: Connection pool, the `linuxssh` provider (TestConnection, Discover) and setup snippets

The pool bounds SSH connections (10 in total, 2 per target), reuses an idle connection for up to 60 s only while the
target's pin still matches it, and frees every slot after any failure. The `linuxsshtest.Emulator` answers helper
command lines exactly like the real helper (Tasks 6–7) so the provider can be tested end to end over a real SSH
session. The provider implements `providers.Provider` and `providers.SetupGuide`: `Open` checks the helper protocol,
`TestConnection` proves SSH, sudo and the helper work, `Discover` reads host keys, the effective sshd settings and
every `authorized_keys` file the helper lists, and turns them into the inventory input with warnings. `setup.go`
generates the `authorized_keys` line, the two sudoers profiles of spec §12.3 and the root setup script.

**Files:**
- Create: `internal/providers/linuxssh/pool.go`, `internal/providers/linuxssh/pool_test.go`
- Create: `internal/providers/linuxssh/linuxsshtest/emulator.go`
- Create: `internal/providers/linuxssh/provider.go`, `internal/providers/linuxssh/discover.go`

```go
package linuxssh

import (

	"net"
	"testing"

	"github.com/google/uuid"
	"github.com/stretchr/testify/assert"
	"github.com/stretchr/testify/require"

	"alice/internal/providers/linuxssh/linuxsshtest"
)

var otherTarget = uuid.MustParse("0190f5a0-0000-7000-8000-0000000000a2")

type poolEnv struct {
	srv  *linuxsshtest.Server
	cfg  Config
	cred *fakeCred
	hk   *memHostKeys
	pool *Pool
}

func newPoolEnv(t *testing.T, clk clock.Clock, max, perTarget int) *poolEnv {
	t.Helper()
	srv, cfg, cred := testServer(t, okHandler)
	hk := &memHostKeys{}
	hk.pin(srv.HostKey())
	p := NewPool(&Dialer{Clock: clk, HostKeys: hk}, max, perTarget, IdleTimeout)
	t.Cleanup(p.Close)
	return &poolEnv{srv: srv, cfg: cfg, cred: cred, hk: hk, pool: p}
}

func shortCtx(t *testing.T, d time.Duration) context.Context {
	t.Helper()
	ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(context.Background(), d)
	t.Cleanup(cancel)
	return ctx
}

func TestPoolReusesIdleConnectionUntilItExpires(t *testing.T) {
	fake := clock.NewFake(time.Date(2026, 10, 1, 9, 0, 0, 0, time.UTC))
	e := newPoolEnv(t, fake, 2, 1)
	ctx := context.Background()

	c1, rel1, err := e.pool.Acquire(ctx, testTarget, e.cfg, e.cred)
	require.NoError(t, err)
	rel1(true)
	afterFirst := e.srv.AuthAttempts()
	require.Positive(t, afterFirst)

	c2, rel2, err := e.pool.Acquire(ctx, testTarget, e.cfg, e.cred)
	require.NoError(t, err)
	assert.Same(t, c1, c2, "an idle connection is reused")
	assert.Equal(t, afterFirst, e.srv.AuthAttempts(), "no new connection")
	rel2(true)

	fake.Advance(IdleTimeout)
	c3, rel3, err := e.pool.Acquire(ctx, testTarget, e.cfg, e.cred)
	require.NoError(t, err)
	defer rel3(true)
	assert.NotSame(t, c1, c3, "an expired idle connection is closed, not reused")
	assert.False(t, c1.Healthy())
	assert.Greater(t, e.srv.AuthAttempts(), afterFirst)
}

func TestPoolLimitsConnectionsPerTarget(t *testing.T) {
	e := newPoolEnv(t, clock.Real{}, 2, 1)
	_, rel1, err := e.pool.Acquire(context.Background(), testTarget, e.cfg, e.cred)
	require.NoError(t, err)

	_, _, err = e.pool.Acquire(shortCtx(t, 200*time.Millisecond), testTarget, e.cfg, e.cred)
	pe := providerCode(t, err)
	assert.Equal(t, "ssh.timeout", pe.Code)
	assert.True(t, pe.Retryable)

	rel1(true)
	_, rel2, err := e.pool.Acquire(shortCtx(t, 2*time.Second), testTarget, e.cfg, e.cred)
	require.NoError(t, err)
	rel2(true)
}

func TestPoolLimitsConnectionsInTotal(t *testing.T) {
	e := newPoolEnv(t, clock.Real{}, 1, 1)
	_, rel1, err := e.pool.Acquire(context.Background(), testTarget, e.cfg, e.cred)
	require.NoError(t, err)
	_, _, err = e.pool.Acquire(shortCtx(t, 200*time.Millisecond), otherTarget, e.cfg, e.cred)
	assert.Equal(t, "ssh.timeout", providerCode(t, err).Code)
	rel1(true)
	_, rel2, err := e.pool.Acquire(shortCtx(t, 2*time.Second), otherTarget, e.cfg, e.cred)
	require.NoError(t, err)
	rel2(true)
}

// Review Focus 3: a failed dial and a connection broken by a timeout both give their slot back,
// and a broken connection is never handed out again.
func TestPoolReleasesSlotAfterFailure(t *testing.T) {
	e := newPoolEnv(t, clock.Real{}, 1, 1)
	ln, err := net.Listen("tcp", "127.0.0.1:0")
	require.NoError(t, err)
	deadPort := ln.Addr().(*net.TCPAddr).Port
	require.NoError(t, ln.Close())
	dead := Config{Host: "127.0.0.1", Port: deadPort, Username: "alice-svc"}

	_, _, err = e.pool.Acquire(context.Background(), testTarget, dead, e.cred)
	assert.Equal(t, "ssh.unreachable", providerCode(t, err).Code)

	c, rel, err := e.pool.Acquire(shortCtx(t, 2*time.Second), testTarget, e.cfg, e.cred)
	require.NoError(t, err, "the failed dial freed its slot")

	e.srv.SetHandler(func(string, []byte) linuxsshtest.Response {
		return linuxsshtest.Response{Delay: 10 * time.Second}
	})
	cmd := CmdSSHDDump()
	cmd.timeout = 300 * time.Millisecond
	_, err = c.Run(context.Background(), cmd)
	assert.Equal(t, "ssh.timeout", providerCode(t, err).Code)
	before := e.srv.AuthAttempts()
	rel(true) // the caller claims healthy; the pool checks the connection itself

	c2, rel2, err := e.pool.Acquire(shortCtx(t, 2*time.Second), testTarget, e.cfg, e.cred)
	require.NoError(t, err, "the broken connection freed its slot")
	defer rel2(true)
	assert.NotSame(t, c, c2)
	assert.Greater(t, e.srv.AuthAttempts(), before, "a new connection was opened")
}

// An idle connection belongs to the key that was pinned when it was opened: after a re-pin it is
// closed and the next connection is checked against the new pin.
func TestPoolDropsIdleConnectionAfterRepin(t *testing.T) {
	e := newPoolEnv(t, clock.Real{}, 2, 1)
	c1, rel1, err := e.pool.Acquire(context.Background(), testTarget, e.cfg, e.cred)
	require.NoError(t, err)
	rel1(true)
	e.hk.pin(linuxsshtest.NewHostKey(t).PublicKey())

	_, _, err = e.pool.Acquire(context.Background(), testTarget, e.cfg, e.cred)
	assert.Equal(t, "target.host_key_changed", providerCode(t, err).Code)
	assert.False(t, c1.Healthy())
}

func TestPoolCloseClosesIdleConnectionsAndRefusesAcquire(t *testing.T) {
	e := newPoolEnv(t, clock.Real{}, 2, 1)
	c1, rel1, err := e.pool.Acquire(context.Background(), testTarget, e.cfg, e.cred)
	require.NoError(t, err)
	rel1(true)
	e.pool.Close()
	assert.False(t, c1.Healthy())
	_, _, err = e.pool.Acquire(context.Background(), testTarget, e.cfg, e.cred)
	assert.Equal(t, "ssh.unreachable", providerCode(t, err).Code)
}

func TestPoolReleaseIsIdempotent(t *testing.T) {
	e := newPoolEnv(t, clock.Real{}, 1, 1)
	_, rel, err := e.pool.Acquire(context.Background(), testTarget, e.cfg, e.cred)
	require.NoError(t, err)
	rel(false)
	rel(false) // a second release must not free a slot twice (it would block forever on an empty channel)
	_, rel2, err := e.pool.Acquire(shortCtx(t, 2*time.Second), testTarget, e.cfg, e.cred)
	require.NoError(t, err)
	rel2(true)
}
```

- [ ] **Step 2: Implement the pool**

Create `internal/providers/linuxssh/pool.go`:

```go
package linuxssh

import (
	"context"
	"crypto/subtle"
	"errors"
	"sync"
	"time"

	"github.com/google/uuid"

	"alice/internal/providers"
)

// Connection limits (spec §8.5, §12.5; R37 item 17).
const (
	MaxConnections          = 10
	MaxConnectionsPerTarget = 2
	IdleTimeout             = 60 * time.Second
)

var errPoolClosed = errors.New("linuxssh: connection pool closed")

type idleConn struct {
	conn  *Conn
	since time.Time
}

// Pool bounds SSH connections: at most max in use (and at most max idle), at most perTarget in use
// per target. An idle connection is reused for at most idle time, and only while the target's
// pinned key is still the key the connection was opened with.
type Pool struct {
	dialer    *Dialer
	idleFor   time.Duration
	perTarget int
	maxIdle   int
	global    chan struct{}

	mu      sync.Mutex
	closed  bool
	targets map[uuid.UUID]chan struct{}
	idle    map[uuid.UUID][]idleConn
	idleN   int
}

// NewPool returns a pool; zero or negative limits take the defaults.
func NewPool(d *Dialer, max, perTarget int, idle time.Duration) *Pool {
	if max <= 0 {
		max = MaxConnections
	}
	if perTarget <= 0 {
		perTarget = MaxConnectionsPerTarget
	}
	if perTarget > max {
		perTarget = max
	}
	if idle <= 0 {
		idle = IdleTimeout
	}
	return &Pool{
		dialer: d, idleFor: idle, perTarget: perTarget, maxIdle: max,
		global:  make(chan struct{}, max),
		targets: map[uuid.UUID]chan struct{}{},
		idle:    map[uuid.UUID][]idleConn{},
	}
}

func waitSlot(ctx context.Context, ch chan struct{}) error {
	select {
	case ch <- struct{}{}:
		return nil
	case <-ctx.Done():
		return ctx.Err()
	}
}

func slotError(err error) error {
	return providers.NewError("ssh.timeout", true, err, map[string]string{"wait": "connection_slot"})
}

func (p *Pool) targetSlots(target uuid.UUID) (chan struct{}, error) {
	p.mu.Lock()
	defer p.mu.Unlock()
	if p.closed {
		return nil, providers.NewError("ssh.unreachable", false, errPoolClosed, nil)
	}
	ch, ok := p.targets[target]
	if !ok {
		ch = make(chan struct{}, p.perTarget)
		p.targets[target] = ch
	}
	return ch, nil
}

// Acquire returns a connection to target and its release function. release(healthy) must be called
// exactly once (later calls do nothing); a connection that is not healthy is closed, never reused.
func (p *Pool) Acquire(ctx context.Context, target uuid.UUID, cfg Config, cred providers.CredentialSource) (*Conn, func(healthy bool), error) {
	tsem, err := p.targetSlots(target)
	if err != nil {
		return nil, nil, err
	}
	if err := waitSlot(ctx, tsem); err != nil {
		return nil, nil, slotError(err)
	}
	if err := waitSlot(ctx, p.global); err != nil {
		<-tsem
		return nil, nil, slotError(err)
	}
	slots := func() {
		<-p.global
		<-tsem
	}
	if c := p.takeIdle(ctx, target, cfg); c != nil {
		return c, p.releaser(target, c, slots), nil
	}
	c, err := p.dialer.Dial(ctx, target, cfg, cred)
	if err != nil {
		slots()
		return nil, nil, err
	}
	return c, p.releaser(target, c, slots), nil
}

// takeIdle hands out an idle connection of target opened with cfg whose key is still pinned.
func (p *Pool) takeIdle(ctx context.Context, target uuid.UUID, cfg Config) *Conn {
	now := p.dialer.clk().Now()
	var found *Conn
	var stale []*Conn
	p.mu.Lock()
	list := p.idle[target]
	keep := list[:0]
	for _, ic := range list {
		expired := now.Sub(ic.since) >= p.idleFor
		switch {
		case found == nil && !expired && ic.conn.cfg == cfg && ic.conn.Healthy():
			found = ic.conn
		case expired || !ic.conn.Healthy():
			stale = append(stale, ic.conn)
		default:
			keep = append(keep, ic)
		}
	}
	p.idleN -= len(list) - len(keep)
	if len(keep) == 0 {
		delete(p.idle, target)
	} else {
		p.idle[target] = keep
	}
	p.mu.Unlock()
	for _, c := range stale {
		_ = c.Close()
	}
	if found == nil {
		return nil
	}
	pinned, err := p.dialer.HostKeys.Pinned(ctx, target)
	if err != nil || subtle.ConstantTimeCompare(pinned.PublicKey, found.hostKey.PublicKey) != 1 {
		_ = found.Close()
		return nil
	}
	return found
}

// sweepLocked removes expired idle connections; the caller closes them after unlocking.
func (p *Pool) sweepLocked(now time.Time) []*Conn {
	var stale []*Conn
	for t, list := range p.idle {
		keep := list[:0]
		for _, ic := range list {
			if now.Sub(ic.since) >= p.idleFor {
				stale = append(stale, ic.conn)
				continue
			}
			keep = append(keep, ic)
		}
		p.idleN -= len(list) - len(keep)
		if len(keep) == 0 {
			delete(p.idle, t)
		} else {
			p.idle[t] = keep
		}
	}
	return stale
}

func (p *Pool) releaser(target uuid.UUID, c *Conn, slots func()) func(bool) {
	var once sync.Once
	return func(healthy bool) {
		once.Do(func() {
			defer slots()
			now := p.dialer.clk().Now()
			p.mu.Lock()
			stale := p.sweepLocked(now)
			keep := healthy && c.Healthy() && !p.closed && p.idleN < p.maxIdle
			if keep {
				p.idle[target] = append(p.idle[target], idleConn{conn: c, since: now})
				p.idleN++
			}
			p.mu.Unlock()
			for _, s := range stale {
				_ = s.Close()
			}
			if !keep {
				_ = c.Close()
			}
		})
	}
}

// Close closes every idle connection; connections in use are closed when released, and later
// Acquire calls fail.
func (p *Pool) Close() {
	p.mu.Lock()
	p.closed = true
	var all []*Conn
	for t, list := range p.idle {
		for _, ic := range list {
			all = append(all, ic.conn)
		}
		delete(p.idle, t)
	}
	p.idleN = 0
	p.mu.Unlock()
	for _, c := range all {
		_ = c.Close()
	}
}
```

```go
package linuxsshtest

import (
	"crypto/sha256"
	"encoding/base64"
	"encoding/hex"
	"encoding/json"
	"sort"
	"strings"
	"sync"

	"alice/internal/providers/linuxssh/helperproto"
	"alice/internal/providers/linuxssh/sshdconf"
)

// DefaultSSHD is the sshd -T text the emulator answers by default (OpenSSH defaults).
const DefaultSSHD = `port 22
pubkeyauthentication yes
passwordauthentication no
permitrootlogin prohibit-password
authorizedkeysfile .ssh/authorized_keys .ssh/authorized_keys2
authorizedkeyscommand none
strictmodes yes
hostkey /etc/ssh/ssh_host_ed25519_key
`

// DefaultOSRelease is what "cat /etc/os-release" answers by default.
const DefaultOSRelease = "PRETTY_NAME=\"Ubuntu 22.04.4 LTS\"\nNAME=\"Ubuntu\"\nVERSION_ID=\"22.04\"\nID=ubuntu\n"

type emuUser struct {
	name string
	uid  int
	home string
}

// Emulator answers alice-helper command lines the way the real helper does (cmd/alice-helper):
// the same JSON shapes, exit codes and argument checks, with the users and files given to it.
type Emulator struct {
	mu          sync.Mutex
	users       []emuUser
	files       map[string][]byte
	sshd        string
	osRelease   string
	protocol    int
	missing     bool
	insecure    map[string]bool
	failRead    map[string]bool
	hostKeys    []helperproto.HostKeyInfo
	beforeWrite func(path string)
	writes      []string
}

// NewEmulator returns an emulator with the users root, deploy (uid 1001) and alice-svc (uid 998,
// the SUDO_USER the real helper always lists) and no authorized_keys files.
func NewEmulator() *Emulator {
	return &Emulator{
		users: []emuUser{
			{name: "root", uid: 0, home: "/root"},
			{name: "deploy", uid: 1001, home: "/home/deploy"},
			{name: "alice-svc", uid: 998, home: "/var/lib/alice-svc"},
		},
		files:     map[string][]byte{},
		sshd:      DefaultSSHD,
		osRelease: DefaultOSRelease,
		protocol:  helperproto.Protocol,
		insecure:  map[string]bool{},
		failRead:  map[string]bool{},
		hostKeys: []helperproto.HostKeyInfo{{
			Type: "ssh-ed25519", Bits: 256, Fingerprint: "SHA256:emulatedHostKey00000000000000000000000000000",
			Path: "/etc/ssh/ssh_host_ed25519_key.pub",
		}},
	}
}

// SetFile stores a file (an authorized_keys file of one of the users).
func (e *Emulator) SetFile(path string, content []byte) {
	e.mu.Lock()
	defer e.mu.Unlock()
	e.files[path] = append([]byte(nil), content...)
}

// File returns a stored file.
func (e *Emulator) File(path string) ([]byte, bool) {
	e.mu.Lock()
	defer e.mu.Unlock()
	c, ok := e.files[path]
	return append([]byte(nil), c...), ok
}

// SetSSHD sets the sshd -T text; "" makes sshd -T fail (the helper then answers fallback).
func (e *Emulator) SetSSHD(config string) {
	e.mu.Lock()
	defer e.mu.Unlock()
	e.sshd = config
}

// SetOSRelease sets the answer of "cat /etc/os-release".
func (e *Emulator) SetOSRelease(text string) {
	e.mu.Lock()
	defer e.mu.Unlock()
	e.osRelease = text
}

// SetProtocol sets the protocol "version" answers.
func (e *Emulator) SetProtocol(p int) {
	e.mu.Lock()
	defer e.mu.Unlock()
	e.protocol = p
}

// SetHelperMissing makes every helper command fail like a server without alice-helper or sudoers.
func (e *Emulator) SetHelperMissing(missing bool) {
	e.mu.Lock()
	defer e.mu.Unlock()
	e.missing = missing
}

// AddUser adds an account with a home directory.
func (e *Emulator) AddUser(name string, uid int, home string) {
	e.mu.Lock()
	defer e.mu.Unlock()
	e.users = append(e.users, emuUser{name: name, uid: uid, home: home})
}

// SetInsecure reports path as failing sshd's StrictModes checks.
func (e *Emulator) SetInsecure(path string) {
	e.mu.Lock()
	defer e.mu.Unlock()
	e.insecure[path] = true
}

// FailRead makes authkeys-read of path fail with IO_ERROR.
func (e *Emulator) FailRead(path string) {
	e.mu.Lock()
	defer e.mu.Unlock()
	e.failRead[path] = true
}

// SetHostKeys sets the answer of "hostkeys".
func (e *Emulator) SetHostKeys(keys []helperproto.HostKeyInfo) {
	e.mu.Lock()
	defer e.mu.Unlock()
	e.hostKeys = append([]helperproto.HostKeyInfo(nil), keys...)
}

// BeforeWrite runs fn with the path of every authkeys-write, before the hash comparison (F-38).
func (e *Emulator) BeforeWrite(fn func(path string)) {
	e.mu.Lock()
	defer e.mu.Unlock()
	e.beforeWrite = fn
}

// Writes returns the paths authkeys-write changed, in order.
func (e *Emulator) Writes() []string {
	e.mu.Lock()
	defer e.mu.Unlock()
	return append([]string(nil), e.writes...)
}

// Handler answers command lines.
func (e *Emulator) Handler() Handler { return e.handle }

func answer(v any) Response {
	b, err := json.Marshal(v)
	if err != nil {
		return refuse(helperproto.ExitFailed, helperproto.CodeIOError)
	}
	return Response{Stdout: b}
}

func refuse(exit int, code string) Response {
	b, _ := json.Marshal(helperproto.ErrorResponse{OK: false, Code: code, Message: "refused by the emulator"})
	return Response{Stdout: b, Exit: exit}
}

func sum(b []byte) string {
	h := sha256.Sum256(b)
	return hex.EncodeToString(h[:])
}

// parseLine splits "[sudo -n ]<helper> <sub> <args>" and unquotes the arguments like the remote
// shell would; it reports ok=false for anything that is not a helper command line.
func parseLine(cmd string) (sudo bool, sub string, args []string, valid bool, ok bool) {
	rest := cmd
	if r, found := strings.CutPrefix(rest, "sudo -n "); found {
		sudo, rest = true, r
	}
	r, found := strings.CutPrefix(rest, helperproto.HelperPath+" ")
	if !found {
		return false, "", nil, false, false
	}
	fields := strings.Split(r, " ")
	sub = fields[0]
	valid = true
	for _, f := range fields[1:] {
		if f == "--expect-sha256" || f == "--op" {
			args = append(args, f)
			continue
		}
		if len(f) < 2 || f[0] != '\'' || f[len(f)-1] != '\'' || !helperproto.ValidArg(f[1:len(f)-1]) {
			valid = false
			continue
		}
		args = append(args, f[1:len(f)-1])
	}
	return sudo, sub, args, valid, true
}

func (e *Emulator) handle(cmd string, stdin []byte) Response {
	if cmd == "cat /etc/os-release" {
		e.mu.Lock()
		defer e.mu.Unlock()
		return Response{Stdout: []byte(e.osRelease)}
	}
	sudo, sub, args, valid, ok := parseLine(cmd)
	if !ok {
		return Response{Stderr: []byte("sh: command not found\n"), Exit: 127}
	}
	e.mu.Lock()
	missing := e.missing
	e.mu.Unlock()
	if missing {
		if sudo {
			return Response{Stderr: []byte("sudo: " + helperproto.HelperPath + ": command not found\n"), Exit: 1}
		}
		return Response{Stderr: []byte("sh: " + helperproto.HelperPath + ": not found\n"), Exit: 127}
	}
	if !valid {
		return refuse(helperproto.ExitRefused, helperproto.CodeInvalidArgument)
	}
	if sub != helperproto.SubVersion && !sudo {
		return refuse(helperproto.ExitRefused, helperproto.CodeNotRoot)
	}
	switch sub {
	case helperproto.SubVersion:
		e.mu.Lock()
		p := e.protocol
		e.mu.Unlock()
		return answer(helperproto.VersionResponse{OK: true, Helper: helperproto.Version, Protocol: p})
	case helperproto.SubSSHDDump:
		e.mu.Lock()
		cfg := e.sshd
		e.mu.Unlock()
		return answer(helperproto.SSHDDumpResponse{OK: true, Config: cfg, Fallback: cfg == ""})
	case helperproto.SubHostKeys:
		e.mu.Lock()
		keys := append([]helperproto.HostKeyInfo(nil), e.hostKeys...)
		e.mu.Unlock()
		return answer(helperproto.HostKeysResponse{OK: true, Keys: keys})
	case helperproto.SubAuthKeysList:
		e.mu.Lock()
		users, command := e.candidatesLocked()
		e.mu.Unlock()
		return answer(helperproto.AuthKeysListResponse{OK: true, Users: users, AuthorizedKeysCommand: command, Warnings: []string{}})
	case helperproto.SubAuthKeysRead:
		return e.read(args)
	case helperproto.SubAuthKeysWrite:
		return e.write(args, stdin)
	case helperproto.SubCleanup:
		if len(args) != 2 || args[0] != "--op" || !helperproto.ValidOpID(args[1]) {
			return refuse(helperproto.ExitRefused, helperproto.CodeUsage)
		}
		return answer(helperproto.CleanupResponse{OK: true, Removed: 1})
	default:
		return refuse(helperproto.ExitRefused, helperproto.CodeUnknownSubcommand)
	}
}

// candidatesLocked computes, like the helper, the authorized_keys paths of every user from the
// AuthorizedKeysFile patterns of the sshd configuration (the defaults when sshd -T fails).
func (e *Emulator) candidatesLocked() ([]helperproto.UserFiles, string) {
	patterns := sshdconf.DefaultAuthorizedKeysFile
	command := "none"
	if e.sshd != "" {
		if cfg, err := sshdconf.Parse([]byte(e.sshd)); err == nil {
			if len(cfg.AuthorizedKeysFile) > 0 {
				patterns = cfg.AuthorizedKeysFile
			}
			if cfg.AuthorizedKeysCommand != "" {
				command = cfg.AuthorizedKeysCommand
			}
		}
	}
	users := append([]emuUser(nil), e.users...)
	// The helper lists users by uid, then name.
	sort.Slice(users, func(i, j int) bool {
		if users[i].uid != users[j].uid {
			return users[i].uid < users[j].uid
		}
		return users[i].name < users[j].name
	})
	out := make([]helperproto.UserFiles, 0, len(users))
	for _, u := range users {
		uf := helperproto.UserFiles{User: u.name, UID: u.uid, Home: u.home, Files: []helperproto.FileInfo{}}
		for _, pat := range patterns {
			path, err := sshdconf.Expand(pat, u.name, u.home, u.uid)
			if err != nil {
				continue
			}
			fi := helperproto.FileInfo{Path: path, Mode: "0600", Owner: u.name, StrictModesOK: !e.insecure[path]}
			if c, ok := e.files[path]; ok {
				fi.Exists, fi.Size = true, int64(len(c))
				fi.TooLarge = len(c) > helperproto.MaxAuthorizedKeysSize
				if !fi.TooLarge {
					fi.SHA256 = sum(c) // the helper hashes only files it would read
				}
			}
			uf.Files = append(uf.Files, fi)
		}
		out = append(out, uf)
	}
	return out, command
}

func (e *Emulator) isCandidateLocked(path string) bool {
	users, _ := e.candidatesLocked()
	for _, u := range users {
		for _, f := range u.Files {
			if f.Path == path {
				return true
			}
		}
	}
	return false
}

func (e *Emulator) read(args []string) Response {
	if len(args) != 1 || !helperproto.ValidPath(args[0]) {
		return refuse(helperproto.ExitRefused, helperproto.CodeUsage)
	}
	path := args[0]
	e.mu.Lock()
	defer e.mu.Unlock()
	switch c, exists := e.files[path]; {
	case !e.isCandidateLocked(path):
		return refuse(helperproto.ExitRefused, helperproto.CodePathNotAllowed)
	case e.failRead[path]:
		return refuse(helperproto.ExitFailed, helperproto.CodeIOError)
	case !exists:
		return refuse(helperproto.ExitPrecondition, helperproto.CodeNotFound)
	case len(c) > helperproto.MaxAuthorizedKeysSize:
		return refuse(helperproto.ExitRefused, helperproto.CodeTooLarge)
	default:
		return answer(helperproto.AuthKeysReadResponse{OK: true, Path: path, SHA256: sum(c), ContentB64: base64.StdEncoding.EncodeToString(c)})
	}
}

func (e *Emulator) write(args []string, stdin []byte) Response {
	if len(args) != 5 || args[1] != "--expect-sha256" || args[3] != "--op" ||
		!helperproto.ValidPath(args[0]) || !helperproto.ValidSHA256(args[2]) || !helperproto.ValidOpID(args[4]) {
		return refuse(helperproto.ExitRefused, helperproto.CodeUsage)
	}
	path, expect, op := args[0], args[2], args[4]
	if len(stdin) > helperproto.MaxAuthorizedKeysSize {
		return refuse(helperproto.ExitRefused, helperproto.CodeTooLarge)
	}
	e.mu.Lock()
	hook := e.beforeWrite
	allowed := e.isCandidateLocked(path)
	e.mu.Unlock()
	if !allowed {
		return refuse(helperproto.ExitRefused, helperproto.CodePathNotAllowed)
	}
	if hook != nil {
		hook(path)
	}
	e.mu.Lock()
	defer e.mu.Unlock()
	current := helperproto.AbsentSHA256
	if c, ok := e.files[path]; ok {
		current = sum(c)
	}
	if current != expect {
		return refuse(helperproto.ExitPrecondition, helperproto.CodeHashMismatch)
	}
	e.files[path] = append([]byte(nil), stdin...)
	e.writes = append(e.writes, path)
	return answer(helperproto.AuthKeysWriteResponse{OK: true, SHA256: sum(stdin), Backup: helperproto.BackupRoot + "/" + op + "/1.bak"})
}
```

```go
func TestSudoersProfilesMatchTheSpec(t *testing.T) {

	assert.NotContains(t, linux, "nginx", "a generic Linux target never gains nginx subcommands")
	_, err = Sudoers("root")
	assert.Error(t, err)

func TestAuthorizedKeysLine(t *testing.T) {

	assert.Equal(t, `from="10.0.0.5",no-agent-forwarding,no-port-forwarding,no-X11-forwarding `+key,

		AuthorizedKeysLine(key, `1.2.3.4",command="sh`))
}

func TestSetupScriptRefusesLinesThatCouldBreakTheScript(t *testing.T) {
	for _, bad := range []string{"", "ssh-ed25519 AAAA x'; rm -rf / #", "ssh-ed25519 AAAA\nrm -rf /", "ssh-ed25519 AAAA \x00"} {
```

```go
package linuxssh

import (
	"errors"
	"regexp"
	"strings"
	"unicode/utf8"
)

// The sudoers file of spec §12.3. Profile "linux" allows only ALICE_COMMON (SSH-key work);
// profile "nginx" also allows the certificate subcommands (implemented by the helper from Phase 4).
const sudoersHead = `# Managed by Alice. Do not edit. Validate with: visudo -cf /etc/sudoers.d/alice
Defaults:alice-svc !requiretty
Defaults:alice-svc !lecture
Defaults:alice-svc env_reset
Defaults:alice-svc secure_path="/usr/sbin:/usr/bin:/sbin:/bin"
Defaults:alice-svc log_output

Cmnd_Alias ALICE_COMMON = \
    /usr/local/libexec/alice-helper sshd-dump, \
    /usr/local/libexec/alice-helper hostkeys, \
    /usr/local/libexec/alice-helper cleanup *, \
    /usr/local/libexec/alice-helper authkeys-list *, \
    /usr/local/libexec/alice-helper authkeys-read *, \
    /usr/local/libexec/alice-helper authkeys-write *
`

const sudoersNginxOnly = `
Cmnd_Alias ALICE_NGINX_ONLY = \
    /usr/local/libexec/alice-helper nginx-dump, \
    /usr/local/libexec/alice-helper nginx-test, \
    /usr/local/libexec/alice-helper nginx-reload, \
    /usr/local/libexec/alice-helper stat *, \
    /usr/local/libexec/alice-helper read-cert *, \
    /usr/local/libexec/alice-helper install-cert *, \
    /usr/local/libexec/alice-helper backup *, \
    /usr/local/libexec/alice-helper restore *
`

var errUnknownProfile = errors.New(`linuxssh: unknown sudoers profile (want "linux" or "nginx")`)

// Sudoers returns /etc/sudoers.d/alice for a profile.
func Sudoers(profile string) (string, error) {
	switch profile {
	case "linux":
		return sudoersHead + "\nalice-svc ALL=(root) NOPASSWD: ALICE_COMMON\n", nil
	case "nginx":
		return sudoersHead + sudoersNginxOnly + "\nalice-svc ALL=(root) NOPASSWD: ALICE_COMMON, ALICE_NGINX_ONLY\n", nil
	default:
		return "", errUnknownProfile
	}
}

// fromPattern is the address-list vocabulary of the from= option (addresses, CIDR, wildcards,
// negation); anything else is dropped rather than embedded in quotes.
var fromPattern = regexp.MustCompile(`^[0-9A-Fa-f.:/,*?!]{1,512}$`)

// AuthorizedKeysLine is the line that authorizes Alice's key for alice-svc (SEC-082). from limits
// the source addresses and is optional (NAT, HA).
func AuthorizedKeysLine(publicKey, from string) string {
	opts := "no-agent-forwarding,no-port-forwarding,no-X11-forwarding"
	if from != "" && fromPattern.MatchString(from) {
		opts = `from="` + from + `",` + opts
	}
	return opts + " " + publicKey
}

const scriptTemplate = `#!/bin/sh
# Prepares this server for Alice (profile: __PROFILE__). Run it as root in the directory that
# holds alice-helper from the Alice bundle. Running it again is safe.
set -eu
umask 077
if [ "$(id -u)" -ne 0 ]; then
    echo "Run this script as root." >&2
    exit 1
fi
if [ ! -f ./alice-helper ]; then
    echo "Copy alice-helper from the Alice bundle into this directory first." >&2
    exit 1
fi
install -d -m 0755 -o root -g root /usr/local/libexec
install -m 0755 -o root -g root ./alice-helper /usr/local/libexec/alice-helper
if ! id alice-svc >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    useradd --system --create-home --home-dir /var/lib/alice-svc --shell /bin/bash alice-svc
fi
usermod -p '*' alice-svc
install -d -m 0700 -o alice-svc -g alice-svc /var/lib/alice-svc/.ssh
printf '%s\n' '__LINE__' > /var/lib/alice-svc/.ssh/authorized_keys
chown alice-svc:alice-svc /var/lib/alice-svc/.ssh/authorized_keys
chmod 0600 /var/lib/alice-svc/.ssh/authorized_keys
cat > /etc/sudoers.d/.alice.tmp <<'ALICE_SUDOERS'
__SUDOERS__ALICE_SUDOERS
chmod 0440 /etc/sudoers.d/.alice.tmp
visudo -cf /etc/sudoers.d/.alice.tmp
mv /etc/sudoers.d/.alice.tmp /etc/sudoers.d/alice
install -d -m 0700 -o root -g root /var/lib/alice-helper /var/lib/alice-helper/backups
echo "This server is ready for Alice."
`

var errBadKeyLine = errors.New("linuxssh: the authorized_keys line cannot be embedded in the setup script")

// SetupScript is the root script of spec §12.2 for a profile. "usermod -p '*'" leaves alice-svc
// without a password but not locked, so sshd also accepts its key with UsePAM no. The sudoers file
// is installed only after visudo accepted it (a file name with a dot is ignored by sudo).
func SetupScript(profile, authorizedKeysLine string) (string, error) {
	sudoers, err := Sudoers(profile)
	if err != nil {
		return "", err
	}
	if authorizedKeysLine == "" || !utf8.ValidString(authorizedKeysLine) || strings.ContainsRune(authorizedKeysLine, '\'') ||
		strings.ContainsFunc(authorizedKeysLine, func(r rune) bool { return r < 0x20 || r == 0x7f }) {
		return "", errBadKeyLine
	}
	return strings.NewReplacer("__PROFILE__", profile, "__LINE__", authorizedKeysLine, "__SUDOERS__", sudoers).
		Replace(scriptTemplate), nil
}
```

```go
func newProvEnv(t *testing.T) *provEnv {

	emu := linuxsshtest.NewEmulator()
	srv := linuxsshtest.NewServer(t, emu.Handler())
	cred := newFakeCred(t)
	srv.Authorize(cred.signer.PublicKey())
	hk := &memHostKeys{}
	hk.pin(srv.HostKey())
	pool := NewPool(&Dialer{Clock: clock.Real{}, HostKeys: hk}, MaxConnections, MaxConnectionsPerTarget, IdleTimeout)
	t.Cleanup(pool.Close)
	host, port := srv.Addr()
	return &provEnv{
		srv: srv, emu: emu, cred: cred, hk: hk, pool: pool, prov: New(Options{Pool: pool}),
		ref: providers.TargetRef{ID: testTarget, Name: "web-01", Kind: providers.KindLinuxSSH,
			Config: providers.TargetConfig{"host": host, "port": port, "username": "alice-svc"}},
	}
}

func (e *provEnv) open(t *testing.T) providers.Session {
	t.Helper()
	s, err := e.prov.Open(context.Background(), e.ref, e.cred, providers.Env{Clock: clock.Real{}, HostKeys: e.hk})
	require.NoError(t, err)
	t.Cleanup(func() { _ = s.Close() })
	return s
}

// keyLine returns an authorized_keys line for a fresh key ("ed25519" or "rsa1024") and its fingerprint.
func keyLine(t testing.TB, kind, options, comment string) (string, string) {
	t.Helper()
	var pub ssh.PublicKey
	switch kind {
	case "ed25519":
		p, _, err := ed25519.GenerateKey(rand.Reader)
		require.NoError(t, err)
		pub, err = ssh.NewPublicKey(p)
		require.NoError(t, err)
	case "rsa1024":
		k, err := rsa.GenerateKey(rand.Reader, 1024)
		require.NoError(t, err)
		pub, err = ssh.NewPublicKey(&k.PublicKey)
		require.NoError(t, err)
	default:
		t.Fatalf("unknown key kind %q", kind)
	}
	line := strings.TrimSpace(string(ssh.MarshalAuthorizedKey(pub))) + " " + comment
	if options != "" {
		line = options + " " + line
	}
	return line, ssh.FingerprintSHA256(pub)
}

func hasWarning(ws []providers.Warning, code, path string) bool {
	for _, w := range ws {
		if w.Code == code && (path == "" || w.Params["path"] == path) {
			return true
		}
	}
	return false
}

func TestDiscoverListsKeysWithUsersAndFlags(t *testing.T) {
	e := newProvEnv(t)
	rootFrom, rootFromFP := keyLine(t, "ed25519", `from="10.0.0.0/8"`, "root@bastion")
	rootBare, rootBareFP := keyLine(t, "ed25519", "", "root@laptop")
	deployKey, deployFP := keyLine(t, "ed25519", "", "deploy@laptop")
	weak, weakFP := keyLine(t, "rsa1024", "", "ci@old")
	platform := "no-agent-forwarding " + strings.TrimSpace(string(ssh.MarshalAuthorizedKey(e.cred.signer.PublicKey()))) + " alice-platform"
	e.emu.SetFile(rootFile, []byte(rootFrom+"\n"+rootBare+"\n"))
	e.emu.SetFile(deployFile, []byte("# deploy keys\n"+deployKey+"\n"+weak+"\n"+deployKey+"\nthis is not a key\n"))
	e.emu.SetFile(aliceFile, []byte(platform+"\n"))

	res, err := e.open(t).Discover(context.Background(), providers.DiscoverRequest{SSHKeys: true})
	require.NoError(t, err)

	assert.False(t, res.Partial)
	assert.ElementsMatch(t, []string{rootFile, deployFile, aliceFile}, res.ReadFiles)
	assert.True(t, res.SSHD.Read)
	assert.False(t, res.SSHD.KeysManagedElsewhere)
	assert.Equal(t, []string{".ssh/authorized_keys", ".ssh/authorized_keys2"}, res.SSHD.AuthorizedKeysFile)
	require.Len(t, res.HostKeys, 1)
	assert.Equal(t, "ssh-ed25519", res.HostKeys[0].KeyType)

	type found struct {
		user, path string
		line       int
		fp         string
	}
	var got []found
	byLine := map[found]providers.DiscoveredSSHKey{}
	for _, k := range res.SSHKeys {
		f := found{k.OSUser, k.FilePath, k.LineNo, k.Fingerprint}
		got = append(got, f)
		byLine[f] = k
	}
	platformFP := ssh.FingerprintSHA256(e.cred.signer.PublicKey())
	want := []found{
		{"root", rootFile, 1, rootFromFP},
		{"root", rootFile, 2, rootBareFP},
		{"deploy", deployFile, 2, deployFP},
		{"deploy", deployFile, 3, weakFP},
		{"deploy", deployFile, 4, deployFP},
		{"alice-svc", aliceFile, 1, platformFP},
	}
	assert.ElementsMatch(t, want, got)
	assert.NotContains(t, byLine[want[0]].Flags, providers.FlagRootWithoutFrom)
	assert.Equal(t, `from="10.0.0.0/8"`, byLine[want[0]].Options)
	assert.Contains(t, byLine[want[1]].Flags, providers.FlagRootWithoutFrom)
	assert.Contains(t, byLine[want[2]].Flags, providers.FlagDuplicate)
	assert.Contains(t, byLine[want[3]].Flags, providers.FlagWeak)
	assert.Equal(t, 1024, byLine[want[3]].Bits)
	assert.Equal(t, "ci@old", byLine[want[3]].Comment)
	assert.Contains(t, byLine[want[4]].Flags, providers.FlagDuplicate)

	assert.Equal(t, []providers.UnreadableLine{{OSUser: "deploy", FilePath: deployFile, LineNo: 5}}, res.UnreadableLines)
	assert.True(t, hasWarning(res.Warnings, "unreadable_line", deployFile))
	for _, w := range res.Warnings {
		if w.Code == "unreadable_line" {
			assert.Equal(t, "1", w.Params["count"])
		}
	}
}
```

Create `internal/providers/linuxssh/provider.go`:

```go
package linuxssh

import (
	"context"
	"strconv"
	"sync"

	"alice/internal/platform/validate"
	"alice/internal/providers"
	"alice/internal/providers/linuxssh/helperproto"
)

// Options are the provider's dependencies.
type Options struct {
	Pool *Pool
}

// Provider is the linuxssh provider (spec §6.6, §13). It also prepares hosts (providers.SetupGuide).
type Provider struct {
	pool *Pool
}

var (
	_ providers.Provider   = (*Provider)(nil)
	_ providers.SetupGuide = (*Provider)(nil)
	_ providers.Session    = (*session)(nil)
)

// New returns the provider.
func New(o Options) *Provider { return &Provider{pool: o.Pool} }

// Kind implements providers.Provider.
func (p *Provider) Kind() providers.Kind { return providers.KindLinuxSSH }

// DisplayNameKey implements providers.Provider.
func (p *Provider) DisplayNameKey() string { return "provider.linuxssh.name" }

// Capabilities implements providers.Provider.
func (p *Provider) Capabilities() providers.CapabilitySet {
	return providers.NewCapabilitySet(providers.CapTestConnection, providers.CapDiscoverSSHKeys)
}

// ConfigSchema implements providers.Provider.
func (p *Provider) ConfigSchema() providers.ConfigSchema {
	return providers.ConfigSchema{Fields: []providers.Field{
		{Name: "host", Type: "host", Required: true, Min: 1, Max: 253,
			LabelKey: "provider.linuxssh.fields.host.label", HelpKey: "provider.linuxssh.fields.host.help"},
		{Name: "port", Type: "int", Default: 22, Min: 1, Max: 65535,
			LabelKey: "provider.linuxssh.fields.port.label", HelpKey: "provider.linuxssh.fields.port.help"},
		{Name: "username", Type: "string", Default: ServiceUser, Pattern: `^[a-z_][a-z0-9_-]{0,31}$`, Min: 1, Max: 32,
			LabelKey: "provider.linuxssh.fields.username.label", HelpKey: "provider.linuxssh.fields.username.help"},
	}}
}

// CredentialSchema implements providers.Provider: every target uses the platform key.
func (p *Provider) CredentialSchema() providers.CredentialSchema { return providers.CredentialSchema{} }

// ValidateConfig implements providers.Provider.
func (p *Provider) ValidateConfig(cfg providers.TargetConfig) []validate.FieldError {
	_, errs := ParseConfig(cfg)
	return errs
}

// SetupSnippets implements providers.SetupGuide.
func (p *Provider) SetupSnippets(authorizedKeysLine string) map[string]providers.SetupSnippet {
	out := map[string]providers.SetupSnippet{}
	for _, profile := range []string{"linux", "nginx"} {
		sudoers, _ := Sudoers(profile)
		script, _ := SetupScript(profile, authorizedKeysLine) // "" when the line cannot be embedded
		out[profile] = providers.SetupSnippet{Profile: profile, Sudoers: sudoers, Script: script}
	}
	return out
}

// HelperInfo implements providers.SetupGuide.
func (p *Provider) HelperInfo() (string, int) { return helperproto.HelperPath, helperproto.Protocol }

// Open connects through the pool (the pool's dialer holds the host-key store) and checks that
// alice-helper answers with a protocol this Alice can use. env is not needed beyond that.
func (p *Provider) Open(ctx context.Context, t providers.TargetRef, cred providers.CredentialSource, _ providers.Env) (providers.Session, error) {
	cfg, errs := ParseConfig(t.Config)
	if len(errs) > 0 {
		return nil, providers.NewError("target.invalid_config", false, validate.Errors(errs), nil)
	}
	conn, release, err := p.pool.Acquire(ctx, t.ID, cfg, cred)
	if err != nil {
		return nil, err
	}
	v, err := runHelper[helperproto.VersionResponse](ctx, conn, CmdVersion())
	if err != nil {
		release(conn.Healthy())
		return nil, err
	}
	if v.Protocol < helperproto.Protocol {
		release(true)
		return nil, providers.NewError("ssh.helper_outdated", false, nil, map[string]string{
			"helper_protocol": strconv.Itoa(v.Protocol), "required_protocol": strconv.Itoa(helperproto.Protocol)})
	}
	v.Helper = cleanValue(v.Helper, 40)
	return &session{conn: conn, cfg: cfg, version: v, release: release}, nil
}

// session is one pooled connection to a linuxssh target.
type session struct {
	providers.UnsupportedSession
	conn    *Conn
	cfg     Config
	version helperproto.VersionResponse
	release func(bool)
	once    sync.Once
}

// Close returns the connection to the pool (closed when it is no longer healthy).
func (s *session) Close() error {
	s.once.Do(func() { s.release(s.conn.Healthy()) })
	return nil
}

// TestConnection proves SSH, sudo and the helper work: os-release, then sshd-dump through sudo.
func (s *session) TestConnection(ctx context.Context) (providers.ConnectionReport, error) {
	osr, err := s.conn.OSRelease(ctx)
	if err != nil {
		return providers.ConnectionReport{}, err
	}
	d, err := runHelper[helperproto.SSHDDumpResponse](ctx, s.conn, CmdSSHDDump())
	if err != nil {
		return providers.ConnectionReport{}, err
	}
	rep := providers.ConnectionReport{
		HostKey: s.conn.HostKey(), HelperVersion: s.version.Helper, HelperProtocol: s.version.Protocol, OS: osr,
	}
	if d.Fallback {
		rep.Warnings = append(rep.Warnings, warn("sshd_unreadable"))
	}
	return rep, nil
}

// ListAuthorizedKeys returns the keys a full discovery finds.
func (s *session) ListAuthorizedKeys(ctx context.Context) ([]providers.DiscoveredSSHKey, error) {
	res, err := s.Discover(ctx, providers.DiscoverRequest{SSHKeys: true})
	if err != nil {
		return nil, err
	}
	return res.SSHKeys, nil
}
```
