```go
package linuxssh

import (
	"context"
	"crypto/sha256"
	"encoding/base64"
	"encoding/hex"
	"errors"
	"regexp"
	"strconv"

	"alice/internal/providers"
	"alice/internal/providers/linuxssh/helperproto"
	"alice/internal/providers/linuxssh/sshdconf"
)

var warningCodeRE = regexp.MustCompile(`^[a-z][a-z_]{0,39}$`)

// warn builds a warning; kv are parameter name/value pairs (values are cleaned remote text).
func warn(code string, kv ...string) providers.Warning {
	w := providers.Warning{Code: code, Params: map[string]string{}}
	for i := 0; i+1 < len(kv); i += 2 {
		w.Params[kv[i]] = cleanValue(kv[i+1], maxFactLength)
	}
	return w
}

// runHelper runs one helper command and decodes its answer.
func runHelper[T any](ctx context.Context, c *Conn, cmd HelperCommand) (T, error) {
	res, err := c.Run(ctx, cmd)
	if err != nil {
		var zero T
		return zero, err
	}
	return DecodeHelper[T](res, cmd.Subcommand())
}

func weakHostKey(keyType string, bits int) bool {
	return keyType == "ssh-dss" || (keyType == "ssh-rsa" && bits < 2048)
}

func isSet(v string) bool { return v != "" && v != "none" }

// sshd reads the effective sshd settings (spec §13.2). When sshd -T fails the defaults apply and
// the warning says so.
func (s *session) sshd(ctx context.Context) (providers.SSHDSummary, []providers.Warning, error) {
	d, err := runHelper[helperproto.SSHDDumpResponse](ctx, s.conn, CmdSSHDDump())
	if err != nil {
		return providers.SSHDSummary{}, nil, err
	}
	if d.Fallback {
		return providers.SSHDSummary{
			AuthorizedKeysFile:    append([]string(nil), sshdconf.DefaultAuthorizedKeysFile...),
			AuthorizedKeysCommand: "none",
		}, []providers.Warning{warn("sshd_unreadable")}, nil
	}
	cfg, err := sshdconf.Parse([]byte(d.Config))
	if err != nil {
		return providers.SSHDSummary{}, nil, providers.NewError("ssh.protocol_error", false, err,
			map[string]string{"subcommand": helperproto.SubSSHDDump})
	}
	sum := providers.SSHDSummary{
		Read:                   true,
		PubkeyAuthentication:   cleanValue(cfg.PubkeyAuthentication, maxFactLength),
		PasswordAuthentication: cleanValue(cfg.PasswordAuthentication, maxFactLength),
		PermitRootLogin:        cleanValue(cfg.PermitRootLogin, maxFactLength),
		AuthorizedKeysCommand:  cleanValue(cfg.AuthorizedKeysCommand, maxFactLength),
	}
	for _, f := range cfg.AuthorizedKeysFile {
		sum.AuthorizedKeysFile = append(sum.AuthorizedKeysFile, cleanValue(f, maxFactLength))
	}
	if len(sum.AuthorizedKeysFile) == 0 {
		sum.AuthorizedKeysFile = append([]string(nil), sshdconf.DefaultAuthorizedKeysFile...)
	}
	if sum.AuthorizedKeysCommand == "" {
		sum.AuthorizedKeysCommand = "none"
	}
	var warns []providers.Warning
	sum.KeysManagedElsewhere = sum.AuthorizedKeysCommand != "none"
	if sum.KeysManagedElsewhere {
		warns = append(warns, warn("keys_managed_elsewhere"))
	}
	sum.CertificatesInUse = isSet(cfg.TrustedUserCAKeys) || isSet(cfg.AuthorizedPrincipalsFile)
	if sum.CertificatesInUse {
		warns = append(warns, warn("certificates_in_use"))
	}
	if sum.PubkeyAuthentication == "no" {
		warns = append(warns, warn("pubkey_disabled"))
	}
	return sum, warns, nil
}

// readFile reads one authorized_keys file through the helper. exists is false when the file does
// not exist (helper code NOT_FOUND); the content's SHA-256 is checked against the helper's.
func (s *session) readFile(ctx context.Context, path string) ([]byte, string, bool, error) {
	cmd, err := CmdAuthKeysRead(path)
	if err != nil {
		return nil, "", false, providers.NewError("ssh.helper_refused", false, err,
			map[string]string{"subcommand": helperproto.SubAuthKeysRead, "helper_code": helperproto.CodeInvalidArgument})
	}
	r, err := runHelper[helperproto.AuthKeysReadResponse](ctx, s.conn, cmd)
	if isHelperCode(err, helperproto.CodeNotFound) {
		return nil, helperproto.AbsentSHA256, false, nil
	}
	if err != nil {
		return nil, "", false, err
	}
	content, err := base64.StdEncoding.DecodeString(r.ContentB64)
	if err != nil {
		return nil, "", false, providers.NewError("ssh.protocol_error", false, err,
			map[string]string{"subcommand": helperproto.SubAuthKeysRead})
	}
	h := sha256.Sum256(content)
	sum := hex.EncodeToString(h[:])
	if sum != r.SHA256 {
		return nil, "", false, providers.NewError("ssh.protocol_error", false, errors.New("linuxssh: content does not match its hash"),
			map[string]string{"subcommand": helperproto.SubAuthKeysRead})
	}
	return content, sum, true, nil
}

// isHelperCode reports whether err is the helper refusing with code.
func isHelperCode(err error, code string) bool {
	var pe *providers.Error
	return errors.As(err, &pe) && pe.Code == "ssh.helper_refused" && pe.Params["helper_code"] == code
}

// Discover reads the host keys, the sshd settings and, when asked, every authorized_keys file the
// helper lists (spec §13.2, §13.3). One unreadable file makes the result partial (inventory never
// marks keys missing from files it did not read); skipped files are only reported.
func (s *session) Discover(ctx context.Context, req providers.DiscoverRequest) (providers.DiscoveryResult, error) {
	var res providers.DiscoveryResult
	hk, err := runHelper[helperproto.HostKeysResponse](ctx, s.conn, CmdHostKeys())
	if err != nil {
		return providers.DiscoveryResult{}, err
	}
	for _, k := range hk.Keys {
		res.HostKeys = append(res.HostKeys, providers.DiscoveredHostKey{
			KeyType: cleanValue(k.Type, 64), Bits: k.Bits, Fingerprint: cleanValue(k.Fingerprint, 128),
			Weak: weakHostKey(k.Type, k.Bits),
		})
	}
	sum, warns, err := s.sshd(ctx)
	if err != nil {
		return providers.DiscoveryResult{}, err
	}
	res.SSHD = sum
	res.Warnings = append(res.Warnings, warns...)
	if !req.SSHKeys {
		return res, nil
	}
	list, err := runHelper[helperproto.AuthKeysListResponse](ctx, s.conn, CmdAuthKeysList())
	if err != nil {
		return providers.DiscoveryResult{}, err
	}
	for _, w := range list.Warnings {
		if warningCodeRE.MatchString(w) {
			res.Warnings = append(res.Warnings, warn(w))
		}
	}
	for _, u := range list.Users {
		for _, f := range u.Files {
			if !f.Exists {
				continue
			}
			switch {
			case !helperproto.ValidUser(u.User) || !helperproto.ValidPath(f.Path):
				res.Warnings = append(res.Warnings, warn("unsupported_path", "user", u.User, "path", f.Path))
				continue
			case f.TooLarge:
				res.Warnings = append(res.Warnings, warn("file_too_large", "user", u.User, "path", f.Path))
				continue
			}
			if !f.StrictModesOK {
				res.Warnings = append(res.Warnings, warn("strict_modes", "user", u.User, "path", f.Path))
			}
			content, _, exists, err := s.readFile(ctx, f.Path)
			if err != nil {
				if !s.conn.Healthy() {
					return providers.DiscoveryResult{}, err
				}
				res.Partial = true
				res.Warnings = append(res.Warnings, warn("file_unreadable", "user", u.User, "path", f.Path))
				continue
			}
			if !exists {
				continue
			}
			ak, err := ParseAuthorizedKeys(content)
			if err != nil {
				res.Warnings = append(res.Warnings, warn("file_too_large", "user", u.User, "path", f.Path))
				continue
			}
			keys, bad := ak.Keys(u.User, f.Path)
			res.SSHKeys = append(res.SSHKeys, keys...)
			res.UnreadableLines = append(res.UnreadableLines, bad...)
			if len(bad) > 0 {
				res.Warnings = append(res.Warnings, warn("unreadable_line", "user", u.User, "path", f.Path, "count", strconv.Itoa(len(bad))))
			}
			res.ReadFiles = append(res.ReadFiles, f.Path)
		}
	}
	return res, nil
}
```

### Task 10: `authorized_keys` changes over SSH — remove and add with compare-and-swap and own-key refusal (F-36, F-37, F-38)

`keyops.go` implements `RemoveAuthorizedKey` and `AddAuthorizedKey` on the linuxssh session (spec §13.4). A key whose
fingerprint is protected (Alice's own key) is refused before any remote command, independent of the caller (§6.6);
a host whose keys come from `AuthorizedKeysCommand` is refused; the file is read, transformed in memory with the
Task 5 parser (unreadable and comment lines are never touched, CRLF is kept), written with
`authkeys-write --expect-sha256 <hash of what was read>`, re-read and verified. A concurrent change makes the helper
answer `HASH_MISMATCH`; the operation re-reads and retries, at most three attempts in total (§13.4), then fails with
`ssh.file_changed`. Removing the last key of `root` needs an explicit confirmation, removing the last key of the account
Alice signs in with is refused, `cert-authority` lines are never removed. The provider now advertises
`authorized_keys`.

**Files:**
- Create: `internal/providers/linuxssh/keyops.go`, `internal/providers/linuxssh/keyops_test.go`
- Modify: `internal/providers/linuxssh/provider.go` (capabilities), `internal/providers/linuxssh/provider_test.go`
  (expected capabilities)

**Interfaces:**
- Consumes (Task 9): `session` (`conn`, `cfg`, `readFile`, `sshd`), `runHelper`, `isHelperCode`, test helpers
  `provEnv`, `newProvEnv`, `(*provEnv).open`, `keyLine`, `rootFile`, `deployFile`, `aliceFile`; (Task 8)
  `CmdAuthKeysWrite`, `providerCode`; (Task 5) `ParseAuthorizedKeys`, `AuthorizedKeys.Lines`, `Line.Kind`,
  `Line.Options`, `Line.Fingerprint`, `LineKey`, `AuthorizedKeys.AddLine`, `RemoveFingerprint`, `CountKeys`,
  `Bytes`; `helperproto.AuthKeysWriteResponse`, `AbsentSHA256`, `CodeInvalidArgument`, `ValidPath`, `ValidUser`;
  `linuxsshtest.Emulator.BeforeWrite`, `Writes`, `File`, `SetFile`, `SetSSHD`, `DefaultSSHD`.
- Consumes (Task 4): `providers.AuthKeyChange`, `AuthKeyResult`, `StepLogger`, `StepStatus`, `CapAuthorizedKeys`.
- Produces: `(*session) RemoveAuthorizedKey(ctx, providers.AuthKeyChange, providers.StepLogger) (providers.AuthKeyResult, error)`,
  `(*session) AddAuthorizedKey(ctx, providers.AuthKeyChange, providers.StepLogger) (providers.AuthKeyResult, error)`;
  `const maxWriteAttempts = 3`; the unexported test hook `var beforeAuthKeysWrite func(path string)` (called, when
  non-nil, just before every `authkeys-write`; Task 19 uses it for the real-OpenSSH F-38 race).
- Step names logged (`StepLogger`): `precheck`, `read`, `write`, `verify`, each `started` then `ok` or `failed`
  (params `attempt`, and `reason` on failure). A `nil` logger is allowed.
- Error reasons: `sshkey.own_key_protected` (params `reason`: `protected_fingerprint` | `last_key_of_connection_account`),
  `sshkey.last_root_key`, `sshkey.not_removable` (`reason`: `cert_authority` | `file_too_large`),
  `ssh.keys_managed_elsewhere`, `ssh.file_changed` (retryable, `attempts`), `ssh.helper_refused`
  (`helper_code` `INVALID_ARGUMENT` for a request outside the vocabulary or a line `AddLine` refuses).
- Result semantics for Task 15's handler: `Changed=false` when nothing had to change (key absent, file absent, key
  already present); `Verified=false` with no error when the re-read after a successful write shows other content (the
  handler records it, it is not retried); an error after the write was sent is returned with the partially filled
  result, so the handler never retries a mutation blindly.

```go
package linuxssh

import (
	"context"
	"strings"
	"sync"
	"testing"

	"github.com/google/uuid"
	"github.com/stretchr/testify/assert"
	"github.com/stretchr/testify/require"
	"golang.org/x/crypto/ssh"

	"alice/internal/providers"
	"alice/internal/providers/linuxssh/linuxsshtest"
)

var keyOp = uuid.MustParse("0190f5a0-0000-7000-8000-0000000000bb")

type stepLog struct {
	mu    sync.Mutex
	steps []string
}

func (l *stepLog) Step(name string, status providers.StepStatus, _ map[string]string) {
	l.mu.Lock()
	defer l.mu.Unlock()
	l.steps = append(l.steps, name+":"+string(status))
}

func (l *stepLog) all() []string {
	l.mu.Lock()
	defer l.mu.Unlock()
	return append([]string(nil), l.steps...)
}

func removeReq(user, path, fp string, protected ...string) providers.AuthKeyChange {
	return providers.AuthKeyChange{OperationID: keyOp, OSUser: user, FilePath: path, Fingerprint: fp, ProtectedFingerprints: protected}
}

func platformLine(e *provEnv, options, comment string) (string, string) {
	pub := e.cred.signer.PublicKey()
	line := strings.TrimSpace(string(ssh.MarshalAuthorizedKey(pub))) + " " + comment
	if options != "" {
		line = options + " " + line
	}
	return line, ssh.FingerprintSHA256(pub)
}

func fileOf(t *testing.T, e *provEnv, path string) string {
	t.Helper()
	b, ok := e.emu.File(path)
	require.True(t, ok)
	return string(b)
}

func TestProviderAdvertisesAuthorizedKeys(t *testing.T) {
	assert.True(t, newProvEnv(t).prov.Capabilities().Has(providers.CapAuthorizedKeys))
}

// F-36: Alice's own key is refused by fingerprint (another comment or other options do not
// matter), before any remote command, in any file.
func TestRemoveRefusesAlicesOwnKey(t *testing.T) {
	e := newProvEnv(t)
	own, ownFP := platformLine(e, `from="10.9.9.9",no-pty`, "renamed-by-someone")
	other, _ := keyLine(t, "ed25519", "", "deploy@laptop")
	e.emu.SetFile(aliceFile, []byte(own+"\n"+other+"\n"))
	e.emu.SetFile(deployFile, []byte(own+"\n"))
	s := e.open(t)

	for _, path := range []string{aliceFile, deployFile} {
		user := "alice-svc"
		if path == deployFile {
			user = "deploy"
		}
		_, err := s.RemoveAuthorizedKey(context.Background(), removeReq(user, path, ownFP, ownFP), nil)
		pe := providerCode(t, err)
		assert.Equal(t, "sshkey.own_key_protected", pe.Code, path)
		assert.Equal(t, "protected_fingerprint", pe.Params["reason"])
	}
	assert.Equal(t, []string{"/usr/local/libexec/alice-helper version"}, e.srv.Commands(), "nothing beyond Open ran")
	assert.Empty(t, e.emu.Writes())
	assert.Equal(t, own+"\n"+other+"\n", fileOf(t, e, aliceFile))
}

// Removing the last key of the account Alice signs in with would lock Alice out of the server.
func TestRemoveRefusesTheLastKeyOfTheConnectionAccount(t *testing.T) {
	e := newProvEnv(t)
	only, onlyFP := keyLine(t, "ed25519", "", "someone@laptop")
	e.emu.SetFile(aliceFile, []byte(only+"\n"))
	_, err := e.open(t).RemoveAuthorizedKey(context.Background(), removeReq("alice-svc", aliceFile, onlyFP), nil)
	pe := providerCode(t, err)
	assert.Equal(t, "sshkey.own_key_protected", pe.Code)
	assert.Equal(t, "last_key_of_connection_account", pe.Params["reason"])
	assert.Empty(t, e.emu.Writes())
}

func TestRemoveLastRootKeyNeedsConfirmation(t *testing.T) {
	e := newProvEnv(t)
	k, fp := keyLine(t, "ed25519", `from="10.0.0.0/8"`, "root@bastion")
	e.emu.SetFile(rootFile, []byte(k+"\n"))
	s := e.open(t)
	_, err := s.RemoveAuthorizedKey(context.Background(), removeReq("root", rootFile, fp), nil)
	assert.Equal(t, "sshkey.last_root_key", providerCode(t, err).Code)
	assert.Empty(t, e.emu.Writes())

	req := removeReq("root", rootFile, fp)
	req.AllowLastRootKey = true
	res, err := s.RemoveAuthorizedKey(context.Background(), req, nil)
	require.NoError(t, err)
	assert.True(t, res.Changed)
	assert.True(t, res.Verified)
	assert.Equal(t, 1, res.Removed)
	assert.Empty(t, fileOf(t, e, rootFile))
}

// F-35: no key change on a host whose keys come from AuthorizedKeysCommand.
func TestRemoveRefusedWhenKeysAreManagedElsewhere(t *testing.T) {
	e := newProvEnv(t)
	e.emu.SetSSHD(strings.Replace(linuxsshtest.DefaultSSHD, "authorizedkeyscommand none",
		"authorizedkeyscommand /usr/bin/sss_ssh_authorizedkeys", 1))
	k, fp := keyLine(t, "ed25519", "", "deploy@laptop")
	e.emu.SetFile(deployFile, []byte(k+"\n"))
	_, err := e.open(t).RemoveAuthorizedKey(context.Background(), removeReq("deploy", deployFile, fp), nil)
	assert.Equal(t, "ssh.keys_managed_elsewhere", providerCode(t, err).Code)
	for _, c := range e.srv.Commands() {
		assert.NotContains(t, c, "authkeys-", "the file is neither read nor written")
	}
}

func TestRemoveRefusesCertAuthorityLines(t *testing.T) {
	e := newProvEnv(t)
	ca, caFP := keyLine(t, "ed25519", "cert-authority", "ca@corp")
	k, _ := keyLine(t, "ed25519", "", "deploy@laptop")
	e.emu.SetFile(deployFile, []byte(ca+"\n"+k+"\n"))
	_, err := e.open(t).RemoveAuthorizedKey(context.Background(), removeReq("deploy", deployFile, caFP), nil)
	pe := providerCode(t, err)
	assert.Equal(t, "sshkey.not_removable", pe.Code)
	assert.Equal(t, "cert_authority", pe.Params["reason"])
	assert.Empty(t, e.emu.Writes())
}

// Review Focus 1: CRLF endings, comments, unreadable lines and other keys stay byte-for-byte.
func TestRemoveKeepsCRLFAndForeignLines(t *testing.T) {
	e := newProvEnv(t)
	a, _ := keyLine(t, "ed25519", "", "a@x")
	target, fp := keyLine(t, "ed25519", `command="echo a,b",from="10.0.0.0/8"`, "target@x")
	b, _ := keyLine(t, "ed25519", "", "b@x")
	before := a + "\r\n# a comment\r\n" + target + "\r\ngarbage that is not a key\r\n" + target + "\r\n" + b + "\r\n"
	e.emu.SetFile(deployFile, []byte(before))
	res, err := e.open(t).RemoveAuthorizedKey(context.Background(), removeReq("deploy", deployFile, fp), nil)
	require.NoError(t, err)
	assert.Equal(t, 2, res.Removed, "every line with the fingerprint goes")
	assert.Equal(t, a+"\r\n# a comment\r\ngarbage that is not a key\r\n"+b+"\r\n", fileOf(t, e, deployFile))
	assert.True(t, res.Verified)
	assert.NotEqual(t, res.OldSHA256, res.NewSHA256)
}

func TestRemoveIsIdempotentAndLogsSteps(t *testing.T) {
	e := newProvEnv(t)
	k, fp := keyLine(t, "ed25519", "", "deploy@laptop")
	keep, _ := keyLine(t, "ed25519", "", "deploy@desktop")
	e.emu.SetFile(deployFile, []byte(k+"\n"+keep+"\n"))
	s := e.open(t)
	log := &stepLog{}
	res, err := s.RemoveAuthorizedKey(context.Background(), removeReq("deploy", deployFile, fp), log)
	require.NoError(t, err)
	assert.True(t, res.Changed)
	assert.Equal(t, []string{"precheck:started", "precheck:ok", "read:started", "read:ok", "write:started", "write:ok",
		"verify:started", "verify:ok"}, log.all())

	again, err := s.RemoveAuthorizedKey(context.Background(), removeReq("deploy", deployFile, fp), nil)
	require.NoError(t, err)
	assert.False(t, again.Changed)
	assert.Equal(t, again.OldSHA256, again.NewSHA256)
	assert.Len(t, e.emu.Writes(), 1, "the second removal wrote nothing")
	assert.Equal(t, keep+"\n", fileOf(t, e, deployFile))
}

func TestRemoveFromAMissingFileChangesNothing(t *testing.T) {
	e := newProvEnv(t)
	_, fp := keyLine(t, "ed25519", "", "x")
	res, err := e.open(t).RemoveAuthorizedKey(context.Background(), removeReq("deploy", deployFile, fp), nil)
	require.NoError(t, err)
	assert.False(t, res.Changed)
	assert.Empty(t, e.emu.Writes())
}

// A request outside the helper vocabulary never reaches a command line.
func TestKeyOperationsRefuseHostileRequests(t *testing.T) {
	e := newProvEnv(t)
	s := e.open(t)
	_, fp := keyLine(t, "ed25519", "", "x")
	for _, req := range []providers.AuthKeyChange{
		removeReq("deploy", "/home/deploy/.ssh/authorized_keys; id", fp),
		removeReq("deploy\nroot", deployFile, fp),
		removeReq("deploy", deployFile, ""),
		{OSUser: "deploy", FilePath: deployFile, Fingerprint: fp}, // no operation id
	} {
		_, err := s.RemoveAuthorizedKey(context.Background(), req, nil)
		pe := providerCode(t, err)
		assert.Equal(t, "ssh.helper_refused", pe.Code)
		assert.Equal(t, "INVALID_ARGUMENT", pe.Params["helper_code"])
	}
	assert.Equal(t, []string{"/usr/local/libexec/alice-helper version"}, e.srv.Commands())
}

// F-37: a file without a trailing newline gets the new key on its own line; the old bytes stay.
func TestAddAppendsOnItsOwnLine(t *testing.T) {
	e := newProvEnv(t)
	old, _ := keyLine(t, "ed25519", "", "old@x")
	e.emu.SetFile(deployFile, []byte("# keys\n"+old)) // no trailing newline
	add, _ := keyLine(t, "ed25519", "", "new@x")
	res, err := e.open(t).AddAuthorizedKey(context.Background(),
		providers.AuthKeyChange{OperationID: keyOp, OSUser: "deploy", FilePath: deployFile, Line: add}, nil)
	require.NoError(t, err)
	assert.True(t, res.Changed)
	assert.True(t, res.Verified)
	assert.Equal(t, "# keys\n"+old+"\n"+add+"\n", fileOf(t, e, deployFile))
}

func TestAddCreatesAMissingFile(t *testing.T) {
	e := newProvEnv(t)
	add, _ := keyLine(t, "ed25519", "", "new@x")
	res, err := e.open(t).AddAuthorizedKey(context.Background(),
		providers.AuthKeyChange{OperationID: keyOp, OSUser: "deploy", FilePath: deployFile, Line: add}, nil)
	require.NoError(t, err)
	assert.True(t, res.Changed)
	assert.Equal(t, "absent", res.OldSHA256)
	assert.Equal(t, add+"\n", fileOf(t, e, deployFile))
	found := false
	for _, c := range e.srv.Commands() {
		found = found || strings.Contains(c, "authkeys-write '"+deployFile+"' --expect-sha256 'absent'")
	}
	assert.True(t, found, "the write expects the file to be absent")
}

func TestAddExistingKeyChangesNothing(t *testing.T) {
	e := newProvEnv(t)
	k, _ := keyLine(t, "ed25519", "", "x@y")
	e.emu.SetFile(deployFile, []byte(k+"\n"))
	res, err := e.open(t).AddAuthorizedKey(context.Background(),
		providers.AuthKeyChange{OperationID: keyOp, OSUser: "deploy", FilePath: deployFile, Line: k + "-other-comment"}, nil)
	require.NoError(t, err)
	assert.False(t, res.Changed)
	assert.Empty(t, e.emu.Writes())
}

func TestAddRefusesALineThatIsNotOneKey(t *testing.T) {
	e := newProvEnv(t)
	k, _ := keyLine(t, "ed25519", "", "x@y")
	for _, bad := range []string{"not a key", k + "\n" + k, k + "\x1b[31m"} {
		_, err := e.open(t).AddAuthorizedKey(context.Background(),
			providers.AuthKeyChange{OperationID: keyOp, OSUser: "deploy", FilePath: deployFile, Line: bad}, nil)
		assert.Equal(t, "ssh.helper_refused", providerCode(t, err).Code, "%q", bad)
	}
	assert.Empty(t, e.emu.Writes())
}

// F-38: the file changes between read and write once; the write is refused (hash mismatch), the
// file is read again and the change is kept.
func TestConcurrentChangeIsRetriedAndKept(t *testing.T) {
	e := newProvEnv(t)
	k, fp := keyLine(t, "ed25519", "", "deploy@laptop")
	keep, _ := keyLine(t, "ed25519", "", "deploy@desktop")
	e.emu.SetFile(deployFile, []byte(k+"\n"+keep+"\n"))
	calls := 0
	e.emu.BeforeWrite(func(path string) {
		calls++
		if calls == 1 {
			cur, _ := e.emu.File(path)
			e.emu.SetFile(path, append(cur, []byte("# added by someone else\n")...))
		}
	})
	log := &stepLog{}
	res, err := e.open(t).RemoveAuthorizedKey(context.Background(), removeReq("deploy", deployFile, fp), log)
	require.NoError(t, err)
	assert.True(t, res.Verified)
	assert.Equal(t, 2, calls)
	assert.Equal(t, keep+"\n# added by someone else\n", fileOf(t, e, deployFile))
	assert.Contains(t, log.all(), "write:failed")
}

func TestConcurrentChangeEveryTimeFailsAfterThreeAttempts(t *testing.T) {
	e := newProvEnv(t)
	k, fp := keyLine(t, "ed25519", "", "deploy@laptop")
	keep, _ := keyLine(t, "ed25519", "", "deploy@desktop")
	e.emu.SetFile(deployFile, []byte(k+"\n"+keep+"\n"))
	calls := 0
	e.emu.BeforeWrite(func(path string) {
		calls++
		cur, _ := e.emu.File(path)
		e.emu.SetFile(path, append(cur, []byte("# busy\n")...))
	})
	_, err := e.open(t).RemoveAuthorizedKey(context.Background(), removeReq("deploy", deployFile, fp), nil)
	pe := providerCode(t, err)
	assert.Equal(t, "ssh.file_changed", pe.Code)
	assert.True(t, pe.Retryable)
	assert.Equal(t, "3", pe.Params["attempts"])
	assert.Equal(t, 3, calls)
	assert.Empty(t, e.emu.Writes())
	assert.Contains(t, fileOf(t, e, deployFile), k, "the key is still there: nothing was written")
}

func TestBeforeWriteHookSeesEveryWrite(t *testing.T) {
	e := newProvEnv(t)
	k, fp := keyLine(t, "ed25519", "", "deploy@laptop")
	keep, _ := keyLine(t, "ed25519", "", "deploy@desktop")
	e.emu.SetFile(deployFile, []byte(k+"\n"+keep+"\n"))
	var seen []string
	beforeAuthKeysWrite = func(path string) { seen = append(seen, path) }
	t.Cleanup(func() { beforeAuthKeysWrite = nil })
	_, err := e.open(t).RemoveAuthorizedKey(context.Background(), removeReq("deploy", deployFile, fp), nil)
	require.NoError(t, err)
	assert.Equal(t, []string{deployFile}, seen)
}
```

- [ ] **Step 2: Implement the key operations**

Create `internal/providers/linuxssh/keyops.go`:

```go
package linuxssh

import (
	"context"
	"crypto/sha256"
	"encoding/hex"
	"errors"
	"strconv"
	"strings"

	"github.com/google/uuid"

	"alice/internal/providers"
	"alice/internal/providers/linuxssh/helperproto"
)

// maxWriteAttempts bounds the re-read-and-retry loop after a concurrent change (spec §13.4).
const maxWriteAttempts = 3

// beforeAuthKeysWrite is a test hook (nil in production): it runs just before every authkeys-write.
var beforeAuthKeysWrite func(path string)

func step(log providers.StepLogger, name string, status string, params map[string]string) {
	if log != nil {
		log.Step(name, providers.StepStatus(status), params)
	}
}

func attemptParams(attempt int) map[string]string {
	return map[string]string{"attempt": strconv.Itoa(attempt)}
}

func failParams(attempt int, err error) map[string]string {
	p := attemptParams(attempt)
	var pe *providers.Error
	if errors.As(err, &pe) {
		p["reason"] = pe.Code
	}
	return p
}

func refusedRequest(field string) error {
	return providers.NewError("ssh.helper_refused", false, nil,
		map[string]string{"helper_code": helperproto.CodeInvalidArgument, "field": field})
}

func hexSHA256(b []byte) string {
	h := sha256.Sum256(b)
	return hex.EncodeToString(h[:])
}

func hasOption(options []string, name string) bool {
	for _, o := range options {
		k, _, _ := strings.Cut(o, "=")
		if strings.EqualFold(strings.TrimSpace(k), name) {
			return true
		}
	}
	return false
}

// precheck validates the request locally (nothing outside the helper vocabulary is sent), refuses
// a protected key before any remote command, and refuses hosts whose keys come from
// AuthorizedKeysCommand (spec §13.2, §13.4 step 1).
func (s *session) precheck(ctx context.Context, req providers.AuthKeyChange, remove bool) error {
	switch {
	case req.OperationID == uuid.Nil:
		return refusedRequest("operation_id")
	case !helperproto.ValidUser(req.OSUser):
		return refusedRequest("os_user")
	case !helperproto.ValidPath(req.FilePath):
		return refusedRequest("file_path")
	case remove && req.Fingerprint == "":
		return refusedRequest("fingerprint")
	case !remove && req.Line == "":
		return refusedRequest("line")
	}
	if remove {
		for _, p := range req.ProtectedFingerprints {
			if p != "" && p == req.Fingerprint {
				return providers.NewError("sshkey.own_key_protected", false, nil, map[string]string{"reason": "protected_fingerprint"})
			}
		}
	}
	sum, _, err := s.sshd(ctx)
	if err != nil {
		return err
	}
	if sum.KeysManagedElsewhere {
		return providers.NewError("ssh.keys_managed_elsewhere", false, nil, nil)
	}
	return nil
}

// RemoveAuthorizedKey removes every line of the key's fingerprint from one file. Comment and
// unreadable lines and every other key stay byte-for-byte.
func (s *session) RemoveAuthorizedKey(ctx context.Context, req providers.AuthKeyChange, log providers.StepLogger) (providers.AuthKeyResult, error) {
	step(log, "precheck", "started", nil)
	if err := s.precheck(ctx, req, true); err != nil {
		step(log, "precheck", "failed", failParams(0, err))
		return providers.AuthKeyResult{}, err
	}
	step(log, "precheck", "ok", nil)
	for attempt := 1; attempt <= maxWriteAttempts; attempt++ {
		res, retry, err := s.removeOnce(ctx, req, log, attempt)
		if !retry {
			return res, err
		}
	}
	return providers.AuthKeyResult{}, providers.NewError("ssh.file_changed", true, nil,
		map[string]string{"attempts": strconv.Itoa(maxWriteAttempts)})
}

func (s *session) removeOnce(ctx context.Context, req providers.AuthKeyChange, log providers.StepLogger, attempt int) (providers.AuthKeyResult, bool, error) {
	step(log, "read", "started", attemptParams(attempt))
	content, h0, exists, err := s.readFile(ctx, req.FilePath)
	if err != nil {
		step(log, "read", "failed", failParams(attempt, err))
		return providers.AuthKeyResult{}, false, err
	}
	step(log, "read", "ok", attemptParams(attempt))
	if !exists {
		return providers.AuthKeyResult{OldSHA256: helperproto.AbsentSHA256, NewSHA256: helperproto.AbsentSHA256}, false, nil
	}
	ak, err := ParseAuthorizedKeys(content)
	if err != nil {
		return providers.AuthKeyResult{}, false, providers.NewError("sshkey.not_removable", false, err,
			map[string]string{"reason": "file_too_large"})
	}
	for _, l := range ak.Lines {
		if l.Kind == LineKey && l.Fingerprint == req.Fingerprint && hasOption(l.Options, "cert-authority") {
			return providers.AuthKeyResult{}, false, providers.NewError("sshkey.not_removable", false, nil,
				map[string]string{"reason": "cert_authority"})
		}
	}
	next, removed := ak.RemoveFingerprint(req.Fingerprint)
	if removed == 0 {
		return providers.AuthKeyResult{OldSHA256: h0, NewSHA256: h0}, false, nil
	}
	if next.CountKeys() == 0 {
		if req.OSUser == s.cfg.Username {
			return providers.AuthKeyResult{}, false, providers.NewError("sshkey.own_key_protected", false, nil,
				map[string]string{"reason": "last_key_of_connection_account"})
		}
		if req.OSUser == "root" && !req.AllowLastRootKey {
			return providers.AuthKeyResult{}, false, providers.NewError("sshkey.last_root_key", false, nil, nil)
		}
	}
	return s.writeAndVerify(ctx, req, log, attempt, h0, next.Bytes(), removed)
}

// AddAuthorizedKey appends one key line (on its own line, also when the file lacks a trailing
// newline); a key already present by fingerprint changes nothing.
func (s *session) AddAuthorizedKey(ctx context.Context, req providers.AuthKeyChange, log providers.StepLogger) (providers.AuthKeyResult, error) {
	step(log, "precheck", "started", nil)
	if err := s.precheck(ctx, req, false); err != nil {
		step(log, "precheck", "failed", failParams(0, err))
		return providers.AuthKeyResult{}, err
	}
	step(log, "precheck", "ok", nil)
	for attempt := 1; attempt <= maxWriteAttempts; attempt++ {
		res, retry, err := s.addOnce(ctx, req, log, attempt)
		if !retry {
			return res, err
		}
	}
	return providers.AuthKeyResult{}, providers.NewError("ssh.file_changed", true, nil,
		map[string]string{"attempts": strconv.Itoa(maxWriteAttempts)})
}

func (s *session) addOnce(ctx context.Context, req providers.AuthKeyChange, log providers.StepLogger, attempt int) (providers.AuthKeyResult, bool, error) {
	step(log, "read", "started", attemptParams(attempt))
	content, h0, _, err := s.readFile(ctx, req.FilePath)
	if err != nil {
		step(log, "read", "failed", failParams(attempt, err))
		return providers.AuthKeyResult{}, false, err
	}
	step(log, "read", "ok", attemptParams(attempt))
	ak, err := ParseAuthorizedKeys(content)
	if err != nil {
		return providers.AuthKeyResult{}, false, providers.NewError("sshkey.not_removable", false, err,
			map[string]string{"reason": "file_too_large"})
	}
	next, added, err := ak.AddLine(req.Line)
	if err != nil {
		return providers.AuthKeyResult{}, false, refusedRequest("line")
	}
	if !added {
		return providers.AuthKeyResult{OldSHA256: h0, NewSHA256: h0}, false, nil
	}
	return s.writeAndVerify(ctx, req, log, attempt, h0, next.Bytes(), 0)
}

// writeAndVerify writes newContent if the file still has hash h0, then reads it back. retry is
// true only when the helper refused the write because the file changed (nothing was written).
func (s *session) writeAndVerify(ctx context.Context, req providers.AuthKeyChange, log providers.StepLogger,
	attempt int, h0 string, newContent []byte, removed int) (providers.AuthKeyResult, bool, error) {
	step(log, "write", "started", attemptParams(attempt))
	cmd, err := CmdAuthKeysWrite(req.FilePath, h0, req.OperationID, newContent)
	if err != nil {
		step(log, "write", "failed", attemptParams(attempt))
		return providers.AuthKeyResult{}, false, refusedRequest("content")
	}
	if beforeAuthKeysWrite != nil {
		beforeAuthKeysWrite(req.FilePath)
	}
	_, err = runHelper[helperproto.AuthKeysWriteResponse](ctx, s.conn, cmd)
	var pe *providers.Error
	if errors.As(err, &pe) && pe.Code == "ssh.file_changed" {
		step(log, "write", "failed", failParams(attempt, err))
		return providers.AuthKeyResult{}, true, err
	}
	want := hexSHA256(newContent)
	res := providers.AuthKeyResult{Changed: true, Removed: removed, OldSHA256: h0, NewSHA256: want}
	if err != nil {
		// The outcome is uncertain (the write may have happened): the caller must not retry blindly.
		step(log, "write", "failed", failParams(attempt, err))
		return res, false, err
	}
	step(log, "write", "ok", attemptParams(attempt))
	step(log, "verify", "started", attemptParams(attempt))
	_, got, exists, err := s.readFile(ctx, req.FilePath)
	if err != nil {
		step(log, "verify", "failed", failParams(attempt, err))
		return res, false, err
	}
	res.Verified = exists && got == want
	if res.Verified {
		step(log, "verify", "ok", attemptParams(attempt))
	} else {
		step(log, "verify", "failed", map[string]string{"attempt": strconv.Itoa(attempt), "reason": "content_differs"})
	}
	return res, false, nil
}
```

### Task 11: Durable job queue — enqueue, claim with per-target locks, runner, retries, license gate, `blocked_license` (F-69, L-81)

The PostgreSQL queue of spec §8.1–§8.6 next to the Phase 2 periodic scheduler (which stays unchanged in this task).
`Queue` writes jobs in the caller's transaction with an HMAC over the payload (J-1); `Runner` claims one job per
transaction with `FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED`, takes the target's `target_locks` row in the same transaction (so two jobs
for one server can never both start), heartbeats the lease, classifies failures, retries with exponential backoff and
jitter, and asks the license gate before every claim and again right after it. In lock, queued external-change jobs
become `blocked_license` and wait for an Administrator's confirmation after the renewal (R29, L-81); queued read-only
jobs are cancelled (§8.6). All times are bind parameters from the injected clock.

`internal/inventory/jobs.go` is created here (the job-type names, `JobRequest`, `Enqueuer`) so the queue compiles before
the rest of the inventory package exists (Task 13).

**Contract additions (recorded for Task 23's R37 notes):** `QueueConfig.Gate Gate` (Confirm must refuse while locked);
`QueueConfig.Keyring` has the type `jobs.Deriver` (`Derive(label string) []byte`, satisfied by `*secrets.Keyring`)
because `internal/archtest` does not let `jobs` import `secrets`; the label constant `payloadMACLabel` equals
`secrets.LabelJob` (asserted by a test); `jobs.ErrBadCursor` (the API answers 400 for it).

**Files:**
- Create: `internal/inventory/jobs.go`
- Modify: `internal/jobs/types.go` (job types, `Kind`, `Status`, `MaxAttemptsFor`)
- Create: `internal/jobs/failure.go`, `internal/jobs/queue.go`, `internal/jobs/runner.go`
- Test: `internal/jobs/queue_test.go` (unit), `internal/jobs/queue_integration_test.go`, `internal/jobs/runner_integration_test.go`

**Interfaces:**
- Consumes: `license.Class`, `license.ErrLocked` (`internal/license/class.go`, `errors.go`); `audit.Log.Append`,
  `audit.SystemActor` (`internal/audit/audit.go`); `db.InTx` (`internal/platform/db/tx.go`); `clock.Clock`;
  `providers.Error`, `providers.NewError`, `providers.StepLogger`, `providers.StepStatus` (Task 4); the `jobs`,
  `job_attempts`, `target_locks`, `targets`, `credentials` tables exactly as in the contract (Task 3);
  `pgtest.New`, `pgtest.Main` (`internal/testutil/pgtest`); `fakeGate`, `quiet` (`internal/jobs/scheduler_test.go`).
- Produces (`internal/inventory/jobs.go`):
  ```go
  const JobTestConnection = "target.test_connection"; const JobDiscover = "target.discover"; const JobSSHKeyRemove = "sshkey.remove"
  type JobRequest struct { Type string; TargetID uuid.UUID; Payload map[string]string; Kind string; CreatedBy uuid.UUID; CreatedByRole string; DedupeKey string }
  type Enqueuer interface { EnqueueTx(ctx context.Context, tx pgx.Tx, r JobRequest) (uuid.UUID, error) }
  ```
- Produces (`internal/jobs`): `TargetTestConnection`, `TargetDiscover`, `SSHKeyRemove` (types); `Kind` (`KindUser`,
  `KindScheduled`, `KindSystem`); `Status` (`StatusQueued`, `StatusRunning`, `StatusSucceeded`, `StatusFailed`,
  `StatusCancelled`, `StatusDead`, `StatusBlocked`); `MaxAttemptsFor(Type) int`; `FailureClass` (`Retryable`,
  `Permanent`, `NeedsAttention`), `Failure`, `Retry`, `Fail`, `Attention`, `FromProvider`; `Deriver`; `QueueConfig`
  `{Pool, Keyring Deriver, Audit, Clock, Gate}`; `Spec`, `Job`, `View`, `ListFilter`; `ErrNotFound`, `ErrNotWaiting`,
  `ErrUnknownType`, `ErrBadCursor`; `NewQueue`, `(*Queue).Add/Enqueue/EnqueueTx/Get/List/Confirm/Discard`;

```go
package jobs

import (
	"bytes"
	"context"
	"errors"
	"testing"
	"time"

	"github.com/google/uuid"
	"github.com/stretchr/testify/assert"
	"github.com/stretchr/testify/require"

	"alice/internal/inventory"
	"alice/internal/license"

	"alice/internal/secrets"
)

func TestPayloadMACLabelIsTheSecretsLabel(t *testing.T) {
	assert.Equal(t, secrets.LabelJob, payloadMACLabel, "the job MAC key is the J-1 sub-key")
}

func TestPayloadMACCoversEveryField(t *testing.T) {
	key := bytes.Repeat([]byte{3}, 32)
	id, target, by := uuid.New(), uuid.New(), uuid.New()
	payload := canonicalPayload(map[string]string{"location_id": "a"})
	base := payloadMAC(key, id, "sshkey.remove", target, payload, by)
	require.Len(t, base, 32)
	assert.Equal(t, base, payloadMAC(key, id, "sshkey.remove", target, payload, by), "deterministic")
	for name, other := range map[string][]byte{
		"key":        payloadMAC(bytes.Repeat([]byte{4}, 32), id, "sshkey.remove", target, payload, by),
		"id":         payloadMAC(key, uuid.New(), "sshkey.remove", target, payload, by),
		"type":       payloadMAC(key, id, "target.discover", target, payload, by),
		"target":     payloadMAC(key, id, "sshkey.remove", uuid.New(), payload, by),
		"no target":  payloadMAC(key, id, "sshkey.remove", uuid.Nil, payload, by),
		"payload":    payloadMAC(key, id, "sshkey.remove", target, canonicalPayload(map[string]string{"location_id": "b"}), by),
		"created by": payloadMAC(key, id, "sshkey.remove", target, payload, uuid.Nil),
	} {
		assert.NotEqual(t, base, other, name)
	}
}

func TestCanonicalPayloadIsOrderIndependentAndNeverNull(t *testing.T) {
	assert.Equal(t, `{}`, string(canonicalPayload(nil)))
	a := canonicalPayload(map[string]string{"b": "2", "a": "1"})
	assert.Equal(t, `{"a":"1","b":"2"}`, string(a))
}

func TestBackoff(t *testing.T) {
	for _, tc := range []struct {
		attempt int
		jitter  float64
		want    time.Duration
	}{
		{0, 0, 30 * time.Second},
		{1, 0, 30 * time.Second},
		{2, 0, time.Minute},
		{3, 0, 2 * time.Minute},
		{6, 0, 16 * time.Minute},
		{7, 0, 30 * time.Minute},
		{40, 0, 30 * time.Minute},
		{1, 0.2, 36 * time.Second},
		{1, -0.2, 24 * time.Second},
		{1, 5, 36 * time.Second}, // jitter is clamped to ±20 %
	} {
		assert.Equal(t, tc.want, Backoff(tc.attempt, tc.jitter), "attempt %d jitter %v", tc.attempt, tc.jitter)
	}
}

func TestFromProvider(t *testing.T) {
	var f *Failure
	err := FromProvider(providers.NewError("ssh.unreachable", true, errors.New("dial tcp: refused"), map[string]string{"host": "web-01"}))
	require.ErrorAs(t, err, &f)
	assert.Equal(t, Retryable, f.Class)
	assert.Equal(t, "ssh.unreachable", f.Reason)
	assert.Equal(t, map[string]string{"host": "web-01"}, f.Params)

	err = FromProvider(providers.NewError("ssh.auth_failed", false, nil, nil))
	require.ErrorAs(t, err, &f)
	assert.Equal(t, Permanent, f.Class)
	assert.Equal(t, "ssh.auth_failed", f.Reason)

	same := Fail("sshkey.own_key_protected", nil, nil)
	assert.Same(t, same, FromProvider(same), "a classified failure passes through")

	err = FromProvider(errors.New("boom"))
	require.ErrorAs(t, err, &f)
	assert.Equal(t, Retryable, f.Class)
	assert.Equal(t, "internal.unexpected", f.Reason)
	assert.NoError(t, FromProvider(nil))
}

func TestFailureMessageHidesTheCause(t *testing.T) {
	err := Retry("ssh.timeout", nil, errors.New("CANARY-secret-detail"))
	assert.Equal(t, "jobs: ssh.timeout", err.Error())
	assert.NotContains(t, err.Error(), "CANARY")
	assert.ErrorContains(t, errors.Unwrap(err), "CANARY", "the cause stays reachable for errors.Is/As")
}

func TestMaxAttemptsFor(t *testing.T) {
	assert.Equal(t, 1, MaxAttemptsFor(TargetTestConnection))
	assert.Equal(t, 5, MaxAttemptsFor(TargetDiscover))
	assert.Equal(t, 3, MaxAttemptsFor(SSHKeyRemove))
}

func TestPhase3JobTypesDeclareTheirLicenseClass(t *testing.T) {
	assert.Equal(t, Type{Name: inventory.JobTestConnection, Class: license.ClassReadOnly}, TargetTestConnection)
	assert.Equal(t, Type{Name: inventory.JobDiscover, Class: license.ClassReadOnly}, TargetDiscover)
	assert.Equal(t, Type{Name: inventory.JobSSHKeyRemove, Class: license.ClassChange}, SSHKeyRemove)
}

func TestHandleRefusesUnregisteredAndDuplicateHandlers(t *testing.T) {
	r := NewRunner(RunnerConfig{})
	h := func(_ context.Context, _ Job, _ StepRecorder) (map[string]any, error) { return nil, nil }
	assert.Panics(t, func() { r.Handle(Type{Name: "never.registered", Class: license.ClassAlways}, h) })
	assert.Panics(t, func() { r.Handle(Type{Name: TargetDiscover.Name, Class: license.ClassAlways}, h) }, "class must match the registry")
	r.Handle(TargetDiscover, h)
	assert.Panics(t, func() { r.Handle(TargetDiscover, h) })
}

func TestNewRunnerDefaults(t *testing.T) {
	r := NewRunner(RunnerConfig{})
	assert.Equal(t, 8, r.cfg.Workers)
	assert.Equal(t, 45*time.Second, r.cfg.Lease)
	assert.Equal(t, 15*time.Second, r.cfg.Heartbeat)
	assert.Equal(t, time.Second, r.cfg.Poll)
	assert.Equal(t, time.Minute, r.cfg.ReapEvery)
	assert.Equal(t, time.Minute, r.cfg.ShutdownGrace)
	assert.NotEmpty(t, r.cfg.WorkerID)
	for range 100 {
		j := r.cfg.Jitter()
		assert.True(t, j >= -0.2 && j <= 0.2, "jitter %v", j)
	}
}
```

```go
// Kind says who asked for a job (jobs.kind).

	KindScheduled Kind = "scheduled"
	KindSystem    Kind = "system"
```

- [ ] **Step 4: Write the failure classification**

Create `internal/jobs/failure.go`:

```go
package jobs

import (
	"errors"

	"alice/internal/providers"
)

// FailureClass says what the runner does with a failed job (spec §8.4).
type FailureClass int

// Failure classes.
const (
	// Retryable failures run again after Backoff until MaxAttempts, then the job is dead.
	Retryable FailureClass = iota
	// Permanent failures (authentication failed, host key changed) never retry.
	Permanent
	// NeedsAttention failures stop and are flagged for a person.
	NeedsAttention
)

// Failure is a classified job error. Reason is a stable reason ("ssh.auth_failed") that the
// API maps to an ALC code; Params are shown with it. Cause is kept for errors.Is/As and its
// type for the logs; its text is never stored, logged or shown.
type Failure struct {
	Class  FailureClass
	Reason string
	Params map[string]string
	Cause  error
}

// Error names the reason only: the cause's text may carry remote output or values.
func (f *Failure) Error() string { return "jobs: " + f.Reason }

// Unwrap returns the cause.
func (f *Failure) Unwrap() error { return f.Cause }

// Retry is a failure that may succeed later.
func Retry(reason string, params map[string]string, cause error) error {
	return &Failure{Class: Retryable, Reason: reason, Params: params, Cause: cause}
}

// Fail is a failure that never succeeds by trying again.
func Fail(reason string, params map[string]string, cause error) error {
	return &Failure{Class: Permanent, Reason: reason, Params: params, Cause: cause}
}

// Attention is a failure a person must look at.
func Attention(reason string, params map[string]string, cause error) error {
	return &Failure{Class: NeedsAttention, Reason: reason, Params: params, Cause: cause}
}

// FromProvider classifies err: a *Failure passes through, a *providers.Error keeps its code
// and params (retryable or permanent as the provider says), anything else is an unexpected,
// retryable failure.
func FromProvider(err error) error {
	if err == nil {
		return nil
	}
	var f *Failure
	if errors.As(err, &f) {
		return f
	}
	var pe *providers.Error
	if errors.As(err, &pe) {
		if pe.Retryable {
			return Retry(pe.Code, pe.Params, err)
		}
		return Fail(pe.Code, pe.Params, err)
	}
	return Retry("internal.unexpected", nil, err)
}

// classify turns any handler error into a *Failure.
func classify(err error) *Failure {
	var f *Failure
	if errors.As(FromProvider(err), &f) {
		return f
	}
	return &Failure{Class: Retryable, Reason: "internal.unexpected", Cause: err}
}
```
