- [ ] **Step 5: Write the queue**

Create `internal/jobs/queue.go`:

```go
package jobs

import (
	"context"
	"crypto/hmac"
	"crypto/sha256"
	"encoding/base64"
	"encoding/json"
	"errors"
	"fmt"
	"strconv"
	"strings"
	"time"

	"github.com/google/uuid"
	"github.com/jackc/pgx/v5"
	"github.com/jackc/pgx/v5/pgxpool"

	"alice/internal/audit"
	"alice/internal/inventory"
	"alice/internal/license"
	"alice/internal/platform/clock"
	"alice/internal/platform/db"
)

// Errors of the queue.
var (
	ErrNotFound    = errors.New("jobs: not found")
	ErrNotWaiting  = errors.New("jobs: the job is not waiting for a confirmation")
	ErrUnknownType = errors.New("jobs: job type is not registered")
	ErrBadCursor   = errors.New("jobs: invalid cursor")
)

// Deriver derives a sub-key from the master key; *secrets.Keyring implements it. jobs may not
// import secrets (spec §5.4), so the queue takes this one-method view of the keyring.
type Deriver interface {
	Derive(label string) []byte
}

// payloadMACLabel is secrets.LabelJob (a test asserts it): the HKDF label of the job payload
// MAC (threat J-1: a row inserted or edited in the database is never executed).
const payloadMACLabel = "alice/job/v1"

// jobsActor is the audit actor of the queue's own decisions.
var jobsActor = audit.SystemActor("jobs")

// liveStatuses are the statuses under which a dedupe key is taken (jobs_dedupe_live).
const liveStatuses = `('queued', 'running', 'blocked_license')`

// QueueConfig holds the queue's dependencies.
type QueueConfig struct {
	Pool    *pgxpool.Pool
	Keyring Deriver // payload MAC under secrets.LabelJob
	Audit   *audit.Log
	Clock   clock.Clock
	Gate    Gate // Confirm refuses while the gate refuses external changes; nil refuses always
}

// Queue writes and reads jobs.
type Queue struct {
	pool    *pgxpool.Pool
	keyring Deriver
	audit   *audit.Log
	clock   clock.Clock
	gate    Gate
}

// NewQueue returns a Queue.
func NewQueue(c QueueConfig) *Queue {
	return &Queue{pool: c.Pool, keyring: c.Keyring, audit: c.Audit, clock: c.Clock, gate: c.Gate}
}

var _ inventory.Enqueuer = (*Queue)(nil)

// Spec describes a job to enqueue.
type Spec struct {
	Type          Type
	TargetID      uuid.UUID // uuid.Nil = none
	Payload       map[string]string
	Kind          Kind
	Priority      int       // 0 = 1 for user jobs, 5 otherwise
	MaxAttempts   int       // 0 = the type's default (MaxAttemptsFor)
	RunAt         time.Time // zero = now
	DedupeKey     string
	CreatedBy     uuid.UUID
	CreatedByRole string
}

// Job is what a handler receives.
type Job struct {
	ID            uuid.UUID
	Type          Type
	Kind          Kind
	TargetID      uuid.UUID
	Payload       map[string]string
	Attempt       int // 1 for the first run
	MaxAttempts   int
	CreatedBy     uuid.UUID
	CreatedByRole string
}

// View is a stored job as the API shows it.
type View struct {
	ID            uuid.UUID
	Type          string
	Kind          string
	Status        Status
	TargetID      uuid.UUID
	Attempts      int
	MaxAttempts   int
	LastErrorCode string
	ErrorParams   map[string]string
	Result        map[string]any
	CreatedBy     uuid.UUID
	CreatedAt     time.Time
	RunAt         time.Time
	StartedAt     *time.Time
	FinishedAt    *time.Time
}

// ListFilter selects jobs, newest first.
type ListFilter struct {
	Status   Status    // "" = all
	TargetID uuid.UUID // uuid.Nil = all
	Cursor   string
	Limit    int // 1..200, default 50
}

// canonicalPayload is the payload's JSON with sorted keys; a nil payload is {}.
func canonicalPayload(p map[string]string) []byte {
	if p == nil {
		p = map[string]string{}
	}
	b, err := json.Marshal(p)
	if err != nil {
		panic("jobs: encode payload: " + err.Error()) // a map of strings always encodes
	}
	return b
}

func uuidText(u uuid.UUID) string {
	if u == uuid.Nil {
		return ""
	}
	return u.String()
}

// payloadMAC is HMAC-SHA256 over everything that decides what a job does.
func payloadMAC(key []byte, id uuid.UUID, typ string, target uuid.UUID, payload []byte, createdBy uuid.UUID) []byte {
	m := hmac.New(sha256.New, key)
	m.Write([]byte("alice-job-v1\n" + id.String() + "\n" + typ + "\n" + uuidText(target) + "\n"))
	m.Write(payload)
	m.Write([]byte("\n" + uuidText(createdBy)))
	return m.Sum(nil)
}

// mac derives the key for one computation and clears it afterwards.
func (q *Queue) mac(id uuid.UUID, typ string, target uuid.UUID, payload []byte, createdBy uuid.UUID) []byte {
	key := q.keyring.Derive(payloadMACLabel)
	defer clear(key)
	return payloadMAC(key, id, typ, target, payload, createdBy)
}

func nullUUID(u uuid.UUID) *uuid.UUID {
	if u == uuid.Nil {
		return nil
	}
	return &u
}

func nullString(s string) *string {
	if s == "" {
		return nil
	}
	return &s
}

// Add writes a job in tx. When a live job (queued, running or blocked) holds the same dedupe
// key, nothing is written and that job's id is returned with true.
func (q *Queue) Add(ctx context.Context, tx pgx.Tx, s Spec) (uuid.UUID, bool, error) {
	reg, ok := lookup(s.Type.Name)
	if !ok || reg != s.Type {
		return uuid.Nil, false, fmt.Errorf("%w: %q", ErrUnknownType, s.Type.Name)
	}
	if !s.Kind.valid() {
		return uuid.Nil, false, fmt.Errorf("jobs: invalid job kind %q", s.Kind)
	}
	priority := s.Priority
	if priority == 0 {
		priority = 5
		if s.Kind == KindUser {
			priority = 1
		}
	}
	maxAttempts := s.MaxAttempts
	if maxAttempts <= 0 {
		maxAttempts = MaxAttemptsFor(s.Type)
	}
	now := q.clock.Now().UTC()
	runAt := s.RunAt.UTC()
	if s.RunAt.IsZero() {
		runAt = now
	}
	payload := canonicalPayload(s.Payload)
	id := uuid.Must(uuid.NewV7())
	var inserted uuid.UUID
	err := tx.QueryRow(ctx, `INSERT INTO jobs (id, type, class, kind, payload, payload_mac, target_id, dedupe_key, status,
    priority, run_at, max_attempts, created_by, created_by_role, created_at)
VALUES ($1, $2, $3, $4, $5::jsonb, $6, $7, $8, 'queued', $9, $10, $11, $12, $13, $14)
ON CONFLICT (dedupe_key) WHERE status IN `+liveStatuses+` DO NOTHING
RETURNING id`,
		id, s.Type.Name, s.Type.Class.String(), string(s.Kind), string(payload), q.mac(id, s.Type.Name, s.TargetID, payload, s.CreatedBy),
		nullUUID(s.TargetID), nullString(s.DedupeKey), priority, runAt, maxAttempts, nullUUID(s.CreatedBy), s.CreatedByRole, now,
	).Scan(&inserted)
	if err == nil {
		return inserted, false, nil
	}
	if !errors.Is(err, pgx.ErrNoRows) {
		return uuid.Nil, false, fmt.Errorf("jobs: enqueue %s: %w", s.Type.Name, err)
	}
	var existing uuid.UUID
	if err := tx.QueryRow(ctx, `SELECT id FROM jobs WHERE dedupe_key = $1 AND status IN `+liveStatuses,
		s.DedupeKey).Scan(&existing); err != nil {
		return uuid.Nil, false, fmt.Errorf("jobs: read the job holding the dedupe key: %w", err)
	}
	return existing, true, nil
}

// Enqueue is Add in its own transaction.
func (q *Queue) Enqueue(ctx context.Context, s Spec) (uuid.UUID, bool, error) {
	var id uuid.UUID
	var dup bool
	err := db.InTx(ctx, q.pool, func(tx pgx.Tx) error {
		var err error
		id, dup, err = q.Add(ctx, tx, s)
		return err
	})
	return id, dup, err
}

// EnqueueTx implements inventory.Enqueuer.
func (q *Queue) EnqueueTx(ctx context.Context, tx pgx.Tx, r inventory.JobRequest) (uuid.UUID, error) {
	t, ok := lookup(r.Type)
	if !ok {
		return uuid.Nil, fmt.Errorf("%w: %q", ErrUnknownType, r.Type)
	}
	id, _, err := q.Add(ctx, tx, Spec{
		Type: t, TargetID: r.TargetID, Payload: r.Payload, Kind: Kind(r.Kind), DedupeKey: r.DedupeKey,
		CreatedBy: r.CreatedBy, CreatedByRole: r.CreatedByRole,
	})
	return id, err
}

const viewColumns = `id, type, kind, status, target_id, attempts, max_attempts, last_error_code, result, created_by,
    created_at, run_at, started_at, finished_at`

func scanView(row pgx.Row) (View, error) {
	var (
		v          View
		status     string
		target, by *uuid.UUID
		result     []byte
	)
	if err := row.Scan(&v.ID, &v.Type, &v.Kind, &status, &target, &v.Attempts, &v.MaxAttempts, &v.LastErrorCode, &result,
		&by, &v.CreatedAt, &v.RunAt, &v.StartedAt, &v.FinishedAt); err != nil {
		return View{}, err
	}
	v.Status = Status(status)
	if target != nil {
		v.TargetID = *target
	}
	if by != nil {
		v.CreatedBy = *by
	}
	v.CreatedAt, v.RunAt = v.CreatedAt.UTC(), v.RunAt.UTC()
	for _, t := range []*time.Time{v.StartedAt, v.FinishedAt} {
		if t != nil {
			*t = t.UTC()
		}
	}
	v.Result = map[string]any{}
	if err := json.Unmarshal(result, &v.Result); err != nil {
		return View{}, fmt.Errorf("jobs: decode result: %w", err)
	}
	if params, ok := v.Result["error_params"].(map[string]any); ok {
		v.ErrorParams = map[string]string{}
		for k, val := range params {
			if s, ok := val.(string); ok {
				v.ErrorParams[k] = s
			}
		}
	}
	return v, nil
}

// Get returns one job.
func (q *Queue) Get(ctx context.Context, id uuid.UUID) (View, error) {
	v, err := scanView(q.pool.QueryRow(ctx, `SELECT `+viewColumns+` FROM jobs WHERE id = $1`, id))
	if errors.Is(err, pgx.ErrNoRows) {
		return View{}, ErrNotFound
	}
	if err != nil {
		return View{}, fmt.Errorf("jobs: read job: %w", err)
	}
	return v, nil
}

func encodeCursor(at time.Time, id uuid.UUID) string {
	return base64.RawURLEncoding.EncodeToString([]byte(strconv.FormatInt(at.UnixMicro(), 10) + "|" + id.String()))
}

func decodeCursor(c string) (time.Time, uuid.UUID, error) {
	raw, err := base64.RawURLEncoding.DecodeString(c)
	if err != nil {
		return time.Time{}, uuid.Nil, ErrBadCursor
	}
	at, id, ok := strings.Cut(string(raw), "|")
	if !ok {
		return time.Time{}, uuid.Nil, ErrBadCursor
	}
	micros, err := strconv.ParseInt(at, 10, 64)
	if err != nil {
		return time.Time{}, uuid.Nil, ErrBadCursor
	}
	u, err := uuid.Parse(id)
	if err != nil {
		return time.Time{}, uuid.Nil, ErrBadCursor
	}
	return time.UnixMicro(micros).UTC(), u, nil
}

// List pages jobs newest first. The returned cursor is "" on the last page.
func (q *Queue) List(ctx context.Context, f ListFilter) ([]View, string, error) {
	limit := f.Limit
	if limit <= 0 {
		limit = 50
	}
	limit = min(limit, 200)
	var (
		afterAt *time.Time
		afterID *uuid.UUID
	)
	if f.Cursor != "" {
		at, id, err := decodeCursor(f.Cursor)
		if err != nil {
			return nil, "", err
		}
		afterAt, afterID = &at, &id
	}
	rows, err := q.pool.Query(ctx, `SELECT `+viewColumns+` FROM jobs
WHERE ($1::text IS NULL OR status = $1)
  AND ($2::uuid IS NULL OR target_id = $2)
  AND ($3::timestamptz IS NULL OR (created_at, id) < ($3, $4::uuid))
ORDER BY created_at DESC, id DESC
LIMIT $5`, nullString(string(f.Status)), nullUUID(f.TargetID), afterAt, afterID, limit+1)
	if err != nil {
		return nil, "", fmt.Errorf("jobs: list: %w", err)
	}
	defer rows.Close()
	var out []View
	for rows.Next() {
		v, err := scanView(rows)
		if err != nil {
			return nil, "", fmt.Errorf("jobs: list: %w", err)
		}
		out = append(out, v)
	}
	if err := rows.Err(); err != nil {
		return nil, "", fmt.Errorf("jobs: list: %w", err)
	}
	next := ""
	if len(out) > limit {
		out = out[:limit]
		last := out[len(out)-1]
		next = encodeCursor(last.CreatedAt, last.ID)
	}
	return out, next, nil
}

// lockStatus reads a job's status and type under its row lock.
func lockStatus(ctx context.Context, tx pgx.Tx, id uuid.UUID) (Status, string, error) {
	var status, typ string
	err := tx.QueryRow(ctx, `SELECT status, type FROM jobs WHERE id = $1 FOR UPDATE`, id).Scan(&status, &typ)
	if errors.Is(err, pgx.ErrNoRows) {
		return "", "", ErrNotFound
	}
	if err != nil {
		return "", "", fmt.Errorf("jobs: read job: %w", err)
	}
	return Status(status), typ, nil
}

// Confirm lets an Administrator start work that was held while the license was expired (R29,
// L-81): blocked_license -> queued. It is refused while the gate still refuses the work.
func (q *Queue) Confirm(ctx context.Context, actor audit.Actor, by uuid.UUID, id uuid.UUID) error {
	return db.InTx(ctx, q.pool, func(tx pgx.Tx) error {
		status, typ, err := lockStatus(ctx, tx, id)
		if err != nil {
			return err
		}
		if status != StatusBlocked {
			return ErrNotWaiting
		}
		t, ok := lookup(typ)
		if !ok {
			return fmt.Errorf("%w: %q", ErrUnknownType, typ)
		}
		if q.gate == nil {
			return license.ErrLocked
		}
		if err := q.gate.Allow(t.Class); err != nil {
			return err
		}
		now := q.clock.Now().UTC()
		if _, err := tx.Exec(ctx, `UPDATE jobs SET status = 'queued', run_at = $2, confirmed_by = $3, confirmed_at = $2,
    last_error_code = '' WHERE id = $1`, id, now, nullUUID(by)); err != nil {
			return fmt.Errorf("jobs: confirm: %w", err)
		}
		_, err = q.audit.Append(ctx, tx, audit.Event{Actor: actor, Action: "job.confirmed", ObjectType: "job",
			ObjectID: id.String(), Result: audit.Success, Details: map[string]string{"type": typ}})
		return err
	})
}

// Discard cancels a job that waits for a confirmation or has not started yet.
func (q *Queue) Discard(ctx context.Context, actor audit.Actor, by uuid.UUID, id uuid.UUID) error {
	return db.InTx(ctx, q.pool, func(tx pgx.Tx) error {
		status, typ, err := lockStatus(ctx, tx, id)
		if err != nil {
			return err
		}
		if status != StatusBlocked && status != StatusQueued {
			return ErrNotWaiting
		}
		now := q.clock.Now().UTC()
		if _, err := tx.Exec(ctx, `UPDATE jobs SET status = 'cancelled', finished_at = $2, confirmed_by = $3, confirmed_at = $2
WHERE id = $1`, id, now, nullUUID(by)); err != nil {
			return fmt.Errorf("jobs: discard: %w", err)
		}
		_, err = q.audit.Append(ctx, tx, audit.Event{Actor: actor, Action: "job.discarded", ObjectType: "job",
			ObjectID: id.String(), Result: audit.Success, Details: map[string]string{"type": typ, "from_status": string(status)}})
		return err
	})
}
```

- [ ] **Step 6: Write the runner**

Create `internal/jobs/runner.go`:

```go
package jobs

import (
	"context"
	"crypto/hmac"
	"crypto/rand"
	"encoding/binary"
	"encoding/json"
	"errors"
	"fmt"
	"io"
	"log/slog"
	"os"
	"sort"
	"strconv"
	"sync"
	"sync/atomic"
	"time"

	"github.com/google/uuid"
	"github.com/jackc/pgx/v5"
	"github.com/jackc/pgx/v5/pgconn"
	"github.com/jackc/pgx/v5/pgxpool"

	"alice/internal/audit"
	"alice/internal/license"
	"alice/internal/platform/clock"
	"alice/internal/platform/db"
	"alice/internal/providers"
)

// StepRecorder records the externally visible steps of a job (spec §6.3 item 2); the steps are
// stored in the job's result.
type StepRecorder interface {
	providers.StepLogger
}

// HandlerFunc runs one job. Its result map is stored as the job's result; it must hold ids and
// public facts only, never secrets. Errors are classified with FromProvider.
type HandlerFunc func(ctx context.Context, j Job, steps StepRecorder) (map[string]any, error)

// RunnerConfig holds the runner's dependencies and limits.
type RunnerConfig struct {
	Pool          *pgxpool.Pool
	Queue         *Queue
	Gate          Gate
	Audit         *audit.Log
	Clock         clock.Clock
	Log           *slog.Logger
	Workers       int            // default 8
	WorkerID      string         // default "<hostname>-<pid>-<random>"
	Lease         time.Duration  // default 45 s
	Heartbeat     time.Duration  // default 15 s
	Poll          time.Duration  // default 1 s
	ReapEvery     time.Duration  // default 60 s
	ShutdownGrace time.Duration  // default 60 s
	Jitter        func() float64 // in [-0.2, 0.2]; default crypto/rand
}

// Runner claims and runs queued jobs (spec §8.1, §8.4, §8.5, §8.8).
type Runner struct {
	cfg      RunnerConfig
	mu       sync.Mutex
	handlers map[string]HandlerFunc
	stopping atomic.Bool // Run is shutting down: interrupted jobs are released, not failed
}

const (
	baseBackoff = 30 * time.Second
	maxBackoff  = 30 * time.Minute
)

// Backoff is the wait before the next attempt (spec §8.4): min(30 s · 2^(attempt-1), 30 min)
// times (1 + jitter), jitter clamped to ±20 %.
func Backoff(attempt int, jitter float64) time.Duration {
	if attempt < 1 {
		attempt = 1
	}
	d := maxBackoff
	if attempt <= 7 { // 30 s · 2^6 = 32 min is already above the cap
		d = min(baseBackoff<<(attempt-1), maxBackoff)
	}
	jitter = max(-0.2, min(0.2, jitter))
	return time.Duration(float64(d) * (1 + jitter))
}

func cryptoJitter() float64 {
	var b [8]byte
	_, _ = rand.Read(b[:])
	u := float64(binary.BigEndian.Uint64(b[:])>>11) / (1 << 53) // [0, 1)
	return u*0.4 - 0.2
}

func defaultWorkerID() string {
	host, err := os.Hostname()
	if err != nil {
		host = "alice"
	}
	return host + "-" + strconv.Itoa(os.Getpid()) + "-" + rand.Text()[:8]
}

// NewRunner applies the defaults of RunnerConfig.
func NewRunner(c RunnerConfig) *Runner {
	if c.Workers <= 0 {
		c.Workers = 8
	}
	if c.WorkerID == "" {
		c.WorkerID = defaultWorkerID()
	}
	for _, d := range []struct {
		v   *time.Duration
		def time.Duration
	}{{&c.Lease, 45 * time.Second}, {&c.Heartbeat, 15 * time.Second}, {&c.Poll, time.Second},
		{&c.ReapEvery, time.Minute}, {&c.ShutdownGrace, time.Minute}} {
		if *d.v <= 0 {
			*d.v = d.def
		}
	}
	if c.Jitter == nil {
		c.Jitter = cryptoJitter
	}
	if c.Log == nil {
		c.Log = slog.New(slog.NewTextHandler(io.Discard, nil))
	}
	return &Runner{cfg: c, handlers: map[string]HandlerFunc{}}
}

// Handle installs the handler of a job type. It panics for a type that is not registered (with
// the same class) or that already has a handler.
func (r *Runner) Handle(t Type, h HandlerFunc) {
	reg, ok := lookup(t.Name)
	if !ok || reg != t || h == nil {
		panic(fmt.Sprintf("jobs: handler for unregistered job type %q", t.Name))
	}
	r.mu.Lock()
	defer r.mu.Unlock()
	if _, dup := r.handlers[t.Name]; dup {
		panic(fmt.Sprintf("jobs: job type %q has two handlers", t.Name))
	}
	r.handlers[t.Name] = h
}

func (r *Runner) handler(name string) HandlerFunc {
	r.mu.Lock()
	defer r.mu.Unlock()
	return r.handlers[name]
}

// handled returns the job types this runner can run; it never claims others.
func (r *Runner) handled() []string {
	r.mu.Lock()
	defer r.mu.Unlock()
	out := make([]string, 0, len(r.handlers))
	for name := range r.handlers {
		out = append(out, name)
	}
	sort.Strings(out)
	return out
}

func (r *Runner) jobEvent(action string, result audit.Result, id uuid.UUID, details map[string]string) audit.Event {
	return audit.Event{Actor: jobsActor, Action: action, ObjectType: "job", ObjectID: id.String(), Result: result, Details: details}
}

// claimed is a job this worker holds the lease of.
type claimed struct {
	id          uuid.UUID
	typ         string
	kind        string
	payload     []byte
	mac         []byte
	target      uuid.UUID
	attempts    int // after the claim: this run's attempt number
	maxAttempts int
	createdBy   uuid.UUID
	role        string
}

var allClasses = []string{license.ClassAlways.String(), license.ClassReadOnly.String(), license.ClassChange.String()}

// maxCandidates bounds how many busy-target jobs one claim skips before it gives up.
const maxCandidates = 10

// claim takes the next due job in one transaction: the job row (SKIP LOCKED), the target lock
// and the attempt row commit together, so a target never runs two jobs. In lock it first moves
// queued external-change jobs to blocked_license and cancels queued read-only jobs (§8.6), then
// claims only always-class work.
func (r *Runner) claim(ctx context.Context) (*claimed, error) {
	types := r.handled()
	if len(types) == 0 {
		return nil, nil
	}
	now := r.cfg.Clock.Now().UTC()
	classes := allClasses
	locked := errors.Is(r.cfg.Gate.Allow(license.ClassChange), license.ErrLocked)
	var c *claimed
	err := db.InTx(ctx, r.cfg.Pool, func(tx pgx.Tx) error {
		if locked {
			if err := r.sweepLocked(ctx, tx, now); err != nil {
				return err
			}
			classes = []string{license.ClassAlways.String()}
		}
		skip := []string{} // never nil: ANY(NULL) would exclude every row
		for range maxCandidates {
			var (
				cand             claimed
				target, by       *uuid.UUID
				attempts, maxAtt int
			)
			err := tx.QueryRow(ctx, `SELECT id, type, kind, payload, payload_mac, target_id, attempts, max_attempts, created_by, created_by_role
FROM jobs j
WHERE status = 'queued' AND run_at <= $1 AND class = ANY($2) AND type = ANY($3) AND NOT (id::text = ANY($4::text[]))
  AND (target_id IS NULL OR NOT EXISTS (
        SELECT 1 FROM target_locks l WHERE l.target_id = j.target_id AND l.lease_until > $1))
ORDER BY priority, run_at, id
FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED
LIMIT 1`, now, classes, types, skip).Scan(&cand.id, &cand.typ, &cand.kind, &cand.payload, &cand.mac, &target,
				&attempts, &maxAtt, &by, &cand.role)
			if errors.Is(err, pgx.ErrNoRows) {
				return nil
			}
			if err != nil {
				return fmt.Errorf("jobs: select a job: %w", err)
			}
			if target != nil {
				cand.target = *target
				var got uuid.UUID
				err := tx.QueryRow(ctx, `INSERT INTO target_locks (target_id, job_id, operation, locked_by, heartbeat_at, lease_until)
VALUES ($1, $2, $3, $4, $5, $6)
ON CONFLICT (target_id) DO UPDATE SET job_id = EXCLUDED.job_id, operation = EXCLUDED.operation,
    locked_by = EXCLUDED.locked_by, heartbeat_at = EXCLUDED.heartbeat_at, lease_until = EXCLUDED.lease_until
WHERE target_locks.lease_until <= $5
RETURNING target_id`, cand.target, cand.id, cand.typ, r.cfg.WorkerID, now, now.Add(r.cfg.Lease)).Scan(&got)
				if errors.Is(err, pgx.ErrNoRows) {
					skip = append(skip, cand.id.String()) // another job holds the target (§12.5)
					continue
				}
				if err != nil {
					return fmt.Errorf("jobs: lock the target: %w", err)
				}
			}
			if by != nil {
				cand.createdBy = *by
			}
			if _, err := tx.Exec(ctx, `UPDATE jobs SET status = 'running', locked_by = $2, locked_until = $3, heartbeat_at = $4,
    attempts = attempts + 1, started_at = coalesce(started_at, $4)
WHERE id = $1`, cand.id, r.cfg.WorkerID, now.Add(r.cfg.Lease), now); err != nil {
				return fmt.Errorf("jobs: mark running: %w", err)
			}
			cand.attempts, cand.maxAttempts = attempts+1, maxAtt
			if _, err := tx.Exec(ctx, `INSERT INTO job_attempts (id, job_id, attempt, worker_id, started_at) VALUES ($1, $2, $3, $4, $5)`,
				uuid.Must(uuid.NewV7()), cand.id, cand.attempts, r.cfg.WorkerID, now); err != nil {
				return fmt.Errorf("jobs: record the attempt: %w", err)
			}
			c = &cand
			return nil
		}
		return nil
	})
	if err != nil {
		return nil, err
	}
	return c, nil
}

// sweepLocked holds queued external-change work for an Administrator's confirmation and
// cancels queued read-only work while the license is expired (spec §8.6, R29, L-81).
func (r *Runner) sweepLocked(ctx context.Context, tx pgx.Tx, now time.Time) error {
	rows, err := tx.Query(ctx, `UPDATE jobs SET status = 'blocked_license' WHERE status = 'queued' AND class = 'change' RETURNING id, type`)
	if err != nil {
		return fmt.Errorf("jobs: hold changes in lock: %w", err)
	}
	type held struct {
		id  uuid.UUID
		typ string
	}
	var blocked []held
	for rows.Next() {
		var h held
		if err := rows.Scan(&h.id, &h.typ); err != nil {
			rows.Close()
			return fmt.Errorf("jobs: hold changes in lock: %w", err)
		}
		blocked = append(blocked, h)
	}
	rows.Close()
	if err := rows.Err(); err != nil {
		return fmt.Errorf("jobs: hold changes in lock: %w", err)
	}
	for _, h := range blocked {
		if _, err := r.cfg.Audit.Append(ctx, tx, r.jobEvent("job.blocked_license", audit.Denied, h.id, map[string]string{"type": h.typ})); err != nil {
			return err
		}
	}
	if _, err := tx.Exec(ctx, `UPDATE jobs SET status = 'cancelled', last_error_code = 'license.locked', finished_at = $1
WHERE status = 'queued' AND class = 'read_only'`, now); err != nil {
		return fmt.Errorf("jobs: cancel read-only work in lock: %w", err)
	}
	return nil
}

var errLeaseLost = errors.New("jobs: the lease was lost")

// settle ends this worker's run of c in one transaction: set changes the job row (and must
// match it only while this worker still holds it), then the attempt is closed, the target lock
// released and the audit events written. It reports false when the lease was lost: another
// worker or the reaper owns the job now, and nothing is written.
func (r *Runner) settle(ctx context.Context, c *claimed, errorCode string,
	set func(tx pgx.Tx, now time.Time) (pgconn.CommandTag, error), events ...audit.Event) bool {
	err := db.InTx(ctx, r.cfg.Pool, func(tx pgx.Tx) error {
		now := r.cfg.Clock.Now().UTC()
		tag, err := set(tx, now)
		if err != nil {
			return err
		}
		if tag.RowsAffected() != 1 {
			return errLeaseLost
		}
		if _, err := tx.Exec(ctx, `UPDATE job_attempts SET finished_at = $3, error_code = $4 WHERE job_id = $1 AND attempt = $2`,
			c.id, c.attempts, now, errorCode); err != nil {
			return fmt.Errorf("jobs: close the attempt: %w", err)
		}
		if _, err := tx.Exec(ctx, `DELETE FROM target_locks WHERE job_id = $1`, c.id); err != nil {
			return fmt.Errorf("jobs: release the target: %w", err)
		}
		for _, ev := range events {
			if _, err := r.cfg.Audit.Append(ctx, tx, ev); err != nil {
				return err
			}
		}
		return nil
	})
	switch {
	case errors.Is(err, errLeaseLost):
		r.cfg.Log.Warn("job lease lost before the job finished; another worker owns it now", "job_id", c.id.String(), "job_type", c.typ)
		return false
	case err != nil:
		r.cfg.Log.Error("could not record the end of a job", "job_id", c.id.String(), "job_type", c.typ, "error_type", fmt.Sprintf("%T", err))
		return false
	}
	return true
}

// mine is the WHERE clause that makes a job update apply only while this worker holds it.
const mine = `WHERE id = $1 AND locked_by = $2 AND status = 'running'`

// terminate ends c without running it (unknown type, tampered payload).
func (r *Runner) terminate(ctx context.Context, c *claimed, reason, action string) {
	r.settle(ctx, c, reason, func(tx pgx.Tx, now time.Time) (pgconn.CommandTag, error) {
		return tx.Exec(ctx, `UPDATE jobs SET status = 'dead', last_error_code = $3, finished_at = $4, locked_by = NULL,
    locked_until = NULL `+mine, c.id, r.cfg.WorkerID, reason, now)
	}, r.jobEvent(action, audit.Failure, c.id, map[string]string{"type": c.typ, "reason": reason, "attempt": strconv.Itoa(c.attempts)}))
}

// revert undoes a claim the gate refused after it was taken (the lock began in between).
func (r *Runner) revert(ctx context.Context, c *claimed, t Type) {
	if t.Class == license.ClassChange {
		r.settle(ctx, c, "license.locked", func(tx pgx.Tx, _ time.Time) (pgconn.CommandTag, error) {
			return tx.Exec(ctx, `UPDATE jobs SET status = 'blocked_license', attempts = attempts - 1, locked_by = NULL,
    locked_until = NULL `+mine, c.id, r.cfg.WorkerID)
		}, r.jobEvent("job.blocked_license", audit.Denied, c.id, map[string]string{"type": c.typ}))
		return
	}
	r.settle(ctx, c, "license.locked", func(tx pgx.Tx, now time.Time) (pgconn.CommandTag, error) {
		return tx.Exec(ctx, `UPDATE jobs SET status = 'cancelled', last_error_code = 'license.locked', finished_at = $3,
    locked_by = NULL, locked_until = NULL `+mine, c.id, r.cfg.WorkerID, now)
	})
}

// stepLog collects a job's steps for its result.
type stepLog struct {
	mu    sync.Mutex
	steps []map[string]any
}

func (s *stepLog) Step(name string, status providers.StepStatus, params map[string]string) {
	s.mu.Lock()
	defer s.mu.Unlock()
	if params == nil {
		params = map[string]string{}
	}
	s.steps = append(s.steps, map[string]any{"name": name, "status": string(status), "params": params})
}

func (s *stepLog) list() []map[string]any {
	s.mu.Lock()
	defer s.mu.Unlock()
	return append([]map[string]any(nil), s.steps...)
}

// call runs the handler; a panic becomes a retryable failure and its value is never logged
// (it may hold data from the job).
func (r *Runner) call(ctx context.Context, h HandlerFunc, j Job, steps StepRecorder) (res map[string]any, err error) {
	defer func() {
		if p := recover(); p != nil {
			r.cfg.Log.Error("job handler panicked", "job_id", j.ID.String(), "job_type", j.Type.Name)
			res, err = nil, Retry("internal.unexpected", nil, errors.New("jobs: handler panicked"))
		}
	}()
	return h(ctx, j, steps)
}

// heartbeat extends the lease every Heartbeat until stop is called. When the job row is no
// longer this worker's (the reaper took it), it cancels the handler's context.
func (r *Runner) heartbeat(c *claimed, cancel context.CancelFunc) (stop func()) {
	done := make(chan struct{})
	var wg sync.WaitGroup
	wg.Add(1)
	go func() {
		defer wg.Done()
		t := r.cfg.Clock.NewTicker(r.cfg.Heartbeat)
		defer t.Stop()
		for {
			select {
			case <-done:
				return
			case <-t.C():
				ctx, cancelBeat := context.WithTimeout(context.Background(), 5*time.Second)
				now := r.cfg.Clock.Now().UTC()
				tag, err := r.cfg.Pool.Exec(ctx, `UPDATE jobs SET locked_until = $3, heartbeat_at = $4 `+mine,
					c.id, r.cfg.WorkerID, now.Add(r.cfg.Lease), now)
				if err == nil && tag.RowsAffected() == 0 {
					cancelBeat()
					r.cfg.Log.Warn("job lease lost; stopping the handler", "job_id", c.id.String(), "job_type", c.typ)
					cancel()
					return
				}
				if err == nil {
					_, err = r.cfg.Pool.Exec(ctx, `UPDATE target_locks SET heartbeat_at = $3, lease_until = $4 WHERE job_id = $1 AND locked_by = $2`,
						c.id, r.cfg.WorkerID, now, now.Add(r.cfg.Lease))
				}
				cancelBeat()
				if err != nil {
					r.cfg.Log.Warn("job heartbeat failed", "job_id", c.id.String(), "error_type", fmt.Sprintf("%T", err))
				}
			}
		}
	}()
	return func() {
		close(done)
		wg.Wait()
	}
}

// execute checks a claimed job (payload MAC, type, gate) and runs it.
func (r *Runner) execute(jobCtx context.Context, c *claimed) {
	ctx := context.WithoutCancel(jobCtx) // bookkeeping finishes even while shutting down
	t, ok := lookup(c.typ)
	if !ok {
		r.terminate(ctx, c, "job.unknown_type", "job.dead")
		return
	}
	var payload map[string]string
	if err := json.Unmarshal(c.payload, &payload); err != nil ||
		!hmac.Equal(c.mac, r.cfg.Queue.mac(c.id, c.typ, c.target, canonicalPayload(payload), c.createdBy)) {
		r.cfg.Log.Error("job payload does not match its MAC; the job is not run", "job_id", c.id.String(), "job_type", c.typ)
		r.terminate(ctx, c, "job.tampered", "job.tampered")
		return
	}
	if err := r.cfg.Gate.Allow(t.Class); err != nil {
		if !errors.Is(err, license.ErrLocked) {
			r.terminate(ctx, c, "job.unknown_type", "job.dead")
			return
		}
		r.revert(ctx, c, t)
		return
	}
	h := r.handler(c.typ)
	if h == nil { // claim only selects handled types; a handler is never removed
		r.terminate(ctx, c, "job.unknown_type", "job.dead")
		return
	}
	j := Job{ID: c.id, Type: t, Kind: Kind(c.kind), TargetID: c.target, Payload: payload, Attempt: c.attempts,
		MaxAttempts: c.maxAttempts, CreatedBy: c.createdBy, CreatedByRole: c.role}
	hctx, cancel := context.WithCancel(jobCtx)
	stop := r.heartbeat(c, cancel)
	steps := &stepLog{}
	res, err := r.call(hctx, h, j, steps)
	stop()
	cancel()
	r.finish(ctx, jobCtx, c, res, steps.list(), err)
}

func encodeResult(res map[string]any, steps []map[string]any, f *Failure) (string, error) {
	out := map[string]any{}
	for k, v := range res {
		out[k] = v
	}
	if len(steps) > 0 {
		out["steps"] = steps
	}
	if f != nil {
		if len(f.Params) > 0 {
			out["error_params"] = f.Params
		}
		if f.Class == NeedsAttention {
			out["needs_attention"] = true
		}
	}
	b, err := json.Marshal(out)
	return string(b), err
}

// finish records the outcome of a run (spec §8.4).
func (r *Runner) finish(ctx, jobCtx context.Context, c *claimed, res map[string]any, steps []map[string]any, err error) {
	if err == nil {
		result, encErr := encodeResult(res, steps, nil)
		if encErr != nil {
			err = Retry("internal.unexpected", nil, encErr)
		} else {
			r.settle(ctx, c, "", func(tx pgx.Tx, now time.Time) (pgconn.CommandTag, error) {
				return tx.Exec(ctx, `UPDATE jobs SET status = 'succeeded', result = $3::jsonb, last_error_code = '', finished_at = $4,
    locked_by = NULL, locked_until = NULL `+mine, c.id, r.cfg.WorkerID, result, now)
			})
			return
		}
	}
	if r.stopping.Load() && jobCtx.Err() != nil {
		r.release(ctx, c) // interrupted by the shutdown: it runs again after the restart (§8.8)
		return
	}
	f := classify(err)
	if f.Reason == "internal.unexpected" {
		r.cfg.Log.Error("job failed unexpectedly", "job_id", c.id.String(), "job_type", c.typ, "error_type", fmt.Sprintf("%T", errors.Unwrap(f)))
	}
	result, encErr := encodeResult(res, steps, f)
	if encErr != nil {
		result = `{}`
	}
	switch {
	case f.Class == Retryable && c.attempts < c.maxAttempts:
		next := Backoff(c.attempts, r.cfg.Jitter())
		r.settle(ctx, c, f.Reason, func(tx pgx.Tx, now time.Time) (pgconn.CommandTag, error) {
			return tx.Exec(ctx, `UPDATE jobs SET status = 'queued', run_at = $3, last_error_code = $4, result = $5::jsonb,
    locked_by = NULL, locked_until = NULL `+mine, c.id, r.cfg.WorkerID, now.Add(next), f.Reason, result)
		})
	case f.Class == Retryable:
		r.settle(ctx, c, f.Reason, func(tx pgx.Tx, now time.Time) (pgconn.CommandTag, error) {
			return tx.Exec(ctx, `UPDATE jobs SET status = 'dead', last_error_code = $3, result = $4::jsonb, finished_at = $5,
    locked_by = NULL, locked_until = NULL `+mine, c.id, r.cfg.WorkerID, f.Reason, result, now)
		}, r.jobEvent("job.dead", audit.Failure, c.id, map[string]string{"type": c.typ, "reason": f.Reason, "attempt": strconv.Itoa(c.attempts)}))
	default:
		r.settle(ctx, c, f.Reason, func(tx pgx.Tx, now time.Time) (pgconn.CommandTag, error) {
			return tx.Exec(ctx, `UPDATE jobs SET status = 'failed', last_error_code = $3, result = $4::jsonb, finished_at = $5,
    locked_by = NULL, locked_until = NULL `+mine, c.id, r.cfg.WorkerID, f.Reason, result, now)
		})
	}
}

// release hands an unfinished job back to the queue (graceful shutdown). The attempt counts:
// users see it like an expired lease.
func (r *Runner) release(ctx context.Context, c *claimed) {
	r.settle(ctx, c, "job.lease_expired", func(tx pgx.Tx, now time.Time) (pgconn.CommandTag, error) {
		return tx.Exec(ctx, `UPDATE jobs SET status = 'queued', run_at = $3, last_error_code = 'job.lease_expired',
    locked_by = NULL, locked_until = NULL `+mine, c.id, r.cfg.WorkerID, now)
	})
}

// RunOnce claims and runs one due job. It reports false when none was due.
func (r *Runner) RunOnce(ctx context.Context) (bool, error) { return r.runOnce(ctx, ctx) }

func (r *Runner) runOnce(claimCtx, jobCtx context.Context) (bool, error) {
	c, err := r.claim(claimCtx)
	if err != nil || c == nil {
		return false, err
	}
	r.execute(jobCtx, c)
	return true, nil
}

// Reap re-queues jobs whose lease expired (their worker stopped: crash, kill, lost database
// connection; spec §8.8). The attempt that was cut off counts; a job without attempts left is
// dead. Expired target locks are released.
func (r *Runner) Reap(ctx context.Context) (int, error) {
	n := 0
	err := db.InTx(ctx, r.cfg.Pool, func(tx pgx.Tx) error {
		now := r.cfg.Clock.Now().UTC()
		rows, err := tx.Query(ctx, `UPDATE jobs SET
    status = CASE WHEN attempts >= max_attempts THEN 'dead' ELSE 'queued' END,
    finished_at = CASE WHEN attempts >= max_attempts THEN $1::timestamptz ELSE NULL END,
    locked_by = NULL, locked_until = NULL, run_at = $1, last_error_code = 'job.lease_expired'
WHERE status = 'running' AND locked_until < $1
RETURNING id, type, attempts, status`, now)
		if err != nil {
			return fmt.Errorf("jobs: reap: %w", err)
		}
		type reaped struct {
			id       uuid.UUID
			typ      string
			attempts int
			status   string
		}
		var all []reaped
		for rows.Next() {
			var x reaped
			if err := rows.Scan(&x.id, &x.typ, &x.attempts, &x.status); err != nil {
				rows.Close()
				return fmt.Errorf("jobs: reap: %w", err)
			}
			all = append(all, x)
		}
		rows.Close()
		if err := rows.Err(); err != nil {
			return fmt.Errorf("jobs: reap: %w", err)
		}
		ids := make([]string, 0, len(all))
		for _, x := range all {
			ids = append(ids, x.id.String())
			if _, err := tx.Exec(ctx, `UPDATE job_attempts SET finished_at = $2, error_code = 'job.lease_expired'
WHERE job_id = $1 AND finished_at IS NULL`, x.id, now); err != nil {
				return fmt.Errorf("jobs: reap: %w", err)
			}
			details := map[string]string{"type": x.typ, "attempt": strconv.Itoa(x.attempts), "reason": "job.lease_expired"}
			action, result := "job.recovered", audit.Success
			if x.status == string(StatusDead) {
				action, result = "job.dead", audit.Failure
			}
			if _, err := r.cfg.Audit.Append(ctx, tx, r.jobEvent(action, result, x.id, details)); err != nil {
				return err
			}
		}
		if _, err := tx.Exec(ctx, `DELETE FROM target_locks WHERE lease_until < $1 OR job_id::text = ANY($2::text[])`, now, ids); err != nil {
			return fmt.Errorf("jobs: release expired target locks: %w", err)
		}
		n = len(all)
		return nil
	})
	return n, err
}

// Recover is the startup pass of spec §8.8: before the workers start, jobs whose lease expired
// are re-queued. Leases that have not expired may belong to a live process (F-69) and are left
// to the reaper.
func (r *Runner) Recover(ctx context.Context) (int, error) {
	n, err := r.Reap(ctx)
	if err == nil && n > 0 {
		r.cfg.Log.Info("recovered jobs whose worker stopped", "count", n)
	}
	return n, err
}

// Run runs Workers workers and the reaper until ctx ends. Then it stops claiming, waits up to
// ShutdownGrace for running jobs, cancels them, waits up to ShutdownGrace again and finally
// releases the leases of jobs that still have not returned, so they resume after a restart.
func (r *Runner) Run(ctx context.Context) {
	jobsCtx, cancelJobs := context.WithCancel(context.WithoutCancel(ctx))
	defer cancelJobs()
	var workers sync.WaitGroup
	for range r.cfg.Workers {
		workers.Add(1)
		go func() {
			defer workers.Done()
			for ctx.Err() == nil {
				ran, err := r.runOnce(ctx, jobsCtx)
				if err != nil && ctx.Err() == nil {
					r.cfg.Log.Error("claiming a job failed", "error_type", fmt.Sprintf("%T", err))
				}
				if !ran {
					select {
					case <-ctx.Done():
					case <-r.cfg.Clock.After(r.cfg.Poll):
					}
				}
			}
		}()
	}
	reaperDone := make(chan struct{})
	go func() {
		defer close(reaperDone)
		for {
			select {
			case <-ctx.Done():
				return
			case <-r.cfg.Clock.After(r.cfg.ReapEvery):
				if _, err := r.Reap(ctx); err != nil && ctx.Err() == nil {
					r.cfg.Log.Error("reaping expired job leases failed", "error_type", fmt.Sprintf("%T", err))
				}
			}
		}
	}()
	<-ctx.Done()
	done := make(chan struct{})
	go func() {
		workers.Wait()
		close(done)
	}()
	select {
	case <-done:
	case <-r.cfg.Clock.After(r.cfg.ShutdownGrace):
		r.stopping.Store(true)
		cancelJobs()
		select {
		case <-done:
		case <-r.cfg.Clock.After(r.cfg.ShutdownGrace):
		}
	}
	<-reaperDone
	r.releaseAll(context.WithoutCancel(ctx))
}

// releaseAll hands every job this worker still holds back to the queue.
func (r *Runner) releaseAll(ctx context.Context) {
	err := db.InTx(ctx, r.cfg.Pool, func(tx pgx.Tx) error {
		now := r.cfg.Clock.Now().UTC()
		rows, err := tx.Query(ctx, `UPDATE jobs SET status = 'queued', run_at = $2, last_error_code = 'job.lease_expired',
    locked_by = NULL, locked_until = NULL
WHERE locked_by = $1 AND status = 'running' RETURNING id`, r.cfg.WorkerID, now)
		if err != nil {
			return err
		}
		ids := []string{}
		for rows.Next() {
			var id uuid.UUID
			if err := rows.Scan(&id); err != nil {
				rows.Close()
				return err
			}
			ids = append(ids, id.String())
		}
		rows.Close()
		if err := rows.Err(); err != nil {
			return err
		}
		if _, err := tx.Exec(ctx, `UPDATE job_attempts SET finished_at = $2, error_code = 'job.lease_expired'
WHERE job_id::text = ANY($1::text[]) AND finished_at IS NULL`, ids, now); err != nil {
			return err
		}
		_, err = tx.Exec(ctx, `DELETE FROM target_locks WHERE locked_by = $1`, r.cfg.WorkerID)
		return err
	})
	if err != nil {
		r.cfg.Log.Error("could not release the leases of unfinished jobs; they resume when the leases expire",
			"error_type", fmt.Sprintf("%T", err))
	}
}
```

```go
func TestSameTargetJobsNeverOverlap(t *testing.T) {
	e := newQEnv(t)
	targets := []uuid.UUID{insertTarget(t, e.d), insertTarget(t, e.d), insertTarget(t, e.d)}
	for i := range 60 {
		e.enqueue(t, Spec{Type: testQueueJob, TargetID: targets[i%3]})
	}
	var (
		mu        sync.Mutex
		perTarget = map[uuid.UUID]int{}
		maxPer    int
		inFlight  atomic.Int32
		maxGlobal atomic.Int32
	)
	r := e.runner(t, "w1")
	r.Handle(testQueueJob, func(_ context.Context, j Job, _ StepRecorder) (map[string]any, error) {
		mu.Lock()
		perTarget[j.TargetID]++
		maxPer = max(maxPer, perTarget[j.TargetID])
		mu.Unlock()
		n := inFlight.Add(1)
		for {
			m := maxGlobal.Load()
			if n <= m || maxGlobal.CompareAndSwap(m, n) {
				break
			}
		}
		time.Sleep(3 * time.Millisecond)
		inFlight.Add(-1)
		mu.Lock()
		perTarget[j.TargetID]--
		mu.Unlock()
		return nil, nil
	})
	var wg sync.WaitGroup
	for range 8 {
		wg.Add(1)
		go func() {
			defer wg.Done()
			for e.count(t, `SELECT count(*) FROM jobs WHERE status IN ('queued', 'running')`) > 0 {
				if ran, err := r.RunOnce(e.ctx); err != nil {
					t.Error(err)
					return
				} else if !ran {
					time.Sleep(time.Millisecond)
				}
			}
		}()
	}
	wg.Wait()
	assert.Equal(t, 1, maxPer, "one running job per target (§8.5, §12.5)")
	assert.GreaterOrEqual(t, maxGlobal.Load(), int32(2), "different targets did run in parallel (the test is not serial)")
	assert.Equal(t, 60, e.count(t, `SELECT count(*) FROM jobs WHERE status = 'succeeded'`))
	assert.Zero(t, e.count(t, `SELECT count(*) FROM target_locks`))
}

// F-69: SKIP LOCKED proven with 20 workers in two runners (two processes' worth) and 1000 jobs.
func TestTwentyWorkersRunThousandJobsExactlyOnce(t *testing.T) {
	e := newQEnvWith(t, clock.Real{})
	ids := make([]uuid.UUID, 0, 1000)
	for range 1000 {
		ids = append(ids, e.enqueue(t, Spec{Type: testQueueJob}))
	}
	var counts sync.Map
	handler := func(_ context.Context, j Job, _ StepRecorder) (map[string]any, error) {
		n, _ := counts.LoadOrStore(j.ID, new(atomic.Int32))
		n.(*atomic.Int32).Add(1)
		return nil, nil
	}
	ctx, cancel := context.WithCancel(e.ctx)
	var wg sync.WaitGroup
	for _, name := range []string{"process-a", "process-b"} {
		r := e.runner(t, name, func(c *RunnerConfig) { c.Workers, c.Poll = 10, 5*time.Millisecond })
		r.Handle(testQueueJob, handler)
		wg.Add(1)
		go func() {
			defer wg.Done()
			r.Run(ctx)
		}()
	}
	require.Eventually(t, func() bool {
		return e.count(t, `SELECT count(*) FROM jobs WHERE status = 'succeeded'`) == 1000
	}, 2*time.Minute, 50*time.Millisecond)
	cancel()
	wg.Wait()
	for _, id := range ids {
		n, ok := counts.Load(id)
		require.True(t, ok, "job %s never ran", id)
		assert.Equal(t, int32(1), n.(*atomic.Int32).Load(), "job %s ran more than once", id)
	}
	assert.Equal(t, 1000, e.count(t, `SELECT count(*) FROM job_attempts`))
	assert.Equal(t, 1000, e.count(t, `SELECT count(*) FROM jobs WHERE attempts = 1`))
}
```

```go
package jobs

func TestRetryBacksOffThenSucceeds(t *testing.T) {
	e := newQEnv(t)
	id := e.enqueue(t, Spec{Type: testQueueJob, MaxAttempts: 3})
	var runs atomic.Int32
	r := e.runner(t, "w1")
	r.Handle(testQueueJob, func(_ context.Context, j Job, _ StepRecorder) (map[string]any, error) {
		assert.Equal(t, int(runs.Load())+1, j.Attempt)
		if runs.Add(1) < 3 {
			return nil, Retry("ssh.unreachable", map[string]string{"host": "web-01"}, errors.New("refused"))
		}
		return map[string]any{"ok": true}, nil
	})
	ran, err := r.RunOnce(e.ctx)
	require.NoError(t, err)
	require.True(t, ran)
	got := e.row(t, id)
	assert.Equal(t, "queued", got.status)
	assert.Equal(t, "ssh.unreachable", got.lastError)
	assert.Equal(t, queueStart.Add(30*time.Second), got.runAt)
	assert.Empty(t, got.lockedBy)
	v, err := e.q.Get(e.ctx, id)
	require.NoError(t, err)
	assert.Equal(t, map[string]string{"host": "web-01"}, v.ErrorParams)

	ran, err = r.RunOnce(e.ctx)
	require.NoError(t, err)
	assert.False(t, ran, "not due before its backoff")
	e.fake.Advance(30 * time.Second)
	_, err = r.RunOnce(e.ctx)
	require.NoError(t, err)
	assert.Equal(t, queueStart.Add(30*time.Second+time.Minute), e.row(t, id).runAt, "the second wait doubles")
	e.fake.Advance(time.Minute)
	_, err = r.RunOnce(e.ctx)
	require.NoError(t, err)
	got = e.row(t, id)
	assert.Equal(t, "succeeded", got.status)
	assert.Equal(t, 3, got.attempts)
	assert.Empty(t, got.lastError)
	assert.Equal(t, 3, e.count(t, `SELECT count(*) FROM job_attempts WHERE job_id = $1 AND finished_at IS NOT NULL`, id))
	assert.Equal(t, 2, e.count(t, `SELECT count(*) FROM job_attempts WHERE job_id = $1 AND error_code = 'ssh.unreachable'`, id))
}

	require.NoError(t, err)
	got := e.row(t, id)
	assert.Equal(t, "failed", got.status)
	assert.Equal(t, "ssh.auth_failed", got.lastError)
	assert.Equal(t, 1, got.attempts)
	v, err := e.q.Get(e.ctx, id)
	require.NoError(t, err)
	assert.Equal(t, map[string]string{"user": "alice-svc"}, v.ErrorParams)
	assert.NotNil(t, v.FinishedAt)
	e.fake.Advance(time.Hour)
	ran, err := r.RunOnce(e.ctx)
	require.NoError(t, err)
	assert.False(t, ran)
}

func TestPanickingHandlerIsRetriedAndItsValueNeverLogged(t *testing.T) {

	r.Handle(testQueueJob, func(context.Context, Job, StepRecorder) (map[string]any, error) {
		panic("CANARY-panic-value")
	})

	assert.Equal(t, "internal.unexpected", got.lastError)
	assert.Contains(t, logs.String(), "job handler panicked")
	assert.NotContains(t, logs.String(), "CANARY")
}

// L-81: a deploy-like external change queued before the lock is not claimed in lock, waits as
// blocked_license, does not run by itself after the renewal and runs once after an
// Administrator confirms it (R29).
func TestLockHoldsChangeJobsUntilAnAdministratorConfirms(t *testing.T) {
	e := newQEnv(t)
	target := insertTarget(t, e.d)
	id := e.enqueue(t, Spec{Type: SSHKeyRemove, Kind: KindUser, TargetID: target, Payload: map[string]string{"location_id": "l1"}})
	var runs atomic.Int32
	r := e.runner(t, "w1")
	r.Handle(SSHKeyRemove, func(context.Context, Job, StepRecorder) (map[string]any, error) { runs.Add(1); return nil, nil })

	e.gate.set(true) // the license locks
	ran, err := r.RunOnce(e.ctx)
	require.NoError(t, err)
	assert.False(t, ran)
	assert.Zero(t, runs.Load())
	assert.Equal(t, "blocked_license", e.row(t, id).status)
	assert.Equal(t, 1, e.audits(t, "job.blocked_license"))
	assert.ErrorIs(t, e.q.Confirm(e.ctx, admin, admin.ID, id), license.ErrLocked, "confirming is refused while locked")

	e.gate.set(false) // renewal
	ran, err = r.RunOnce(e.ctx)
	require.NoError(t, err)
	assert.False(t, ran, "after the renewal the held change does not start on its own")
	assert.Equal(t, "blocked_license", e.row(t, id).status)
	blocked, _, err := e.q.List(e.ctx, ListFilter{Status: StatusBlocked})
	require.NoError(t, err)
	require.Len(t, blocked, 1)
	assert.Equal(t, id, blocked[0].ID)

	require.NoError(t, e.q.Confirm(e.ctx, admin, admin.ID, id))
	assert.Equal(t, 1, e.audits(t, "job.confirmed"))
	ran, err = r.RunOnce(e.ctx)
	require.NoError(t, err)
	assert.True(t, ran)
	assert.Equal(t, int32(1), runs.Load())
	assert.Equal(t, "succeeded", e.row(t, id).status)
	assert.ErrorIs(t, e.q.Confirm(e.ctx, admin, admin.ID, id), ErrNotWaiting)
}

func TestLockCancelsQueuedReadOnlyWork(t *testing.T) {
	e := newQEnv(t)
	id := e.enqueue(t, Spec{Type: testReadOnlyJob, Kind: KindScheduled})
	always := e.enqueue(t, Spec{Type: testQueueJob})
	var readOnlyRuns, alwaysRuns atomic.Int32
	r := e.runner(t, "w1")
	r.Handle(testReadOnlyJob, func(context.Context, Job, StepRecorder) (map[string]any, error) { readOnlyRuns.Add(1); return nil, nil })
	r.Handle(testQueueJob, func(context.Context, Job, StepRecorder) (map[string]any, error) { alwaysRuns.Add(1); return nil, nil })
	e.gate.set(true)
	for {
		ran, err := r.RunOnce(e.ctx)
		require.NoError(t, err)
		if !ran {
			break
		}
	}
	assert.Zero(t, readOnlyRuns.Load())
	assert.Equal(t, int32(1), alwaysRuns.Load(), "always-class work keeps running in lock")
	got := e.row(t, id)
	assert.Equal(t, "cancelled", got.status)
	assert.Equal(t, "license.locked", got.lastError)
	assert.Equal(t, "succeeded", e.row(t, always).status)
}

// flipGate allows the first question and refuses everything after it: the lock begins
// between the claim and the run.
type flipGate struct{ asked atomic.Int32 }

func (g *flipGate) Allow(license.Class) error {
	if g.asked.Add(1) == 1 {
		return nil
	}
	return license.ErrLocked
}

func TestGateIsAskedAgainAfterTheClaim(t *testing.T) {
	e := newQEnv(t)
	target := insertTarget(t, e.d)
	id := e.enqueue(t, Spec{Type: SSHKeyRemove, Kind: KindUser, TargetID: target})
	var runs atomic.Int32
	r := e.runner(t, "w1", func(c *RunnerConfig) { c.Gate = &flipGate{} })
	r.Handle(SSHKeyRemove, func(context.Context, Job, StepRecorder) (map[string]any, error) { runs.Add(1); return nil, nil })
	ran, err := r.RunOnce(e.ctx)
	require.NoError(t, err)
	assert.True(t, ran, "it was claimed")
	assert.Zero(t, runs.Load(), "but not run: the lock began in between (§8.6 'right after claim')")
	got := e.row(t, id)
	assert.Equal(t, "blocked_license", got.status)
	assert.Zero(t, got.attempts, "the refused claim is not an attempt")
	assert.Empty(t, got.lockedBy)
	assert.Zero(t, e.count(t, `SELECT count(*) FROM target_locks`))
}

func TestDiscard(t *testing.T) {
	e := newQEnv(t)

	assert.ErrorIs(t, e.q.Confirm(e.ctx, admin, admin.ID, id), ErrNotWaiting)
}

func TestGetAndListPages(t *testing.T) {
	e := newQEnv(t)
	target := insertTarget(t, e.d)
	var ids []uuid.UUID
	for i := range 3 {
		ids = append(ids, e.enqueue(t, Spec{Type: testQueueJob, TargetID: target}))
		e.fake.Advance(time.Duration(i+1) * time.Second)
	}
	_ = e.enqueue(t, Spec{Type: testQueueJob})
	page, next, err := e.q.List(e.ctx, ListFilter{TargetID: target, Limit: 2})
	require.NoError(t, err)
	require.Len(t, page, 2)
	assert.Equal(t, []uuid.UUID{ids[2], ids[1]}, []uuid.UUID{page[0].ID, page[1].ID}, "newest first")
	require.NotEmpty(t, next)
	rest, next, err := e.q.List(e.ctx, ListFilter{TargetID: target, Limit: 2, Cursor: next})
	require.NoError(t, err)
	require.Len(t, rest, 1)
	assert.Equal(t, ids[0], rest[0].ID)
	assert.Empty(t, next)
	_, _, err = e.q.List(e.ctx, ListFilter{Cursor: "not-a-cursor"})
	assert.ErrorIs(t, err, ErrBadCursor)

	v, err := e.q.Get(e.ctx, ids[0])
	require.NoError(t, err)
	assert.Equal(t, testQueueJob.Name, v.Type)
	assert.Equal(t, StatusQueued, v.Status)
	assert.Equal(t, target, v.TargetID)
	_, err = e.q.Get(e.ctx, uuid.New())
	assert.ErrorIs(t, err, ErrNotFound)
}

func TestReapRequeuesExpiredLeasesOnce(t *testing.T) {
	e := newQEnv(t)
	target := insertTarget(t, e.d)
	live := e.enqueue(t, Spec{Type: testQueueJob, TargetID: target, MaxAttempts: 3})
	last := e.enqueue(t, Spec{Type: testQueueJob, MaxAttempts: 1})
	for _, x := range []struct {
		id       uuid.UUID
		attempts int
	}{{live, 1}, {last, 1}} {
		_, err := e.d.Owner.Exec(e.ctx, `UPDATE jobs SET status = 'running', locked_by = 'dead-worker', attempts = $2,
    locked_until = $3 WHERE id = $1`, x.id, x.attempts, queueStart.Add(-time.Second))
		require.NoError(t, err)
	}
	_, err := e.d.Owner.Exec(e.ctx, `INSERT INTO target_locks (target_id, job_id, operation, locked_by, heartbeat_at, lease_until)
VALUES ($1, $2, 'test.queue', 'dead-worker', $3, $3)`, target, live, queueStart.Add(-time.Second))
	require.NoError(t, err)
	r := e.runner(t, "w1")
	n, err := r.Recover(e.ctx)
	require.NoError(t, err)
	assert.Equal(t, 2, n)
	got := e.row(t, live)
	assert.Equal(t, "queued", got.status)
	assert.Equal(t, "job.lease_expired", got.lastError)
	assert.Equal(t, 1, got.attempts, "the cut-off attempt counts")
	assert.Equal(t, "dead", e.row(t, last).status, "no attempt left")
	assert.Equal(t, 1, e.audits(t, "job.recovered"))
	assert.Equal(t, 1, e.audits(t, "job.dead"))
	assert.Zero(t, e.count(t, `SELECT count(*) FROM target_locks`))
	n, err = r.Reap(e.ctx)
	require.NoError(t, err)
	assert.Zero(t, n, "a second pass changes nothing")
}

func TestHeartbeatLossStopsTheHandlerAndItsResultIsDropped(t *testing.T) {
	e := newQEnv(t)
	id := e.enqueue(t, Spec{Type: testQueueJob})
	started, cancelled := make(chan struct{}), make(chan struct{})
	r := e.runner(t, "w1")
	r.Handle(testQueueJob, func(ctx context.Context, _ Job, _ StepRecorder) (map[string]any, error) {
		close(started)
		select {
		case <-ctx.Done():
			close(cancelled)
			return nil, ctx.Err()
		case <-time.After(10 * time.Second):
			return map[string]any{"finished": true}, nil
		}
	})
	done := make(chan struct{})
	go func() {
		_, _ = r.RunOnce(e.ctx)
		close(done)
	}()
	<-started
	_, err := e.d.Owner.Exec(e.ctx, `UPDATE jobs SET locked_by = 'reaper-gave-it-away' WHERE id = $1`, id)
	require.NoError(t, err)
	require.Eventually(t, func() bool {
		e.fake.Advance(15 * time.Second)
		select {
		case <-cancelled:
			return true
		default:
			return false
		}
	}, 5*time.Second, 10*time.Millisecond)
	<-done
	got := e.row(t, id)
	assert.Equal(t, "running", got.status, "this worker no longer owns the job, so it writes nothing")
	assert.Equal(t, "reaper-gave-it-away", got.lockedBy)
}
```

scheduled work (R37 item 15). Wiring the periodic tasks into `alice serve` is Task 18.

```go
//go:build integration

package jobs

import (
	"bytes"
	"context"
	"os"
	"os/exec"
	"path/filepath"
	"sync/atomic"
	"testing"
	"time"

	"github.com/stretchr/testify/assert"
	"github.com/stretchr/testify/require"

	"alice/internal/audit"
	"alice/internal/license"
	"alice/internal/platform/clock"
	"alice/internal/platform/db"
)

const (
	crashChildEnv  = "ALICE_JOBS_CRASH_CHILD"
	crashDBEnv     = "ALICE_JOBS_CRASH_DB"
	crashMarkerEnv = "ALICE_JOBS_CRASH_MARKER"
)

var testCrash = Register("test.crash", license.ClassAlways)

// TestCrashChildProcess is the worker process that TestKilledWorkerJobIsRecoveredOnce kills
// while its job runs. It does nothing when run on its own.
func TestCrashChildProcess(t *testing.T) {
	if os.Getenv(crashChildEnv) != "1" {
		t.Skip("runs only as the child process of TestKilledWorkerJobIsRecoveredOnce")
	}
	ctx := context.Background()
	pool, err := db.Open(ctx, os.Getenv(crashDBEnv))
	require.NoError(t, err)
	al := audit.New(clock.Real{})
	q := NewQueue(QueueConfig{Pool: pool, Keyring: testKeyring(t), Audit: al, Clock: clock.Real{}, Gate: &fakeGate{}})
	r := NewRunner(RunnerConfig{Pool: pool, Queue: q, Gate: &fakeGate{}, Audit: al, Clock: clock.Real{}, Log: quiet,
		WorkerID: "crash-child", Lease: time.Second, Heartbeat: 200 * time.Millisecond})
	r.Handle(testCrash, func(_ context.Context, j Job, _ StepRecorder) (map[string]any, error) {
		require.NoError(t, os.WriteFile(os.Getenv(crashMarkerEnv), []byte(j.ID.String()), 0o600))
		time.Sleep(time.Hour) // the parent kills this process here
		return nil, nil
	})
	_, err = r.RunOnce(ctx)
	t.Fatalf("the child must be killed while its job runs (RunOnce returned %v)", err)
}

// F-66 (framework part): a worker process killed with SIGKILL in the middle of a job. Its
// lease expires, the reaper re-queues the job once (job.lease_expired, audit job.recovered),
// the target lock is released, and the job then runs exactly once more to success.
func TestKilledWorkerJobIsRecoveredOnce(t *testing.T) {
	e := newQEnvWith(t, clock.Real{})
	target := insertTarget(t, e.d)
	id := e.enqueue(t, Spec{Type: testCrash, TargetID: target})
	marker := filepath.Join(t.TempDir(), "claimed")

	cmd := exec.Command(os.Args[0], "-test.run=^TestCrashChildProcess$", "-test.count=1")
	cmd.Env = append(os.Environ(), crashChildEnv+"=1", crashDBEnv+"="+e.d.AppURL, crashMarkerEnv+"="+marker)
	var out bytes.Buffer
	cmd.Stdout, cmd.Stderr = &out, &out
	require.NoError(t, cmd.Start())
	t.Cleanup(func() { _ = cmd.Process.Kill() })
	require.Eventually(t, func() bool {
		b, err := os.ReadFile(marker)
		return err == nil && string(b) == id.String()
	}, time.Minute, 50*time.Millisecond, "the child never claimed the job; its output: %s", &out)
	got := e.row(t, id)
	require.Equal(t, "running", got.status)
	require.Equal(t, "crash-child", got.lockedBy)
	require.Equal(t, 1, e.count(t, `SELECT count(*) FROM target_locks WHERE target_id = $1`, target))

	require.NoError(t, cmd.Process.Kill())
	_ = cmd.Wait()

	var runs atomic.Int32
	r := e.runner(t, "parent", func(c *RunnerConfig) { c.Lease = time.Second })
	r.Handle(testCrash, func(context.Context, Job, StepRecorder) (map[string]any, error) { runs.Add(1); return nil, nil })
	require.Eventually(t, func() bool {
		n, err := r.Reap(e.ctx)
		return err == nil && n == 1
	}, 15*time.Second, 100*time.Millisecond, "the dead worker's lease never expired")
	got = e.row(t, id)
	assert.Equal(t, "queued", got.status)
	assert.Equal(t, "job.lease_expired", got.lastError)
	assert.Equal(t, 1, got.attempts, "the killed attempt counts")
	assert.Equal(t, 1, e.audits(t, "job.recovered"))
	assert.Zero(t, e.count(t, `SELECT count(*) FROM target_locks`))

	ran, err := r.RunOnce(e.ctx)
	require.NoError(t, err)
	require.True(t, ran)
	assert.Equal(t, int32(1), runs.Load())
	got = e.row(t, id)
	assert.Equal(t, "succeeded", got.status)
	assert.Equal(t, 2, got.attempts)
	ran, err = r.RunOnce(e.ctx)
	require.NoError(t, err)
	assert.False(t, ran, "nothing runs twice")
	n, err := r.Reap(e.ctx)
	require.NoError(t, err)
	assert.Zero(t, n)
	assert.Equal(t, 1, e.audits(t, "job.recovered"), "recovered exactly once")
}
```

```go
//go:build integration

package jobs

func runInBackground(r *Runner, ctx context.Context) <-chan struct{} {
	done := make(chan struct{})
	go func() {
		r.Run(ctx)
		close(done)
	}()
	return done

func waitClosed(t *testing.T, ch <-chan struct{}, within time.Duration, what string) {
	t.Helper()
	select {
	case <-ch:
	case <-time.After(within):
		t.Fatalf("%s did not happen within %s", what, within)
	}
}

func TestShutdownLetsShortJobsFinishAndClaimsNothingNew(t *testing.T) {
	e := newQEnvWith(t, clock.Real{})
	first := e.enqueue(t, Spec{Type: testQueueJob, Kind: KindUser})
	second := e.enqueue(t, Spec{Type: testQueueJob})
	started := make(chan struct{}, 2)
	r := e.runner(t, "w1", func(c *RunnerConfig) { c.Workers, c.Poll, c.ShutdownGrace = 1, 5*time.Millisecond, 2*time.Second })
	r.Handle(testQueueJob, func(context.Context, Job, StepRecorder) (map[string]any, error) {
		started <- struct{}{}
		time.Sleep(50 * time.Millisecond)
		return nil, nil
	})
	ctx, cancel := context.WithCancel(e.ctx)
	done := runInBackground(r, ctx)
	<-started
	cancel()
	waitClosed(t, done, 5*time.Second, "Run returning")
	assert.Equal(t, "succeeded", e.row(t, first).status, "a job that ends within the grace period completes")
	assert.Equal(t, "queued", e.row(t, second).status, "no new job is claimed after the shutdown began")
}

func TestShutdownReleasesInterruptedJobs(t *testing.T) {
	e := newQEnvWith(t, clock.Real{})
	target := insertTarget(t, e.d)
	id := e.enqueue(t, Spec{Type: testQueueJob, TargetID: target})
	started := make(chan struct{})
	r := e.runner(t, "w1", func(c *RunnerConfig) { c.Workers, c.Poll, c.ShutdownGrace = 1, 5*time.Millisecond, 100*time.Millisecond })
	r.Handle(testQueueJob, func(ctx context.Context, _ Job, _ StepRecorder) (map[string]any, error) {
		close(started)
		<-ctx.Done()
		return nil, ctx.Err()
	})
	ctx, cancel := context.WithCancel(e.ctx)
	done := runInBackground(r, ctx)
	<-started
	cancel()
	waitClosed(t, done, 5*time.Second, "Run returning")
	got := e.row(t, id)
	assert.Equal(t, "queued", got.status, "an interrupted job resumes after the restart (§8.8), it is not failed")
	assert.Empty(t, got.lockedBy)
	assert.Equal(t, "job.lease_expired", got.lastError)
	assert.Equal(t, 1, got.attempts, "the interrupted attempt counts")
	assert.Zero(t, e.count(t, `SELECT count(*) FROM target_locks`))
	assert.Zero(t, e.count(t, `SELECT count(*) FROM job_attempts WHERE finished_at IS NULL`))
}

func TestShutdownReleasesJobsWhoseHandlerIgnoresCancellation(t *testing.T) {
	e := newQEnvWith(t, clock.Real{})
	id := e.enqueue(t, Spec{Type: testQueueJob})
	started, release, returned := make(chan struct{}), make(chan struct{}), make(chan struct{})
	r := e.runner(t, "w1", func(c *RunnerConfig) { c.Workers, c.Poll, c.ShutdownGrace = 1, 5*time.Millisecond, 100*time.Millisecond })
	r.Handle(testQueueJob, func(context.Context, Job, StepRecorder) (map[string]any, error) {
		close(started)
		<-release
		defer close(returned)
		return map[string]any{"late": true}, nil
	})
	ctx, cancel := context.WithCancel(e.ctx)
	done := runInBackground(r, ctx)
	<-started
	cancel()
	waitClosed(t, done, 5*time.Second, "Run returning while a handler is stuck")
	assert.Equal(t, "queued", e.row(t, id).status)
	close(release)
	waitClosed(t, returned, 5*time.Second, "the stuck handler returning")
	time.Sleep(100 * time.Millisecond) // let its finish attempt reach the database
	got := e.row(t, id)
	assert.Equal(t, "queued", got.status, "a late result of a released job is not written")
	assert.Empty(t, got.lockedBy)
}
```

```go
func TestLeaderLockIsExclusiveAndSurvivesALostConnection(t *testing.T) {

	l1, l2 := NewLeader(e.d.App, quiet), NewLeader(e.d.App, quiet)
	t.Cleanup(l1.Close)
	t.Cleanup(l2.Close)
	require.True(t, l1.IsLeader(e.ctx))
	assert.False(t, l2.IsLeader(e.ctx))
	assert.True(t, l1.IsLeader(e.ctx), "leadership is kept across checks")

	l1.mu.Lock()
	pid := l1.conn.Conn().PgConn().PID()
	l1.mu.Unlock()
	_, err := e.d.Owner.Exec(e.ctx, `SELECT pg_terminate_backend($1)`, pid)

	assert.False(t, l1.IsLeader(e.ctx), "the old leader notices it lost the lock")

	l2.Close()
	assert.False(t, l2.IsLeader(e.ctx), "a closed leader never leads again")
	assert.True(t, l1.IsLeader(e.ctx), "closing releases the lock at once")
}

	s2 := NewScheduler(clk, &fakeGate{}, quiet, Task{Type: testLeaderTask, Every: time.Minute,

	assert.Zero(t, runs2.Load(), "the second process never runs scheduled work while the first leads")

	l1.Close() // process 1 stops
	require.Eventually(t, func() bool { clk.Advance(time.Minute); return runs2.Load() >= 1 }, 10*time.Second, 5*time.Millisecond)
```

Create `internal/jobs/leader.go`:

```go
package jobs

import (
	"context"
	"log/slog"
	"sync"
	"time"

	"github.com/jackc/pgx/v5/pgxpool"
)

// leaderLockKey is the session advisory lock held by the process that schedules periodic work
// (spec §8.3, P2-06). An arbitrary constant next to the audit (…300) and target-limit (…302) keys.
const leaderLockKey int64 = 7160927315633811303

// Leader holds the scheduling advisory lock on one dedicated connection. The lock lives as long
// as that database session: when the session dies the lock is free for another process.
type Leader struct {
	pool   *pgxpool.Pool
	log    *slog.Logger
	mu     sync.Mutex
	conn   *pgxpool.Conn // non-nil while this process leads
	closed bool
}

// NewLeader returns a Leader that has not tried to lead yet.
func NewLeader(pool *pgxpool.Pool, log *slog.Logger) *Leader {
	return &Leader{pool: pool, log: log}
}

// IsLeader reports whether this process holds the lock, taking it when it is free. A held
// connection that no longer answers is dropped (its lock died with it) and the lock is tried
// again.
func (l *Leader) IsLeader(ctx context.Context) bool {
	l.mu.Lock()
	defer l.mu.Unlock()
	if l.closed {
		return false
	}
	if l.conn != nil {
		pingCtx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(ctx, 2*time.Second)
		err := l.conn.Ping(pingCtx)
		cancel()
		if err == nil {
			return true
		}
		l.log.Warn("lost the scheduling lock's database session; trying to take the lock again")
		_ = l.conn.Conn().Close(context.WithoutCancel(ctx))
		l.conn.Release() // a closed connection is destroyed, not returned to the pool
		l.conn = nil
	}
	c, err := l.pool.Acquire(ctx)
	if err != nil {
		return false
	}
	var ok bool
	if err := c.QueryRow(ctx, `SELECT pg_try_advisory_lock($1)`, leaderLockKey).Scan(&ok); err != nil || !ok {
		c.Release()
		return false
	}
	l.conn = c
	l.log.Info("this process schedules periodic work")
	return true
}

// Close gives up leadership for good: the lock is released and the connection returned.
func (l *Leader) Close() {
	l.mu.Lock()
	defer l.mu.Unlock()
	l.closed = true
	if l.conn == nil {
		return
	}
	ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(context.Background(), 2*time.Second)
	defer cancel()
	if _, err := l.conn.Exec(ctx, `SELECT pg_advisory_unlock($1)`, leaderLockKey); err != nil {
		_ = l.conn.Conn().Close(ctx) // the lock dies with the session
	}
	l.conn.Release()
	l.conn = nil
}
```

```go
	live := session(now.Add(time.Hour), now.Add(10*time.Minute), nil)
	session(now.Add(-time.Second), now.Add(10*time.Minute), nil)  // absolute lifetime over
	session(now.Add(time.Hour), now.Add(-time.Second), nil)       // idle too long
	session(now.Add(time.Hour), now.Add(10*time.Minute), &oldRevoke)
	revokedRecently := session(now.Add(time.Hour), now.Add(10*time.Minute), &recentRevoke)
	for _, idle := range []time.Time{now.Add(-time.Minute), now.Add(time.Minute)} {

		_, err := e.db.Owner.Exec(e.ctx, `INSERT INTO setup_sessions (id_hash, created_at, idle_expires_at) VALUES ($1, $2, $3)`,

	assert.Equal(t, int64(4), n, "three dead sessions and one expired setup session")
	var kept [][]byte
	rows, err := e.db.Owner.Query(e.ctx, `SELECT id_hash FROM sessions ORDER BY id_hash`)
	require.NoError(t, err)
	for rows.Next() {
		var id []byte
		require.NoError(t, rows.Scan(&id))
		kept = append(kept, id)
	}
	rows.Close()
	assert.ElementsMatch(t, [][]byte{live, revokedRecently}, kept)
	var setups int
	require.NoError(t, e.db.Owner.QueryRow(e.ctx, `SELECT count(*) FROM setup_sessions`).Scan(&setups))
	assert.Equal(t, 1, setups)

	n, err = e.svc.PruneExpired(e.ctx)
	require.NoError(t, err)
	assert.Zero(t, n)
}
```

- [ ] **Step 6: Implement pruning and register the scheduled job types**

Append to `internal/jobs/queue.go`:

```go
// Prune deletes finished jobs (and, through the foreign key, their attempts) that ended more
// than olderThan ago (maintenance.cleanup, spec §8.2: 90 days). Unfinished jobs are kept.
func (q *Queue) Prune(ctx context.Context, olderThan time.Duration) (int, error) {
	cutoff := q.clock.Now().UTC().Add(-olderThan)
	tag, err := q.pool.Exec(ctx, `DELETE FROM jobs WHERE finished_at < $1 AND status IN ('succeeded', 'failed', 'cancelled', 'dead')`, cutoff)
	if err != nil {
		return 0, fmt.Errorf("jobs: prune: %w", err)
	}
	return int(tag.RowsAffected()), nil
}
```

Create `internal/auth/prune.go`:

```go
package auth

import (
	"context"
	"fmt"
	"time"
)

// revokedKeep is how long a revoked session row is kept (it can explain a "signed out
// everywhere" in support cases); after that it is pruned like an expired one.
const revokedKeep = 24 * time.Hour

// PruneExpired deletes sessions that can never authenticate again (absolute or idle lifetime
// over, or revoked more than a day ago) and expired setup-wizard sessions (maintenance.cleanup,
// spec §8.2). It returns the number of rows deleted.
func (s *Service) PruneExpired(ctx context.Context) (int64, error) {
	now := s.clock.Now().UTC()
	tag, err := s.pool.Exec(ctx, `DELETE FROM sessions
WHERE expires_at < $1 OR idle_expires_at < $1 OR (revoked_at IS NOT NULL AND revoked_at < $2)`, now, now.Add(-revokedKeep))
	if err != nil {
		return 0, fmt.Errorf("auth: prune sessions: %w", err)
	}
	setupTag, err := s.pool.Exec(ctx, `DELETE FROM setup_sessions WHERE idle_expires_at < $1`, now)
	if err != nil {
		return 0, fmt.Errorf("auth: prune setup sessions: %w", err)
	}
	return tag.RowsAffected() + setupTag.RowsAffected(), nil
}
```

### Task 13: Inventory — platform key, targets with the license check, address validation

Spec §7.2 (credentials, envelope columns, AAD), §7.3 (`targets`, license counting query, duplicate index, soft
delete), §13.5 ("Alice's own connection key … stored the same way"), §18.5 step 7, §23.7 (L-04, L-70..L-79), SEC-062,
SEC-065, R30, R37 items 1, 10, 11. This task creates the rest of `internal/inventory` (Task 11 created only
`internal/inventory/jobs.go`): the service shell, the platform Ed25519 key (generated once, sealed with the master
key, never logged), the setup guide, target create/update/delete/list with `license.Service.CheckCanAddTarget` inside
the insert transaction, the target counter the license module counts with, and strict address normalization.

Decisions made here (recorded in R37 by Task 23):
- The platform key comment is the fixed string `alice-platform` (the contract's `alice@<installation>` would need the
  license module's installation ID inside inventory for a cosmetic comment; the fingerprint identifies the key).
- Loopback addresses (`127.0.0.0/8`, `::1`, `localhost`) are allowed, like private ranges: SEC-065 blocks only
  link-local and metadata ranges (`169.254.0.0/16`, `fe80::/10`), and the unspecified, multicast and broadcast
  addresses are refused because they never name one server. The API integration suite (Task 17) runs its fake SSH
  server on `127.0.0.1`.
- Deleting a target does not touch rows of the `jobs` table (owned by `internal/jobs`): queued jobs of a deleted
  target fail at run time because `TargetRef` answers `ErrNotFound` for deleted targets (Task 15 handlers map it to
  `system.not_found`).
- `targets.version` changes only with user edits (name, interval) and deletion, so a background status update never
  makes an administrator's `If-Match` stale.

```go
import "errors"

// Errors of the inventory service. The API maps each to a stable ALC code (Task 16). None of

	ErrHostKeyUnconfirmed   = errors.New("inventory: the server's fingerprint is not confirmed")

	ErrHostKeyStale         = errors.New("inventory: the fingerprint is not the one the server presented")
	ErrHostKeyState         = errors.New("inventory: the host key cannot be confirmed in this state")
	ErrOwnKeyProtected      = errors.New("inventory: Alice's own key cannot be removed")
	ErrLastRootKey          = errors.New("inventory: this is the last key of root")
	ErrKeysManagedElsewhere = errors.New("inventory: keys on this server are managed by AuthorizedKeysCommand")
```

```go
package inventory

import (
	"time"

	"github.com/google/uuid"

	"alice/internal/audit"
	"alice/internal/providers"
	"alice/internal/rbac"
)

// Fixed names (spec §12.2, R37 item 1).
const (
	ServiceUser        = "alice-svc"
	PlatformKeyComment = "alice-platform"
	defaultSSHPort     = 22
	defaultInterval    = 24 * time.Hour
)

// Target statuses (targets.status, R37 item 6).
const (
	StatusPendingHostKey = "pending_host_key"
	StatusChecking       = "checking"
	StatusOK             = "ok"
	StatusUnreachable    = "unreachable"
	StatusHostKeyChanged = "host_key_changed"
	StatusAuthFailed     = "auth_failed"
	StatusDisabled       = "disabled"
)

// Actor is who asks: the audit actor plus the user and role behind it.
type Actor struct {
	Audit  audit.Actor
	UserID uuid.UUID
	Role   rbac.Role
}

// systemActor is the actor of work Alice does on its own (job handlers, scheduling).
func systemActor(name string) Actor { return Actor{Audit: audit.SystemActor(name)} }

// jobKind is "user" for a person's request and "system" for Alice's own.
func (a Actor) jobKind() string {
	if a.UserID == uuid.Nil {
		return "system"
	}
	return "user"
}

// PlatformKey is the public half of Alice's own SSH key.
type PlatformKey struct {
	ID          uuid.UUID
	PublicKey   string
	Fingerprint string
}

// Guide is what an administrator needs to prepare a server (setup snippet, §12.2).
type Guide struct {
	PlatformKey
	AuthorizedKeysLine string
	HelperPath         string
	HelperProtocol     int
	Profiles           map[string]providers.SetupSnippet
}

// Target is one managed server. It never carries credentials.
type Target struct {
	ID                   uuid.UUID
	Name                 string
	Type                 string
	Host                 string
	Port                 int
	Username             string
	Status               string
	LastErrorCode        string
	LastSuccessAt        *time.Time
	LastDiscoveryAt      *time.Time
	DiscoveryInterval    time.Duration
	KeysManagedElsewhere bool
	Facts                Facts
	Capabilities         []string
	Version              int
	CreatedAt, UpdatedAt time.Time
}

// Facts are what the last connection test and discovery learned (targets.facts).
type Facts struct {
	OS             providers.OSRelease           `json:"os"`
	HelperVersion  string                        `json:"helper_version"`
	HelperProtocol int                           `json:"helper_protocol"`
	SSHD           *providers.SSHDSummary        `json:"sshd,omitempty"`
	HostKeys       []providers.DiscoveredHostKey `json:"host_keys,omitempty"`
	Warnings       []providers.Warning           `json:"warnings,omitempty"`
	Unreadable     []providers.UnreadableLine    `json:"unreadable,omitempty"`
}

// NewTarget is the input of CreateTarget.
type NewTarget struct {
	Name     string
	Type     string // "linux" in Phase 3
	Host     string
	Port     int    // 0 = 22
	Username string // "" = alice-svc
}

// TargetPatch is the input of UpdateTarget; nil fields stay unchanged (R37 item 10).
type TargetPatch struct {
	Name                   *string
	DiscoveryIntervalHours *int // 1..720
}

// targetConfig is targets.config.
type targetConfig struct {
	Host     string `json:"host"`
	Port     int    `json:"port"`
	Username string `json:"username"`
}
```

Create `internal/inventory/validate.go`:

```go
package inventory

import (
	"net/netip"
	"regexp"
	"strconv"
	"strings"
	"unicode"
	"unicode/utf8"

	"alice/internal/platform/validate"
)

// Validation codes added by this package (texts in locales/common, validation.*).
const (
	CodeHostPort       = "validation.host_port"        // a port typed into the address field
	CodeHostNotAllowed = "validation.host_not_allowed" // link-local, multicast, unspecified, broadcast
	CodeHostASCII      = "validation.host_ascii"       // non-ASCII host name: type the xn-- form or the IP address
)

const (
	maxNameRunes = 100
	maxHostLen   = 253
)

// usernameRE is SEC-062's OS user name rule. It equals helperproto.ValidUser (inventory may not
// import the linuxssh packages, §5.4); a test in Task 16 compares the two.
var usernameRE = regexp.MustCompile(`^[a-z_][a-z0-9_-]{0,31}$`)

// labelRE is one RFC 1123 host name label (ASCII letters, digits, inner hyphens).
var labelRE = regexp.MustCompile(`^[a-z0-9]([a-z0-9-]{0,61}[a-z0-9])?$`)

// foldASCII lowercases ASCII letters only (strings.ToLower is banned: Turkish İ/ı).
func foldASCII(s string) string {
	b := []byte(s)
	for i, c := range b {
		if 'A' <= c && c <= 'Z' {
			b[i] = c + ('a' - 'A')
		}
	}
	return string(b)
}

func hostProblem(code string, params map[string]string) *validate.FieldError {
	return &validate.FieldError{Field: "host", Code: code, Params: params}
}

// NormalizeHost turns what a person typed into the stored host (Review Focus 2): surrounding
// space and one trailing dot are dropped, ASCII is lowercased, an IPv6 literal may be written in
// brackets and is stored without them. A port, scheme, path, user part, zone, non-ASCII name or
// a link-local, multicast, unspecified or broadcast address (SEC-065) is refused with the reason.
func NormalizeHost(raw string) (string, *validate.FieldError) {
	s := strings.TrimSpace(raw)
	if s == "" {
		return "", hostProblem(validate.Required, nil)
	}
	if strings.ContainsAny(s, "/@\\%") {
		return "", hostProblem(validate.Pattern, nil)
	}
	if strings.HasPrefix(s, "[") {
		inner, ok := strings.CutSuffix(strings.TrimPrefix(s, "["), "]")
		a, err := netip.ParseAddr(inner)
		if !ok || err != nil || !a.Is6() || a.Zone() != "" {
			return "", hostProblem(validate.Pattern, nil)
		}
		return checkAddr(a)
	}
	if a, err := netip.ParseAddr(s); err == nil {
		if a.Zone() != "" {
			return "", hostProblem(validate.Pattern, nil)
		}
		return checkAddr(a)
	}
	if i := strings.LastIndexByte(s, ':'); i >= 0 {
		if _, err := strconv.Atoi(s[i+1:]); err == nil && strings.Count(s, ":") == 1 {
			return "", hostProblem(CodeHostPort, nil)
		}
		return "", hostProblem(validate.Pattern, nil)
	}
	for i := 0; i < len(s); i++ {
		if s[i] >= utf8.RuneSelf {
			return "", hostProblem(CodeHostASCII, nil)
		}
	}
	s = strings.TrimSuffix(foldASCII(s), ".")
	if len(s) > maxHostLen {
		return "", hostProblem(validate.TooLong, map[string]string{"max": strconv.Itoa(maxHostLen)})
	}
	for _, label := range strings.Split(s, ".") {
		if !labelRE.MatchString(label) {
			return "", hostProblem(validate.Pattern, nil)
		}
	}
	return s, nil
}

// checkAddr refuses addresses that are never a managed server: link-local (including the cloud
// metadata address 169.254.169.254, SEC-065), multicast, unspecified and the IPv4 broadcast
// address. Loopback and private addresses are allowed.
func checkAddr(a netip.Addr) (string, *validate.FieldError) {
	u := a.Unmap()
	if u.IsLinkLocalUnicast() || u.IsLinkLocalMulticast() || u.IsInterfaceLocalMulticast() ||
		u.IsMulticast() || u.IsUnspecified() || u == netip.AddrFrom4([4]byte{255, 255, 255, 255}) {
		return "", hostProblem(CodeHostNotAllowed, nil)
	}
	return u.String(), nil
}

// validName checks a display name: 1..100 characters, no control or bidirectional override
// characters (they could disguise a name in the UI and the audit log).
func validName(field, raw string) (string, *validate.FieldError) {
	s := strings.TrimSpace(raw)
	switch {
	case s == "":
		return "", &validate.FieldError{Field: field, Code: validate.Required}
	case !utf8.ValidString(s):
		return "", &validate.FieldError{Field: field, Code: validate.Pattern}
	case utf8.RuneCountInString(s) > maxNameRunes:
		return "", &validate.FieldError{Field: field, Code: validate.TooLong, Params: map[string]string{"max": strconv.Itoa(maxNameRunes)}}
	}
	for _, r := range s {
		if unicode.IsControl(r) || unicode.Is(unicode.Bidi_Control, r) {
			return "", &validate.FieldError{Field: field, Code: validate.Pattern}
		}
	}
	return s, nil
}

// validateNewTarget normalizes and checks a new target; it returns the stored form.
func validateNewTarget(in NewTarget) (NewTarget, validate.Errors) {
	var errs validate.Errors
	out := in
	if name, fe := validName("name", in.Name); fe != nil {
		errs = append(errs, *fe)
	} else {
		out.Name = name
	}
	if in.Type != "linux" {
		errs.Add("type", validate.OneOf, map[string]string{"values": "linux"})
	}
	if host, fe := NormalizeHost(in.Host); fe != nil {
		errs = append(errs, *fe)
	} else {
		out.Host = host
	}
	switch {
	case in.Port == 0:
		out.Port = defaultSSHPort
	case in.Port < 1 || in.Port > 65535:
		errs.Add("port", validate.OutOfRange, map[string]string{"min": "1", "max": "65535"})
	}
	out.Username = strings.TrimSpace(in.Username)
	if out.Username == "" {
		out.Username = ServiceUser
	} else if !usernameRE.MatchString(out.Username) {
		errs.Add("username", validate.Pattern, nil)
	}
	return out, errs
}
```

Note: `validate.OneOf` exists in `internal/platform/validate` (`OneOf = "validation.one_of"`).
