```go
package api

import (
	"strings"
	"time"

	"github.com/google/uuid"

	"alice/internal/inventory"
	"alice/internal/jobs"
	"alice/internal/providers"
)

// Wire forms of the Phase 3 resources (contract "API"). No DTO has a credential, private-key or
// secret field: Operators and Auditors see server metadata only (R3).

// errorRefDTO names a stored failure reason by its documented code.
type errorRefDTO struct {
	Code   string            `json:"code"`
	Reason string            `json:"reason"`
	Params map[string]string `json:"params,omitempty"`
}

// errorRef maps a stored reason; an unknown reason becomes the generic internal.unexpected so the
// UI always has a translated text.
func errorRef(reason string, params map[string]string) *errorRefDTO {
	if reason == "" {
		return nil
	}
	ec := codeForReason(reason)
	return &errorRefDTO{Code: ec.Code, Reason: ec.Reason, Params: params}
}

type acceptedDTO struct {
	JobID     string `json:"job_id"`
	StatusURL string `json:"status_url"`
}

func accepted(id uuid.UUID) acceptedDTO {
	return acceptedDTO{JobID: id.String(), StatusURL: "/api/v1/jobs/" + id.String()}
}

type osDTO struct {
	ID         string `json:"id"`
	VersionID  string `json:"version_id"`
	PrettyName string `json:"pretty_name"`
}

type sshdDTO struct {
	Read                   bool     `json:"read"`
	PubkeyAuthentication   string   `json:"pubkey_authentication"`
	PasswordAuthentication string   `json:"password_authentication"`
	PermitRootLogin        string   `json:"permit_root_login"`
	AuthorizedKeysFile     []string `json:"authorized_keys_file"`
	AuthorizedKeysCommand  string   `json:"authorized_keys_command"`
	KeysManagedElsewhere   bool     `json:"keys_managed_elsewhere"`
	CertificatesInUse      bool     `json:"certificates_in_use"`
}

type discoveredHostKeyDTO struct {
	KeyType     string `json:"key_type"`
	Bits        int    `json:"bits"`
	Fingerprint string `json:"fingerprint"`
	Weak        bool   `json:"weak"`
}

type warningDTO struct {
	Code   string            `json:"code"`
	Params map[string]string `json:"params"`
}

type unreadableDTO struct {
	OSUser   string `json:"os_user"`
	FilePath string `json:"file_path"`
	LineNo   int    `json:"line_no"`
}

type factsDTO struct {
	OS             osDTO                  `json:"os"`
	HelperVersion  string                 `json:"helper_version"`
	HelperProtocol int                    `json:"helper_protocol"`
	SSHD           *sshdDTO               `json:"sshd"`
	HostKeys       []discoveredHostKeyDTO `json:"host_keys"`
	Warnings       []warningDTO           `json:"warnings"`
	Unreadable     []unreadableDTO        `json:"unreadable"`
}

type targetDTO struct {
	ID                     string       `json:"id"`
	Name                   string       `json:"name"`
	Type                   string       `json:"type"`
	Host                   string       `json:"host"`
	Port                   int          `json:"port"`
	Username               string       `json:"username"`
	Status                 string       `json:"status"`
	LastError              *errorRefDTO `json:"last_error"`
	LastSuccessAt          *time.Time   `json:"last_success_at"`
	LastDiscoveryAt        *time.Time   `json:"last_discovery_at"`
	DiscoveryIntervalHours int          `json:"discovery_interval_hours"`
	KeysManagedElsewhere   bool         `json:"keys_managed_elsewhere"`
	Capabilities           []string     `json:"capabilities"`
	Facts                  factsDTO     `json:"facts"`
	Version                int          `json:"version"`
	CreatedAt              time.Time    `json:"created_at"`
	UpdatedAt              time.Time    `json:"updated_at"`
}

func utcPtr(t *time.Time) *time.Time {
	if t == nil {
		return nil
	}
	u := t.UTC()
	return &u
}

func nonNil[T any](s []T) []T {
	if s == nil {
		return []T{}
	}
	return s
}

func factsJSON(f inventory.Facts) factsDTO {
	d := factsDTO{
		OS:            osDTO{ID: f.OS.ID, VersionID: f.OS.VersionID, PrettyName: f.OS.PrettyName},
		HelperVersion: f.HelperVersion, HelperProtocol: f.HelperProtocol,
		HostKeys: []discoveredHostKeyDTO{}, Warnings: []warningDTO{}, Unreadable: []unreadableDTO{},
	}
	if f.SSHD != nil {
		d.SSHD = &sshdDTO{
			Read: f.SSHD.Read, PubkeyAuthentication: f.SSHD.PubkeyAuthentication, PasswordAuthentication: f.SSHD.PasswordAuthentication,
			PermitRootLogin: f.SSHD.PermitRootLogin, AuthorizedKeysFile: nonNil(f.SSHD.AuthorizedKeysFile),
			AuthorizedKeysCommand: f.SSHD.AuthorizedKeysCommand, KeysManagedElsewhere: f.SSHD.KeysManagedElsewhere,
			CertificatesInUse: f.SSHD.CertificatesInUse,
		}
	}
	for _, k := range f.HostKeys {
		d.HostKeys = append(d.HostKeys, discoveredHostKeyDTO{KeyType: k.KeyType, Bits: k.Bits, Fingerprint: k.Fingerprint, Weak: k.Weak})
	}
	for _, w := range f.Warnings {
		params := w.Params
		if params == nil {
			params = map[string]string{}
		}
		d.Warnings = append(d.Warnings, warningDTO{Code: w.Code, Params: params})
	}
	for _, u := range f.Unreadable {
		d.Unreadable = append(d.Unreadable, unreadableDTO{OSUser: u.OSUser, FilePath: u.FilePath, LineNo: u.LineNo})
	}
	return d
}

func targetJSON(t inventory.Target) targetDTO {
	return targetDTO{
		ID: t.ID.String(), Name: t.Name, Type: t.Type, Host: t.Host, Port: t.Port, Username: t.Username,
		Status: t.Status, LastError: errorRef(t.LastErrorCode, nil),
		LastSuccessAt: utcPtr(t.LastSuccessAt), LastDiscoveryAt: utcPtr(t.LastDiscoveryAt),
		DiscoveryIntervalHours: int(t.DiscoveryInterval / time.Hour), KeysManagedElsewhere: t.KeysManagedElsewhere,
		Capabilities: nonNil(t.Capabilities), Facts: factsJSON(t.Facts), Version: t.Version,
		CreatedAt: t.CreatedAt.UTC(), UpdatedAt: t.UpdatedAt.UTC(),
	}
}

type hostKeyDTO struct {
	ID              string     `json:"id"`
	KeyType         string     `json:"key_type"`
	Fingerprint     string     `json:"fingerprint"`
	Status          string     `json:"status"`
	ObservedAt      time.Time  `json:"observed_at"`
	ConfirmedAt     *time.Time `json:"confirmed_at"`
	ConfirmedByName string     `json:"confirmed_by_name"`
	SupersededAt    *time.Time `json:"superseded_at"`
	VerifyCommand   string     `json:"verify_command"`
}

// verifyCommand is what an administrator runs on the server to see the same fingerprint (R33).
func verifyCommand(keyType string) string {
	name := "rsa"
	switch {
	case keyType == "ssh-ed25519":
		name = "ed25519"
	case strings.HasPrefix(keyType, "ecdsa-"):
		name = "ecdsa"
	}
	return "ssh-keygen -lf /etc/ssh/ssh_host_" + name + "_key.pub"
}

func hostKeyJSON(k inventory.HostKeyRecord) hostKeyDTO {
	return hostKeyDTO{
		ID: k.ID.String(), KeyType: k.KeyType, Fingerprint: k.Fingerprint, Status: k.Status, ObservedAt: k.ObservedAt.UTC(),
		ConfirmedAt: utcPtr(k.ConfirmedAt), ConfirmedByName: k.ConfirmedByName, SupersededAt: utcPtr(k.SupersededAt),
		VerifyCommand: verifyCommand(k.KeyType),
	}
}

type keyLocationDTO struct {
	ID                   string     `json:"id"`

	Comment              string     `json:"comment"`
	Flags                []string   `json:"flags"`
	FirstSeenAt          time.Time  `json:"first_seen_at"`
	LastSeenAt           time.Time  `json:"last_seen_at"`
	MissingSince         *time.Time `json:"missing_since"`
	RemovedAt            *time.Time `json:"removed_at"`
	IsAliceConnectionKey bool       `json:"is_alice_connection_key"`
}

func keyLocationJSON(l inventory.KeyLocation) keyLocationDTO {
	return keyLocationDTO{
		ID: l.ID.String(), SSHKeyID: l.SSHKeyID.String(), Fingerprint: l.Fingerprint, KeyType: l.KeyType,
		TargetID: l.TargetID.String(), TargetName: l.TargetName, OSUser: l.OSUser, FilePath: l.FilePath, LineNo: l.LineNo,
		Options: l.Options, Comment: l.Comment, Flags: nonNil(l.Flags), FirstSeenAt: l.FirstSeenAt.UTC(),
		LastSeenAt: l.LastSeenAt.UTC(), MissingSince: utcPtr(l.MissingSince), RemovedAt: utcPtr(l.RemovedAt),
		IsAliceConnectionKey: l.IsAliceConnectionKey,
	}
}

type sshKeyDTO struct {
	ID            string           `json:"id"`
	Fingerprint   string           `json:"fingerprint"`
	KeyType       string           `json:"key_type"`
	Bits          int              `json:"bits"`
	PublicKey     string           `json:"public_key"`
	Managed       bool             `json:"managed"`
	IsPlatformKey bool             `json:"is_platform_key"`
	Weak          bool             `json:"weak"`
	Comment       string           `json:"comment"`
	LocationCount int              `json:"location_count"`
	TargetCount   int              `json:"target_count"`
	FirstSeenAt   time.Time        `json:"first_seen_at"`
	Locations     []keyLocationDTO `json:"locations,omitempty"`
}

// sshKeyJSON renders a key; withLocations adds the locations array (always present, possibly empty).
func sshKeyJSON(k inventory.SSHKey, withLocations bool) sshKeyDTO {
	d := sshKeyDTO{
		ID: k.ID.String(), Fingerprint: k.Fingerprint, KeyType: k.KeyType, Bits: k.Bits, PublicKey: k.PublicKey,
		Managed: k.Managed, IsPlatformKey: k.IsPlatformKey, Weak: k.Weak, Comment: k.Comment,
		LocationCount: k.LocationCount, TargetCount: k.TargetCount, FirstSeenAt: k.FirstSeenAt.UTC(),
	}
	if withLocations {
		d.Locations = make([]keyLocationDTO, 0, len(k.Locations))
		for _, l := range k.Locations {
			d.Locations = append(d.Locations, keyLocationJSON(l))
		}
	}
	return d
}

type snippetDTO struct {
	Sudoers string `json:"sudoers"`
	Script  string `json:"script"`
}

type platformKeyDTO struct {
	PublicKey          string                `json:"public_key"`
	Fingerprint        string                `json:"fingerprint"`
	AuthorizedKeysLine string                `json:"authorized_keys_line"`
	HelperPath         string                `json:"helper_path"`
	HelperProtocol     int                   `json:"helper_protocol"`
	Profiles           map[string]snippetDTO `json:"profiles"`
}

func platformKeyJSON(g inventory.Guide) platformKeyDTO {
	d := platformKeyDTO{
		PublicKey: g.PublicKey, Fingerprint: g.Fingerprint, AuthorizedKeysLine: g.AuthorizedKeysLine,
		HelperPath: g.HelperPath, HelperProtocol: g.HelperProtocol, Profiles: map[string]snippetDTO{},
	}
	for name, p := range g.Profiles {
		d.Profiles[name] = snippetDTO{Sudoers: p.Sudoers, Script: p.Script}
	}
	return d
}

type jobDTO struct {
	ID          string         `json:"id"`
	Type        string         `json:"type"`
	Kind        string         `json:"kind"`
	Status      string         `json:"status"`
	TargetID    *string        `json:"target_id"`
	Attempts    int            `json:"attempts"`
	MaxAttempts int            `json:"max_attempts"`
	Error       *errorRefDTO   `json:"error"`
	Result      map[string]any `json:"result"`
	CreatedAt   time.Time      `json:"created_at"`
	RunAt       time.Time      `json:"run_at"`
	StartedAt   *time.Time     `json:"started_at"`
	FinishedAt  *time.Time     `json:"finished_at"`
}

func jobJSON(v jobs.View) jobDTO {
	d := jobDTO{
		ID: v.ID.String(), Type: v.Type, Kind: v.Kind, Status: string(v.Status), Attempts: v.Attempts, MaxAttempts: v.MaxAttempts,
		Error: errorRef(v.LastErrorCode, v.ErrorParams), Result: v.Result, CreatedAt: v.CreatedAt.UTC(), RunAt: v.RunAt.UTC(),
		StartedAt: utcPtr(v.StartedAt), FinishedAt: utcPtr(v.FinishedAt),
	}
	if v.TargetID != uuid.Nil {
		id := v.TargetID.String()
		d.TargetID = &id
	}
	if d.Result == nil {
		d.Result = map[string]any{}
	}
	return d
}

type fieldDTO struct {
	Name     string   `json:"name"`
	Type     string   `json:"type"`
	Required bool     `json:"required"`
	Default  any      `json:"default"`
	LabelKey string   `json:"label_key"`
	HelpKey  string   `json:"help_key"`
	Pattern  string   `json:"pattern"`
	Min      int      `json:"min"`
	Max      int      `json:"max"`
	Values   []string `json:"values"`
}

type providerDTO struct {
	Kind           string   `json:"kind"`
	DisplayNameKey string   `json:"display_name_key"`
	Capabilities   []string `json:"capabilities"`
	ConfigSchema   struct {
		Fields []fieldDTO `json:"fields"`
	} `json:"config_schema"`
}

func providerJSON(d providers.Descriptor) providerDTO {
	out := providerDTO{Kind: string(d.Kind), DisplayNameKey: d.DisplayNameKey, Capabilities: []string{}}
	for _, c := range d.Capabilities {
		out.Capabilities = append(out.Capabilities, string(c))
	}
	out.ConfigSchema.Fields = []fieldDTO{}
	for _, f := range d.ConfigSchema.Fields {
		out.ConfigSchema.Fields = append(out.ConfigSchema.Fields, fieldDTO{
			Name: f.Name, Type: string(f.Type), Required: f.Required, Default: f.Default, LabelKey: f.LabelKey,
			HelpKey: f.HelpKey, Pattern: f.Pattern, Min: f.Min, Max: f.Max, Values: nonNil(f.Values),
		})
	}
	return out
}
```

```go
package api

import (
	"net/http"
	"regexp"
	"strconv"

	"github.com/google/uuid"

	"alice/internal/inventory"
	"alice/internal/license"
	"alice/internal/platform/validate"
	"alice/internal/rbac"
)

// targetRoutes manage servers and their host keys (spec §9.6 "targets", R37 items 8 and 12). Adding,
// changing and removing a server and confirming a fingerprint are infrastructure changes (refused in
// lock); test and discovery are recurring read-only work (also paused in lock, §8.6).
func (s *server) targetRoutes() []route {
	return []route{
		{method: http.MethodGet, pattern: "/api/v1/targets", perm: rbac.Read, handler: s.listTargets},
		{method: http.MethodPost, pattern: "/api/v1/targets", perm: rbac.TargetsManage, lic: license.ClassChange, handler: s.createTarget},
		{method: http.MethodGet, pattern: "/api/v1/targets/{id}", perm: rbac.Read, handler: s.getTarget},
		{method: http.MethodPatch, pattern: "/api/v1/targets/{id}", perm: rbac.TargetsManage, lic: license.ClassChange, handler: s.updateTarget},
		{method: http.MethodDelete, pattern: "/api/v1/targets/{id}", perm: rbac.TargetsManage, lic: license.ClassChange, handler: s.deleteTarget},
		{method: http.MethodPost, pattern: "/api/v1/targets/{id}/actions/test", perm: rbac.InventoryOperate, lic: license.ClassReadOnly, handler: s.testTarget},
		{method: http.MethodPost, pattern: "/api/v1/targets/{id}/actions/discover", perm: rbac.InventoryOperate, lic: license.ClassReadOnly, handler: s.discoverTarget},
		{method: http.MethodGet, pattern: "/api/v1/targets/{id}/host-keys", perm: rbac.Read, handler: s.listHostKeys},
		{method: http.MethodPost, pattern: "/api/v1/targets/{id}/host-keys/{key_id}/actions/confirm", perm: rbac.HostKeysConfirm, lic: license.ClassChange, handler: s.confirmHostKey},
		{method: http.MethodPost, pattern: "/api/v1/targets/{id}/host-keys/{key_id}/actions/repin", perm: rbac.HostKeysRepin, lic: license.ClassChange, handler: s.repinHostKey},
		{method: http.MethodGet, pattern: "/api/v1/targets/{id}/ssh-keys", perm: rbac.Read, handler: s.listTargetKeys},
	}
}

// maxRepinBody caps the re-pin request (a fingerprint and a reason of at most 500 characters).
const maxRepinBody = 8 << 10

// actor is the caller as the inventory needs it: audit identity, user and role.
func (s *server) actor(r *http.Request) inventory.Actor {
	p := principalFrom(r.Context())
	return inventory.Actor{Audit: p.Actor(s.meta(r)), UserID: p.UserID, Role: p.Role}
}

// etag is the strong validator of a target version.
func etag(version int) string { return `"` + strconv.Itoa(version) + `"` }

var ifMatchRE = regexp.MustCompile(`^"([1-9][0-9]{0,9})"$`)

// ifMatch returns the target version named by a single strong If-Match validator. Weak validators,
// lists and "*" are refused: a change must name the exact version it was based on (§9.1).
func ifMatch(r *http.Request) (int, bool) {
	m := ifMatchRE.FindStringSubmatch(r.Header.Get("If-Match"))
	if m == nil {
		return 0, false
	}
	n, err := strconv.Atoi(m[1])
	return n, err == nil
}

// parseBool reads an optional boolean query parameter ("true" or "false").
func parseBool(raw, field string, v *validate.Errors) bool {
	switch raw {
	case "", "false":
		return false
	case "true":
		return true
	default:
		v.Add(field, validate.OneOf, map[string]string{"values": "true, false"})
		return false
	}
}

func (s *server) listTargets(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
	ts, err := s.deps.Inventory.ListTargets(r.Context())
	if err != nil {
		s.fail(w, r, err)
		return
	}
	items := make([]targetDTO, 0, len(ts))
	for _, t := range ts {
		items = append(items, targetJSON(t))
	}
	writeJSON(w, http.StatusOK, map[string]any{"items": items, "next_cursor": nil})
}

func (s *server) createTarget(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
	var req struct {
		Name     string `json:"name"`
		Type     string `json:"type"`
		Host     string `json:"host"`
		Port     int    `json:"port"`
		Username string `json:"username"`
	}
	if !s.decode(w, r, &req) {
		return
	}
	if req.Type == "" {
		req.Type = "linux"
	}
	t, jobID, err := s.deps.Inventory.CreateTarget(r.Context(), s.actor(r), inventory.NewTarget{
		Name: req.Name, Type: req.Type, Host: req.Host, Port: req.Port, Username: req.Username,
	})
	if err != nil {
		s.fail(w, r, err)
		return
	}
	a := accepted(jobID)
	w.Header().Set("ETag", etag(t.Version))
	writeJSON(w, http.StatusCreated, map[string]any{"target": targetJSON(t), "job_id": a.JobID, "status_url": a.StatusURL})
}

func (s *server) getTarget(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
	id, ok := pathUUID(r, "id")
	if !ok {
		s.writeError(w, r, ErrNotFound)
		return
	}
	t, err := s.deps.Inventory.GetTarget(r.Context(), id)
	if err != nil {
		s.fail(w, r, err)
		return
	}
	w.Header().Set("ETag", etag(t.Version))
	writeJSON(w, http.StatusOK, targetJSON(t))
}

func (s *server) updateTarget(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
	id, ok := pathUUID(r, "id")
	if !ok {
		s.writeError(w, r, ErrNotFound)
		return
	}
	version, ok := ifMatch(r)
	if !ok {
		s.writeError(w, r, ErrPreconditionFailed)
		return
	}
	var req struct {
		Name                   *string `json:"name"`
		DiscoveryIntervalHours *int    `json:"discovery_interval_hours"`
	}
	if !s.decode(w, r, &req) {
		return
	}
	t, err := s.deps.Inventory.UpdateTarget(r.Context(), s.actor(r), id, version,
		inventory.TargetPatch{Name: req.Name, DiscoveryIntervalHours: req.DiscoveryIntervalHours})
	if err != nil {
		s.fail(w, r, err)
		return
	}
	w.Header().Set("ETag", etag(t.Version))
	writeJSON(w, http.StatusOK, targetJSON(t))
}

func (s *server) deleteTarget(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
	id, ok := pathUUID(r, "id")
	if !ok {
		s.writeError(w, r, ErrNotFound)
		return
	}
	if err := s.deps.Inventory.DeleteTarget(r.Context(), s.actor(r), id); err != nil {
		s.fail(w, r, err)
		return
	}
	noContent(w)
}

func (s *server) testTarget(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
	id, ok := pathUUID(r, "id")
	if !ok {
		s.writeError(w, r, ErrNotFound)
		return
	}
	jobID, err := s.deps.Inventory.RequestTest(r.Context(), s.actor(r), id)
	if err != nil {
		s.fail(w, r, err)
		return
	}
	writeJSON(w, http.StatusAccepted, accepted(jobID))
}

func (s *server) discoverTarget(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
	id, ok := pathUUID(r, "id")
	if !ok {
		s.writeError(w, r, ErrNotFound)
		return
	}
	jobID, err := s.deps.Inventory.RequestDiscovery(r.Context(), s.actor(r), id)
	if err != nil {
		s.fail(w, r, err)
		return
	}
	writeJSON(w, http.StatusAccepted, accepted(jobID))
}

func (s *server) listHostKeys(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
	id, ok := pathUUID(r, "id")
	if !ok {
		s.writeError(w, r, ErrNotFound)
		return
	}
	keys, err := s.deps.Inventory.ListHostKeys(r.Context(), id)
	if err != nil {
		s.fail(w, r, err)
		return
	}
	items := make([]hostKeyDTO, 0, len(keys))
	for _, k := range keys {
		items = append(items, hostKeyJSON(k))
	}
	writeJSON(w, http.StatusOK, map[string][]hostKeyDTO{"items": items})
}

// hostKeyIDs parses both path identifiers of a host-key action; on failure it has answered 404.
func (s *server) hostKeyIDs(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) (target, key uuid.UUID, ok bool) {
	t, ok1 := pathUUID(r, "id")
	k, ok2 := pathUUID(r, "key_id")
	if !ok1 || !ok2 {
		s.writeError(w, r, ErrNotFound)
		return uuid.Nil, uuid.Nil, false
	}
	return t, k, true
}

func (s *server) confirmHostKey(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
	targetID, keyID, ok := s.hostKeyIDs(w, r)
	if !ok {
		return
	}
	var req struct {
		Fingerprint string `json:"fingerprint"`
	}
	if !s.decode(w, r, &req) {
		return
	}
	if req.Fingerprint == "" {
		var v validate.Errors
		v.Add("fingerprint", validate.Required, nil)
		s.fail(w, r, v)
		return
	}
	jobID, err := s.deps.Inventory.ConfirmHostKey(r.Context(), s.actor(r), targetID, keyID, req.Fingerprint)
	if err != nil {
		s.fail(w, r, err)
		return
	}
	writeJSON(w, http.StatusAccepted, accepted(jobID))
}

func (s *server) repinHostKey(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
	targetID, keyID, ok := s.hostKeyIDs(w, r)
	if !ok {
		return
	}
	var req struct {
		Fingerprint string `json:"fingerprint"`
		Reason      string `json:"reason"`
	}
	if !s.decodeLimit(w, r, &req, maxRepinBody) {
		return
	}
	if req.Fingerprint == "" {
		var v validate.Errors
		v.Add("fingerprint", validate.Required, nil)
		s.fail(w, r, v)
		return
	}
	// The reason rules (10–500 characters, no PEM block, S-05) are enforced by the inventory.
	jobID, err := s.deps.Inventory.RepinHostKey(r.Context(), s.actor(r), targetID, keyID, req.Fingerprint, req.Reason)
	if err != nil {
		s.fail(w, r, err)
		return
	}
	writeJSON(w, http.StatusAccepted, accepted(jobID))
}

func (s *server) listTargetKeys(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
	id, ok := pathUUID(r, "id")
	if !ok {
		s.writeError(w, r, ErrNotFound)
		return
	}
	var v validate.Errors
	missing := parseBool(r.URL.Query().Get("missing"), "missing", &v)
	if err := v.Err(); err != nil {
		s.fail(w, r, err)
		return
	}
	locs, err := s.deps.Inventory.ListTargetKeys(r.Context(), id, missing)
	if err != nil {
		s.fail(w, r, err)
		return
	}
	items := make([]keyLocationDTO, 0, len(locs))
	for _, l := range locs {
		items = append(items, keyLocationJSON(l))
	}
	writeJSON(w, http.StatusOK, map[string][]keyLocationDTO{"items": items})
}
```

Create `internal/api/sshkeys_handlers.go`:

```go
package api

import (
	"net/http"
	"net/netip"
	"slices"
	"strconv"
	"unicode/utf8"

	"github.com/google/uuid"

	"alice/internal/inventory"
	"alice/internal/license"
	"alice/internal/platform/validate"
	"alice/internal/providers"
	"alice/internal/rbac"
)

// sshKeyRoutes are the SSH key inventory (§9.6 "ssh-keys"). Removing a key changes a managed
// server (ClassChange, refused in lock); Operators may remove keys (§15.4); Alice's own key is
// refused by the inventory, the provider and a database trigger (SEC-081).
func (s *server) sshKeyRoutes() []route {
	return []route{
		{method: http.MethodGet, pattern: "/api/v1/ssh-keys", perm: rbac.Read, handler: s.listSSHKeys},
		{method: http.MethodGet, pattern: "/api/v1/ssh-keys/platform-key", perm: rbac.TargetsManage, handler: s.platformKey},
		{method: http.MethodGet, pattern: "/api/v1/ssh-keys/{id}", perm: rbac.Read, handler: s.getSSHKey},
		{method: http.MethodPost, pattern: "/api/v1/ssh-keys/locations/{id}/actions/remove", perm: rbac.InventoryOperate, lic: license.ClassChange, handler: s.removeKeyLocation},
	}
}

// knownFlags are the flag filter values (providers.Flag*).
var knownFlags = []string{providers.FlagWeak, providers.FlagCommand, providers.FlagRootWithoutFrom,
	providers.FlagDuplicate, providers.FlagCertAuthority, providers.FlagSecurityKey}

// Query parameter bounds of the key list.
const (
	maxQueryRunes  = 200
	maxCursorBytes = 512
	maxOSUserBytes = 32
)

// pageLimit reads ?limit= (1..200, default 50).
func pageLimit(raw string, v *validate.Errors) int {
	if raw == "" {
		return 50
	}
	n, err := strconv.Atoi(raw)
	if err != nil || n < 1 || n > 200 {
		v.Add("limit", validate.OutOfRange, map[string]string{"min": "1", "max": "200"})
		return 0
	}
	return n
}

// optionalUUID reads an optional UUID query parameter.
func optionalUUID(raw, field string, v *validate.Errors) uuid.UUID {
	if raw == "" {
		return uuid.Nil
	}
	id, err := uuid.Parse(raw)
	if err != nil {
		v.Add(field, validate.Pattern, nil)
		return uuid.Nil
	}
	return id
}

func (s *server) listSSHKeys(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
	q := r.URL.Query()
	var v validate.Errors
	f := inventory.KeyFilter{
		TargetID:       optionalUUID(q.Get("target_id"), "target_id", &v),
		OSUser:         q.Get("os_user"),
		Query:          q.Get("q"),
		Flag:           q.Get("flag"),
		IncludeMissing: parseBool(q.Get("missing"), "missing", &v),
		Cursor:         q.Get("cursor"),
		Limit:          pageLimit(q.Get("limit"), &v),
	}
	if len(f.OSUser) > maxOSUserBytes {
		v.Add("os_user", validate.TooLong, map[string]string{"max": strconv.Itoa(maxOSUserBytes)})
	}
	if utf8.RuneCountInString(f.Query) > maxQueryRunes {
		v.Add("q", validate.TooLong, map[string]string{"max": strconv.Itoa(maxQueryRunes)})
	}
	if f.Flag != "" && !slices.Contains(knownFlags, f.Flag) {
		v.Add("flag", validate.OneOf, map[string]string{"values": joinValues(knownFlags)})
	}
	if len(f.Cursor) > maxCursorBytes {
		v.Add("cursor", validate.TooLong, map[string]string{"max": strconv.Itoa(maxCursorBytes)})
	}
	if err := v.Err(); err != nil {
		s.fail(w, r, err)
		return
	}
	page, err := s.deps.Inventory.ListSSHKeys(r.Context(), f)
	if err != nil {
		s.fail(w, r, err)
		return
	}
	items := make([]sshKeyDTO, 0, len(page.Items))
	for _, k := range page.Items {
		items = append(items, sshKeyJSON(k, false))
	}
	var next any
	if page.NextCursor != "" {
		next = page.NextCursor
	}
	writeJSON(w, http.StatusOK, map[string]any{"items": items, "next_cursor": next})
}

// joinValues renders allowed values for validate.OneOf.
func joinValues(vs []string) string {
	out := ""
	for i, v := range vs {
		if i > 0 {
			out += ", "
		}
		out += v
	}
	return out
}

func (s *server) getSSHKey(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
	id, ok := pathUUID(r, "id")
	if !ok {
		s.writeError(w, r, ErrNotFound)
		return
	}
	k, err := s.deps.Inventory.GetSSHKey(r.Context(), id)
	if err != nil {
		s.fail(w, r, err)
		return
	}
	writeJSON(w, http.StatusOK, sshKeyJSON(k, true))
}

// platformKey returns Alice's public key and the setup snippets (§12.2, §18.5 step 7). ?from= adds
// a from="…" restriction to the authorized_keys line (SEC-082); it must be an IP address.
func (s *server) platformKey(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
	from := r.URL.Query().Get("from")
	if from != "" {
		if _, err := netip.ParseAddr(from); err != nil {
			var v validate.Errors
			v.Add("from", validate.Pattern, nil)
			s.fail(w, r, v)
			return
		}
	}
	g, err := s.deps.Inventory.SetupGuide(r.Context(), from)
	if err != nil {
		s.fail(w, r, err)
		return
	}
	writeJSON(w, http.StatusOK, platformKeyJSON(g))
}

func (s *server) removeKeyLocation(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
	id, ok := pathUUID(r, "id")
	if !ok {
		s.writeError(w, r, ErrNotFound)
		return
	}
	var req struct {
		ConfirmLastRootKey bool `json:"confirm_last_root_key"`
	}
	// The body is optional: an empty POST removes the key without the root confirmation.
	if r.ContentLength != 0 && !s.decode(w, r, &req) {
		return
	}
	jobID, err := s.deps.Inventory.RequestKeyRemoval(r.Context(), s.actor(r), id, req.ConfirmLastRootKey)
	if err != nil {
		s.fail(w, r, err)
		return
	}
	writeJSON(w, http.StatusAccepted, accepted(jobID))
}
```

Create `internal/api/jobs_handlers.go`:

```go
package api

import (
	"context"
	"net/http"
	"slices"
	"strconv"

	"github.com/google/uuid"

	"alice/internal/audit"
	"alice/internal/jobs"
	"alice/internal/license"
	"alice/internal/platform/validate"
	"alice/internal/rbac"
)

// jobRoutes show background work and let an Administrator run or discard work that the license
// paused (R29, L-81). Both actions start or stop external work, so they are refused in lock.
func (s *server) jobRoutes() []route {
	return []route{
		{method: http.MethodGet, pattern: "/api/v1/jobs", perm: rbac.Read, handler: s.listJobs},
		{method: http.MethodGet, pattern: "/api/v1/jobs/{id}", perm: rbac.Read, handler: s.getJob},
		{method: http.MethodPost, pattern: "/api/v1/jobs/{id}/actions/confirm", perm: rbac.JobsConfirm, lic: license.ClassChange, handler: s.confirmJob},
		{method: http.MethodPost, pattern: "/api/v1/jobs/{id}/actions/discard", perm: rbac.JobsConfirm, lic: license.ClassChange, handler: s.discardJob},
	}
}

var jobStatuses = []string{"queued", "running", "succeeded", "failed", "cancelled", "dead", "blocked_license"}

func (s *server) listJobs(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
	q := r.URL.Query()
	var v validate.Errors
	f := jobs.ListFilter{
		Status:   jobs.Status(q.Get("status")),
		TargetID: optionalUUID(q.Get("target_id"), "target_id", &v),
		Cursor:   q.Get("cursor"),
		Limit:    pageLimit(q.Get("limit"), &v),
	}
	if f.Status != "" && !slices.Contains(jobStatuses, string(f.Status)) {
		v.Add("status", validate.OneOf, map[string]string{"values": joinValues(jobStatuses)})
	}
	if len(f.Cursor) > maxCursorBytes {
		v.Add("cursor", validate.TooLong, map[string]string{"max": strconv.Itoa(maxCursorBytes)})
	}
	if err := v.Err(); err != nil {
		s.fail(w, r, err)
		return
	}
	views, next, err := s.deps.Jobs.List(r.Context(), f)
	if err != nil {
		s.fail(w, r, err)
		return
	}
	items := make([]jobDTO, 0, len(views))
	for _, jv := range views {
		items = append(items, jobJSON(jv))
	}
	var nextCursor any
	if next != "" {
		nextCursor = next
	}
	writeJSON(w, http.StatusOK, map[string]any{"items": items, "next_cursor": nextCursor})
}

func (s *server) getJob(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
	id, ok := pathUUID(r, "id")
	if !ok {
		s.writeError(w, r, ErrNotFound)
		return
	}
	jv, err := s.deps.Jobs.Get(r.Context(), id)
	if err != nil {
		s.fail(w, r, err)
		return
	}
	writeJSON(w, http.StatusOK, jobJSON(jv))
}

func (s *server) confirmJob(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
	s.jobAction(w, r, s.deps.Jobs.Confirm)
}

func (s *server) discardJob(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
	s.jobAction(w, r, s.deps.Jobs.Discard)
}

// jobAction runs confirm or discard as the caller and answers with the job's new state.
func (s *server) jobAction(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request, act func(ctx context.Context, actor audit.Actor, by, id uuid.UUID) error) {
	id, ok := pathUUID(r, "id")
	if !ok {
		s.writeError(w, r, ErrNotFound)
		return
	}
	p := principalFrom(r.Context())
	if err := act(r.Context(), p.Actor(s.meta(r)), p.UserID, id); err != nil {
		s.fail(w, r, err)
		return
	}
	jv, err := s.deps.Jobs.Get(r.Context(), id)
	if err != nil {
		s.fail(w, r, err)
		return
	}
	writeJSON(w, http.StatusOK, jobJSON(jv))
}
```

```yaml
        "422": { $ref: "#/components/responses/Error" }

    delete:

        default: { $ref: "#/components/responses/Error" }

        "202":
          description: Queued
          content:
            application/json:

        default: { $ref: "#/components/responses/Error" }
  /api/v1/targets/{id}/actions/discover:

      responses:

            application/json:

        "409": { $ref: "#/components/responses/Error" }
        default: { $ref: "#/components/responses/Error" }
  /api/v1/targets/{id}/host-keys:
```

### Task 17: API integration — journeys with the fake SSH server, secret-leak suite with SSH keys, lock (L-04, L-26, L-29, L-81)

Task 16's handler tests fake every service. This task runs the whole stack instead: the real `inventory.Service`,
`jobs.Queue` and `jobs.Runner` (driven step by step with `RunOnce`, no goroutines), the `targetjobs` handlers, the
real `linuxssh` provider and dialer, and an in-process SSH server (`linuxsshtest.Server`) whose command handler is the
`alice-helper` emulator (`linuxsshtest.Emulator`). The journeys follow the owner's Phase 3 steps over HTTP: add a server,
see the fingerprint, confirm it, see the keys, try to remove Alice's own key, remove another key, see a changed host key
block everything until an Administrator re-pins with step-up. The lock journeys re-run L-26, L-29 and L-81 against the
real jobs (carry 3), L-04 against real targets, and the secret-leak suite gains the platform SSH key (§25.2 "SSH private
key (PEM and OpenSSH formats)").

**Files:**
- Modify: `internal/api/stack_integration_test.go` (`stack` fields, `start`, `deps`)
- Create: `internal/api/targets_integration_test.go`
- Create: `internal/api/platformkey_leak_integration_test.go`

**Interfaces:**
- Consumes (contract): `inventory.New`, `inventory.Config`, `inventory.Counter`, `(*inventory.Service).EnsurePlatformKey`,
  `PlatformKey`, `HostKeyStore`, `ScheduleDiscovery`; `jobs.NewQueue(jobs.QueueConfig{Pool, Keyring, Audit, Clock, Gate})`
  (Task 11 added `Gate`; `Keyring` accepts `*secrets.Keyring`), `jobs.NewRunner(jobs.RunnerConfig{…})`,
  `(*jobs.Runner).RunOnce`; `targetjobs.Register(r, targetjobs.Deps{Inventory, Registry, Clock, Log})`;
  `providers.NewRegistry`, `Register`, `Freeze`; `linuxssh.New(linuxssh.Options{Pool})`, `linuxssh.NewPool`,
  `linuxssh.Dialer{Clock, HostKeys}`, `linuxssh.MaxConnections`, `MaxConnectionsPerTarget`, `IdleTimeout`;
  `linuxsshtest.NewServer`, `Server.Addr/HostKey/SetHostKey/Authorize/AuthAttempts/Commands/SetHandler`,
  `linuxsshtest.NewHostKey`, `linuxsshtest.NewEmulator`, `Emulator.SetFile/File/SetSSHD/Writes/Handler`,
  `linuxsshtest.Response`; `license.Config.Targets`; the Task 16 routes and codes.
- Produces: stack fields `inv *inventory.Service`, `queue *jobs.Queue`, `runner *jobs.Runner`, `registry *providers.Registry`;
  helpers `(*stack).sshFixture() *sshFixture`, `addServer`, `pinServer`, `runJobs`, `job`, `auditCount`,
  `targetLocations`, `platformSeed` (test-only; Task 22 does not use them).

Behaviour this task relies on from Tasks 13–15 (stated in the contract or the owning task): a target is created in
status `pending_host_key` with a `target.test_connection` job; the first connection records the presented key as
`observed` and fails the job with `target.host_key_unconfirmed` before any authentication; confirming enqueues a new test,
whose success enqueues `target.discover`; a target in `host_key_changed` answers `RequestDiscovery` and
`RequestKeyRemoval` with `inventory.ErrHostKeyChanged`, while `RequestTest` still queues a test that fails without
dialing; `ScheduleDiscovery` only schedules targets in status `ok`; adding or deleting a target runs `license.Tick`
after the commit; the target host `127.0.0.1` (the fake SSH server) is accepted by the address validation.

Create `internal/api/targets_integration_test.go`:

```go
//go:build integration

package api

import (
	"context"
	"crypto/ed25519"
	"crypto/rand"
	"fmt"
	"net/http"
	"strings"
	"testing"
	"time"

	"github.com/stretchr/testify/assert"
	"github.com/stretchr/testify/require"
	"golang.org/x/crypto/ssh"

	"alice/internal/providers/linuxssh/linuxsshtest"
)

// End-to-end API journeys for Phase 3 (spec §26.5 owner steps 2–6, F-30..F-33, F-36, L-04,
// L-26, L-29, L-81): real services and jobs, a fake SSH server answering like alice-helper.

const (
	rootKeysPath   = "/root/.ssh/authorized_keys"
	deployKeysPath = "/home/deploy/.ssh/authorized_keys"
	aliceKeysPath  = "/var/lib/alice-svc/.ssh/authorized_keys"
)

// fixtureKey is a public key generated for one test (no key material is committed).
type fixtureKey struct {
	line string // "ssh-ed25519 AAAA…" without comment
	fp   string
}

func newFixtureKey(t *testing.T) fixtureKey {
	t.Helper()
	pub, _, err := ed25519.GenerateKey(rand.Reader)
	require.NoError(t, err)
	sp, err := ssh.NewPublicKey(pub)
	require.NoError(t, err)
	return fixtureKey{line: strings.TrimSpace(string(ssh.MarshalAuthorizedKey(sp))), fp: ssh.FingerprintSHA256(sp)}
}

// sshFixture is one Linux server: the fake SSH server, its emulated helper and the files on it.
type sshFixture struct {
	server            *linuxsshtest.Server
	emu               *linuxsshtest.Emulator
	host              string
	port              int
	laptop, ci, root  fixtureKey
	platform          string // Alice's key as "type base64"
	platformFP        string
	files             map[string]string // path -> content as seeded
}

func (s *stack) sshFixture() *sshFixture {
	t := s.t
	t.Helper()
	pk, err := s.inv.PlatformKey(context.Background())
	require.NoError(t, err)
	fields := strings.Fields(pk.PublicKey)
	require.GreaterOrEqual(t, len(fields), 2)
	pub, _, _, _, err := ssh.ParseAuthorizedKey([]byte(pk.PublicKey))
	require.NoError(t, err)

	f := &sshFixture{laptop: newFixtureKey(t), ci: newFixtureKey(t), root: newFixtureKey(t),
		platform: fields[0] + " " + fields[1], platformFP: pk.Fingerprint}
	require.Equal(t, ssh.FingerprintSHA256(pub), f.platformFP)
	f.files = map[string]string{
		rootKeysPath: `from="10.0.0.0/8" ` + f.root.line + " root@bastion\n",
		// Alice's key also sits in deploy's file under another comment: still Alice's key (F-36).
		deployKeysPath: f.laptop.line + " deploy@laptop\n" + f.ci.line + " ci@build\n" + f.platform + " copied-by-hand\n",
		aliceKeysPath:  "no-agent-forwarding,no-port-forwarding,no-X11-forwarding " + f.platform + " alice\n",
	}
	f.emu = linuxsshtest.NewEmulator()
	f.emu.SetSSHD("authorizedkeysfile .ssh/authorized_keys\nauthorizedkeyscommand none\npubkeyauthentication yes\n" +
		"passwordauthentication no\npermitrootlogin prohibit-password\nhostkey /etc/ssh/ssh_host_ed25519_key\n")
	for p, c := range f.files {
		f.emu.SetFile(p, []byte(c))
	}
	f.server = linuxsshtest.NewServer(t, f.emu.Handler())
	f.server.Authorize(pub)
	f.host, f.port = f.server.Addr()
	return f
}

// runJobs runs due jobs until none is due and returns how many ran.
func (s *stack) runJobs() int {
	s.t.Helper()
	for n := 0; n < 20; n++ {
		ran, err := s.runner.RunOnce(context.Background())
		require.NoError(s.t, err)
		if !ran {
			return n
		}
	}
	s.t.Fatal("jobs did not settle after 20 runs")
	return 0
}

func (s *stack) job(c *client, id string) map[string]any {
	s.t.Helper()
	rec := c.do(http.MethodGet, "/api/v1/jobs/"+id, nil)
	requireStatus(s.t, rec, http.StatusOK)
	return decodeBody[map[string]any](s.t, rec)
}

func jobErrorCode(job map[string]any) string {
	e, _ := job["error"].(map[string]any)
	code, _ := e["code"].(string)
	return code
}

func (s *stack) target(c *client, id string) map[string]any {
	s.t.Helper()
	rec := c.do(http.MethodGet, "/api/v1/targets/"+id, nil)
	requireStatus(s.t, rec, http.StatusOK)
	return decodeBody[map[string]any](s.t, rec)
}

func (s *stack) auditCount(action string) int {
	s.t.Helper()
	var n int
	require.NoError(s.t, s.db.Owner.QueryRow(context.Background(), "SELECT count(*) FROM audit_log WHERE action = $1", action).Scan(&n))
	return n
}

// addServer adds the fixture as a Linux server and returns the target and job IDs.
func (s *stack) addServer(c *client, name string, f *sshFixture) (string, string) {
	s.t.Helper()
	rec := c.do(http.MethodPost, "/api/v1/targets", map[string]any{"name": name, "host": f.host, "port": f.port, "username": "alice-svc"})
	requireStatus(s.t, rec, http.StatusCreated)
	body := decodeBody[map[string]any](s.t, rec)
	return body["target"].(map[string]any)["id"].(string), body["job_id"].(string)
}

// hostKeys lists the server's host keys.
func (s *stack) hostKeys(c *client, targetID string) []map[string]any {
	s.t.Helper()
	rec := c.do(http.MethodGet, "/api/v1/targets/"+targetID+"/host-keys", nil)
	requireStatus(s.t, rec, http.StatusOK)
	return decodeBody[struct {
		Items []map[string]any `json:"items"`
	}](s.t, rec).Items
}

func withStatus(keys []map[string]any, status string) []map[string]any {
	var out []map[string]any
	for _, k := range keys {
		if k["status"] == status {
			out = append(out, k)
		}
	}
	return out
}

// pinServer runs the first test, confirms the observed fingerprint and runs the test and the
// discovery that follow.
func (s *stack) pinServer(c *client, targetID string) {
	s.t.Helper()
	s.runJobs()
	observed := withStatus(s.hostKeys(c, targetID), "observed")
	require.Len(s.t, observed, 1)
	rec := c.do(http.MethodPost, "/api/v1/targets/"+targetID+"/host-keys/"+observed[0]["id"].(string)+"/actions/confirm",
		map[string]string{"fingerprint": observed[0]["fingerprint"].(string)})
	requireStatus(s.t, rec, http.StatusAccepted)
	s.runJobs()
	require.Equal(s.t, "ok", s.target(c, targetID)["status"])
}

func (s *stack) targetLocations(c *client, targetID string, missing bool) []map[string]any {
	s.t.Helper()
	path := "/api/v1/targets/" + targetID + "/ssh-keys"
	if missing {
		path += "?missing=true"
	}
	rec := c.do(http.MethodGet, path, nil)
	requireStatus(s.t, rec, http.StatusOK)
	return decodeBody[struct {
		Items []map[string]any `json:"items"`
	}](s.t, rec).Items
}

func locationOf(t *testing.T, locs []map[string]any, osUser, fp string) map[string]any {
	t.Helper()
	for _, l := range locs {
		if l["os_user"] == osUser && l["fingerprint"] == fp {
			return l
		}
	}
	t.Fatalf("no location of %s for %s", fp, osUser)
	return nil
}

// F-30, owner steps 2–3: the fingerprint is shown, nothing is trusted or run until an
// Administrator confirms it; then the inventory matches the server's files exactly.
func TestAddServerJourney(t *testing.T) {
	s, admin, _ := installed(t)
	f := s.sshFixture()
	targetID, jobID := s.addServer(admin, "web-01", f)

	assert.Equal(t, 1, s.runJobs())
	job := s.job(admin, jobID)
	assert.Equal(t, "failed", job["status"])
	assert.Equal(t, "ALC-TGT-0002", jobErrorCode(job))
	assert.Equal(t, "pending_host_key", s.target(admin, targetID)["status"])
	assert.Zero(t, f.server.AuthAttempts(), "no authentication before the fingerprint is confirmed")
	assert.Empty(t, f.server.Commands(), "no command before the fingerprint is confirmed")

	keys := s.hostKeys(admin, targetID)
	require.Len(t, keys, 1)
	assert.Equal(t, "observed", keys[0]["status"])
	assert.Equal(t, ssh.FingerprintSHA256(f.server.HostKey()), keys[0]["fingerprint"])
	assert.Equal(t, "ssh-keygen -lf /etc/ssh/ssh_host_ed25519_key.pub", keys[0]["verify_command"])

	confirm := "/api/v1/targets/" + targetID + "/host-keys/" + keys[0]["id"].(string) + "/actions/confirm"
	requireError(t, admin.do(http.MethodPost, confirm, map[string]string{"fingerprint": "SHA256:" + strings.Repeat("A", 43)}),
		http.StatusConflict, "ALC-TGT-0003")
	assert.Empty(t, withStatus(s.hostKeys(admin, targetID), "pinned"))
	assert.Zero(t, s.auditCount("hostkey.pinned"))

	requireStatus(t, admin.do(http.MethodPost, confirm, map[string]string{"fingerprint": keys[0]["fingerprint"].(string)}), http.StatusAccepted)
	var who string
	require.NoError(t, s.db.Owner.QueryRow(context.Background(), "SELECT actor_name FROM audit_log WHERE action = 'hostkey.pinned'").Scan(&who))
	assert.Equal(t, "ada", who, "F-30: the pin is audited with the confirming user")

	assert.Equal(t, 2, s.runJobs(), "a connection test, then the discovery it starts")
	tg := s.target(admin, targetID)
	assert.Equal(t, "ok", tg["status"])
	assert.Equal(t, float64(1), tg["facts"].(map[string]any)["helper_protocol"])
	assert.Positive(t, f.server.AuthAttempts())

	got := map[string]bool{}
	for _, l := range s.targetLocations(admin, targetID, false) {
		got[fmt.Sprintf("%s|%s|%s|%v", l["os_user"], l["file_path"], l["fingerprint"], l["is_alice_connection_key"])] = true
	}
	assert.Equal(t, map[string]bool{
		"root|" + rootKeysPath + "|" + f.root.fp + "|false":                true,
		"deploy|" + deployKeysPath + "|" + f.laptop.fp + "|false":          true,
		"deploy|" + deployKeysPath + "|" + f.ci.fp + "|false":              true,
		"deploy|" + deployKeysPath + "|" + f.platformFP + "|true":          true,
		"alice-svc|" + aliceKeysPath + "|" + f.platformFP + "|true":        true,
	}, got, "the inventory matches the seeded files exactly (§26.5 exit criterion)")

	rec := admin.do(http.MethodGet, "/api/v1/ssh-keys?target_id="+targetID, nil)
	requireStatus(t, rec, http.StatusOK)
	page := decodeBody[struct {
		Items []map[string]any `json:"items"`
	}](t, rec)
	assert.Len(t, page.Items, 4, "one row per distinct key")
	for _, k := range page.Items {
		assert.Equal(t, k["fingerprint"] == f.platformFP, k["is_platform_key"], k["fingerprint"])
	}
}

// F-36, owner step 4: Alice's own key is refused in every file and under any comment; nothing is
// written and no job is queued.
func TestOwnKeyRemovalIsRefused(t *testing.T) {
	s, admin, _ := installed(t)
	f := s.sshFixture()
	targetID, _ := s.addServer(admin, "web-01", f)
	s.pinServer(admin, targetID)
	locs := s.targetLocations(admin, targetID, false)

	for _, user := range []string{"alice-svc", "deploy"} {
		loc := locationOf(t, locs, user, f.platformFP)
		rec := admin.do(http.MethodPost, "/api/v1/ssh-keys/locations/"+loc["id"].(string)+"/actions/remove", nil)
		requireError(t, rec, http.StatusConflict, "ALC-KEY-0001")
		assert.Contains(t, decodeBody[apiError](t, rec).Error.Message, "Alice needs this key to connect to this server and will not remove it.")
	}
	assert.Equal(t, 2, s.auditCount("sshkey.remove.denied"))
	assert.Empty(t, f.emu.Writes())
	var queued int
	require.NoError(t, s.db.Owner.QueryRow(context.Background(), "SELECT count(*) FROM jobs WHERE type = 'sshkey.remove'").Scan(&queued))
	assert.Zero(t, queued)
	for p, c := range f.files {
		got, ok := f.emu.File(p)
		require.True(t, ok)
		assert.Equal(t, c, string(got), p)
	}
}

// An Operator removes another key (§15.4): only that line goes, every other byte stays.
func TestRemoveKeyJourney(t *testing.T) {
	s, admin, adminAcct := installed(t)
	f := s.sshFixture()
	targetID, _ := s.addServer(admin, "web-01", f)
	s.pinServer(admin, targetID)
	operator := s.createUser(admin, adminAcct, "otto", "operator", "operator-password-2026")
	oc := s.freshClient()
	s.firstSignIn(oc, operator)

	loc := locationOf(t, s.targetLocations(oc, targetID, false), "deploy", f.laptop.fp)
	rec := oc.do(http.MethodPost, "/api/v1/ssh-keys/locations/"+loc["id"].(string)+"/actions/remove", nil)
	requireStatus(t, rec, http.StatusAccepted)
	jobID := decodeBody[map[string]string](t, rec)["job_id"]
	assert.Equal(t, 1, s.runJobs())
	assert.Equal(t, "succeeded", s.job(oc, jobID)["status"])

	deploy, _ := f.emu.File(deployKeysPath)
	assert.Equal(t, f.ci.line+" ci@build\n"+f.platform+" copied-by-hand\n", string(deploy), "only the removed line is gone")
	for _, p := range []string{rootKeysPath, aliceKeysPath} {
		got, _ := f.emu.File(p)
		assert.Equal(t, f.files[p], string(got), p)
	}
	assert.Equal(t, []string{deployKeysPath}, f.emu.Writes())
	assert.Equal(t, 1, s.auditCount("sshkey.removed"))
	removed := locationOf(t, s.targetLocations(oc, targetID, true), "deploy", f.laptop.fp)
	assert.NotNil(t, removed["removed_at"])
}

// F-31..F-33, owner step 5, Review Focus 5: a changed host key stops everything before
// authentication, emails the administrators once, and only an Administrator with step-up and a
// reason can accept it; the old fingerprint stays in the history.
func TestChangedHostKeyJourney(t *testing.T) {
	s, admin, adminAcct := installed(t)
	s.stepUp(admin, adminAcct)
	requireStatus(t, admin.do(http.MethodPatch, "/api/v1/users/"+adminAcct.id, map[string]string{"email": "ada@example.com"}), http.StatusOK)
	f := s.sshFixture()
	targetID, _ := s.addServer(admin, "web-01", f)
	s.pinServer(admin, targetID)
	oldFP := ssh.FingerprintSHA256(f.server.HostKey())
	laptop := locationOf(t, s.targetLocations(admin, targetID, false), "deploy", f.laptop.fp)

	attempts, commands := f.server.AuthAttempts(), len(f.server.Commands())
	f.server.SetHostKey(linuxsshtest.NewHostKey(t))
	outbox := func() int {
		var n int
		require.NoError(t, s.db.Owner.QueryRow(context.Background(),
			"SELECT count(*) FROM notifications_outbox WHERE template_key = 'target.host_key_changed'").Scan(&n))
		return n
	}

	for i := 0; i < 2; i++ { // the second test must neither dial nor email again
		requireStatus(t, admin.do(http.MethodPost, "/api/v1/targets/"+targetID+"/actions/test", nil), http.StatusAccepted)
		assert.Equal(t, 1, s.runJobs())
	}
	assert.Equal(t, "host_key_changed", s.target(admin, targetID)["status"])
	assert.Equal(t, attempts, f.server.AuthAttempts(), "F-31: no authentication reaches the server")
	assert.Equal(t, commands, len(f.server.Commands()))
	assert.Equal(t, 1, outbox(), "one email for the one administrator with an address")
	assert.Equal(t, 1, s.auditCount("hostkey.changed"))

	requireError(t, admin.do(http.MethodPost, "/api/v1/targets/"+targetID+"/actions/discover", nil), http.StatusConflict, "ALC-TGT-0004")
	requireError(t, admin.do(http.MethodPost, "/api/v1/ssh-keys/locations/"+laptop["id"].(string)+"/actions/remove", nil),
		http.StatusConflict, "ALC-TGT-0004")

	s.clock.Advance(25 * time.Hour) // nightly discovery is due, but the server is blocked
	n, err := s.inv.ScheduleDiscovery(context.Background())
	require.NoError(t, err)
	assert.Zero(t, n)
	assert.Zero(t, s.runJobs())
	assert.Equal(t, commands, len(f.server.Commands()))

	s.signIn(admin, adminAcct) // the old session reached its 12-hour limit
	operator := s.createUser(admin, adminAcct, "otto", "operator", "operator-password-2026")
	oc := s.freshClient()
	s.firstSignIn(oc, operator)
	observed := withStatus(s.hostKeys(admin, targetID), "observed")
	require.Len(t, observed, 1)
	newFP := observed[0]["fingerprint"].(string)
	assert.NotEqual(t, oldFP, newFP)
	repin := "/api/v1/targets/" + targetID + "/host-keys/" + observed[0]["id"].(string) + "/actions/repin"
	body := map[string]string{"fingerprint": newFP, "reason": "Server reinstalled by the platform team (ticket 4711)"}

	denied := s.auditCount("authz.denied")
	requireError(t, oc.do(http.MethodPost, repin, body), http.StatusForbidden, "ALC-AUTH-0002") // F-33
	assert.Equal(t, denied+1, s.auditCount("authz.denied"))

	s.clock.Advance(6 * time.Minute) // the step-up window of the sign-in has closed
	requireError(t, admin.do(http.MethodPost, repin, body), http.StatusForbidden, "ALC-AUTH-0003")
	s.stepUp(admin, adminAcct)
	requireError(t, admin.do(http.MethodPost, repin, map[string]string{"fingerprint": newFP, "reason": "short"}),
		http.StatusUnprocessableEntity, "ALC-SYS-0006")
	requireStatus(t, admin.do(http.MethodPost, repin, body), http.StatusAccepted)
	assert.Equal(t, 1, s.auditCount("hostkey.repinned"))

	history := s.hostKeys(admin, targetID)
	require.Len(t, withStatus(history, "pinned"), 1)
	assert.Equal(t, newFP, withStatus(history, "pinned")[0]["fingerprint"])
	require.Len(t, withStatus(history, "superseded"), 1)
	assert.Equal(t, oldFP, withStatus(history, "superseded")[0]["fingerprint"], "F-32: the old fingerprint stays in the history")

	assert.GreaterOrEqual(t, s.runJobs(), 1)
	assert.Equal(t, "ok", s.target(admin, targetID)["status"])
	assert.Greater(t, f.server.AuthAttempts(), attempts, "operations resume after the re-pin")
}

// L-26, L-29: in lock every infrastructure change is refused and audited, reads work, queued
// read-only work is not claimed, and no command reaches the server.
func TestLockRefusesInfrastructureChanges(t *testing.T) {
	s, admin, adminAcct := installed(t)
	f := s.sshFixture()
	targetID, _ := s.addServer(admin, "web-01", f)
	s.pinServer(admin, targetID)
	laptop := locationOf(t, s.targetLocations(admin, targetID, false), "deploy", f.laptop.fp)
	rec := admin.do(http.MethodPost, "/api/v1/targets/"+targetID+"/actions/discover", nil)
	requireStatus(t, rec, http.StatusAccepted)
	queuedDiscovery := decodeBody[map[string]string](t, rec)["job_id"]

	counts := func() map[string]int {
		out := map[string]int{}
		for _, table := range []string{"targets", "host_keys", "ssh_keys", "ssh_key_locations", "credentials"} {
			out[table] = s.count(table)
		}
		return out
	}
	before, commands := counts(), len(f.server.Commands())

	s.clock.Advance(31 * 24 * time.Hour) // the evaluation ends (R1)
	require.NoError(t, s.license.Tick(t.Context()))
	require.True(t, s.license.Snapshot().Eval.Locked())
	s.signIn(admin, adminAcct)

	denied := s.auditCount("request.denied_license")
	for _, rq := range []struct {
		path string
		body any
	}{
		{"/api/v1/targets", map[string]any{"name": "web-02", "host": "web-02.example.test"}},
		{"/api/v1/targets/" + targetID + "/actions/test", nil},
		{"/api/v1/targets/" + targetID + "/actions/discover", nil},
		{"/api/v1/ssh-keys/locations/" + laptop["id"].(string) + "/actions/remove", nil},
	} {
		requireError(t, admin.do(http.MethodPost, rq.path, rq.body), http.StatusForbidden, "ALC-LIC-0001")
	}
	assert.Equal(t, denied+4, s.auditCount("request.denied_license"))
	for _, path := range []string{"/api/v1/targets", "/api/v1/targets/" + targetID, "/api/v1/targets/" + targetID + "/ssh-keys",
		"/api/v1/targets/" + targetID + "/host-keys", "/api/v1/ssh-keys", "/api/v1/jobs"} {
		requireStatus(t, admin.do(http.MethodGet, path, nil), http.StatusOK)
	}

	s.runJobs()
	assert.Equal(t, "cancelled", s.job(admin, queuedDiscovery)["status"], "§8.6: queued read-only work is cancelled in lock")
	assert.Equal(t, commands, len(f.server.Commands()), "L-29: no remote command in lock")
	assert.Equal(t, before, counts(), "L-29: nothing deleted or added")
}

// L-81, R29: a removal queued before the lock is not run; after the renewal it waits for an
// Administrator's confirmation, then runs.
func TestBlockedRemovalNeedsConfirmation(t *testing.T) {
	s, admin, adminAcct := installed(t)
	f := s.sshFixture()
	targetID, _ := s.addServer(admin, "web-01", f)
	s.pinServer(admin, targetID)
	laptop := locationOf(t, s.targetLocations(admin, targetID, false), "deploy", f.laptop.fp)
	rec := admin.do(http.MethodPost, "/api/v1/ssh-keys/locations/"+laptop["id"].(string)+"/actions/remove", nil)
	requireStatus(t, rec, http.StatusAccepted)
	jobID := decodeBody[map[string]string](t, rec)["job_id"]

	s.clock.Advance(31 * 24 * time.Hour)
	require.NoError(t, s.license.Tick(t.Context()))
	s.signIn(admin, adminAcct)
	s.runJobs()
	assert.Equal(t, "blocked_license", s.job(admin, jobID)["status"])
	assert.GreaterOrEqual(t, s.auditCount("job.blocked_license"), 1)
	assert.Empty(t, f.emu.Writes())

	rec = admin.do(http.MethodGet, "/api/v1/jobs?status=blocked_license", nil)
	requireStatus(t, rec, http.StatusOK)
	var listed []string
	for _, j := range decodeBody[struct {
		Items []map[string]any `json:"items"`
	}](t, rec).Items {
		listed = append(listed, j["id"].(string))
	}
	assert.Equal(t, []string{jobID}, listed)

	now := s.clock.Now()
	s.stepUp(admin, adminAcct)
	requireStatus(t, admin.do(http.MethodPost, "/api/v1/license", map[string]string{"license": s.signedLicense("LIC-R", now, now.AddDate(1, 0, 0), 10)}),
		http.StatusOK)
	assert.Zero(t, s.runJobs(), "after the renewal the paused change does not start by itself")
	assert.Equal(t, "blocked_license", s.job(admin, jobID)["status"])

	operator := s.createUser(admin, adminAcct, "otto", "operator", "operator-password-2026")
	oc := s.freshClient()
	s.firstSignIn(oc, operator)
	requireError(t, oc.do(http.MethodPost, "/api/v1/jobs/"+jobID+"/actions/confirm", nil), http.StatusForbidden, "ALC-AUTH-0002")

	rec = admin.do(http.MethodPost, "/api/v1/jobs/"+jobID+"/actions/confirm", nil)
	requireStatus(t, rec, http.StatusOK)
	assert.Equal(t, "queued", decodeBody[map[string]any](t, rec)["status"])
	assert.Equal(t, 1, s.auditCount("job.confirmed"))
	requireError(t, admin.do(http.MethodPost, "/api/v1/jobs/"+jobID+"/actions/confirm", nil), http.StatusConflict, "ALC-JOB-0001")

	assert.Equal(t, 1, s.runJobs())
	assert.Equal(t, "succeeded", s.job(admin, jobID)["status"])
	deploy, _ := f.emu.File(deployKeysPath)
	assert.NotContains(t, string(deploy), f.laptop.line)
}

// L-04, carry 5: the evaluation allows five servers; the sixth is refused and audited, and the
// administrator sees the "all licensed targets in use" banner.
func TestEvaluationLimitViaAPI(t *testing.T) {
	s, admin, _ := installed(t)
	for i := 1; i <= 5; i++ {
		rec := admin.do(http.MethodPost, "/api/v1/targets", map[string]any{"name": fmt.Sprintf("web-%d", i), "host": fmt.Sprintf("web-%d.example.test", i)})
		requireStatus(t, rec, http.StatusCreated)
	}
	rec := admin.do(http.MethodPost, "/api/v1/targets", map[string]any{"name": "web-6", "host": "web-6.example.test"})
	requireError(t, rec, http.StatusConflict, "ALC-LIC-0008")
	assert.Equal(t, map[string]string{"used": "5", "max": "5"}, decodeBody[paramsBody](t, rec).Error.Params)
	assert.Equal(t, 5, s.count("targets"))
	assert.Equal(t, 1, s.auditCount("target.add.denied_license"))

	st := decodeBody[map[string]any](t, admin.do(http.MethodGet, "/api/v1/license/status", nil))
	var kinds []string
	for _, b := range st["banners"].([]any) {
		kinds = append(kinds, b.(map[string]any)["kind"].(string))
	}
	assert.Contains(t, kinds, "limit_reached", "the snapshot counts targets right after the commit")
}
```

```go
// startInventory builds the Phase 3 services the way cmd/alice does: the job queue, the inventory
// with the platform key, the linuxssh provider over a real dialer (pinned against the inventory's
// host-key store) and a job runner with the target handlers. Tests drive the runner with RunOnce.
// The dialer uses the real clock: it only measures network timeouts.
func (s *stack) startInventory(keyring *secrets.Keyring, auditLog *audit.Log) {
	t := s.t
	t.Helper()
	log := logging.New(s.logs, slog.LevelDebug)
	s.queue = jobs.NewQueue(jobs.QueueConfig{Pool: s.db.App, Keyring: keyring, Audit: auditLog, Clock: s.clock, Gate: s.license})
	s.registry = providers.NewRegistry()
	s.inv = inventory.New(inventory.Config{
		Pool: s.db.App, Keyring: keyring, Audit: auditLog, Clock: s.clock, License: s.license, Registry: s.registry,
		Jobs: s.queue, Notifier: notify.AdminNotifier{Clock: s.clock}, Log: log,
	})
	pool := linuxssh.NewPool(&linuxssh.Dialer{Clock: clock.Real{}, HostKeys: s.inv.HostKeyStore()},
		linuxssh.MaxConnections, linuxssh.MaxConnectionsPerTarget, linuxssh.IdleTimeout)
	t.Cleanup(pool.Close)
	s.registry.Register(linuxssh.New(linuxssh.Options{Pool: pool}))
	s.registry.Freeze()
	_, err := s.inv.EnsurePlatformKey(context.Background())
	require.NoError(t, err)
	s.runner = jobs.NewRunner(jobs.RunnerConfig{
		Pool: s.db.App, Queue: s.queue, Gate: s.license, Audit: auditLog, Clock: s.clock, Log: log,
		Jitter: func() float64 { return 0 },
	})
	targetjobs.Register(s.runner, targetjobs.Deps{Inventory: s.inv, Registry: s.registry, Clock: s.clock, Log: log})
}
```

```go
//go:build integration

package api

import (
	"bytes"
	"context"
	"crypto/ed25519"
	"encoding/base64"
	"encoding/pem"
	"fmt"
	"net/http"
	"strings"
	"testing"

	"github.com/google/uuid"
	"github.com/stretchr/testify/assert"
	"github.com/stretchr/testify/require"
	"golang.org/x/crypto/ssh"

	"alice/internal/providers/linuxssh/linuxsshtest"
	"alice/internal/secrets"
)

// platformSeed decrypts the stored platform key (test-only, with the stack's keyring) and checks
// it is the key Alice presents.
func (s *stack) platformSeed() ([]byte, []byte) {
	s.t.Helper()
	ctx := context.Background()
	var id uuid.UUID
	var env secrets.Envelope
	require.NoError(s.t, s.db.Owner.QueryRow(ctx,
		`SELECT id, ciphertext, nonce, wrapped_dek, key_version FROM credentials WHERE purpose = 'platform_ssh'`).
		Scan(&id, &env.Ciphertext, &env.Nonce, &env.WrappedDEK, &env.KeyVersion))
	pt, err := s.keyring.Open(secrets.Location{Table: "credentials", RowID: id.String(), Column: "ciphertext"}, env)
	require.NoError(s.t, err)
	seed := append([]byte(nil), pt.Bytes()...)
	pt.Zero()
	require.Len(s.t, seed, ed25519.SeedSize)
	pub, err := ssh.NewPublicKey(ed25519.NewKeyFromSeed(seed).Public())
	require.NoError(s.t, err)
	pk, err := s.inv.PlatformKey(ctx)
	require.NoError(s.t, err)
	require.Equal(s.t, pk.Fingerprint, ssh.FingerprintSHA256(pub), "the decrypted seed is Alice's platform key")
	return seed, env.Ciphertext
}

// §25.2 with SSH keys (S-01..S-04): Alice's private key, in every spelling, never appears in logs,
// responses or any table other than as its envelope; hostile helper output is not echoed.
func TestPlatformKeyNeverLeaks(t *testing.T) {
	s, admin, adminAcct := installed(t)
	f := s.sshFixture()
	hostile := canary("hostile-helper")

	targetID, _ := s.addServer(admin, "web-01", f)
	s.runJobs()
	observed := withStatus(s.hostKeys(admin, targetID), "observed")
	require.Len(t, observed, 1)
	confirm := "/api/v1/targets/" + targetID + "/host-keys/" + observed[0]["id"].(string) + "/actions/confirm"
	requireError(t, admin.do(http.MethodPost, confirm, map[string]string{"fingerprint": "SHA256:" + strings.Repeat("B", 43)}), http.StatusConflict, "ALC-TGT-0003")
	requireStatus(t, admin.do(http.MethodPost, confirm, map[string]string{"fingerprint": observed[0]["fingerprint"].(string)}), http.StatusAccepted)
	s.runJobs()

	// A hostile or broken helper (SC-4): a refusal whose message and stderr carry a PEM marker and a canary.
	normal := f.emu.Handler()
	f.server.SetHandler(func(cmd string, stdin []byte) linuxsshtest.Response {
		if strings.Contains(cmd, " authkeys-list") {
			return linuxsshtest.Response{
				Exit:   4,
				Stdout: []byte(`{"ok":false,"code":"IO_ERROR","message":"` + hostile + ` -----BEGIN OPENSSH PRIVATE KEY-----"}`),
				Stderr: []byte("-----BEGIN OPENSSH PRIVATE KEY-----\n" + hostile + "\n-----END OPENSSH PRIVATE KEY-----\n"),
			}
		}
		return normal(cmd, stdin)
	})
	rec := admin.do(http.MethodPost, "/api/v1/targets/"+targetID+"/actions/discover", nil)
	requireStatus(t, rec, http.StatusAccepted)
	failedJob := decodeBody[map[string]string](t, rec)["job_id"]
	s.runJobs()
	assert.NotEqual(t, "succeeded", s.job(admin, failedJob)["status"])
	f.server.SetHandler(normal)
	requireStatus(t, admin.do(http.MethodPost, "/api/v1/targets/"+targetID+"/actions/discover", nil), http.StatusAccepted)
	s.runJobs()

	// Own-key refusal and a real removal.
	locs := s.targetLocations(admin, targetID, false)
	own := locationOf(t, locs, "alice-svc", f.platformFP)
	requireError(t, admin.do(http.MethodPost, "/api/v1/ssh-keys/locations/"+own["id"].(string)+"/actions/remove", nil), http.StatusConflict, "ALC-KEY-0001")
	laptop := locationOf(t, locs, "deploy", f.laptop.fp)
	requireStatus(t, admin.do(http.MethodPost, "/api/v1/ssh-keys/locations/"+laptop["id"].(string)+"/actions/remove", nil), http.StatusAccepted)
	s.runJobs()

	// Every read that returns Phase 3 data, so its response is scanned too.
	s.stepUp(admin, adminAcct)
	rec = admin.do(http.MethodGet, "/api/v1/ssh-keys/platform-key", nil)
	requireStatus(t, rec, http.StatusOK)
	pk, err := s.inv.PlatformKey(context.Background())
	require.NoError(t, err)
	require.Contains(t, rec.Body.String(), strings.Fields(pk.PublicKey)[1], "the scan sees the real platform-key response")
	for _, path := range []string{"/api/v1/targets", "/api/v1/targets/" + targetID, "/api/v1/targets/" + targetID + "/host-keys",
		"/api/v1/targets/" + targetID + "/ssh-keys?missing=true", "/api/v1/ssh-keys", "/api/v1/ssh-keys/" + laptop["ssh_key_id"].(string),
		"/api/v1/jobs", "/api/v1/jobs/" + failedJob, "/api/v1/providers", "/api/v1/audit", "/api/v1/audit/export?format=json"} {
		requireStatus(t, admin.do(http.MethodGet, path, nil), http.StatusOK)
	}

	seed, ciphertext := s.platformSeed()
	priv := ed25519.NewKeyFromSeed(seed)
	block, err := ssh.MarshalPrivateKey(priv, "")
	require.NoError(t, err)
	pemText := string(pem.EncodeToMemory(block))
	secs := []secretValue{
		{name: "platform key seed", forms: binaryForms(seed)},
		{name: "platform private key", forms: binaryForms(priv)},
		{name: "platform key (OpenSSH PEM)", forms: []string{pemText, base64.StdEncoding.EncodeToString(block.Bytes)}},
		{name: "hostile helper output", value: hostile},
	}

	logs := s.logs.String()
	assertNoSecret(t, "logs", logs, secs)
	for _, m := range privateKeyMarkers {
		assert.NotContains(t, logs, m, "logs")
	}
	for _, ex := range s.recorded() {
		text := string(ex.body) + fmt.Sprint(ex.header)
		assertNoSecret(t, "response "+ex.key(), text, secs)
		for _, m := range privateKeyMarkers {
			assert.NotContains(t, text, m, "response %s", ex.key())
		}
	}
	dump := s.dump()
	assertNoSecret(t, "database", dump, secs)
	for _, m := range privateKeyMarkers {
		assert.NotContains(t, dump, m, "database")
	}

	// S-04: the stored key is ciphertext with its own DEK; another installation's differs.
	assert.False(t, bytes.Contains(ciphertext, seed), "the seed is not stored in clear")
	other := newStack(t)
	otherSeed, otherCiphertext := other.platformSeed()
	assert.NotEqual(t, seed, otherSeed, "every installation generates its own key")
	assert.NotEqual(t, ciphertext, otherCiphertext)
}
```

§6.4 "registration happens explicitly in `cmd/alice/providers.go`", §8.3, §8.8 "graceful shutdown", R37 items 1, 7,
15, 17). After this task `make up` runs a server that creates its platform key at start, recovers expired job leases,
runs the job workers, schedules discovery, the daily audit verification and the hourly cleanup on one process only
(leader lock), and stops in the order HTTP → scheduler → workers → SSH pool → leader → license time record. The e2e
build gains `/test/license/tamper` (Phase 2 carry 5) and `/test/jobs/drain`, and the e2e compose overlay starts the
SSH test target `sshtarget` that Task 22 prepares with the real setup script.

**Construction order (the registry cycle).** `inventory.Service` needs the provider registry (setup snippets,
`ValidateConfig`, capabilities), and the `linuxssh` dialer needs `inventory.Service.HostKeyStore()`. The registry is a
pointer, so `buildServices` creates an empty `providers.NewRegistry()`, hands it to `inventory.New`, then builds the
dialer with `inv.HostKeyStore()`, the pool, and finally registers the provider and freezes the registry
(`registerProviders`). Nothing reads the registry before `buildServices` returns, so no indirection type is needed.

**Assumptions on neighbouring tasks (contract signatures plus):** `auth.Service.PruneExpired(ctx) (int64, error)`
(Task 12); `providertest.CheckProvider(t testing.TB, p providers.Provider)` (Task 4); `jobs.QueueConfig` has the
contract fields plus `Gate` (Task 11; `lic` is passed) and `Keyring` typed as `jobs.Deriver` (satisfied by `*secrets.Keyring`); the setup script of Task 9 creates
`/usr/local/libexec` itself (`install -D` or `mkdir -p`), because Ubuntu 22.04 does not ship that directory.

```go
package main

import (
	"alice/internal/providers"
	"alice/internal/providers/linuxssh"
)

// registerProviders registers every provider this build ships and freezes the registry
// (spec §6.4: explicit registration in one file, no init() magic). It is the only place that
// imports a provider implementation; nginx (Phase 4) and azurekv (Phase 5) are added here.
func registerProviders(reg *providers.Registry, sshPool *linuxssh.Pool) {
	reg.Register(linuxssh.New(linuxssh.Options{Pool: sshPool}))
	reg.Freeze()
}
```

```go
// At shutdown serve waits for running jobs only until the job budget ends (spec §8.8: up to
// 60 s; the runner then releases the leases of unfinished jobs itself).
func TestWaitForJobsIsBounded(t *testing.T) {
	var logs bytes.Buffer
	log := slog.New(slog.NewTextHandler(&logs, nil))

	done := make(chan struct{})
	close(done)
	assert.True(t, waitForJobs(done, time.Second, log))
	assert.Empty(t, logs.String())

	start := time.Now()
	assert.False(t, waitForJobs(make(chan struct{}), 20*time.Millisecond, log), "workers that never stop do not block shutdown")
	assert.Less(t, time.Since(start), 5*time.Second)
	assert.Contains(t, logs.String(), "level=WARN")
	assert.Contains(t, logs.String(), "background jobs did not stop")
}
```

```go
// jobRetention is how long finished jobs are kept before maintenance.cleanup prunes them (§8.2).
const jobRetention = 90 * 24 * time.Hour

// buildRunner builds the job workers with every Phase 3 handler (spec §8.1–§8.8). Every claim
// passes the license gate.
func buildRunner(pool *pgxpool.Pool, svc *services, clk clock.Clock, log *slog.Logger) *jobs.Runner {
	runner := jobs.NewRunner(jobs.RunnerConfig{Pool: pool, Queue: svc.queue, Gate: svc.license, Audit: svc.auditLog, Clock: clk, Log: log})
	targetjobs.Register(runner, targetjobs.Deps{Inventory: svc.inventory, Registry: svc.registry, Clock: clk, Log: log})
	return runner
}

// buildScheduler is the periodic work of serve (spec §8.2, R37 item 15); every run passes the
// license gate. The e2e tests use the same tasks.
func buildScheduler(svc *services, sender *notify.Sender, clk clock.Clock, log *slog.Logger) *jobs.Scheduler {
	return jobs.NewScheduler(clk, svc.license, log,
		jobs.Task{Type: jobs.LicenseEvaluate, Every: time.Hour, Run: svc.license.Tick},
		jobs.Task{Type: jobs.NotifySend, Every: time.Minute, Run: func(ctx context.Context) error {
			_, err := sender.Drain(ctx)
			return err
		}},
		jobs.Task{Type: jobs.AuditVerify, Every: 24 * time.Hour, Run: func(ctx context.Context) error {
			_, err := svc.audit.Verify(ctx, audit.SystemActor("scheduler"))
			return err
		}},
		jobs.Task{Type: jobs.MaintenanceCleanup, Every: time.Hour, Run: func(ctx context.Context) error {
			_, sessionsErr := svc.auth.PruneExpired(ctx)
			_, jobsErr := svc.queue.Prune(ctx, jobRetention)
			return errors.Join(sessionsErr, jobsErr)
		}},
		jobs.Task{Type: jobs.DiscoverySchedule, Every: time.Minute, Run: func(ctx context.Context) error {
			_, err := svc.inventory.ScheduleDiscovery(ctx)
			return err
		}},
	)
}
```

```go
// jobsShutdownBudget bounds the wait for the job workers at shutdown: the runner itself lets
// running jobs finish for up to 60 s (§8.8) and then releases their leases.
const jobsShutdownBudget = 75 * time.Second

// waitForJobs waits for the job runner to return, at most limit. It reports whether it did.
func waitForJobs(done <-chan struct{}, limit time.Duration, log *slog.Logger) bool {
	timer := time.NewTimer(limit)
	defer timer.Stop()
	select {
	case <-done:
		return true
	case <-timer.C:
		log.Warn("background jobs did not stop within the shutdown time; their leases expire and they resume after the restart")
		return false
	}
}
```

(`time.NewTimer` is allowed here: shutdown budgets are real wall time, not license time; `forbidigo` only bans
`time.Now`.)

```go
	assert.Zero(t, countRows(t, d, "SELECT count(*) FROM jobs WHERE finished_at < '2001-01-01'"))
	assert.Error(t, sched.RunNow(ctx, "unknown.task"), "only the listed tasks exist")
}
```

```go
// maxDrain bounds one POST /test/jobs/drain (a handler that enqueues follow-up jobs, such as a
// connection test that enqueues discovery, must not loop forever).
const maxDrain = 50

var (
	errNoLicenseFile = errors.New("no stored license file")
	customerField    = regexp.MustCompile(`"customer"\s*:\s*"`)
)

// damageLicenseFile prefixes the signed customer name with "tampered-": the file still parses,
// but its signature no longer matches (spec L-49).
func damageLicenseFile(raw []byte) ([]byte, error) {
	loc := customerField.FindIndex(raw)
	if loc == nil {
		return nil, errors.New("the license file has no customer field")
	}
	out := append([]byte{}, raw[:loc[1]]...)
	out = append(out, "tampered-"...)
	return append(out, raw[loc[1]:]...), nil
}

// tamperNewestLicenseFile damages the newest stored license file as the owner role (the
// application role cannot update license_files) and returns its sequence number.
func tamperNewestLicenseFile(ctx context.Context, ownerURL string) (int64, error) {
	pool, err := pgxpool.New(ctx, ownerURL)
	if err != nil {
		return 0, err
	}
	defer pool.Close()
	var seq int64
	err = db.InTx(ctx, pool, func(tx pgx.Tx) error {
		var raw []byte
		err := tx.QueryRow(ctx, "SELECT seq, raw_file FROM license_files ORDER BY seq DESC LIMIT 1 FOR UPDATE").Scan(&seq, &raw)
		if errors.Is(err, pgx.ErrNoRows) {
			return errNoLicenseFile
		}
		if err != nil {
			return err
		}
		damaged, err := damageLicenseFile(raw)
		if err != nil {
			return err
		}
		_, err = tx.Exec(ctx, "UPDATE license_files SET raw_file = $1 WHERE seq = $2", damaged, seq)
		return err
	})
	return seq, err
}
```

```yaml
  # Test-only SSH target for the Phase 3 journeys (web/e2e/phase3.spec.ts): Ubuntu 22.04 with
  # OpenSSH, sudo, fixture users and keys generated at image build time, and alice-helper built
  # from this repository in /opt/alice-bundle. Playwright prepares it with the setup script Alice
  # shows (alice-e2e-prepare) and rotates its host key (alice-e2e-rotate-hostkey) through
  # "docker compose exec". Alice reaches it as sshtarget:22 on the internal backend network.
  sshtarget:
    image: alice-e2e-sshtarget
    build:
      context: ..
      dockerfile: test/images/e2e-target/Dockerfile
    init: true
    networks: [backend]
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD", "pgrep", "-x", "sshd"]
      interval: 5s
      timeout: 3s
      retries: 10
```

Create `test/images/e2e-target/Dockerfile`:

```dockerfile
# syntax=docker/dockerfile:1
# Test-only SSH target for the Playwright suite (deploy/docker-compose.e2e.yml). Never part of a
# release. Keys are generated at build time and their private halves deleted at once, so nothing
# secret is committed (gitleaks) and every build has fresh fixture keys.

FROM golang:1.27.1-alpine AS helper
WORKDIR /src
COPY go.mod go.sum ./
COPY cmd/alice-helper/ cmd/alice-helper/
COPY internal/providers/linuxssh/helperproto/ internal/providers/linuxssh/helperproto/
COPY internal/providers/linuxssh/sshdconf/ internal/providers/linuxssh/sshdconf/
RUN CGO_ENABLED=0 go build -trimpath -ldflags "-s -w" -o /out/alice-helper ./cmd/alice-helper

FROM ubuntu:22.04
RUN apt-get update \
 && DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends openssh-server sudo procps \
 && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/* \
 && mkdir -p /run/sshd /opt/alice-bundle \
 && ssh-keygen -A \
 && sed -i 's/^session\s\+required\s\+pam_loginuid.so/session optional pam_loginuid.so/' /etc/pam.d/sshd
RUN set -eu; \
    useradd --uid 1001 --create-home --shell /bin/bash deploy; \
    install -d -m 0700 -o deploy -g deploy /home/deploy/.ssh; \
    install -d -m 0700 /root/.ssh; \
    tmp="$(mktemp -d)"; \
    ssh-keygen -q -t ed25519 -N '' -C deploy@laptop -f "$tmp/k1"; \
    ssh-keygen -q -t rsa -b 3072 -N '' -C ci@build -f "$tmp/k2"; \
    ssh-keygen -q -t ed25519 -N '' -C root@bastion -f "$tmp/k3"; \
    cat "$tmp/k1.pub" "$tmp/k2.pub" > /home/deploy/.ssh/authorized_keys; \
    printf 'from="10.0.0.0/8" %s\n' "$(cat "$tmp/k3.pub")" > /root/.ssh/authorized_keys; \
    chown deploy:deploy /home/deploy/.ssh/authorized_keys; \
    chmod 0600 /home/deploy/.ssh/authorized_keys /root/.ssh/authorized_keys; \
    rm -rf "$tmp"
COPY --from=helper /out/alice-helper /opt/alice-bundle/alice-helper
COPY test/images/e2e-target/alice-e2e-prepare test/images/e2e-target/alice-e2e-rotate-hostkey /usr/local/sbin/
RUN chmod 0755 /opt/alice-bundle/alice-helper /usr/local/sbin/alice-e2e-prepare /usr/local/sbin/alice-e2e-rotate-hostkey
CMD ["/usr/sbin/sshd", "-D", "-e"]
```

```sh
#!/bin/sh
# Test only: run the setup script that Alice shows (read from stdin) as root, next to the
# alice-helper copy of the bundle, exactly as an administrator would (owner step 1).
```

Create `test/images/e2e-target/alice-e2e-rotate-hostkey`:

```sh
#!/bin/sh
# Test only: give the server new host keys and make the listening sshd load them (owner step 5).
# SIGHUP makes sshd re-execute itself with the new keys; open sessions keep running.
set -eu
rm -f /etc/ssh/ssh_host_*
ssh-keygen -A >/dev/null
pkill -HUP -o -x sshd
```

- [ ] **Step 1: Write the fixture script and the three images**

Create `test/images/sshd/fixtures.sh`:

```sh
#!/bin/sh
# Fixture users and keys for the real-OpenSSH tests (spec §22.6). Runs once at image build time
# as root. Keys are generated here and their private halves deleted at once: nothing secret is
# committed. /root/fixture-keys.tsv lists every key Alice's inventory must show
# (user, fingerprint, comment); keys Alice must NOT show are not listed.
set -eu
out=/root/fixture-keys.tsv
: > "$out"
tmp="$(mktemp -d)"

# newkey <type> <bits or -> <comment>: prints a new public key line.
newkey() {
	if [ "$2" = - ]; then
		ssh-keygen -q -t "$1" -N '' -C "$3" -f "$tmp/k"
	else
		ssh-keygen -q -t "$1" -b "$2" -N '' -C "$3" -f "$tmp/k"
	fi
	cat "$tmp/k.pub"
	rm -f "$tmp/k" "$tmp/k.pub"
}

# record <user> <public key line>: the inventory must list this key for this user.
record() {
	fp="$(printf '%s\n' "$2" | ssh-keygen -lf - | awk '{print $2}')"
	printf '%s\t%s\t%s\n' "$1" "$fp" "$(printf '%s\n' "$2" | awk '{print $3}')" >> "$out"
}

# user <name> <uid> <shell>: a user with a private .ssh directory.
user() {
	useradd --uid "$2" --create-home --shell "$3" "$1"
	install -d -m 0700 -o "$1" -g "$1" "/home/$1/.ssh"
}

# deploy: two keys, file ends with a newline.
user deploy 1001 /bin/bash
k1="$(newkey ed25519 - deploy@laptop)"
k2="$(newkey rsa 3072 ci@build)"
printf '%s\n%s\n' "$k1" "$k2" > /home/deploy/.ssh/authorized_keys
record deploy "$k1"
record deploy "$k2"

# noshell: a key, but no login shell: Alice does not list it (spec §13.1).
user noshell 1002 /usr/sbin/nologin
printf '%s\n' "$(newkey ed25519 - noshell@x)" > /home/noshell/.ssh/authorized_keys

# nonl: one key and no trailing newline (F-37).
user nonl 1003 /bin/bash
k4="$(newkey ed25519 - nonl@desk)"
printf '%s' "$k4" > /home/nonl/.ssh/authorized_keys
record nonl "$k4"

# linky: authorized_keys is a symlink to /etc/shadow (A-13): never read.
user linky 1004 /bin/bash
ln -s /etc/shadow /home/linky/.ssh/authorized_keys

# root: one key restricted with from= (so no root_without_from flag).
install -d -m 0700 /root/.ssh
k5="$(newkey ed25519 - root@bastion)"
printf 'from="10.0.0.0/8" %s\n' "$k5" > /root/.ssh/authorized_keys
record root "$k5"

for u in deploy noshell nonl; do
	chown "$u:$u" "/home/$u/.ssh/authorized_keys"
	chmod 0600 "/home/$u/.ssh/authorized_keys"
done
chmod 0600 /root/.ssh/authorized_keys
rm -rf "$tmp"
```

Create `test/images/sshd/ubuntu22.Dockerfile`:

```dockerfile
# Real OpenSSH target for internal/providers/linuxssh/containers_integration_test.go (spec §22.3).
# alice-helper and the setup script are installed by the test, not by the image.
FROM ubuntu:22.04
RUN apt-get update \
 && DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends openssh-server sudo procps \
 && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/* \
 && mkdir -p /run/sshd \
 && ssh-keygen -A \
 && sed -i 's/^session\s\+required\s\+pam_loginuid.so/session optional pam_loginuid.so/' /etc/pam.d/sshd
COPY fixtures.sh /usr/local/sbin/alice-fixtures.sh
RUN sh /usr/local/sbin/alice-fixtures.sh
EXPOSE 22
CMD ["/usr/sbin/sshd", "-D", "-e"]
```

```dockerfile

FROM rockylinux/rockylinux:9
RUN dnf install -y openssh-server sudo shadow-utils procps-ng util-linux \
 && dnf clean all \
```

(The `pam_loginuid` line is a container accommodation: an unprivileged container cannot write the login UID, and
`required` would end every session. Real servers keep their PAM configuration; the setup script never touches it.)

Run: `for d in ubuntu22 debian12 rocky9; do docker build -f test/images/sshd/$d.Dockerfile -t alice-test/sshd-$d:phase3 test/images/sshd || exit 1; docker run --rm alice-test/sshd-$d:phase3 sh -c 'wc -l < /root/fixture-keys.tsv; test -L /home/linky/.ssh/authorized_keys'; done`
Expected: each build succeeds and prints `4` (deploy ×2, nonl, root).
