Create `web/src/pages/SSHKeysPage.tsx`:

```tsx
import { Anchor, Badge, Button, Code, Group, NativeSelect, SimpleGrid, Stack, Switch, Table, Text, TextInput, Title } from '@mantine/core';
import { useDebouncedValue } from '@mantine/hooks';
import { useInfiniteQuery, useQuery } from '@tanstack/react-query';
import { useState } from 'react';
import { useTranslation } from 'react-i18next';
import { Link } from 'react-router';
import { listSSHKeys, listTargets } from '../api/endpoints';
import { SSH_KEYS_KEY, TARGETS_KEY } from '../api/queryKeys';
import type { KeyFlag, SSHKeyQuery } from '../api/types';
import { ErrorAlert } from '../components/ErrorAlert';
import { WRAP } from '../components/wrap';

const FLAGS: KeyFlag[] = ['weak', 'command', 'root_without_from', 'duplicate', 'cert_authority', 'security_key'];

// SSHKeysPage is the SSH key inventory (spec §13.3, §26.5): one row per key, filtered on the
// server so the page stays fast with thousands of keys; the search is debounced.
export function SSHKeysPage() {
  const { t } = useTranslation();
  const [search, setSearch] = useState('');
  const [user, setUser] = useState('');
  const [targetId, setTargetId] = useState('');
  const [flag, setFlag] = useState<KeyFlag | ''>('');
  const [missing, setMissing] = useState(false);
  const [q] = useDebouncedValue(search.trim(), 300);
  const [osUser] = useDebouncedValue(user.trim(), 300);

  const targets = useQuery({ queryKey: TARGETS_KEY, queryFn: listTargets });
  const filter: SSHKeyQuery = { q, os_user: osUser, target_id: targetId, flag, missing };
  const keys = useInfiniteQuery({
    queryKey: [...SSH_KEYS_KEY, filter],
    queryFn: ({ pageParam }) => listSSHKeys({ ...filter, cursor: pageParam }),
    initialPageParam: null as string | null,
    getNextPageParam: (last) => last.next_cursor,
  });
  const items = keys.data?.pages.flatMap((p) => p.items) ?? [];

  return (
    <Stack gap="md">
      <Title order={1}>{t('sshKeys.title')}</Title>
      <Text size="sm">{t('sshKeys.intro')}</Text>
      <SimpleGrid cols={{ base: 1, sm: 2, lg: 4 }}>
        <TextInput label={t('sshKeys.search')} description={t('sshKeys.searchHelp')} value={search} onChange={(e) => setSearch(e.currentTarget.value)} maxLength={200} />
        <NativeSelect
          label={t('sshKeys.server')}
          value={targetId}
          onChange={(e) => setTargetId(e.currentTarget.value)}
          data={[{ value: '', label: t('sshKeys.allServers') }, ...(targets.data?.items ?? []).map((tg) => ({ value: tg.id, label: tg.name }))]}
        />
        <TextInput label={t('sshKeys.user')} value={user} onChange={(e) => setUser(e.currentTarget.value)} maxLength={32} />
        <NativeSelect
          label={t('sshKeys.flag')}
          value={flag}
          onChange={(e) => setFlag(e.currentTarget.value as KeyFlag | '')}
          data={[{ value: '', label: t('sshKeys.allFlags') }, ...FLAGS.map((f) => ({ value: f, label: t(`sshKeys.flags.${f}`) }))]}
        />
      </SimpleGrid>
      <Switch label={t('sshKeys.showMissing')} checked={missing} onChange={(e) => setMissing(e.currentTarget.checked)} />
      <ErrorAlert error={keys.error} />
      {keys.isSuccess && items.length === 0 && <Text c="gray.7">{t('sshKeys.empty')}</Text>}
      {items.length > 0 && (
        <Table.ScrollContainer minWidth={720}>
          <Table striped data-testid="ssh-keys-table">
            <Table.Thead>
              <Table.Tr>
                <Table.Th>{t('sshKeys.key')}</Table.Th>
                <Table.Th>{t('sshKeys.comment')}</Table.Th>
                <Table.Th>{t('sshKeys.locationCount')}</Table.Th>
                <Table.Th>{t('sshKeys.targetCount')}</Table.Th>
              </Table.Tr>
            </Table.Thead>
            <Table.Tbody>
              {items.map((k) => (
                <Table.Tr key={k.id}>
                  <Table.Td>
                    <Stack gap={2}>
                      <Anchor component={Link} to={`/ssh-keys/${k.id}`}>
                        <Code style={WRAP}>{k.fingerprint}</Code>
                      </Anchor>
                      <Text size="xs">{t('sshKeys.keyType', { type: k.key_type, bits: k.bits })}</Text>
                      <Group gap={4}>
                        {k.is_platform_key && (
                          <Badge variant="light" color="indigo" tt="none">
                            {t('sshKeys.aliceKey')}
                          </Badge>
                        )}
                        {k.weak && (
                          <Badge variant="light" color="orange" tt="none">
                            {t('sshKeys.flags.weak')}
                          </Badge>
                        )}
                      </Group>
                    </Stack>
                  </Table.Td>
                  <Table.Td style={WRAP}>{k.comment}</Table.Td>
                  <Table.Td>{k.location_count}</Table.Td>
                  <Table.Td>{k.target_count}</Table.Td>
                </Table.Tr>
              ))}
            </Table.Tbody>
          </Table>
        </Table.ScrollContainer>
      )}
      {keys.hasNextPage && (
        <Button variant="default" w="fit-content" loading={keys.isFetchingNextPage} onClick={() => void keys.fetchNextPage()}>
          {t('sshKeys.loadMore')}
        </Button>
      )}
    </Stack>
  );
}
```

The fingerprint link's accessible name is the fingerprint text (the `<Code>` is inside the anchor).

Create `web/src/pages/SSHKeyDetailPage.tsx`:

```tsx
import { Anchor, Button, Code, CopyButton, Stack, Table, Text, Title } from '@mantine/core';
import { useQuery, useQueryClient } from '@tanstack/react-query';
import { useState } from 'react';
import { useTranslation } from 'react-i18next';
import { Link, useParams } from 'react-router';
import { getSSHKey } from '../api/endpoints';
import { SSH_KEYS_KEY, TARGETS_KEY } from '../api/queryKeys';
import type { KeyLocation } from '../api/types';
import { useAuth } from '../auth/AuthProvider';
import { PageLoader } from '../auth/guards';
import { ErrorAlert } from '../components/ErrorAlert';
import { KeyFlags } from '../components/KeyFlags';
import { RemoveKeyDialog } from '../components/RemoveKeyDialog';
import { WRAP } from '../components/wrap';
import { formatDateTime } from '../datetime';

// SSHKeyDetailPage is one key and every place it is used (owner step 3: "open one and see where
// it is used"). Operators and Administrators can remove it from one place at a time.
export function SSHKeyDetailPage() {
  const { t, i18n } = useTranslation();
  const { id = '' } = useParams();
  const { session } = useAuth();
  const client = useQueryClient();
  const canOperate = session?.user.role === 'admin' || session?.user.role === 'operator';
  const key = useQuery({ queryKey: [...SSH_KEYS_KEY, id], queryFn: () => getSSHKey(id) });
  const [removing, setRemoving] = useState<KeyLocation | null>(null);

  if (key.isPending) return <PageLoader />;
  if (key.isError || !key.data) return <ErrorAlert error={key.error} />;
  const k = key.data;
  const state = (l: KeyLocation) => (l.removed_at ? t('sshKeys.removedByAlice') : l.missing_since ? t('sshKeys.missing') : t('sshKeys.present'));

  return (
    <Stack gap="md">
      <Title order={1}>{t('sshKeys.detailTitle')}</Title>
      <Text size="sm">{t('sshKeys.keyType', { type: k.key_type, bits: k.bits })}</Text>
      <Text size="sm" fw={600}>
        {t('sshKeys.fingerprintLabel')}
      </Text>
      <Code style={WRAP}>{k.fingerprint}</Code>
      <Text size="sm" fw={600}>
        {t('sshKeys.publicKey')}
      </Text>
      <Code block style={WRAP}>
        {k.public_key}
      </Code>
      <CopyButton value={k.public_key}>
        {({ copied, copy }) => (
          <Button size="xs" variant="light" w="fit-content" onClick={copy}>
            {copied ? t('sshKeys.copied') : t('sshKeys.copy')}
          </Button>
        )}
      </CopyButton>
      <Title order={2} size="h3">
        {t('sshKeys.usedWhere')}
      </Title>
      <Table.ScrollContainer minWidth={880}>
        <Table striped data-testid="key-locations">
          <Table.Thead>
            <Table.Tr>
              <Table.Th>{t('sshKeys.server')}</Table.Th>
              <Table.Th>{t('sshKeys.user')}</Table.Th>
              <Table.Th>{t('sshKeys.file')}</Table.Th>
              <Table.Th>{t('sshKeys.line')}</Table.Th>
              <Table.Th>{t('sshKeys.options')}</Table.Th>
              <Table.Th>{t('sshKeys.comment')}</Table.Th>
              <Table.Th>{t('sshKeys.lastSeen')}</Table.Th>
              <Table.Th>{t('sshKeys.state')}</Table.Th>
              <Table.Th>{t('sshKeys.actions')}</Table.Th>
            </Table.Tr>
          </Table.Thead>
          <Table.Tbody>
            {(k.locations ?? []).map((l) => (
              <Table.Tr key={l.id}>
                <Table.Td>
                  <Anchor component={Link} to={`/servers/${l.target_id}`}>
                    {l.target_name}
                  </Anchor>
                </Table.Td>
                <Table.Td>{l.os_user}</Table.Td>
                <Table.Td>
                  <Code style={WRAP}>{l.file_path}</Code>
                </Table.Td>
                <Table.Td>{l.line_no}</Table.Td>
                <Table.Td>{l.options && <Code style={WRAP}>{l.options}</Code>}</Table.Td>
                <Table.Td style={WRAP}>
                  <Stack gap={2}>
                    <span>{l.comment}</span>
                    <KeyFlags location={l} />
                  </Stack>
                </Table.Td>
                <Table.Td>{formatDateTime(l.last_seen_at, i18n.language)}</Table.Td>
                <Table.Td>{state(l)}</Table.Td>
                <Table.Td>
                  {canOperate && !l.removed_at && !l.missing_since && (
                    <Button size="xs" variant="light" color="red.9" onClick={() => setRemoving(l)} aria-label={t('sshKeys.removeNamed', { user: l.os_user })}>
                      {t('sshKeys.removeConfirm')}
                    </Button>
                  )}
                </Table.Td>
              </Table.Tr>
            ))}
          </Table.Tbody>
        </Table>
      </Table.ScrollContainer>
      {removing && (
        <RemoveKeyDialog
          location={removing}
          onClose={() => setRemoving(null)}
          onDone={() => {
            setRemoving(null);
            void client.invalidateQueries({ queryKey: SSH_KEYS_KEY });
            void client.invalidateQueries({ queryKey: TARGETS_KEY });
          }}
        />
      )}
    </Stack>
  );
}
```

```tsx
import { Alert, Button, Group, Stack, Text, Title } from '@mantine/core';
import { useState } from 'react';
import { useTranslation } from 'react-i18next';
import { AddServerModal } from '../../components/AddServerModal';
import { PlatformKeyPanel } from '../../components/PlatformKeyPanel';

// PlatformStep is wizard step 7 (spec §18.5): Alice's own public key with the commands that
// prepare a server, and an optional first server. It may be skipped; the Servers page offers the
// same later, so the step stores nothing of its own.
export function PlatformStep({ onDone }: { onDone: () => void }) {
  const { t } = useTranslation();
  const [adding, setAdding] = useState(false);
  const [added, setAdded] = useState(false);
  return (
    <Stack>
      <Title order={2}>{t('setup.platform.title')}</Title>
      <Text>{t('setup.platform.help')}</Text>
      <PlatformKeyPanel titleOrder={3} />
      {added && (
        <Alert color="green" role="status">
          {t('targets.added')}
        </Alert>
      )}
      <Group>
        <Button variant="default" onClick={() => setAdding(true)}>
          {t('setup.platform.addNow')}
        </Button>
        <Button onClick={onDone}>{t('setup.platform.continue')}</Button>
      </Group>
      {adding && (
        <AddServerModal
          onClose={() => setAdding(false)}
          onAdded={() => {
            setAdding(false);
            setAdded(true);
          }}
        />
      )}
    </Stack>
  );
}
```

### Task 22: End-to-end — Phase 3 owner journeys in English and Turkish, license banners carry, accessibility

Playwright drives the e2e stack (Task 18: e2e build, `sshtarget` service, `/test/jobs/drain`, `/test/license/tamper`)
through the owner steps of spec §26.5 in both languages: prepare a real OpenSSH server with the commands Alice shows,
add it, compare the fingerprint with `ssh-keygen -lf` on the server and confirm it, see the keys with their users, open a
key and see where it is used, try to remove Alice's own key (refused, explained), remove another key (only that line
disappears from the file), change the server's host key (red warning, operations blocked, Operators cannot accept,
an Administrator accepts with step-up and a reason), and add servers until the license limit. The license banners that
Phase 2 could not reach (`limit_reached`, `over_limit`, `tampered`, carry 5) are checked with axe and for horizontal
overflow at 375, 640, 1280 and 1920 px. A locked installation refuses a new server with the plain-language message while
the inventory stays readable (L-26, R9).

Commands run only inside the `sshtarget` service of the `alice` compose project (`targetExec`), never in any other
container.

**Interfaces:**
- Consumes (Task 18, contract "e2e environment"): service `sshtarget` with `/usr/local/sbin/alice-e2e-prepare` (setup
  script on stdin, run as root in `/opt/alice-bundle`) and `/usr/local/sbin/alice-e2e-rotate-hostkey`; users `deploy`

```ts
import { execFileSync } from 'node:child_process';
import { createHmac } from 'node:crypto';

```

and append at the end of the file:

```ts
// --- Phase 3: the e2e SSH target, background jobs and API calls as the signed-in browser user ---

// COMPOSE addresses the e2e stack of this repository (make e2e-up); tests run from web/.
const COMPOSE = ['compose', '-f', '../deploy/docker-compose.yml', '-f', '../deploy/docker-compose.e2e.yml', '--env-file', '../deploy/.env'];

// targetExec runs a command as root in the e2e SSH target service "sshtarget" and returns its
// standard output. It never addresses any other container.
export function targetExec(args: string[], input?: string): string {
  return execFileSync('docker', [...COMPOSE, 'exec', '-T', 'sshtarget', ...args], {
    input,
    encoding: 'utf8',
    timeout: 120_000,
  });
}

// drainJobs runs every due background job now (e2e build), so tests do not wait for the poll interval.
export async function drainJobs(request: APIRequestContext): Promise<void> {
  const res = await request.post('/test/jobs/drain');
  expect(res.ok(), 'POST /test/jobs/drain (is this the Phase 3 e2e build?)').toBe(true);
}

// settle runs due jobs until done is visible: a job finishes, then the page's polling shows its result.
export async function settle(request: APIRequestContext, done: Locator): Promise<void> {
  await expect(async () => {
    await drainJobs(request);
    await expect(done).toBeVisible({ timeout: 1_500 });
  }).toPass({ timeout: 90_000 });
}

// fingerprintOf extracts "SHA256:…" from the output of ssh-keygen -lf.
export function fingerprintOf(sshKeygenOutput: string): string {
  const m = sshKeygenOutput.match(/SHA256:[A-Za-z0-9+/]+/);
  expect(m, `fingerprint in: ${sshKeygenOutput}`).not.toBeNull();
  return m![0];
}

export interface Api {
  get(path: string): Promise<APIResponse>;
  post(path: string, data?: unknown): Promise<APIResponse>;
  // stepUp confirms the session with a fresh code. The server rotates the session cookie and so the
  // CSRF token; reload the page afterwards before using the UI (the SPA keeps the old token in memory).
  stepUp(totpSecret: string): Promise<void>;
}

// apiAs calls the API as the user signed in on page (same cookies), with the session's CSRF token.
export async function apiAs(page: Page): Promise<Api> {
  const session = await page.request.get('/api/v1/auth/session');
  expect(session.ok(), 'GET /api/v1/auth/session (signed in?)').toBe(true);
  let csrf = ((await session.json()) as { csrf_token: string }).csrf_token;
  const api: Api = {
    get: (path) => page.request.get(path, { headers: { 'X-CSRF-Token': csrf } }),
    post: (path, data) => page.request.post(path, { headers: { 'X-CSRF-Token': csrf }, data: data ?? {} }),
    stepUp: async (totpSecret) => {
      const res = await api.post('/api/v1/auth/stepup', { code: await freshCode(page.request, totpSecret) });
      expect(res.ok(), await res.text()).toBe(true);
      csrf = ((await res.json()) as { csrf_token: string }).csrf_token;
    },
  };
  return api;
}

// expectWide checks a screen with axe and for horizontal overflow on a 375 px phone and at every
// width of expectAccessible (tables scroll inside their own container, never the page).
export async function expectWide(page: Page, screen: string): Promise<void> {
  const original = page.viewportSize();
  try {
    await page.setViewportSize({ width: 375, height: original?.height ?? 720 });
    expect(await seriousViolations(page), `axe: ${screen} at 375 px`).toEqual([]);
    const overflow = await page.evaluate(() => document.documentElement.scrollWidth - document.documentElement.clientWidth);
    expect(overflow, `horizontal overflow: ${screen} at 375 px`).toBeLessThanOrEqual(0);
  } finally {
    if (original) await page.setViewportSize(original);
  }
  await expectAccessible(page, screen);
}
```

```ts
    tampered: 'Lisans verileri Alice dışında değiştirildi',
  },
} as const;

type PCopy = (typeof P)[Lang];

// stepUpIfAsked answers the step-up dialog with a fresh code when the server asks for one.
async function stepUpIfAsked(page: Page, request: APIRequestContext, c: Copy, secret: string): Promise<void> {
  const dialog = page.getByRole('dialog', { name: c.stepUpHeading });
  try {
    await dialog.waitFor({ state: 'visible', timeout: 5_000 });
  } catch {
    return; // the step-up window from the sign-in is still open
  }
  await field(dialog, c.code).fill(await freshCode(request, secret));
  await dialog.getByRole('button', { name: c.stepUpConfirm }).click();
}

async function openServers(page: Page, p: PCopy): Promise<void> {
  await page.getByRole('link', { name: p.navServers, exact: true }).click();
  await expect(page.getByRole('heading', { name: p.navServers, level: 1 })).toBeVisible();
}

// addServerInDialog opens "Add server", fills the form and submits it.
async function addServerInDialog(page: Page, p: PCopy, name: string, address: string) {
  await page.getByRole('button', { name: p.addServer }).click();
  const dialog = page.getByRole('dialog', { name: p.addServer });
  await field(dialog, p.name).fill(name);
  await field(dialog, p.address).fill(address);
  await dialog.getByRole('button', { name: p.connect }).click();
  return dialog;
}
```

- [ ] **Step 2: Write the host preparation guide**

Create `docs/nginx-host-preparation.md`:

````markdown
# Preparing a Server for Alice

Alice manages servers over SSH with its own key. It never logs in as `root` and never runs a shell command of its
own choosing: everything that needs root goes through **alice-helper**, a small program that you install on the
server, owned by root, and that only does a fixed list of things. This guide prepares a server once. It takes about
five minutes per server and you can undo it completely (see "Removing Alice from a server").

Supported systems: Ubuntu 20.04 or later, Debian 11 or later, RHEL, Rocky Linux or AlmaLinux 8 or later, with the
OpenSSH server and `sudo`.

## What the setup commands do

1. Copy `alice-helper` to `/usr/local/libexec/alice-helper`, owned by root, mode 0755. Alice cannot change this
   file; you update it yourself when a new Alice release asks for it ("helper outdated").
2. Create the service user `alice-svc` (home `/var/lib/alice-svc`) if it does not exist, without a password.
3. Put Alice's public key into `/var/lib/alice-svc/.ssh/authorized_keys` with the options
   `no-agent-forwarding,no-port-forwarding,no-X11-forwarding` (and `from="<Alice's address>"` if you choose it).
4. Install `/etc/sudoers.d/alice` (mode 0440, checked with `visudo -cf` before it is installed). It allows
   `alice-svc` to run **only** `alice-helper` with a fixed list of subcommands, without a password.
5. Create `/var/lib/alice-helper/backups` (root only, mode 0700). Before Alice changes an `authorized_keys` file,
   the helper keeps a copy here; copies older than 30 days are removed automatically.

## Two profiles

| Profile | For | Allowed helper subcommands |
|---|---|---|
| `linux` | Servers where Alice manages SSH keys only | `sshd-dump`, `hostkeys`, `cleanup`, `authkeys-list`, `authkeys-read`, `authkeys-write` |
| `nginx` | Nginx servers (certificates arrive in a later release; SSH keys work now) | everything in `linux` plus `nginx-dump`, `nginx-test`, `nginx-reload`, `stat`, `read-cert`, `install-cert`, `backup`, `restore` |

Choose the profile under **Server type** on the **Servers** page. A Linux server never gets the Nginx permissions.

## Steps

1. Get the helper. In a development checkout run `make helper`; it writes `bin/alice-helper-linux-amd64`,
   `bin/alice-helper-linux-arm64` and `bin/alice-helper.sha256`. (Release packages ship the same files in
   `helper/`.) Copy the file for the server's processor to the server as `alice-helper`, in an empty directory,
   and compare its checksum: `sha256sum alice-helper` must print the value from `alice-helper.sha256`.
2. In Alice, sign in as an administrator and open **Servers**. Under **Prepare a server for Alice** choose the
   **Server type** and choose **Copy commands**. The commands contain Alice's public key; the fingerprint shown
   above them is the same one you will see in the authorized_keys file.
3. On the server, in the directory that holds `alice-helper`, run the commands as root (for example
   `sudo sh` and paste). They stop at the first error and change nothing after it.
4. In Alice choose **Add server**, enter a name, the server's address, the SSH port and the user name `alice-svc`,
   and choose **Connect**.
5. Alice shows the server's **fingerprint**. On the server run the command Alice shows
   (for example `ssh-keygen -lf /etc/ssh/ssh_host_ed25519_key.pub`) and compare the `SHA256:…` value character by
   character. Only if it is the same, choose **Yes, this is my server**. If it differs, choose **No, cancel**
   and ask your network or security team: someone may be between Alice and the server.
6. Alice tests the connection and reads the SSH keys. The server shows **Connected** and its keys appear under
   **SSH keys on this server**.

## What Alice reads and changes

- Alice reads `authorized_keys` files of `root`, of every account with a user ID of 1000 or more that has a login
  shell, and of `alice-svc` itself, in the places that the SSH server's `AuthorizedKeysFile` setting names. It
  reads the server's host key fingerprints and its SSH settings (`sshd -T`). It never reads private keys.
- Accounts that exist only in a directory service (LDAP, SSSD) are not listed; Alice shows a warning when the
  server uses one.
- If the SSH server gets keys from a program (`AuthorizedKeysCommand`), Alice shows the keys it finds in files but
  does not change keys on that server ("This server gets its SSH keys from a program").
- Alice changes an `authorized_keys` file only when an administrator or operator asks it to remove a key. It
  removes exactly the lines of that key, keeps every other line (including lines it cannot read) byte for byte,
  checks that nobody changed the file in the meantime, and keeps the previous version in the backup directory.
- Alice never removes its own key, on any account.

## When the server is rebuilt

A rebuilt server has a new host key. Alice then shows **Server identity changed** and stops all work on it until an
administrator compares the new fingerprint (step 5 above) and accepts it with **Review the new fingerprint**,
a fresh authenticator code and a reason. The previous fingerprint stays in the history.

## Removing Alice from a server

As root on the server:

```sh
rm -f /etc/sudoers.d/alice /usr/local/libexec/alice-helper
userdel -r alice-svc
rm -rf /var/lib/alice-helper
```

Then choose **Remove server** on the server's page in Alice. Alice forgets the server and its keys; it never
connects to the server to do this.
````

- [ ] **Step 3: Update the administrator guide**

In `docs/admin-guide.md`, insert before the line `## License`:

````markdown
## Servers

**Servers** lists every server Alice manages with its status: **Connected**, **Waiting for fingerprint
confirmation**, **Checking…**, **Cannot be reached**, **Sign-in refused**, **Server identity changed**. Everyone can
see the list and each server's details; nobody ever sees a password or private key there.

- **Add server** (administrators): see [nginx-host-preparation.md](nginx-host-preparation.md). Each server counts
  toward the license; when the license is full, Alice says "Your license allows N targets." and adds nothing.
- **Test connection** and **Scan for SSH keys** (administrators and operators) run in the background; the page
  updates when they finish. Alice also scans every server once a day on its own.
- **Server identity changed**: Alice stopped all work on the server because its host key is different from the
  one you confirmed. Only an administrator can accept the new fingerprint, after checking it on the server, with a
  fresh authenticator code and a reason. Everything is recorded in the audit log, and administrators with an email
  address get one email when it happens.
- **Remove server** (administrators) makes Alice forget the server and frees its license slot. Nothing is changed on
  the server.
- **Waiting for an administrator** lists work that was paused while the license had expired (for example a key
  removal). After a new license is installed, an administrator chooses **Run now** or **Discard** for each item;
  nothing starts on its own (R29).

## SSH keys

**SSH keys** lists every public key Alice found, once per key, with the number of servers and places where it is
used. Filter by text (fingerprint, comment, key type), server, user or finding (weak key, key without `from=` on
root, key with a forced command, duplicate, certificate authority, security key). **Show keys that are no longer
found** also lists keys that disappeared since the last scan; Alice never deletes them from its records.

Open a key to see **Where this key is used**: server, user, file, line and options. Administrators and operators can
remove a key from one place with **Remove key from <user>**. Alice removes only that key's lines from that file.
It refuses to remove its own key ("Alice needs this key to connect to this server and will not remove it.") and the
last key of `root` unless an administrator confirms it. Generating, deploying and rotating keys arrive in a later
release.
````

- [ ] **Step 4: Update the operator guide (incl. carry 4c)**

In `docs/operator-guide.md`, insert before the line `## Checking an audit export outside Alice`:

````markdown
## Alice's SSH key

On its first start after the Phase 3 update Alice creates its own Ed25519 SSH key. The private key is stored only
encrypted with the master key, inside the database (table `credentials`); there is no key file. Backups of the
database therefore contain it, protected like every other secret. The public key and its fingerprint are shown on
**Servers** and in the setup wizard. Replacing the key is a manual procedure: add the new public key to every
server first, then contact the vendor; Alice never removes its own key from a server.

## Master-key rotation and the installation record

Master-key rotation (§7.2 of the design, `alice keys rotate-master`) is not available yet. When it is added it must,
in the same procedure, re-seal the installation record (`license.installation_seal`, HMAC under the HKDF label
`alice/installation/v1`) and re-write both copies of the license time record (`settings.time.hwm` and
`<ALICE_STATE_DIR>/hwm.dat`, labels `alice/hwm/v1` and `alice/hwm-enc/v1`) with the new key; otherwise the next
start reports the installation as tampered and the evaluation as ended. Do not replace `master.key` by hand.

## Background jobs

Work on servers runs in a job queue stored in PostgreSQL: connection tests, scans and key removals. Each job holds
a lease that it renews every 15 seconds; if Alice stops or crashes, a job whose lease has run out is put back in
the queue (audited as `job.recovered`) and runs again once. Two jobs for the same server never run at the same
time. At most 10 SSH connections are open at once (2 per server); each remote step has its own time limit (30 or 60
seconds). While the license is locked, scans are not started and key removals wait for an administrator after the
next license is installed.

If two Alice processes run against the same database (for example during an update), only one of them schedules
periodic work (a PostgreSQL advisory lock); both may run queued jobs, and each job still runs exactly once.

Periodic work: license evaluation (hourly), email sending (every minute), audit chain verification (daily, recorded
as `audit.verified` by `scheduler`), clean-up (hourly: expired sessions, finished jobs older than 90 days), and
scheduling of the daily server scans (every minute).
````

In `docs/troubleshooting.md`, insert before `## License messages`:

```markdown
## Servers and SSH keys

- **"Connecting to the server…" ends with "Cannot be reached".** Check the address and port, that the server's SSH
  service runs, and that a firewall lets the Alice server through (`ALC-SSH-0001`, `ALC-SSH-0003`).
- **"Sign-in refused" (`ALC-SSH-0002`).** The server does not accept Alice's key for the user you entered. Run the
  setup commands again (they put the key in `/var/lib/alice-svc/.ssh/authorized_keys`), and check that the user
  name is `alice-svc`. Alice does not retry on its own more than once per scan interval, so the server never locks
  the account because of Alice.
- **"The Alice account on this server is not allowed to run the helper" (`ALC-SSH-0004`) or "helper outdated"
  (`ALC-SSH-0005`).** Install the `alice-helper` file from this Alice release and the sudoers file from **Servers →
  Prepare a server for Alice** again.
- **Server identity changed (`ALC-TGT-0004`).** See [nginx-host-preparation.md](nginx-host-preparation.md#when-the-server-is-rebuilt).
  Never accept a new fingerprint you have not compared on the server itself.
- **"This server gets its SSH keys from a program" (`ALC-SSH-0008`).** The server uses `AuthorizedKeysCommand`;
  Alice lists keys but does not change them there.
- **A key removal says "The file changed while Alice was working" (`ALC-SSH-0007`).** Someone or something edited
  the file at the same moment; Alice changed nothing. Try again.
- **"Alice needs this key to connect to this server and will not remove it." (`ALC-KEY-0001`).** This is Alice's
  own key; it is protected on purpose.
```

```markdown
## Unreleased — Phase 3: Servers and SSH key inventory

### Added
- **Servers**: add a Linux server over SSH, confirm its host-key fingerprint before Alice trusts it, test the
  connection, scan it, remove it. Servers count toward the license; the limit and lock mode are enforced when a
  server is added.
- `alice-helper`, a small static program installed root-owned on each server (`make helper`), and a generated
  setup script with two restricted sudoers profiles (`linux`, `nginx`). Alice runs nothing else as root.
- Host-key pinning: a changed host key stops all work on that server, emails administrators once and needs an
  administrator with a fresh authenticator code and a reason to accept the new key.
- **SSH keys**: inventory of every `authorized_keys` entry (users, files, options, comments) with filters and
  findings (weak keys, root keys without `from=`, forced commands, duplicates); servers that use
  `AuthorizedKeysCommand` are detected and not changed.
- Removing a key from one place (administrators and operators); Alice's own key is always refused.
- Alice's own Ed25519 SSH key, created at first start and stored encrypted; shown with the setup commands on
  **Servers** and in the wizard's new **Connect your servers** step.
- A durable job queue in PostgreSQL with leases, retries, crash recovery and one job per server at a time; work
  paused by an expired license waits for an administrator after renewal.
- Daily audit chain verification and hourly clean-up of expired sessions and old jobs.

### Changed
- Every state-changing API route belongs to exactly one license lock group; `GET /api/v1/license/status` answers
  `ALC-SYS-0002` until the first license evaluation has finished.
- A changed installation record is audited once per occurrence (`license.installation_tampered`), and restoring it
  is audited too (`license.installation_restored`).
```

```markdown
- R37 (Phase 3, approved with the Phase 3 plan) Accepted Phase 3 implementation decisions: (1) the platform SSH key is an Ed25519 key generated at the first start after the migration, stored only as an envelope in `credentials` (`purpose = 'platform_ssh'`, payload = the 32-byte seed, AAD `credentials/<id>/ciphertext`); there is no host key file (§18.3 and §20.2 wording superseded) and backups carry it in the database dump; (2) no binary is served over HTTP: `make helper` builds `bin/alice-helper-linux-{amd64,arm64}` and `bin/alice-helper.sha256`, the generated script installs the copy the administrator placed next to it, Phase 8 ships them in the tarball's `helper/`; `GET /api/v1/ssh-keys/platform-key` (Admin) returns the public key, fingerprint, `authorized_keys` line and both profiles' sudoers text and script (§9.6 `/setup/alice-helper` is not built); (3) helper protocol 1 implements `version`, `sshd-dump`, `hostkeys`, `authkeys-list`, `authkeys-read`, `authkeys-write`, `cleanup`; other subcommands answer `UNKNOWN_SUBCOMMAND` until Phase 4 (protocol 2); both sudoers profiles are generated now; (4) the static helper computes host-key fingerprints in Go and reads `/etc/passwd` directly (no `ssh-keygen`, no NSS): directory-service users are not listed (warning `directory_users_not_listed`), and the account running the helper (`SUDO_USER`) is always listed so Alice's own key is in the inventory; (5) no `sudo -l` check (§6.6 wins over SC-5); a refused helper is `ALC-SSH-0004`; (6) a presented, unconfirmed host key is stored as `host_keys.status = 'observed'` and never trusted (F-30 "nothing stored" means "nothing trusted"); exactly one key is pinned per target and `HostKeyAlgorithms` is limited to its type; a missing pinned algorithm counts as a changed key; target status `checking` is added; the host-key inventory of §13.3 lives in `targets.facts`; (7) the job queue takes time from the injected clock as bind parameters, inserts the `target_locks` row in the claim transaction, polls every second instead of LISTEN/NOTIFY, MACs payloads under `alice/job/v1` (J-1) and adds `class`, `payload_mac`, `result`, `created_by_role`, `confirmed_by`, `confirmed_at`, `started_at`, `finished_at` and the status `blocked_license` (L-81); (8) state-changing routes under the infrastructure groups (now including `/api/v1/jobs`) are gated with `ClassChange` or `ClassReadOnly` (`test` and `discover` are read-only); every state-changing route sits in exactly one lock group and no public route is gated; (9) Phase 3 delivers removal of discovered keys (Admin, Operator) and provider-level key addition (F-37, F-38); generation, deployment and rotation stay in Phase 6; (10) a target's host, port and user cannot be edited (delete and add again); (11) `credentials` gains `purpose`, its `target_id` arrives with target-bound credentials (Phase 5), and it is append-only for `alice_app`; (12) permissions `targets.manage` (Admin, operate tokens), `hostkeys.confirm` (Admin session), `hostkeys.repin` (Admin session with step-up), `inventory.operate` (Admin and Operator, operate tokens), `jobs.confirm` (Admin session); (13) authentication failure is a permanent job failure that marks the target `auth_failed`, so a failing key is offered at most once per discovery interval (≥ 1 hour; F-34); (14) a changed host key or failed authentication emails every Administrator once per transition (`target.host_key_changed`, `target.auth_failed`) until the Phase 7 alert engine; (15) `audit.verify` (daily) and `maintenance.cleanup` (hourly: expired sessions and setup sessions, finished jobs older than 90 days) run on the periodic scheduler, which holds a PostgreSQL advisory lock so one process schedules (P2-06); (16) audit actions `target.created`, `target.updated`, `target.deleted`, `target.add.denied_license`, `target.status_changed`, `target.discovered`, `hostkey.pinned`, `hostkey.changed`, `hostkey.repinned`, `sshkey.remove_requested`, `sshkey.remove.denied`, `sshkey.removed`, `sshkey.remove_failed`, `job.recovered`, `job.dead`, `job.tampered`, `job.blocked_license`, `job.confirmed`, `job.discarded`, `platform_key.created`, `license.installation_restored`; error codes `ALC-SYS-0008`, `ALC-TGT-0001..0005`, `ALC-SSH-0001..0010`, `ALC-KEY-0001..0003`, `ALC-JOB-0001..0004`; (17) SSH limits are constants until Settings (Phase 7): 10 connections in total, 2 per target, idle close 60 s, dial 10 s, handshake 15 s, command 30 s (60 s for `sshd-dump` and `authkeys-list`), output 8 MiB; (18) carries: the installation record is audited once per tamper episode and its restoration is audited; the `00004` Down migration no longer restores table-wide `UPDATE ON license`; master-key rotation, when built, must re-seal the installation record and both HWM copies (`docs/operator-guide.md`); L-80, L-82 (Phase 4), L-83..L-86, L-88 (Phase 6) and L-87 (Phases 4/5) stay deferred, L-81 and the Phase 3 parts of L-29 are covered by real jobs; (19) the platform key is created at the first start, so on a fresh installation the audit chain starts with `platform_key.created` (system) instead of `setup.admin_created` (R35 wording superseded); (20) `jobs` may not import `secrets`, so the queue derives its MAC key through a `Derive(label)` interface satisfied by the keyring; a runner claims only the job types it has handlers for; a lease cut off by a crash or shutdown still counts as an attempt; (21) a pooled SSH connection is reused for up to 60 s, so a host-key change is detected on the next new connection, never later than 60 s after the previous use.
```

Create `docs/security/reviews/phase-3.md`:

````markdown
# Security Review — Phase 3 (Provider framework, Linux/SSH targets, alice-helper)

Scope (spec §17.2, Phase 3): host-key TOFU and change handling, the remote command allowlist, sudoers, injection
fuzzing. Exit criteria: the fuzz corpus is clean; a changed host key blocks all operations; no High finding open.

The decisions behind this phase are R37 in `docs/superpowers/specs/alice-v1/00-decisions.md`.

## Evidence

All commands run from the repository root; `-tags integration` needs Docker.

| # | Check | Command | Expected |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Host-key pinning: unconfirmed key stops before authentication, changed key and missing algorithm block, background jobs never pin (F-30, F-31) | `go test ./internal/providers/linuxssh -run 'Pin\|Unconfirmed\|Changed\|Algorithm' -count=1` | ok |
| 2 | Confirmation and re-pin rules, one email per change, history kept (F-30..F-33) | `go test -tags integration ./internal/inventory -run 'HostKey\|Confirm\|Repin\|Changed' -count=1` and `go test -tags integration ./internal/api -run 'TestChangedHostKeyJourney\|TestAddServerJourney' -count=1` | ok |
| 3 | Command surface: only helper constructors and `cat /etc/os-release`; single quoting function; no session call outside `dial.go`; no `InsecureIgnoreHostKey`, no `StrictHostKeyChecking=no` (A-12, SEC-063) | `go test ./internal/providers/linuxssh/... -run 'Command\|Quote\|Guard\|Injection' -count=1` and `make lint` | ok |
| 4 | Helper argument and path validation, candidate-only paths, symlink to `/etc/shadow` refused, atomic compare-and-swap writes (A-12, A-13, F-38) | `go test ./cmd/alice-helper -count=1` | ok |
| 5 | Helper is a static binary | `go test ./cmd/alice-helper -run TestHelperIsStatic -count=1` and `make helper` | ok |
| 6 | Parsers fuzzed (§25.6) | `make fuzz-ssh` | no crasher |
| 7 | Key operations: own key refused by fingerprint, last root key, keys managed elsewhere, CRLF and foreign lines preserved (F-35..F-38) | `go test ./internal/providers/linuxssh -run 'Remove\|Add\|OwnKey' -count=1` | ok |
| 8 | Real OpenSSH on Ubuntu 22.04, Debian 12, Rocky 9: setup script, sudoers profile, discovery, F-31 with a rotated host key, F-35, F-37, F-38 | `go test -tags integration -run TestRealOpenSSH ./internal/providers/linuxssh/ -count=1 -timeout 30m` | ok |
| 9 | Job queue: exactly once with 20 workers and 1000 jobs, per-target exclusivity, retries, MAC tamper, crash recovery kill test, leader lock (F-66, F-69, J-1) | `go test -tags integration ./internal/jobs/... -count=1` | ok |
| 10 | License: target limit and lock with real targets (L-04, L-26, L-29, L-70..L-79, L-81) | `go test -tags integration ./internal/inventory ./internal/api -run 'L0\|L7\|Limit\|Lock\|Blocked\|Evaluation' -count=1` and `go test ./internal/archtest -count=1` | ok |
| 11 | Authorization matrix incl. the five new permissions; lock-group rules | `go test ./internal/api -run 'Authz\|RouteRule\|Lock\|Sensitive' -count=1` and `make authz-doc && git diff --exit-code docs/authz-matrix.md` | ok, no diff |
| 12 | Secret leak with the platform SSH key (seed, OpenSSH PEM) through journeys and error paths; S-04 ciphertext | `go test -tags integration ./internal/api -run 'TestSecretsNeverLeak\|TestPlatformKeyNeverLeaks' -count=1` | ok |
| 13 | Grants: credentials append-only, inventory never deleted, protection trigger; `00004` Down safe | `go test -tags integration ./migrations -count=1` | ok |
| 14 | Coverage floors | `make coverage` | every package ok |
| 15 | E2E EN/TR incl. axe at 375/640/1280/1920 px on the new screens and banners | `make e2e-up && make e2e` | all passed |

## Review checklist

- [ ] `HostKeyCallback` decides from the pinned key only; an unpinned or different key aborts before
      authentication; `Observed` is the only write and never pins.
- [ ] `HostKeyAlgorithms` is the pinned type only; key exchange, ciphers and MACs are the SEC-080 lists.
- [ ] The only command lines are `cat /etc/os-release`, `/usr/local/libexec/alice-helper version` and
      `sudo -n /usr/local/libexec/alice-helper <subcommand> '<arg>'…` with arguments from `[A-Za-z0-9._/@:+-]`.
- [ ] The helper refuses every path it did not compute itself from `/etc/passwd` and `sshd -T`, resolves symlinks
      and keeps them inside the user's home (or the configured directory), never prints private key material, and
      writes with lock, hash check, backup, temporary file, `fsync`, rename and directory `fsync`.
- [ ] sudoers allows only `alice-helper` subcommands of the chosen profile; `!requiretty`, `env_reset`,
      `secure_path`, `log_output`.
- [ ] The platform key seed is only decrypted inside one dial and zeroed afterwards; it never reaches a log,
      error, audit row, job row or response (leak suite).
- [ ] Remote output is size-capped, decoded as one JSON value, and never logged; stderr is discarded.
- [ ] Job payloads are MAC'd; a changed payload is never executed (`job.tampered`).
- [ ] Every target insert calls `CheckCanAddTarget` in its transaction (L-79 static test).

## Findings

| ID | Severity | Description | Decision |
|---|---|---|---|
| P3-01 | High (residual, spec SC-6) | Whoever controls Alice (or its database plus the master key) can sign in to every managed server as `alice-svc` and use the helper's subcommands there. | Accepted residual risk of the product (decisions "Threat model"); mitigations: restricted sudoers, the helper's own validation, optional `from=` in the `authorized_keys` line, audit forwarding. Recorded in `SECURITY-REPORT.md` (Phase 8). |
| P3-02 | Medium (spec SC-1) | Trust on first use: an attacker between Alice and a new server at the moment it is added can present their own key; the administrator must compare the fingerprint out of band. | Accepted; the UI shows the exact command to run on the server and never pins without an administrator's click. |
| P3-03 | Medium (spec J-1) | The job payload MAC is derived from the master key; an attacker with the database and the master key can insert a valid job. | Accepted (same trust boundary as every secret). |
| P3-04 | Low | Accounts known only to LDAP/SSSD are not listed, so their keys are not inventoried. | Accepted for v1 (R37 item 4); a warning names the gap on each such server. |
| P3-05 | Low | sudoers `*` wildcards accept any arguments; the helper is the enforcement point. | Accepted (spec §12.3); helper validation is tested on three distributions. |
| P3-06 | Low | Helper backups of `authorized_keys` (public data) stay on the server for up to 30 days. | Accepted; they are root-only (0700/0600). |
| P3-07 | Info | The `nginx` sudoers profile already allows subcommands that protocol 1 answers with `UNKNOWN_SUBCOMMAND`. | Intended (R37 item 3). |

No High finding is open except the documented product residual P3-01.

## Known limitations

- **No certificates yet (Phase 4).** Nginx servers can be added only as Linux servers; `nginx-*` subcommands and
  the deploy job arrive with protocol 2. L-80 and L-82 need the deploy job.
- **No key generation or rotation (Phase 6).** Keys can be removed, not generated or deployed through the UI;
  L-83..L-86 and L-88 need the rotation runner.
- **Alerts (Phase 7).** Host-key and sign-in emails are sent directly; the alert list, dashboard and email
  settings arrive in Phase 7. SSH limits are constants until Settings exist.
- **Target edits.** Only the name and the scan interval can be changed.
- **Packaging (Phase 8).** The helper is built with `make helper`; the release bundle and its signature arrive in
  Phase 8. Master-key rotation (which must re-seal the installation record and the time record) is not built.
- The Phase 1 and Phase 2 findings still open stay as recorded in their review notes.

## Owner verification

Spec §26.5 "Owner verifies". Use a test Linux server (a virtual machine with Ubuntu 22.04, Debian 12 or Rocky 9)
that you can reach from the Alice machine, and a development stack (`make up`, or `make reset` for a fresh
installation — this deletes the development data). Steps 5 and 6 change the test server and the license use; never
use a production server.

1. Run `make helper`. Copy `bin/alice-helper-linux-amd64` to the test server as `alice-helper` in an empty
   directory. In Alice open **Servers**: **Prepare a server for Alice** shows Alice's public key and the commands.
   Choose **Linux server**, **Copy commands**, and run them as root in that directory on the test server.
   Expected: the commands finish without an error; `sudo -l -U alice-svc` on the server lists only
   `/usr/local/libexec/alice-helper` subcommands.
2. Choose **Add server**, enter a name, the server's address and the user name `alice-svc`, choose **Connect**.
   Alice shows **Is this your server?** with a fingerprint and a command. Run the command on the server and compare.
   Choose **Yes, this is my server**.
   Expected: the server shows **Connected**.
3. Wait a few seconds (or choose **Scan for SSH keys**).
   Expected: **SSH keys on this server** lists the keys of `root`, of normal users and of `alice-svc` (marked
   **Alice's key**) with their user names. Open one key: **Where this key is used** lists the server, user, file and
   line.
4. On Alice's own key choose **Remove key from alice-svc** and confirm.
   Expected: "Alice needs this key to connect to this server and will not remove it." Nothing changes on the server
   (check `/var/lib/alice-svc/.ssh/authorized_keys`).
5. On the test server run `sudo rm /etc/ssh/ssh_host_*; sudo ssh-keygen -A` and restart the SSH service
   (`sudo systemctl restart ssh` on Ubuntu/Debian, `sudo systemctl restart sshd` on Rocky). In Alice choose
   **Test connection**.
   Expected: a red message "The server's identity has changed, so Alice stopped all work on it. …"; the status is
   **Server identity changed**; **Scan for SSH keys** and key removal are refused; administrators with an email
   address get one email. Sign in as an operator in a private window: there is no **Review the new fingerprint**
   button. As the administrator choose **Review the new fingerprint**, compare it on the server, enter your
   authenticator code and a reason, and choose **Accept new fingerprint**: the server returns to **Connected**.
6. The evaluation allows 5 servers. Add servers until there are 5 (the addresses may be other test machines; a
   server that cannot be reached still counts), then try one more.
   Expected: "Your license allows 5 targets." and no new server; the banner says you are using all licensed
   targets.
````

## Phase 3 Done When

Spec §26.5 plus the global Definition of Done (§26.1):

1. The provider interface, capability set and registry exist; `linuxssh` is the one registered provider, passes the
   `providertest` conformance checks, and is wired only in `cmd/alice` (Tasks 4, 9, 18).
2. `alice-helper` is a static Go binary (`make helper`, `TestHelperIsStatic`) that implements protocol 1, validates
   every argument, only touches paths it computed itself, and writes `authorized_keys` with lock, compare-and-swap,
   backup and atomic rename; the generated setup script and both sudoers profiles work on Ubuntu 22.04, Debian 12
   and Rocky 9 (Tasks 6, 7, 9, 19).
3. Alice's Ed25519 key is generated at first start, stored only encrypted, shown with the setup commands on
   **Servers** and in the wizard, and never appears in logs, errors, audit rows, job rows or responses (Tasks 13, 17,
   20, 21).
4. Host keys are pinned only after an Administrator confirms the fingerprint; an unconfirmed or changed key stops
   before authentication; a changed key blocks every operation (manual and scheduled) until an Administrator re-pins
   it with step-up and a reason; F-30..F-33 pass (Tasks 8, 14, 17, 19).
5. Target CRUD goes through `CheckCanAddTarget` in the insert transaction and the lock gate; L-04 and L-70..L-79 pass
   against real targets; L-79's static test passes (Tasks 13, 16, 17).
6. The durable job queue claims with `FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED`, leases and heartbeats, retries with backoff and
   jitter, recovers expired leases (kill test F-66, framework part), runs at most one job per target, runs every job
   exactly once with 20 workers and 1000 jobs (F-69), passes every job through `license.Service.Allow`, and parks
   change jobs in `blocked_license` until an Administrator confirms after renewal (L-81) (Tasks 11, 12, 17).
7. The inventory lists every key of `authorized_keys` files in `/root`, `/home/*`, service accounts and custom
   `AuthorizedKeysFile` locations, with users, files, options and findings; `AuthorizedKeysCommand` servers are
   detected and not changed (F-35); the inventory matches the seeded fixtures exactly on all three distributions;
   removing Alice's own key is refused by API, service, provider and database trigger (F-36); F-37..F-39 pass
   (Tasks 5, 9, 10, 15, 17, 19).
8. `FuzzParseAuthorizedKeys` and `FuzzParseSSHDConfig` run clean (`make fuzz-ssh`); A-12 injection tests pass for the
   command builder and the helper (Tasks 5, 6, 8).
9. The secret-leak suite includes the platform SSH key; the authz matrix covers the five new permissions and
   `docs/authz-matrix.md` is current; every state-changing route is in exactly one lock group (Tasks 1, 16, 17).
10. Playwright passes in English and Turkish: prepare and add a server with fingerprint confirmation, inventory
    shows the keys, own-key removal is refused, a changed host key blocks until re-pinned, the license limit
    message, and the `limit_reached`, `over_limit` and `tampered` banners with axe at 375/640/1280/1920 px (Task 22).
11. Carries 1, 2, 3 (L-81, L-29, L-04, L-70..L-79), 4 and 5 are done; the Phase 1/2 re-deferred `audit.verify`,
    `maintenance.cleanup` and the scheduler leader lock run (Tasks 1, 2, 12, 22).
12. `make ci` is green; coverage floors hold (`coverage-floors.json`); `docs/nginx-host-preparation.md`, the
    admin/operator/first-run guides, troubleshooting, CHANGELOG, R37 and `docs/security/reviews/phase-3.md` are
    written; no High finding is open except the documented product residual P3-01 (Task 23).
13. Owner verification steps 1–6 were run on a clean stack with a disposable test server by the coordinator
    (Task 23, Step 9).

## Known Limitations (carried to later phases)

- **Nginx and certificates (Phase 4).** Nginx servers are managed as Linux servers for SSH keys only; the `nginx-*`
  helper subcommands (protocol 2), discovery and deployment arrive in Phase 4, together with L-80 and L-82.
- **SSH key lifecycle (Phase 6).** Key generation, deployment, the private key download and rotation arrive in
  Phase 6 (L-83..L-86, L-88, F-67). Phase 3 removes keys and adds them only at provider level (tests).
- **Azure Key Vault (Phase 5).** Target-bound credentials (`credentials.target_id`) and L-87.
- **Alerts and settings (Phase 7).** Host-key and sign-in emails are sent directly through the outbox; the alert
  engine, dashboard, email settings and configurable SSH limits (`ssh.max_parallel`) arrive in Phase 7.
- **Packaging (Phase 8).** The helper ships through `make helper` until the release bundle (`helper/`) and its
  signature exist; master-key rotation (which must re-seal the installation record and both time-record copies) is
  not built; the migration owner is still the PostgreSQL superuser in the development stack; `rbac` mutation
  testing runs with the nightly pipeline.
- **Directory-service accounts.** Users that exist only in LDAP/SSSD are not listed (warning per server).
- **Target edits.** Address, port and user cannot be changed; delete and add the server again.
- **TOFU.** The first fingerprint is only as trustworthy as the administrator's out-of-band comparison (P3-02).

## Owner verification (mirrors §26.5)

The full, copy-paste version is in `docs/security/reviews/phase-3.md` ("Owner verification"). In short, with a
disposable test Linux server and a development stack:

1. `make helper`, copy `alice-helper` to the server; **Servers → Prepare a server for Alice** shows Alice's public
   key and the commands; run them as root on the server.
2. **Add server** → **Is this your server?** shows a fingerprint and the command to run on the server; compare and
   choose **Yes, this is my server** → **Connected**.
3. **SSH keys on this server** lists the keys with their user names; opening one shows **Where this key is used**.
4. Removing Alice's own key is refused: "Alice needs this key to connect to this server and will not remove it."
5. Replace the server's host keys and restart SSH; **Test connection** shows the red "The server's identity has
   changed …" message and nothing else runs on that server until an Administrator accepts the new fingerprint with
   an authenticator code and a reason (an Operator cannot).
6. Add servers until the evaluation's 5 are used; the next one is refused with "Your license allows 5 targets."
